##### 5.2.1.13 Configure validity periods for accounts

You can configure validity periods for accounts, including the validity period of an account and the validity period of account activity.

**Usage notes**

> **Important:** After the validity periods of an account end, issues may occur when the user logs in to the console or uses the AccessKey pair. Exercise caution when you configure validity periods for an account.

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Users > Users**.
4. On the Users page, click the **System Users** tab.
5. Search for a user by using the search box or specifying advanced filter conditions above the
user list.
6. Configure validity periods for accounts.
Configure validity periods for an account: Find the user that you want to manage, move the pointer over the icon in the **Actions** column, and then select **Specify Account**
**Validity Period**.
Configure validity periods for multiple accounts: Select multiple users that you want to manage from the user list and click **Specify Account Validity Period** below the user list.
7. In the **Account Validity Period** dialog box, configure the parameters in the **Account**
**Validity Period** and **Account Activity Validity Period** sections.

| Parameter |   | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Account Validity Period | Account Validity Period | Valid values: Permanently Valid, By Duration, and Specific Date. |
|   | Validity Period | If you select By Duration as Account Validity Period, you must configure this parameter. Enter a validity period in the field. The maximum validity period is 365 days. Note The validity period starts from the day when you configure this parameter. |
|   | Expiration Date | If you select Specific Date as Account Validity Period, you must configure this parameter. In the Expiration Date field, select a specific time as the deadline from the time picker. The time is accurate to seconds. The deadline must be later than the current time. |

|   | Access Method | If you select By Duration or Specific Date as Account Validity Period, you can configure this parameter. You can select Disable Access to Console and You are not allowed to use AccessKey pairs to call API operations or other development tools for access. Disable Access to Console: does not allow the user to use the account and password to access the console. You are not allowed to use AccessKey pairs to call API operations or other development tools for access: does not allow the user to use the AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret to initiate requests. Such requests will fail. Process with caution. |
|---|---|---|
| Account Activity Validity Period | Disable Control without Login | Valid values: Unlimited and By Duration. |
|   | Duration Since Last Login | If you select By Duration as Disable Control without Login, you must configure this parameter. Enter a period of time in the field. The maximum period of time is 365 days. Note If a user has never logged in with an account, the account is not subject to the validity period of account activity. |
|   | Access Method | If you select By Duration as Disable Control without Login, you can configure this parameter. You can select Disable Access to Console and Disable the creation of AccessKey ID and AccessKey Secret, and restrict access to APIs or other development tools. Disable Access to Console: does not allow the user to use the account and password to access the console. Disable the creation of AccessKey ID and AccessKey Secret, and restrict access to APIs or other development tools: does not allow the user to use the AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret to initiate requests. Such requests will fail. Process with caution. |

8. Click **OK**.

##### 5.2.1.14 Disable a user

This topic describes how to disable a user.

**Prerequisites**

A user is in the Enabled state.

**Limits**

You cannot disable proxy administrators on the Users page. When you disable a proxy administrator, the corresponding proxy user is also disabled. For more information, see Specify and manage a proxy administrator for an organization and Specify and manage a proxy administrator for a resource set.

> **Important:** After you disable a user, the user is forbidden from logging on to the Apsara Uni- manager Management Console, the AccessKey pairs of the user are disabled, and the user logon status becomes invalid.
> After an AccessKey pair is disabled, the services or applications that reference the AccessKey pair may not run as expected. In this case, enable the user to restore the services or applications.

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Users > Users**.
4. On the Users page, click the **System Users** tab.
5. Search for a user by using the search box or specifying advanced filter conditions above the
user list.
6. Find the user that you want to manage, move the pointer over the
icon in the **Actions** column, and then select **Disable**.
7. In the dialog box that appears, select **I have known the risks and confirm this**
**operation**.
When you move the pointer over the information in the AccessKey Pair Reference Information column, the last 20 reference records within the previous seven days are displayed. To view more records, choose **Enterprise** > **Permissions** > **AccessKey**
**Logs**.
8. Click **Disable**.

##### 5.2.1.15 Enable a user

This topic describes how to enable a user.

**Prerequisites**

A user is in the Disabled state.

**Limits**

You cannot enable proxy administrators on the Users page. When you enable a proxy administrator, the corresponding proxy user is also enabled. For more information, see Specify and manage a proxy administrator for an organization and Specify and manage a proxy administrator for a resource set.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Users > Users**.
4. On the Users page, click the **System Users** tab.
5. Search for a user by using the search box or specifying advanced filter conditions above the
user list.
6. Find the user that you want to manage, move the pointer over the
icon in the **Actions** column, and then select **Enable**.
7. In the message that appears, click **OK**.
When you move the pointer over the information in the AccessKey Pair Reference Information column, the last 20 reference records within the previous seven days are displayed. To view more records, choose **Enterprise** >
**Permissions** > **AccessKey Logs**.

> After a user is enabled, the associated AccessKey pairs are also enabled.

##### 5.2.1.16 Delete a user

This topic describes how to delete a user.

**Limits**

You cannot delete a proxy user on the Users page. To delete a proxy user, go to the details page of the corresponding organization or resource set and delete the proxy user on the Proxy Administrator tab. For more information, see Specify and manage a proxy administrator for an organization and Specify and manage a proxy administrator for a resource set.

> **Important:** After you delete a user, the user is forbidden from logging on to the Apsara Uni- manager Management Console, the AccessKey pairs of the user are deleted, and the user logon status becomes invalid.
> After you delete a user, the user data cannot be recovered. After an AccessKey pair is deleted, the services or applications that use the AccessKey pair may not work as expected. Before you delete a user, we recommend that you disable the user first and troubleshoot issues.

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Users > Users**.
4. On the Users page, click the **System Users** tab.
5. Search for a user by using the search box or specifying advanced filter conditions above the
user list.
6. Find the user that you want to manage, move the pointer over the
icon in the **Actions** column, and then select **Delete**.
7. In the dialog box that appears, select **I have known the risks and confirmed this**
**delete operation**.
When you move the pointer over the information in the AccessKey Pair Reference Information column, the last 20 reference records within the previous seven days are displayed. To view more records, choose **Enterprise** > Permissions > **AccessKey**
**Logs**.
8. Click **Delete**.
The deleted system user is displayed on the **Historical Users** tab. You can restore or permanently delete the user on the Historical Users tab.

##### 5.2.1.17 Restore a user

On the Historical Users tab, you can restore deleted system users. After a user is restored, the user is displayed on the System Users tab.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Users > Users**.
4. Click the **Historical Users** tab.
5. Search for a user by name in the search box above the user list.

#### 5.2.2 User group management

##### 5.2.2.1 Create a user group

User groups help you classify users to simplify permission management. After you create a user group, you can grant permissions to multiple users at a time.

**Relationships between items**

| Item | Description |
|---|---|
| User group and organization | A user group can belong to only one organization. Multiple user groups can be created within an organization. |
| User group and user | A user group can contain zero or more users. A user does not necessarily need to belong to a user group. A user can be added to multiple user groups. |

| User group and role | A role can be assigned to multiple user groups. When a role is assigned to a user group, the permissions that the role has are automatically granted to users within the user group. |
|---|---|
| User group and resource set | A resource set can contain zero or more user groups. A user group can be added to multiple resource sets. |

**Prerequisites**

An organization and roles are created.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Users** > **User Groups**.
4. On the **User Groups** page, click **Create User Group**.
5. In the **Create User Group** dialog box, configure the parameters that are described in the
following table.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| User Group Name | The name of the user group. The name must be 3 to 255 characters in length, and can contain letters, digits, underscores ( ), hyphens (-), periods (.), and at signs _ (@). |
| Organization | The organization to which the user group belongs. |
| Role authorized | The roles that are assigned to the user group. |

6. Click **OK**.

above the user group list.
5. View the user groups in the list.

> **Note:** The User column displays the number of users added to a user group. You can click the number to view the added users. If the number of added users is zero, a hyphen (-) is displayed.
> The Resource Set column displays the resource sets to which a user group is added. If a user group is not added to any resource sets, a hyphen (-) is displayed.

### 5.3 Permission management

#### 5.3.1 Role permissions

##### 5.3.1.1 Overview

A role is a collection of access permissions. In the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, role types include preset roles, custom roles, RAM role-based authorization, and RAM-based authorization.

**Role types**

**Preset role**

A preset role is a collection of preset permissions for specific operations. To implement privilege separation, the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console provides preset roles based on the general use cases in cloud platforms. After a RAM user is assigned a preset role, the user has the corresponding operation permissions. During authentication, the system determines whether the user has the permissions to perform the corresponding operations based on the permissions that belong to the preset role assigned to the user. For more information, see Preset roles.

**Custom role**

You can create a custom role to combine and set permission policies based on your business requirements. You can configure the sharing scope and permissions on resources, applications, and menus for the custom role, and configure custom permission policies to flexibly specify the services that can be accessed by the role, the operations that can be performed by the role, and the resources that can be managed by the role. Compared with preset roles, custom roles are more flexible and can be customized.

> **Note:** Custom roles are commonly used to manage the permissions of users who log on to cloud service consoles. In addition, third-party independent software vendors (ISVs) can create custom roles when they require AccessKey pairs with limited permission scope to call cloud service APIs for application development.

**RAM role-based authorization**

RAM role-based authorization is the process of associating a RAM role with RAM users, other Apsara Stack tenant accounts, or Apsara Stack services. An authorized entity can directly assume a RAM role to obtain the collection of permissions that belong to the role without the need to grant permission policies to the entity.

> **Note:** RAM role-based authorization can be divided into the role of Apsara Stack tenant accounts and the role of Apsara Stack services based on the types of trust entities.
> Role of Apsara Stack tenant accounts: the role that can be assumed by RAM users. RAM users who assume this type of role can belong to the own Apsara Stack tenant accounts or other Apsara Stack tenant accounts. The roles of this type are used for cross-account access or temporarily authorized access.
> Role of Apsara Stack services: the role that can be assumed by cloud services. The roles of this type are used for access across Apsara Stack services.

**RAM-based authorization**

Each RAM user is a user entity with a unique identity. You can assign custom policies to RAM users by using user groups. This way, the RAM users always have these permissions regardless of whether they assume a role.

> **Note:** RAM-based authorization is performed based on RAM user groups other than RAM roles.
> RAM-based authorization is used to enhance the fine-grained permission control of custom roles that are created on a GUI. After you create a custom role, you can use RAM-based authorization to attach a RAM policy to RAM users if some permissions cannot be granted by using the custom role.
> RAM-based authorization must be used together with user groups.

##### 5.3.1.2 RAM policies

This topic describes the elements, structure, and syntax of RAM policies that are used to define the scope of permissions for custom roles, RAM authorization and RAM role-based authorization.

**Structure**

RAM policies are in the JSON format, containing two parts: Version: the version number of the policy. Statements: the statements that specify the permissions. The elements of statements include Effect, Action, Resource, Condition, and Principal.

**Elements in statements**

The elements of statements include Effect, Action, Resource, Condition, and Principal.

**Effect (Required)**

Specifies whether a statement result is an explicit allow or an explicit deny. Valid values: Allow and Deny.

> **Note:** Precedence of Deny: Deny statements take precedence when a user is assigned multiple policies that contain Allow and Deny statements, and when a single policy contains both Allow and Deny statements.

**Example**

```json
"Effect": "Allow"
```

**Action (Required)**

The specific API operations involved in the statement. The Action element is in the following format: `<ram-code>:<action-name>` . `<ram-code>` : the product code. `<action-name>` : the API operation of the product involved in the policy.

> **Note:** The values of the Action element are case-insensitive. However, to ensure consistency, we recommend that you follow the standard capitalization of the product code and API operation names.

**Example**

```json
"Action": [
  "oss:ListBuckets",
  "ecs:Describe*",
  "rds:Describe*"
```

`]`

> **Note:** You can use the asterisk (*) as a wildcard character. For example, in the preceding example, `ecs:Describe*` indicates that all the API operations of Elastic Compute Service (ECS) whose names start with Describe are involved in the policy.

**Resource (Required)**

The resources of cloud services involved in the statement, which are indicated by their Aliyun Resource Names (ARNs) Resource elements are in the following format: `acs:<ram-code>:<region>:<account-id>:`

```xml
<relative-id> .
```

`acs` : the prefix of ARNs. It stands for Alibaba Cloud Service. `<ram-code>` : the product code. `<region>` : the region ID of the resource. You can use the asterisk (*) as a wildcard character to indicate regionless resources or resources in all regions. `<account-id>` : the user ID of the level-1 organization. This is used to specify the resources that belong to a specific level-1 organization. `<relative-id>` : the description of the specific resources. Its syntax is product-specific. For example, the relative-id for an OSS object is a path of that object, such as mybucket/dir1/object1.jpg.

**Example**

```json
"Resource": [
 "acs:ecs:*:*:instance/inst-001",
 "acs:ecs:*:*:instance/inst-002",
 "acs:oss:*:*:mybucket",
 "acs:oss:*:*:mybucket/*"
```

`]`

**Condition (Optional)**

The conditions that are required for the policy to take effect. A Condition element, or a condition block, contains one or multiple conditions. Each condition consists of an operator, a condition key, and a condition value. Condition keys are case-sensitive. The case-sensitivity of the condition values is determined by the operator. For example, assume that a condition key of the string type is specified. if the StringEquals operator is used, the system performs a case-sensitive match. If the StringEqualsIgnoreCase operator is used, the system performs a case-insensitive match. Description: Evaluation logic You can specify one or more values for a condition key. If the value in a request matches one of the values, the condition is met. A condition can have multiple keys that are attached to a single conditional operator. The condition of this type is met only if all requirements for the keys are met. A condition block is met only if all of its conditions are met. Operators Operators are classified into the following types: string, number, data and time, Boolean, and IP address.

| Category | Operator |
|---|---|
| String | StringEquals StringNotEquals StringEqualsIgnoreCase StringNotEqualsIgnoreCase StringLike StringNotLike |
| Number | NumericEquals NumericNotEquals NumericLessThan NumericLessThanEquals NumericGreaterThan NumericGreaterThanEquals |
| Date and time | DateEquals DateNotEquals DateLessThan DateLessThanEquals DateGreaterThan DateGreaterThanEquals |
| Boolean | Bool |
| IP address | IpAddress NotIpAddress |

Condition keys General condition keys are in the following format: `acs:<condition-key>` .

| General condition key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| acs:CurrentTime | Date and time | The time when the server receives the request. Specify the time in the ISO 8601 standard, for example, 2012-11-11T23:59:59Z. |
| acs:SecureTransport | Boolean | Specifies whether a secure channel is used to send a request. For example, a request can be sent over HTTPS. |
| acs:SourceIp | IP address | The IP address of the client that sends the request It can be a single IP address or a CIDR block. If the value is a single IP address, you must specify the specific IP address rather than a CIDR block. For example, you must specify 10.0.0.1 rather than 10.0.0.1/32. |
| acs:MFAPresent | Boolean | Specifies whether multi-factor authentication (MFA) is used when the user who sends the request logged on. |
| acs:PrincipalARN | String | The identity of the requester. This operator is only used in trust policies of RAM roles. |

Service-specific condition keys are in the following format: `<ram-code>:<condition-key>` .

| Service-specific condition key | Cloud service | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| ecs:tag/<tag-key> | Elastic Compute Service (ECS) | String | The condition key for tags of ECS resources, which are customizable. |
| rds:ResourceTag/<t ag-key> | ApsaraDB RDS | String | The condition key for tags of ApsaraDB RDS resources, which are customizable. |
| oss:Delimiter | Objective Storage Service (OSS) | String | The delimiter used by OSS to categorize object names. |
| oss:Prefix | OSS | String | The prefix of an OSS object name. |

**Principal**

The entity that is allowed or denied to call the related API operations. This element is available only for resource-based policies. For example, in a trust policy attached to a RAM role, you can specify the resources that are allowed to assume the role in the Principle element. The Principal element is required in resource-based policies.

> **Note:** You cannot specify the Principal element in identity-based policies. Identity-based policies are attached to RAM identities. The RAM identities to which identity-based policies are attached are the principals.

You can specify multiple types of principals for the Principal element in a policy. You can also specify multiple principals of the same type for the Principal element in a policy. If you specify multiple types of principals, separate the types with commas (,). If you specify multiple principals of the same type, separate the principals with commas (,) and enclose the principals with brackets ([]). Multiple principals are associated with each other by the OR operator, meaning that the policy is attached to all principals in the policy.

**Example**

```json
"Principal": {
 "RAM": [
 "acs:ram::123456789012****:root",
 "acs:ram::987654321098****:root"
```

`],`

```json
 "Service": "ecs.aliyuncs.com"
```

`}` Principals are authenticated RAM entities, which are divided into the following types: Organization account Set the Principal element to the account of the level-1 organization. When you configure the trust policy of a RAM role-based authorization, the account ARN of the selected trust organization will be added to the policy as the principal, such as

```
 acs:ram::165399189392****:root .
```

Cloud service Set the Principal element to a cloud service. When you configure the trust policy of a RAM role-based authorization, the identifier of the selected trust service will be added to the policy as the principal, such as `ecs.aliyuncs.com` .

**Policy syntax**

A RAM policy consists of the version_block and statement_block components.

```xml
policy = {
 <version_block>,
 <statement_block>
```

`}`

**version_block**

The version of the policy. By default, the value is 1.

```xml
<version_block> = "Version" : ("1")
```

**statement_block**

The statements. A RAM policy can contain multiple statements.

```xml
<statement_block> = "Statement" : [ <statement>, <statement>, ... ]
```

Each statement consists of the effect_block, action_block, resource_block, and condition_block elements. condition_block is an optional element.

```xml
<statement> = {
 <effect_block>,
 <action_block>,
 <resource_block>,
 <condition_block?>
```

`}` Valid values of an effect_block element are `Allow` and `Deny` .

```xml
<effect_block> = "Effect" : ("Allow" | "Deny")
```

Multiple action_block and resource_block elements can be specified in each statement.

```xml
<action_block> = "Action" :
 ("*" | [<action_string>, <action_string>, ...])
<resource_block> = "Resource" :
 ("*" | [<resource_string>, <resource_string>, ...])
```

Each condition_block element can contain multiple operators and

```xml
<condition_block> = "Condition" : <condition_map> <condition_map> = {
  <condition_type_string> : {
      <condition_key_string> : <condition_value_list>,
      <condition_key_string> : <condition_value_list>,
      ...
```

`},`

```xml
  <condition_type_string> : {
      <condition_key_string> : <condition_value_list>,
      <condition_key_string> : <condition_value_list>,
      ...
  }, ...
```

`}`

**Valid values of elements**

If an element value is a string, number, date, time, Boolean value, or an IP address, the value must be enclosed in double quotation marks (""). If an element value is a string, you can use asterisks (*) and question marks (?) as wildcard characters. An asterisk (*) indicates 0 or multiple letters. For example, `ecs:Describe*` indicates all the API operations of Elastic Compute Service (ECS) whose names start with Describe. A question mark (?) indicates a single letter.

**Policy syntax check**

RAM policies follow the JSON format. When you create or update a RAM policy, the system automatically checks the validity of the JSON format. We recommend that you use JSON validators or formatters to help you ensure the validity of the policy. For more information about JSON syntax standards, see RFC 7159.

##### 5.3.1.3 Manage preset roles

Preset roles support viewing, authorization, disabling, activation, and replication. Only platform administrator users can operate the Operations Administrator role.

**View preset roles**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Permissions****> Role Permission**.
4. Optional: Switch to the Central Cloud Role tab.

> **Note:** The multi-cloud role tabs for Central Cloud and connected subordinate clouds appear only in multi-cloud scenarios. In single-cloud scenarios, only Central Cloud is available by default, and no tabs are displayed.

5. In the role list, view the following information for preset roles: **Role Name/ID**, **Role Type**,
**Security Level**, **Role Description**, **Authorization Object**, **Sharing Scope**, and **Status**.

> **Note:** At the top of the list, you can filter roles by selecting a role type or entering a role name for quick search.
> The numbers following users and user groups in the Authorization Object column indicate the count of authorized users and user groups. Click to navigate to the Authorized Personnel tab to view detailed lists.
> The Security Level column appears only when security policies enable Security Level-Based Access.

6. Click the role name of a preset role or click **View** in the **Actions** column.
7. On the preset role details page, view basic information, management permissions,
application permissions, and authorized personnel information for the role.

| Display item | Description |
|---|---|
| Basic informatio n | Displays role type, description, sharing scope, management permissions, permission statistics, and authorized personnel. |
| Managem ent permission s | On the Management Permissions tab, select View only authorized to view the management permissions granted to this role. |
| Applicatio n permission s | On the Application Permissions tab, select View only authorized products to view the cloud services and their permissions granted to this role. |
| Menu permission s | On the Menu Permissions tab, select View only authorized to view the menus granted to this role. |
| Authorized personnel | On the Authorized Personnel tab, view information about authorized users and user groups for this role. |

**Authorize users and user groups with preset roles**

Method 1: i. Click **Authorize** in the **Actions** column for the preset role. ii. In the **Authorize** dialog box, on the **Users** and **User Groups** tabs, select the users and user groups to authorize.

> **Note:** Above the lists on the Users and User Groups tabs, you can quickly find target users and user groups by selecting an organization and role, then entering a user or user group name.

iii. Click **OK**. Method 2: i. Click the role name of the preset role or click **View** in the **Actions** column. ii. Switch to the **Authorized Personnel** tab. iii. Authorize users and user groups as needed.

| Action | Description |
|---|---|

| Authorize users | a. In the Authorize User section, click Authorize. b. In the Authorize User dialog box, select the users to authorize. c. Click Confirm authorization. |
|---|---|
| Authorize user groups | a. In the Authorize User Group section, click Authorize. b. In the Authorize User Group dialog box, select the user groups to authorize. c. Click Confirm authorization. |

**Remove authorized users and user groups from preset roles**

1. Click the role name of the preset role or click **Actions** column’s **View**.
2. Switch to the **Authorized Personnel** tab.
3. Remove authorized users and authorized user groups as needed.

| Action | Description |
|---|---|
| Remove authorized users | i. In the Authorized User section, click Actions column’s Remove. ii. Click OK. If you unbind authorization, this user will also be automatically unbound from any resource sets joined through the current role. Proceed with caution. |

| Remove authorized user groups | i. In the Authorized User Group section, click Actions column’s Remove. ii. Click OK. If you unbind authorization, this user group will also be automatically unbound from any resource sets joined through the current role. Proceed with caution. |
|---|---|

**Disable a preset role**

**Prerequisites**

The status of the preset role is **Effective**.
1. Click
in the **Actions** column of the preset role, then select **Disable**.
2. Click **Confirm**. After you disable this role, all users bound to it cannot log in. Proceed with
caution.

**Activate a preset role**

**Prerequisites**

The status of the preset role is **Disabled**.
1. Click
in the **Actions** column of the preset role, then select **Activate**.
2. Click **Confirm**. After you activate this role, users previously bound to it regain the
permissions included in the role.

**Copy a preset role**

1. Click **Copy** in the **Actions** column of the preset role.
2. On the Create Custom Role page, follow the instructions to complete the configuration for
Basic Configuration, Management Permission, Application Permission, and Menu Permission.

> **Note:** Copying a role quickly creates a new role with identical permissions. You can adjust permissions as needed. If you make no changes, the copied role has the same sharing scope, management permission, application permission, and menu permission as the original role.
> You must define a new role name. It cannot be the same as the name of the role being copied.

##### 5.3.1.4 Manage custom roles

Custom roles support the following operations: create, view, edit, update permissions, authorize, disable, activate, copy, and delete.

**Create a custom role**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Permissions****> Role Permissions**.
4. (Optional) Switch to the central cloud role tab.

> **Note:** The multi-cloud scenario displays tabs for both central cloud and connected subordinate clouds. In a single-cloud scenario, only the central cloud exists by default, and no tabs are displayed.

5. Above the role list, click **Create Custom Role,** to go to the **Create Custom Role** page.
6. Configure **Basic Configurations** and click **Next**.

**Operations administrator creates a custom role**

**Organization administrator creates a custom role**

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Role Name | The name of the role. |

| Description | (Optional) The description of the role. |
|---|---|
| Applicable Organization | Select the organization to which the role applies. The operations administrator can select the root organization. |
| Sharing Scope | The visibility scope of the role when you authorize user. If the operations administrator creates a custom role and selects the root organization as the applicable organization, the sharing scope supports only Global. Global: The role is visible across all organizations. Current Organization: The role is is visible only within the current organization. Shared within the Current Organization and Its Subordinate Organizations: The role is visible within the current organization and its subordinate organizations. |
| Management Scope | The resource scope that the role can manage. Combined with the organization of the authorized user, the role can manage resources within the corresponding scope. If the organization administrator creates a custom role, only Specified Organization and Subordinate Organizations and Resource Sets are available. All Organizations: The role can manage cloud service resources in all organizations. Specified Organization and Subordinate Organizations: The role can manage cloud resources in the specified organization and its cascading subordinate organizations. Resource Sets: The role can manage only cloud resources within a specific resource set. For constraints on resource set scope permissions, see Limits on roles. |
| Custom Policy | You can enable or disable Custom Policy. : Disabled. After you disable this option, you cannot define custom policies. : Enabled. After you enable this option, you can define custom policies. |
| Security Level- Based Access | Configure security level for roles whose management scope is resource set. Note Enable this if Security Level-Based Access is activated in security policies and the Management Scope is set to Resource Sets. The security level of your current role determines the maximum security level you can assign to new roles. You can assign only levels equal to or lower than your own. |

7. Configure **Management Permissions**. Select the management permissions that you want
to authorize in the permission list, and then click **Next**. Management permissions define console-related operation permissions for the role, such as authorizing operations on organizations, users, and resource sets.

> **Important:** If you selected Resource Sets in the basic configuration of the custom role, only read- only permissions take effect in this step. Write permissions do not take effect.

8. Configure **Application Permissions**. Select the cloud service permissions that you want to
authorize in the permission list, and then click **Next**. Application permissions define which operations a user can perform on specific cloud services. For example, if you only need to grant users the permission to view Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances, select only the view instance permission under ECS.

> **Important:** The system automatically selects dependent permissions. Removing dependencies may restrict operations. Proceed with caution.
> Resource sharing permissions:
> Resource sharing permissions do not affect normal role authorization. They supplement management permissions specifically for shared resource states.
> When a shareable resource is shared to a target organization or resource set, and the target user's management scope does not cover that resource, management must occur via resource sharing permissions.
> On the right side of each cloud service, click **Read/Write** or **Read-Only** to quickly authorize the role.

9. Configure **Menu Permissions**. Select the menu entries that you want to authorize from
the list, and then click **Next** or **Create**. Menu permissions control which menu items a role can view, enabling entry hiding.

> **Important:** For console users, if platform operation permissions and cloud service permissions are granted via management and application permissions, corresponding menu permissions must also be assigned to ensure users can access those entries.
> If you enabled Custom Policy, click **Next** to configure the custom policy content. If you did not enable custom policies, click **Create** to complete the creation of the custom role.

0. (Optional) Configure the **Custom Policy**. Define applied RAM actions, and then click
**Create**.

**Important**

> You can configure custom policies only after you enable Custom Policy in the Basic Configurations step.

Custom policies precisely describe authorized resources and permitted operations by defining RAM Actions. RAM Actions include Allow and Deny statements: Allow permits operations, Deny rejects them. If both exist, Deny takes precedence. The RAM Action format is <ram-code>:<action-name>. Separate multiple actions with commas (,). <ram-code> represents the RAM code of the cloud service, which is typically the service code. <action-name> represents the name of the OpenAPI operation for the cloud service. For example, if you set `oss:ListBuckets,ecs:Describe*,rds:Describe*` in Allow, the role has the permission to list all Object Storage Service (OSS) buckets, call all ECS APIs starting with Describe, and call all ApsaraDB RDS APIs starting with Describe.

> **Note:** Click **Preview** to view the added actions in the preview dialog box. In the **Preview** dialog box, click **Delete** in the **Operation** column to remove an added action. Click **Close** at the bottom of the **Preview** dialog box to close the preview.

**Batch dd authorization to roles**

In some upgrade scenarios, due to product evolution, certain products require new permission points to be added in the new version. When a specific type of role needs multiple new authorizations added at once, you can use batch role authorization to improve efficiency for subsequent permission additions.

> **Important:** Batch adding authorization to selected roles means supplementing permission points for roles without reducing or overwriting existing role permissions.
> If the original role does not have the selected new permission points, the system adds them.
> If the original role already has them, they remain unaffected.

To remove a selected role, click **Remove** in the **Actions** column of the target role. ii. **Add Management Permissions**: Select the permission points to add for the selected roles. iii. **Add Application Permissions**: Select the product operation permissions to add for the selected roles. iv. **Add Menu Permissions**: Select the menu permissions to add for the selected roles.

role authorization task.

##### 5.3.1.5 Manage RAM role authorization

Resource Access Management (RAM) role authorization supports creating, viewing, editing, managing permission policies, updating trust policies, managing RAM roles, and deleting.

**Create RAM role authorization**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Permissions****> Role Permissions**.
4. (Optional) Switch to the Central Cloud Role tab.

> **Note:** The multi-cloud role tabs for Central Cloud and connected subordinate clouds appear only in multi-cloud scenarios. In single-cloud scenarios, only Central Cloud is available by default, and no tabs are displayed.

5. Click **Create Custom Role,** to go to the **Create Custom Role** page.
6. On the **Create Custom Role** page, expand **Advanced Creation** at the bottom of the
page, and click **Create RAM Role & Attach Policy** .
7. Configure **Basic Configurations**, and click **Next**.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Role Name | Enter a custom name. |

| Description | (Optional) Enter a description for the role. |
|---|---|
| Applicable Organization | Select the organization to which the role applies. Operations administrators can select the root organization. |
| Sharing Scope | Specifies the visibility scope of this role. If an operations administrator creates a role and selects the root organization as the applicable organization, the sharing scope supports only Global. Global: The role is visible to all organizations. Current Organization: The role is visible only to the current organization. Shared within the Current Organization and Its Subordinate Organizations: The role is visible to the current organization and its subordinate organizations. |

8. On the **Configure Custom Policy** page, select policies, and click **Next**.

> **Note:** You can select up to five policies for each role.

**View policy content:** Click **Policy Content** in the **Action** column to view the JSON-
formatted policy content.
**Create policy**: If no suitable policy exists, create a custom policy.
a. Click **Create Policy** in the upper-right corner of the policy list. b. In the **Create Policy** dialog box, enter a policy name, select an applicable organization, specify the sharing scope, add remarks, enter the policy content, and select the sharing scope. c. Click **OK**.
9. On the **Configure Trust Policy** page, select the **Trust Organization** and **Trust Cloud**
**Service**, and click **Next**. The trust policy defines the entities that can assume the RAM role.
You can specify level-1 organizations (Alibaba Cloud accounts) and cloud services to assume the RAM role.

> **Note:** After you enable the OIDC feature, you can also select a trusted OIDC provider to assume the RAM role and configure restriction conditions.

**Trust Organization**: Specify one or more level-1 organizations (Alibaba Cloud accounts)
to assume the RAM role.
**Trust Cloud Service**: Specify one or more cloud services to assume the RAM role.
**Trust Policy**: The system generates JSON-format policy content based on the selected
trust organizations and trust cloud services. As shown in the preceding figure, the policy grants the asr.aliyuncs.com service and specific root users the permission to assume this role. Based on this policy, the system allows the asr.aliyuncs.com service or specific root users to assume the role. "Version": The policy version number. The value here is "1". "Statement": The permission statement list. This field defines one permission statement. "Action": The allowed action. The value here is "sts:AssumeRole", which allows the AssumeRole action. "Effect": Specifies whether to allow or deny the action. The value here is "Allow", which allows the action. "Principal": The entity allowed to assume the role. This can be a service (Service) or a RAM resource (RAM). "Service": The service allowed to assume the role. The value here is "asr.aliyuncs.com", which allows the asr.aliyuncs.com service to assume the role. "RAM": The RAM resource allowed to assume the role. The value here is "acs:ram::125279671240****:root", which allows all RAM users and RAM roles under the Alibaba Cloud account to assume the role. Alibaba Cloud account ARN syntax: `acs:ram::<account-id>:root` . This format represents the RAM users and RAM roles under the Alibaba Cloud account.

> RAM user ARN syntax: `acs:ram::<account-id>:user/<user-name>` . This format represents a RAM user under the Alibaba Cloud account.
> RAM role ARN syntax: `acs:ram::<account-id>:role/<role-name>` . This format represents a RAM role under the Alibaba Cloud account.
> <account-id>: the Alibaba Cloud account ID

0. On the **Policy Preview** page, review the selected policies and trust policy content. After
confirmation, click **Create** to complete the RAM role authorization.

**View a RAM role authorization**

> The number next to the RAM role in the Authorization Object column indicates the number of RAM role instances created under this RAM role authorization. Click the number to go to the RAM Role tab and view the detailed RAM role instances.

2. Click the role name of the RAM role authorization or click **View** in the **Action** column.

roles of this RAM role authorization.

| Trust policy | On the Trust Policy tab, view the trusted entities of this RAM role authorization, including trust organizations and trust cloud services, and the trust policy content in JSON format. |
| RAM role | On the RAM Role tab, view the RAM role instances under this RAM role authorization. |

4. (Optional) Manage the policy list.

| Operation | Description |

Note Enter a policy name above the list to quickly find a policy. Click a policy name to expand its details and view basic information, policy content, and reference records. Note Basic information: displays the policy name, remarks, sharing scope, and creation time. Click Modify to update the policy name and remarks. Policy content: displays the policy content in JSON format. Click Modify Policy content to update the policy content. Reference records: displays roles that reference this policy. Select a role type (RAM Role Authorization and RAM Authorization) and enter a role name to quickly find a role. Click Remove authorization in the Action column to remove the role and unbind the policy from the role. Click the number in the Reference Count column to go to the reference records tab of the policy details page and view the roles that reference this policy. |
|---|---|
| Create a policy | i. In the Policies panel, click Create Policy. ii. In the Create Policy dialog box, set Policy Name, Applicable Organization, Sharing Scope, Remarks, and Policy Content. iii. Click OK. |
| Modify a policy | i. In the Policies panel, click Modify in the Action column for the target policy. ii. In the Modify Permission Policy dialog box, update the policy name and remarks. iii. Click OK. |
| Modify policy content | i. In the Policies panel, click the policy name. ii. On the Policy Details page, go to the Policy Content tab and click Modify Policy content. iii. After updating the policy content, click Save. |

| Delete a policy | Important Before you delete a policy, unbind it from any roles that reference it. i. In the Policies panel, click Delete in the Action column for the target policy. ii. Click Delete. |

After the creation is completed, the system generates a RAM Role. The trusted entities defined in the trust policy can then assume this RAM role to access and manage the corresponding resources. |

Global: The role is visible to all organizations. Current Organization: The role is visible only to the current organization. | Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Role Name | The name of the role. |
| Description | (Optional) The description of the role. |
| Sharing Scope | The visibility scope of the role when you authorize users on behalf of this role. When an operations administrator creates a custom role, only Global is available. Global: The role is shared across all organizations. Current Organization: The role is shared within the current organization. Subordinate Organization: The role is shared with the current organization and its subordinate organizations. |

| Management Scope | The resource management scope of the role. Combined with the organization of the authorized user, it determines which resources the role can manage. When you create a role for the managed Apsara Stack, only the Resource Set management scope is supported. All Organizations: The role can manage cloud resources in all organizations. Current Organization and Cascade Subordinate Organizations: The role can manage cloud resources in the current organization and its cascade subordinate organizations. Resource Set: The role can manage cloud resources only within a specific resource set. |
|---|---|

ii. **Management Permission**: Select the required management permissions in the permission list, then click **Next step**. Management permissions define console-related operation permissions for the role. You can select permissions based on the resource set scope. iii. **Application Permissions**: Select the required cloud service permissions in the permission list, then click **Next**. Application permissions define which operations a user can perform on which cloud services. For example, if you need to grant only the permission to view ECS instances, select only the View Instance permission under Elastic Compute Service (ECS).

> **Important:** The system automatically selects other dependent operation permissions. Removing dependent permissions may restrict operations. Proceed with caution.
> Resource sharing permissions:
> Resource sharing permissions do not affect normal role authorization. They supplement management permissions only when resources are in a shared state.
> When a shareable resource is shared with a target organization or resource set, if the management scope of the target organization’s user does not cover the resource, the user can manage the resource only through resource sharing permissions.
> On the right side of a cloud service, click **Read/Write** or **Read-only** to quickly authorize the role.

iv. **Menu Permissions**: Select the required menu entries in the list, then click **Create**. Menu permissions control which menus the role can view, enabling menu entry hiding.
4. The role is created successfully. Click **Complete**. You can view the role in the role list
under the corresponding resource pool, or select it when authorizing a user with a multicloud role in User Management.

**View managed Apsara Stack roles**

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator (bound to the operations administrator role of the managed Apsara Stack) or a level-1 organization administrator (bound to the organization administrator role of the managed Apsara Stack).
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Permissions****> Role Permission**.
4. Switch to the managed Apsara Stack role tab.

> **Note:** The center cloud and connected managed multi-cloud role tabs appear only in multi- cloud scenarios. In single-cloud scenarios, only the center cloud is available by default, and no tabs are displayed.

5. On the managed Apsara Stack role tab, view the list of roles for the managed Apsara Stack.

> **Note:** After the managed Apsara Stack is connected, the role list displays all roles within the resource set management scope of the managed Apsara Stack.

**Managed public cloud**

**Create a RAM role for the managed public cloud**

**Prerequisites**

The platform administrator has accessed the managed public cloud under **Configuration** >
**Native Hybrid Cloud** > **Multi-Cloud Management**.
The operations administrator has already bound the managedpublic cloud. The operating user is either an operations administrator (bound to a RAM role with the AdministratorAccess permission policy at the managed public cloud account level) or a level-1 organization administrator (bound to a RAM role with the AdministratorAccess permission policy at the managed public cloud account level).
1. On the **Role authorization** page, switch to the managed public cloud role tab.

> **Note:** The center-cloud and connected managed multi-cloud role tabs appear only in multi- cloud scenarios. In single-cloud scenarios, only the center cloud exists by default, and no tabs appear.

2. On the managed public cloud role tab, click **Create RAM Role**.
3. In the **Create RAM Role** dialog box, enter basic information and policies for the RAM role.

| Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|
| Role name | Enter a name for the RAM role in the managed public cloud. The name can be up to 64 characters long and may contain letters, digits, periods (.), and hyphens (-). The first character must be a letter or digit. Example: ecs-readonly-role. |

| Organization | Select an organization that has already bound the managed public cloud from the drop-down list. |
|---|---|
| Bind user | Select a user from the organization bound to the managed public cloud from the drop-down list. This action grants the RAM role to the selected user. |
| Description | Enter a description for the RAM role. |
| Permission scope selection | Select Resource group scope or Alibaba Cloud account scope. When binding a role to a user and selecting Alibaba Cloud account scope, you do not need to add the user to a public cloud resource group. |
| Policy | Select one or more RAM role permission policies. You can choose system policies or custom policies. Policies appear only after you select the user’s organization. The AdministratorAccess and AliyunRAMFullAccess policies carry high risk. We recommend choosing more granular permission policies instead. If you select the AdministratorAccess policy, the High-risk Authorization Reminder dialog box appears. You can choose Replace with PowerUserAccess or Continue using AdministratorAccess. Replace with PowerUserAccess: We recommend using this policy. Continue using AdministratorAccess: To continue using Administrator Access, manually select the checkbox below labeled I understand the risks. for secondary confirmation. |

4. Click OK.
5. Select menu and resource type permissions.

> **Note:** When configuring menu and resource type permissions, you can view the permission policies selected in the basic information and policy section, including policy name, policy type, and description.
> Menu permissions: Configure entry permissions for product menus.
> Resource type permissions: Configure permissions to view resources on the resource retrieval page.

6. Click **Confirm and Modify Role**.
7. In the **Role Authorization** dialog box, click **Cancel** or **Associate Multi-Cloud Resource**
**Set**.

##### 5.3.1.8 Limits on roles

**Limits on the management scope of resource sets**

If you select Resource Sets for Management Permissions when you create a custom role, the role has permissions on the resource sets of the associated user by default. This role is mainly used to manage resources. The permissions described in the following table are beyond the management scope of resource sets and do not take effect even if you select them.

| Management permission | Description |
|---|---|
| User management | Create, delete, enable, disable, lock, unlock, and manage users. |
| Role management | Create, delete, lock, unlock, and manage roles. |
| User group management | View, create, delete, and manage user groups. |
| Organization management | Create, delete, and manage organizations. |
| Resource set management | Create and delete resource sets. |
| AccessKey management | View the AccessKey pairs of organizations and users, create AccessKey pairs for organizations, delete, enable, and disable the AccessKey pairs of organizations, and view AccessKey logs. |
| Access policy | Create, delete, and manage access policies. |
| Change management | Change resource sets, resources, or users. |
| Bill management | View the bills of cloud services, organizations, and resource sets, and export and modify bills. |
| Service-linked role | Create service-linked roles. |
| Process management | View organization applications. |
| Multi-cloud management platform hosting | Configure multi-cloud management platform hosting. |
| Announcement | Manage announcements. |

##### 5.3.1.9 Examples

###### 5.3.1.9.1 Example: Create a role with read-only permissions for ECS (custom role)

**permissions for ECS (custom role)**

**Background information**

CompanyA (Level-1 Organization) needs to assign dedicated O&M responsibilities. The organization must grant Xiao Zhuan, the ECS administrator, view-only permissions for all ECS resources within the company.

**Planning approach**

Xiao Zhuan, as an O&M personnel for ECS resources, needs to view all ECS resources under this company. Therefore, you can create a custom role. Set the role’s management scope to the current organization and its subordinate organizations. Grant only view permissions for ECS resources in application permissions. Then, enable the ECS resource entry in menu permissions. By default, orgA is the Level-1 Organization Administrator of CompanyA. The following steps use orgA as the example operator.
1. orgA logs in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Permissions****> Role** Permission.
4. On the **Role Authorization** page, click **Create Custom Role**.
5. Fill in the basic configuration information, then click **Next**.
**Role Name**: ECS Read-Only Administrator
**Description**: View permissions for ECS resources
**Applicable Organizations**: Select applicable organization
**Sharing Scope**: Share within current organization
**Management Scope**: Current organization and cascading subordinate organizations
6. **Management Permissions** define console-related operational permissions (such as
organization or resource set dimensions). For this ECS read-only role, no authorization is needed. Click **Next** directly.
7. On the **Application Permissions** page, locate the cloud service **Elastic Compute**
**Service (ECS)**. Select view permissions for corresponding resources, or click **Read-Only** in
the upper-right corner to add read-only permissions for ECS to this role. Then, click **Next**.
8. On the **Menu Permissions** page, add the ECS cloud service entry for the ECS read-only
administrator. Otherwise, users cannot access the ECS service after logging in.
9. After adding the Elastic Compute Service (ECS) entry, click **Create**. The ECS read-only
administrator role is now created. After creation, assign this role to user Xiao Zhuan. Xiao Zhuan can then view all ECS resources of CompanyA.

###### 5.3.1.9.2 Example: Modify the ECS Read-Only Administrator Role (Custom Role)

**Administrator Role (Custom Role)**

**Background information**

Due to changes in Company A’s business, Xiao Zhuan needs permission to view all ECS resources and also all VPC resources. The ECS read-only administrator role for Xiao Zhuan is already created. For details, see Example: Create a role with read-only permissions for ECS (custom role).

**Planning approach**

Add read-only permissions for VPC to the existing ECS read-only administrator role. By default, orgA is the level-1 organization administrator of CompanyA. The following steps use orgA as the operating user.
1. orgA logs in to the Apsara Uni-manager management console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Permission Management****>** **Role Authorization**.
4. On the **Role Authorization** page, find the existing ECS read-only administrator role.
5. Click **View** in the **Actions** column for the role.
6. On the role details page, modify the basic role information and add read-only permissions
for VPC resources. Edit basic information: Since the user also needs to view VPC resources, update the **Role**
**Name** and **Description** to “ECS and VPC Read-Only Administrator” and “Permissions to
view ECS and VPC resources,” respectively. Click **Modify Basic Information** in the upper-right corner to make these changes. Add read-only permissions for VPC resources: Click the **Application Permissions** tab, locate the Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) service, then select the view permission or click
**Read-Only** in the upper-right corner.
7. On the **Menu Authorization** page, select the entry point for Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)
resources to grant this role access to VPC operations.
8. Click **Update** to complete the modification of the ECS read-only administrator role. View
the updated role in the role list.

`{`

  "Version": "1",
  "Statement": [

The system automatically populates the ARN of the cloud account, such as `acs:ram::139900176770****:root` . Alibaba Cloud Account ARN syntax: `acs:ram::<account-id>:root` . This represents RAM users and RAM roles under the Alibaba Cloud account.

> RAM User ARN syntax: `acs:ram::<account-id>:user/<user-name>` . This represents a RAM user under the Alibaba Cloud account.

> <account-id>: Represents the Alibaba Cloud account ID.

```
 acs:ram::139900176770****:user/xiaozhuan .
```

0. In the policy preview, confirm the permission policy and trust policy details, and then click
**Create**.
After successful creation, the RAM role template is complete.
1. In the role list, click the role name to go to its details page.

down list, select companyA. This creates the RAM role instance under the companyA cloud account. After creation, the authorized user Xiao Zhuan can assume the RAM role to restart ECS instances within the companyA organization.

#### 5.3.2 Data permissions

On the Data Permissions page, you can authorize specific users to access specific cloud service instances. You can also view and change all data permissions granted to specific users.

**Background information**

In the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, you can view and manage the management permissions, application permissions, and menu permissions granted to users. The preceding permissions allow users to manage resource sets or organizations. However, the scopes of the preceding permissions are still not fine-grained enough to meet the business requirements of customers in specific scenarios. Therefore, the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console allows you to grant data permissions to a user on a specific resource instance. This way, you can not only control access to resource sets or resources, but also manage the operations of a specific user on a specific resource instance. To simplify and optimize data permissions on instances, the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console provides an intuitive and easy-to-use data permission feature. This way, you can grant permissions on cloud service instances to users on the Data Permissions page. Alternatively, you can create policies to grant permissions to users. In this case, you can grant data permissions to users on cloud services that include the cloud services displayed on the Data Permissions page.

**Cloud services that are displayed on the Data Permissions page**

You can grant data permissions on the instances of the following cloud services to users on the Data Permissions page: ApsaraMQ, Object Storage Service (OSS), Simple Log Service (SLS), DataHub, Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK), Key Management Service (KMS), and Tablestore.

**Use cases**

To grant operation permissions on resource instances to users in the console, you can perform the following steps to create a custom role and grant data permissions to the role:
1. Create a custom role to define access permissions on services of resource sets or
organizations. For more information, see the "Create a custom role" section of the Manage custom roles topic.
2. Grant access and operation data permissions on specific resource instances. For more
information, see the Grant data permissions on specific instances on the Data Permissions page section of this topic. For example, you can perform the following authorization to grant the view permissions on all ApsaraMQ instances of resource sets and operation permissions on topics or groups in a specific ApsaraMQ instance.
**First authorization**: You can create a custom role to grant the view permissions on
ApsaraMQ instances of resource sets. This way, users can only view all the ApsaraMQ instances of resource sets in the console.
**Second authorization**: You can grant operation permissions on a specific ApsaraMQ
instance or a specific topic or group in an ApsaraMQ instance on the Data Permissions page.

**Service instances**

**Grant data permissions on specific instances on the Data**

**Permissions page**

> **Note:** You can grant data permissions on specific instances on the Data Permissions page.

**Grant data permissions on ApsaraMQ**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Permissions** > **Data Permissions**.

instance belongs. On the right side of the page, select **Message Queue MQ** for the
**Product Type** parameter.

i. In the ApsaraMQ instance list, find the instance that you want to manage and click
**Authorize** in the **Actions** column.
ii. On the left side of the **Data Permissions** dialog box, select a user to whom you want to grant data permissions. You can also turn on **Batch Grant Permissions** in the upperright corner of the dialog box to grant permissions to multiple users at a time. iii. In the Instance Permission Settings section on the right side of the dialog box, select or deselect **Enabled** to grant or remove specific operation permissions on the instance. You can also select **Enable All** in the upper-right corner of the section to grant users all operation permissions on the instance. iv. Click **OK**. v. In the **View Data Authorization Information** dialog box, view the information in the
**Authorization Information** and **Permission** sections.

> **Note:** The information about data permissions is all information about data permissions of the instance and does not represent only this authorization action.
