**Perform authorization in the ACK console**

> **Note:** You can configure fine-grained role-based access control (RBAC) for Resource Access Management (RAM) users or RAM roles in the ACK console. This way, you can grant access or operation permissions on resources in clusters. For example, you can authorize RAM users or RAM roles to manage resources only in the specified namespace in a cluster.

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Computing** > **Container Service for**
**Kubernetes**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Authorizations**.
4. On the **RAM Users** or RAM Roles tab, find the RAM user or RAM role that you want to
manage and click **Modify Permissions**.
5. In the **Configure Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)** step, click **Add Permissions**.
Select all clusters or a cluster from the Cluster drop-down list. If you select a cluster, you also need to select one or more namespaces of the cluster. Select the preset role or custom role that you want to manage and click **Next Step**. The following table describes the permissions that roles have on clusters and namespaces.

| Role | RBAC permissions on cluster resources |
|---|---|
| Administrator | This role has the read and write permissions on all resources in all namespaces of the corresponding cluster. |
| O&M engineer | This role has the read and write permissions on resources in all namespaces and read-only permissions on nodes, persistent volumes (PVs), namespaces, and service quotas of the corresponding cluster. |
| Developer | This role has the read and write permissions on resources in a specific namespace or all namespaces. |
| Restricted user | This role has the read-only permissions on resources in a specific namespace or all namespaces. |
| Custom role | The permissions of a custom role are determined by the ClusterRole that you select. Before you select a ClusterRole, check the permissions of the ClusterRole to ensure that you grant only the required permissions to the RAM user. |

**Grant data permissions on KMS**

1. On the left side of the **Data Permissions** page, click a resource set to which a KMS key
belongs. On the right side of the page, select **Key Management Service** for the **Product**
**Type** parameter.
2. In the KMS key list, find the key that you want to manage and click **Authorize** in the
**Actions** column.
3. On the left side of the **Data Permissions** dialog box, select a user to whom you want to
grant data permissions. You can also turn on **Batch Grant Permissions** in the upper-right corner of the dialog box to grant permissions to multiple users at a time.
4. In the Instance Permission Settings section on the right side of the dialog box, select or
deselect **Enabled** to grant or remove specific operation permissions on the key. You can also select **Enable All** in the upper-right corner of the section to grant users all operation permissions on the key.
5. Click **OK**.
6. In the **View Data Authorization Information** dialog box, view the information in the
**Authorization Information** and **Permission** sections.

> **Note:** The information about data permissions is all information about data permissions of the key and does not represent only this authorization action.

**Grant data permissions on Tablestore**

1. On the left side of the **Data Permissions** page, click a resource set to which a Tablestore
instance belongs. On the right side of the page, select **Tablestore** for the **Product Type** parameter.
2. In the Tablestore instance list, find the instance that you want to manage and click
**Authorize** in the **Actions** column.
3. On the left side of the **Data Permissions** dialog box, select a user to whom you want to
grant data permissions. You can also turn on **Batch Grant Permissions** in the upper-right corner of the dialog box to grant permissions to multiple users at a time.
4. In the Instance Permission Settings section on the right side of the dialog box, select or
deselect **Enabled** to grant or remove specific operation permissions on the instance. You can also select **Enable All** in the upper-right corner of the section to grant users all operation permissions on the instance.
5. Click **OK**.
6. In the **View Data Authorization Information** dialog box, view the information in the
**Authorization Information** and **Permission** sections.

> **Note:** The information about data permissions is all information about data permissions of the instance and does not represent only this authorization action.

**Grant permissions to a user by creating a policy**

1. On the left side of the **Data Permissions** page, click a user group to which a user belongs.
On the right side of the page, find the user to which you want to grant permissions.
2. View or modify the policies of the user. For more information, see RAM policies.

**View the policies of the user**

a. Find the user and click **View Permissions** in the **Actions** column. b. In the **View Permissions** dialog box, view all the policies of the user. Select a policy in the **Policies** section to view the policy content.

> **Note:** The policy shown in the preceding figure specifies a set of permissions on the resource asc:mq:MQ****. The policy allows the user to create a group on the ApsaraMQ instance. You can attach this policy to a user to allow the user to create a group on the ApsaraMQ instance.

**Modify a policy of the user**

Find the user and click **Edit Permissions** in the **Actions** column. In the **Edit Permissions** dialog box, select a policy in the **Policies** section to modify the policy in the right-side code editor.

#### 5.3.3 Access control

##### 5.3.3.1 Create an access policy

To improve the security of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, you can create access policies as an administrator to control logon access based on the logon time and IP addresses of users.

**Background information**

Access policies are used to control the time periods and IP addresses valid for user logon. After a user is associated with an access policy, user logons are limited based on the logon time and IP addresses specified in the policy. The default policy generated by the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console does not have limits on the time and IP addresses valid for user logon. This policy cannot be deleted.

**Limits**

The platform administrator (the username is super) can only create access policies that are shared within the current organization, and these policies can only be configured for custom operations administrators. Operations administrators can only create globally shared access policies. If you use a custom role whose permissions are shared by all organizations, you can create globally shared access policies, access policies that are shared within the current organization, and access policies that are shared within the current organization and its subordinate organizations. If you use a role whose permissions are shared within the current organization and its subordinate organizations, you can only create access policies that are shared within the current organization and access policies that are shared within the current organization and its subordinate organizations. If you use a custom role whose permissions are shared by resource sets, you cannot create access policies even if you are granted the required permissions.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Permissions** > **Access Control**.
4. On the page that appears, click **Create Access Policy** in the upper-left corner.
5. In the **Create Access Policy** dialog box, configure the **Name**, **Description**, **Sharing**
**Scope**, **Policy Property**, **Logon Time**, and **IP Address** parameters.

**Parameters for creating an access policy**

| Paramet er | Description |
|---|---|
| Name | The name of the access policy. The name must be 2 to 50 characters in length and can contain only letters and digits. The name must be unique in the system. |

| Descript ion | The description of the access policy. |
|---|---|
| Sharing Scope | The scope in which the policy is available. Valid values: Global: The policy is available in all organizations. Current Organization: The policy is available only in the current organization and is unavailable in its subordinate organizations. Subordinate Organization: The policy is available in the current organization and its subordinate organizations. |
| Policy Propert y | The authentication method of the access policy. Important The authentication method takes effect in combination with the Login Time and IP Address parameters. Whitelist: Logins are allowed for users whose logins match the settings of both the Login Time and IP Address parameters. Blacklist: Logins are not allowed for users whose logins match the settings of both the Login Time and IP Address parameters. |
| Login Time | The login time period. Valid values: By Period, Every Day, and Every Week. You can click Add Time Period to add a login time period. By Period: You must specify a start date, an end date, and a specific login period. Every Day: You need to only specify a specific login period. Every Week: You need to select one or more days of the week (from Monday to Sunday) and specify a specific login period. Note The start time of the login period must be earlier than the end time of the login period. You can click Select All Day to quickly set the login period to 00:00 - 23:59. |
| IP Address | The IP address for logins. You can click Add IP Address to add an IP address. IPv4 and IPv6 addresses are supported. An example of IPv4 CIDR blocks: 192.168.1.0/24. If the subnet mask of a login IP address is 32 bits in length, only this IP address is allowed to log in. An example of IPv6 CIDR blocks: 2001:db8:1234:abcd::/64. The CIDR block cannot be empty or duplicated. |

6. Click **OK**.

##### 5.3.3.2 Manage access policies

After you create an access policy, you can view, modify, disable, enable, or delete the access policy.

**Limits**

The default policy of the system is globally shared and is in the Enabled state. You cannot modify, disable, or delete the default policy. If you are the platform administrator, you can view the default policy of the system and the access policies that you created. You can also modify, disable, enable, or delete the access policies that you created. If you use a role whose permissions are shared by all organizations, you can view globally shared access policies, access policies that are shared within the current organization, and access policies that are shared within the current organization and its subordinate organizations. You can also modify, disable, enable, or delete all available access policies except the default policy. If you use a role whose permissions are shared within the current organization and its subordinate organizations, you can view globally shared access policies, access policies that are shared within the current organization, and access policies that are shared within the current organization and its subordinate organizations. You can also modify, disable, enable, or delete the access policies that are available within the management scope. If you use a custom role whose permissions are shared by resource sets, you can view globally shared access policies, access policies that are shared within the current organization, and access policies that are shared within the current organization and its subordinate organizations. You cannot modify, disable, enable, or delete the access policies even if you are granted the required permissions.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Permissions** > **Access Control**.
4. Perform operations on access policies as needed.

| Operation | Procedure |
|---|---|

| View access policies | i. In the access policy list, view the information displayed in the following columns: Policy Name/ID, Policy Property, Status, Sharing Scope, Users, Access Time, Endpoint, Description, Created At, Created By, Modified At, and Last Updated By. Note You can click the icon next to Policy Property, Status, and Sharing Scope, and specify filter conditions to search for an access policy. ii. Find an access policy and click the number in theU sers column. In the Access User panel, view the users who are configured with this access policy. Only the users that can be viewed by the current user are displayed. Note In the Access User panel, you can find a user and click Replace Policy in the Actions column to change the logon policy for the user. |
|---|---|
| Modify an access policy | i. Find an access policy and click Modify in the Actions column. ii. In the Modify an access policy dialog box, modify the parameters such as Name, Description, Policy Property, Logon Time, and IP Address. For more information about the parameters, see Create an access policy. iii. Click OK. |
| Disable an access policy | You can disable an access policy if you do not need it at the moment. Important After an access policy is disabled, users that are associated with the policy cannot log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. i. Find an access policy that is in the Enabled state and click Disable in the Actions column. ii. In the message that appears, click OK. |
| Enable an access policy | Find an access policy that is in the Disabled state and click Enable in the Actions column. |
| Delete an access policy | Important Before you delete an access policy, make sure that it is not associated with any users. i. Find an access policy and click Delete in the Actions column. ii. In the message that appears, click OK. |

#### 5.3.4 Permission boundary

##### 5.3.4.1 Service boundary management

The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console leverages the API control capabilities of the core gateway of Apsara Stack to provide the service boundary feature. You can create service boundaries to implement fine-grained control on API operations based on organizations, usage methods, and time periods.

###### 5.3.4.1.1 Create a service boundary

You can associate API control policies with service boundaries to implement fine-grained control on API operations.

**Background information**

The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console allows you to control operations by organizations, time, and operation methods through setting service boundaries. You can also use service boundaries to trigger approval processes when cloud operations are performed. Service boundaries take effect on operations performed through all methods, including cloud accounts, RAM users, and STS tokens. Specially, they also take effect on operations performed on the console. This is because when users perform operations on the console, the system is calling API operations under the hood.

> **Important:** API operations performed across cloud services (such as when Resource Orchestration Service calls an Elastic Compute Service operation to manage the resources) are also controlled by service boundaries. Therefore, inappropriate configurations may interrupt the normal usage of cloud services. You need to add the ARNs of relevant resources to the whitelist of the service boundaries and make sure that you are aware of the impact of the service boundaries before you enable them.

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**. In the left-side navigation pane, choose
**Permissions** > **Permission Boundary** > **Service Boundary**.
3. On the **Service Boundary Management** page, click **Create Service Boundary**. On the
page that appears, configure the parameters.

| Section | Parameter | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Basic Information | Service Boundary Name | The name of the service boundary. |
|   | Description | The description of the service boundary. |

| Manageme nt Scope | Management Scope | The organizations for which the service boundary takes effect. Valid values: Global and Specified Organization. When you select Specified Organization, you need to select one or more organizations from the Authorize Organization drop-down list. |
|---|---|---|
|   | Associate API Control Policy | The API control policies with which the service boundary is associated. You can select one or more API control policies. In an API control policy, you can specify conditions based on the parameter values of specific API operations. |
| Control Mode | Console Calls | The action on an operation that hits the control policy. Valid values: Reject: rejects the operation. Process Approval: initiates a preconfigured approval process for the operation. If you select this option, you must configure the Process parameter in the Configure Resource Application Process dialog box. You can select an existing process or create a new process |
|   | API Calls | The action on an API call that hits the control policy. The value is set to Reject and cannot be changed. |
| Period Settings | Effective Period | The periods of time during which the service boundary takes effect. Valid values: By Period: If you select this option, you must configure the Start and End Time parameter. Every Day: If you select this option, you must configure the Start and End Time and Effective Time per Day parameters. Every Week: If you select this option, you must configure the Start and End Time, Effective Days per Week, and Effective Time per Day parameters. |
| Settings | Status | The status the service boundary enters immediately when it is created. Valid values: Enable Disable Important We recommend that you disable the service boundary first, and enable it after you have comprehensive knowledge about its influence. |

|   | Whitelist | The resources (RAM authorizations), RAM users, and RAM roles that are exempt from the service boundary. Specify the entities by ARNs. You can perform a fuzzy search and select existing ARNs from the drop-down list, or specify a custom ARN by following the format. Note Up to 10 ARNs can be specified in the whitelist of a service boundary. |
|---|---|---|

4. Click **Submit**.

###### 5.3.4.1.2 Manage service boundaries

You can view, modify, enable, disable, and delete service boundaries and manage their whitelists in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**. In the left-side navigation pane, choose
**Permissions** > **Permission Boundary** > **Service Boundary**.
3. On the Service Boundary page, click **Advanced Filter** and configure the following
parameters: **Service Boundary ID**, **Service Boundary Name**, **Management Scope**,
**Authorize Organization**, **Associated Policy ID**, **Console Calls**, **Status**, and **Created**
**At**. Then, click **Search**.
4. Perform the following operations as needed.

| Operation | Procedure |
|---|---|
| View the details of a service boundary | Find the service boundary that you want to view and click its ID. On the Service Boundary Details page, you can view the details of the service boundary, including its basic information, associated API control policies, approval processes, and whitelists. |
| Modify a service boundary | Modify the configurations of a service boundary: Find the service boundary that you want to modify and click Edit in the Actions column. On the page that appears, you can modify the basic information, management scope, control mode, and effective period of the service boundary. Modify the API control policies associated with a service boundary: Find the service boundary that you want to modify and click Modify Policy in the Actions column. On the Associated Policy tab of the page that appears, click Add API Control Policy to associate control policies. You can also find an API control policy and click Remove in the Actions column to disassociate the control policy. |
| Enable or disable a service boundary | Find the service boundary that you want to enable or disable and click Enabled or Disable in the Actions column. |

| Manage whitelists | Find the service boundary that you want to manage, move the pointer over the More icon in the Actions column, and then select Manage Whitelist. On the Whitelist tab of the page that appears, you can click Add or Edit to add or modify the Alibaba Cloud Resource Names (ARNs) that are exempt from the service boundary. |
|---|---|
| Delete a service boundary | Find the service boundary that you want to delete, move the pointer over the More icon in the Actions column, and then select Delete. In the message that appears, click OK. |

##### 5.3.4.2 Control policy management

API control policies are associated with service boundaries to implement fine-grained access control. In an API control policy, you can specify conditions based on parameter values of specific API operations. After it is associated with a service boundary, actions will be taken when the conditions in the API control policy are met. For example, you can define a control policy that enables service boundaries to take actions when users query details of instances whose names contain a specific string.

**Supported services**

The following table lists the cloud services and their API versions that are supported by API control policies.

> **Note:** The services and API versions listed in the console prevail. We recommend that you refer to relevant API documentation to learn about the operations and their parameters.

| Service name | Service code | API version |
|---|---|---|
| Elastic Compute Service (ECS) | Ecs | 2014-05-26 |
|   |   | 2016-03-14 |
| Apsara File Storage NAS | NAS | 2017-06-26 |
| Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) | Vpc | 2016-04-28 |
| ApsaraDB RDS | Rds | 2014-08-15 |
| PolarDB | polardb | 2017-08-01 |

| KVStore for Redis | R-kvstore | 2015-01-01 |
|---|---|---|
| ApsaraDB for MongoDB | Dds | 2015-12-01 |
|   |   | 2022-11-21 |
| API Gateway | CloudAPI | 2016-02-01 |
|   |   | 2016-07-01 |
|   |   | 2016-07-14 |

**Content of control policies**

The content of a control policy consists of a coordinate and parameters. The policies are stored as a JSON file that can be modified on the control policy details page.

| Element | Description |
|---|---|
| coordinate | The coordinate of the API operation. Format: ${popCode}:${version}:${action} . popCode indicates the product code; version indicates the API version; action indicates the API operation. You can use an asterisk (*) as a wildcard character to replace ${version} so that all API versions are included. |
| parameters | An array that contains details about the rule, including the name of the parameter (key), logical expression (condition), and specified value (value). |
| ﹂condition | The logical relationship between the actual value of the parameter and the specified value. |
| ﹂value | The specified value. Note The value can be left empty only if condition is set to NotNull or IsNull. |
| ﹂key | The name of the controlled API operation. |

**Example**

`[` `{`

```json
  "coordinate": "CloudAPI:2016-02-01:AbolishApi",
  "parameters": [
```

`{`

```json
    "condition": "IsNull",
    "value": "",
    "key": "AccessKeyId"
```

`}` `]` `}` `]`

**Data types of parameter values and logical expressions**

The following table lists the logical expressions that can be specified in API control policies.

| Type | Logical expression | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Numeric (such as INTEGER, LONG, and FLOAT) | NumericEquals | The actual value equals the specified value in the policy. |
|   | NumericNotEquals | The actual value does not equal the specified value in the policy. |
|   | NumericLessThan | The actual value is smaller than the specified value in the policy. |
|   | NumericGreaterThan | The actual value is larger than the specified value in the policy. |
|   | NumericLessThanEquals | The actual value is smaller than or equal to the specified value in the policy. |
|   | NumericGreaterThanEquals | The actual value is larger than or equal to the specified value in the policy. |
|   | IsNull | The parameter is left empty. |
|   | NotNull | The parameter is not empty. |

| String | StringLike | The actual value includes the specified string in the policy. |
|---|---|---|
|   | StringNotLike | The actual value does not include the specified string in the policy. |
|   | StringEquals | The actual value matches the specified string in the policy (case-sensitive). |
|   | StringNotEquals | The actual value does not match the specified string in the policy (case-sensitive). |
|   | StringEqualsIgnoreCase | The actual value matches the specified string in the policy (case-insensitive). |
|   | IsNull | The parameter is left empty. |
|   | NotNull | The parameter is not empty. |
| BOOLEAN | Boolean Equals _ | The actual value matches the specified value in the policy. |
|   | IsNull | The parameter is left empty. |
|   | NotNull | The parameter is not empty. |

###### 5.3.4.2.1 Create an API control policy

In the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, you can create API control policies to control API operations on cloud resources based on values of the request parameters.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**. In the left-side navigation pane, choose
**Permissions** > **Permission Boundary** > **Control Policies**.
3. On the **API control policy management** page, click **Create an API control policy**.
4. On the **Create Control Policy** page, specify the name and description of the policy and
click **Create** in the Control Content section. In the dialog box that appears, configure the following parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Cloud Services | The cloud services whose API operations are to be controlled. |
| Version | The API version. Some cloud services may have multiple API versions. We recommend that you select All Versions for this parameter. |
| API | The API operation that is controlled. Note Each rule is set for a single operation. If you want to specify rules for multiple operations in a single policy, you can click Add Rule. The rules in a policy are in OR logical relations. This means that when the policy is attached to a service boundary, the policy takes effect as long as one of the rules is met. |
| Field | The request parameter to be controlled, a specified value, and the logical relation between the values in actual requests and the specified value. The logical relations vary with the types of the selected request parameters. Valid values include Similar To, Equal to String, Equal to (case-insensitive), Empty, Not Empty. Note You can click Add Field to specify multiple conditions. The conditions in a rule are in AND logical relations. This means that the rule takes effect only if all conditions are met. Example: The following figure shows how to configure the Field parameter for a rule that is created to control the action of creating a VPC named "test". |

5. Click **Create**. Then, you can attach the API control policy to service boundaries.

###### 5.3.4.2.2 Manage API control policies

You can view the details of existing API control policies, including their content and association with service boundaries. You can also modify and delete the policies.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**. In the left-side navigation pane, choose
**Permissions** > **Permission Boundary** > **Control Policies**.
3. On the page that appears, the existing policies are listed, and you can perform operations
on them.

| Operation | Procedure |
|---|---|
| View details of an API control policy | Click the ID of an API control policy. On theP olicy Details tab of the page that appears, you can view the basic information and control content of the policy. On the Reference Information tab, you can view information of the service boundaries with which the policy is associated. You can click Disassociate in the Actions column corresponding to a service boundary to cancel the association. |
| Modify an API control policy | Click Modify in the Actions column corresponding to a policy. In the dialog box that appears, you can modify its name and description. Click Modify Control Content in the Actions column corresponding to a policy. On the policy details page that appears, you can modify or delete the existing rules in the policy, or create new rules. Note When you modify a rule, you cannot change the cloud service, API version, or the API operation involved. After you delete a rule, service boundaries with which the policy is associated will be affected. Proceed with caution. If you are familiar with the format of control policies, you can click Custom Edit to modify the JSON file of the policy. This way, you can modify the cloud service, API version, and the API operation involved. You need to make sure that the modifications comply with the JSON format and that you are aware of the modifications' impact on relevant service boundaries. |
| Delete an API control policy | Click Delete in the Actions column corresponding to a policy. Note Policies that are associated with service boundaries cannot be deleted. |

#### 5.3.5 AccessKey log

This topic describes how to view and export the logs of AccessKey pair calls to understand the usage of AccessKey pairs. This helps you enhance the security of AccessKey pairs.

> **Important:** The AccessKey logs are for reference only. Data collection may miss records or experience delays. Do not use this data to disable AccessKeys.

If an AccessKey pair is used for fat client authentication, the AccessKey pair logs may not record complete information. Tablestore Note This service is partially supported. If an AccessKey pair is used for fat client authentication, the AccessKey pair logs may not record complete information. DataWorks Note This service is partially supported. **View AccessKey pair information**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

4. On the **AccessKey Logs** page, click the **AccessKey Pair Query** tab.

click the icon. View the information about the AccessKey pair in the **Basic Information**

### 5.4 Operation audit

#### 5.4.1 Overview

The Overview page consists of the Basic Data, Event Count Trend, Getting Started, and Unusual IP Address Events sections to help you quickly learn about the overall situation of operation audit.

**Prerequisites**

You are assigned one of the following roles: operations administrator, resource auditor, organization resource auditor, security auditor, global organization security auditor, platform security auditor, organization security administrator, global organization security administrator, security system configuration administrator, platform security administrator, or platform security configuration administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Operation Audit** > **Overview**.
4. View the information.
**Basic Data**: displays the following metrics: **Total Events (Yesterday)**, **Notifications**
**(Yesterday)**, **Total Sensitive Events (Yesterday)**, and **Effective Organizations**.
**Event Count Trend**: displays the number of resource events within a specific period of
time in a column chart. You can select a service and a resource type from the Product Type and Resource Type drop-down lists and select a 7-day, 15-day, or 30-day period. You can move the pointer over a column in the chart to view the specific quantity.
**Getting Started**: displays the features of operation audit and the procedure for using
operation audit to quickly get started.
**Unusual IP Address Events**: records events of access from unusual IP addresses. You
can specify a time range to view the information about unusual IP address events within the time range.

> **Important:** Before you use this feature, you must specify common IP addresses.

**Configure common IP addresses:**

a. In the **Unusual IP Address Events** section, click **Common IP Settings**. b. In the **Common IP Settings** dialog box, specify common IP addresses. You can specify up to 20 common IP addresses.
**Add IP addresses**: Click **Add IP Address**. In the IP address field, enter a
common IP address.

> **Note:** IPv4 and IPv6 addresses are supported.
> An example of IPv4 CIDR blocks: 192.168.1.0/24. If the subnet mask of a login IP address is 32 bits in length, only this IP address is allowed to log in.
> An example of IPv6 CIDR blocks: 2001:db8:1234:abcd::/64.
> The CIDR block cannot be duplicated.

**Remove IP addresses**: Click **Delete** next to an IP address.
**View Historical IP addresses**: Click **View Historical IP Addresses**. Then, the
right-side **Historical IP Addresses** panel displays the historical IP addresses. The IP addresses are sorted in descending order of visits. You can enter an IP address into the search box above the list to search for an IP address. c. Click **OK**.
**View event details**:
You can click **Details** in the **Actions** column of the event list in the Unusual IP Address Events sector to view detailed information in the Event Details panel, including the basic information of the event and API call details.

#### 5.4.5 Audit notifications

By configuring audit notifications, you can detect in real time and quickly respond to potential security threats and abnormal behaviors to ensure system stability and data integrity.

**Prerequisites**

You are assigned one of the following roles: operations administrator, resource auditor, organization resource auditor, security auditor, global organization security auditor, platform security auditor, organization security administrator, global organization security administrator, security system configuration administrator, platform security administrator, or platform security configuration administrator.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Operation Audit** > **Audit Notifications**.
4. Click **Create Notification**.
5. In the Create Notification dialog box, configure the parameters.

| Paramete r | Description |
|---|---|
| Rule Name | The name of the audit notification rule. You can click Select Template to specify a rule template, such as User AccessKey Pair Deletion Event. |
| Check Frequen cy | The check frequency. Valid values: Fixed Interval: Operations are checked against the rule at a fixed interval, such as 5 minutes, 2 hours, or 1 day. Cron: Operations are checked against the rule based on a CRON expression. A CRON expression is a string used to schedule tasks. You can use a CRON expression to specify when to perform tasks in a more fine-grained manner. For more information, see the CRON expressions section of this topic. |
| Trigger Conditio ns | The conditions under which notifications are triggered. You can add multiple trigger conditions and combine them by using AND or OR. If the conditions are combined by using AND, a notification is triggered only when all conditions are met. If the conditions are combined by using OR, a notification is triggered when one of the conditions is met. |
| Notificat ion Title | The notification title. |

| Notificat ion Content | The notification content. |
|---|---|
| Notificat ion Object | One or more users to whom notifications are sent. |
| Status | Specifies whether to enable the audit notification rule. : enables the audit notification rule. : disables the audit notification rule. |

6. Click **OK**. The audit notification rule is created.
7. Perform the following operations as needed.

| Operation | Description |
|---|---|

| View the details of the audit notification rule | i. In the rule list, view the information about the audit notification rule in the following columns: Rule Name, Check Frequency, Trigger Conditions, Status, Notification Object, and Created At. Note You can move the pointer over the value in the Notification Object column to view the specific users. ii. Click Details in the Actions column. iii. In the panel that appears, view the details of the audit notification rule. |
|---|---|
| Modify the audit notification rule | i. Click Edit in the Actions column. ii. In the Edit Notification dialog box, modify the configurations as needed. iii. Click OK. |
| Enable the audit notification rule | Click the icon in the Actions column and select Enabled. Note You can enable an audit notification rule only if it is in theD isabled state. |

| Disable the audit notification rule | i. Click the icon in the Actions column and select Disable. Note You can disable an audit notification rule only if it is in the Enabled state. ii. In the message that appears, click OK. |
|---|---|
| Delete the audit notification rule | i. Move the pointer over the icon in the Actions column and select Delete. ii. In the message that appears, click OK. |

**CRON expressions**

A CRON expression is a string of six or seven fields that are separated with five or six spaces. Each field describes an individual detail of the schedule. Specify the CRON expression in one of the following formats: <Seconds> <Minutes> <Hours> <Day of month> <Months> <Day of week> <Years> <Seconds> <Minutes> <Hours> <Day of month> <Months> <Day of week>

**Valid values of fields**

| Field | Valid value | Supported special character | Remarks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Seconds | 0–59 | - * / | None |
| Minutes | 0–59 | - * / | None |
| Hours | 0–23 | - * / | None |
| Day of month | 1–31 | - * ? / L W C | None |
| Months | 1–12 | JAN-DEC - * / | None |
| Day of week | 1–7 | SUN-SAT - * ? / L C # | A value of 1 indicates Sunday, a value of 2 indicates Monday, and so on. |
| Years (optional) | 1970–2099 | , - * / | The value of this field is automatically generated. |

**Special characters**

| Character | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| * | All values of a field. | Set the Minutes field to an asterisk (*) to run a task every minute. |
| ? | Any value of a field. However, this character can be used only in the Day of month and Day of week fields. For the two fields, using ? in one field allows you to specify a value in the other without creating a conflict. | To run a task on the twentieth day of every month, regardless of the day of the week, use the following CRON expression: 13 13 15 20 * ? . Because the Day of month field is set to 20, the Day of week field must be ? , instead of * . Using * for the Day of week field means every day of the week. This conflicts with the twentieth-day requirement and results in an invalid CRON expression. |
| - | A range of values. | Set the Minutes field to 5-20 to run a task every minute from the fifth minute to the twentieth minute of an hour. |
| / | Separates the start time and interval. | Set the Minutes field to 5/20 to run a task at the fifth, twenty-fifth, and forty-fifth minutes of an hour. |
| , | Separates multiple values. | Set the Minutes field to 5,20 to run a task at the fifth and twentieth minutes of an hour. |
| L | The last day of the month or the last specified day of the week in a month. | Set the Day of week field to 5L to run a task on the last Thursday of a month. |
| C | The specified date (calendar day). If no date is specified, C indicates any day. This character can be used only in the Day of month and Day of week fields. | Set the Day of month field to 5C to run a task on the first day after the fifth day of a month. Set the Day of week field to 1C to run a task on the first day after Sunday. |
| W | The nearest weekday (Monday through Friday) to the specified day of the month. You can use this character only in the Day of month field. | Set the Day of month field to 5W. If the fifth day of a month is a Saturday, the task runs on the fourth day, which is a Friday. If the fifth day of a month is a Sunday, the task runs on the sixth day of the month, which is a Monday. If the fifth day of a month is a weekday, the task runs on that day. The nearest weekday search does not cross month boundaries. |
| LW | The last weekday of a month. | None. |

| # | The N-th occurrence of a day of the week in a month. This character can be used only in the Day of week field. | Set the Day of week field to 4#2 to run a task on the second Wednesday of a month. 4 indicates Wednesday and 2 indicates the second. |
|---|---|---|

**Examples**

*/5 * * * * ? : Run a task every 5 seconds. 0 */1 * * * ? : Run a task at an interval of 1 minute. 0 0 2 1 * ? : Run a task at 02:00 on the first day of every month. 0 15 10 ? * MON-FRI : Run a task at 10:15 every day from Monday to Friday. 0 0 1 ? * L : Run a task at 01:00 every Sunday. 0 15 10 ? * 6#3 : Run a task at 10:15 on the third Friday of every month.

#### 5.4.6 Event fields

This topic describes the key fields in operation events.

**Key fields**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| acsRegion | The region ID. |
| additionalEventData | The additional information about the event. |
| apiVersion | The API version information. |
| eventId | The event ID. |
| eventApi | The operation that was called in the event. |
| eventName | The name of the event, if any. |
| eventRW | The read/write type of the event. Valid values: Write Read |
| eventTime | The time when the event occurred. |

| eventVersion | The format version of the user-initiated event. The current version is 1. |
|---|---|
| errorCode | The error code that is returned when an error occurred during the processing of the API request. |
| errorMessage | The error message that is returned when an error occurred during the processing of the API request. |
| requestId | The request ID. |
| requestParameterJson | The JSON-formatted representation of the requestParameters parameter. |
| resourceName | The name of the event-associated resource. The name is the unique identifier of the resource. |
| resourceType | The type of the event-associated resource. |
| responseElements | The response in the JSON format. |
| referencedResources | The resources that are associated with the event. |
| serviceName | The name of the Apsara Stack service for which the user- initiated event is generated. |
| sourceIpAddress | The IP address from which the user-initiated event is generated. |
| userAgent | The user agent that sends the API request. |
| userIdentity | The identity information about the requester. For more information, see the Fields included in userIdentity section of this topic. |

**Fields included in userIdentity**

| Field | Description |
|---|---|

| type | The type of the identity. Valid values: root-account: an Apsara Stack account. ram-user: a Resource Access Management (RAM) user. assumed-role: a RAM role. |
|---|---|
| userName | The username of the account used to log on to the Apsara Uni- manager Management Console. |
| accountId | The primary key (PK) of the account of the requester. |
| principalId | The Alibaba Cloud Resource Name (ARN) of the RAM role. |
| accessKeyId | The AccessKey ID that is used by the requester. If the requester sends an API request by using an SDK, this field is recorded. If the requester performs an operation in the Apsara Uni- manager Management Console, this field is not recorded. If the requester sends an API request by using a Security Token Service (STS) token, this field is set to the temporary AccessKey ID. |
| orgId | The organization ID of the current user. |
| sysUid | The UID of the account used to log on to the Apsara Uni- manager Management Console. |
| resourceSetId | The resource set ID of the current user. |

#### 5.4.7 Examples

##### 5.4.7.1 Use operation audit to monitor AccessKey pair deletion events

**pair deletion events**

This topic describes how to use the audit notification feature of operation audit to monitor AccessKey pair deletion events and send notifications by using internal messages.

**Background information**

An AccessKey pair consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret, which are used to identify a user and verify the key of the user. Malicious or accidental deletion of AccessKey pairs may cause service interruption and bring serious losses to enterprises or individuals.

**Prerequisites**

You are assigned one of the following roles: Operations Administrator, Resource Auditor, Organization Resource Auditor, Security Auditor, Global Organization Security Auditor, Platform Security Auditor, Organizational Security Administrator, Global Organization Security Administrator, Security System Configuration Administrator, Platform Security Administrator, and Platform Security Configuration Administrator.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Operation Audit** > **Audit Notifications**.
4. Click **Create Notification**.
5. In the Create Notification dialog box, configure the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Rule Name | The name of the rule. Click Select Template. In the Select Template panel, find the User AccessKey Pair Deletion Event template and click Set. |
| Check Frequency | The check frequency of the rule. In this example, a fixed interval of 15 minutes is configured. |
| Trigger Conditions | The trigger conditions of the rule. In this example, Operation Name = DeleteUserAccessKey is configured. |
| Notification Title | The title of the notification. In this example, User AccessKey Pair Deletion Event Notification is used. |

| Notification Content | The content of the notification. In this example, the following content is used: A user AccessKey pair deletion event occurred in the account in the past 15 minutes. |
|---|---|
| Notification Object | The recipient of the notification. In this example, admin is selected. |
| Status | The status of the rule. In this example, the switch is turned on. |

**Verify the feature**

> **Note:** In this example, the following operations are performed by the admin user.

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the upper-right corner of the page, click the profile picture and select **User Information**.
3. In the AccessKey Pair section, find an AccessKey pair and click **Delete** in the **Actions**
column.
4. In the dialog box that appears, select the checkbox and click **Delete**.
5. Click the
icon in the upper-right corner. In the Message window, click More to view internal messages. The following figure shows an example.
6. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**. In the left-side navigation pane, choose
**Operation Audit** > **Advanced Query**. On the Advanced Query page, select
DeleteUserAccessKey from the Operation Name drop-down list and click Run to view the corresponding logs.

### 5.5 Alibaba Cloud platform management configurations

**management configurations**

This directory includes topics related to resource synchronization configurations and resource ownership configurations for Alibaba Cloud platforms.

#### 5.5.1 Configure resource synchronization for an Alibaba Cloud platform

**an Alibaba Cloud platform**

You can enable or disable resource synchronization based on your business requirements. If you enable the resource synchronization feature for a cloud platform, the status of instances in the cloud platform is synchronized in real time. If you disable the resource synchronization feature for the cloud platform, you can no longer obtain information about instances in the cloud platform in real time. As a result, the instance information in the resource list is updated with a delay.

**Prerequisites**

You have connected an Alibaba Cloud platform to the central cloud platform as a platform administrator. To connect an Alibaba Cloud platform to the central cloud platform, log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. In the top navigation bar, click
**Configurations**. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Native Hybrid Cloud** > **Multi-**
**cloud Management**.
You are the operations administrator of the managed Alibaba Cloud platform. The operations administrator is assigned a Resource Access Management (RAM) role to which the AdministratorAccess policy of the Alibaba Cloud account is attached.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Public Cloud Management Configurations**.
4. On the Public Cloud Management Configurations page, find the Alibaba Cloud platform that
you want to manage and click **Resource Synchronization** in the **Actions** column.
5. In the **Resource Synchronization Configurations** dialog box, turn on or off **Enable**
**Incremental Synchronization for Resources** and configure parameters.
: The resource synchronization feature is disabled. : The resource synchronization feature is enabled.

| Parameter or section |   | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Synchr onize Cloud Servic e Config uratio ns | Activate Cloud Service | Select the cloud service that you want to synchronize from the drop- down list. |
|   | Cloud Service Region | Select the region to which the cloud service that you want to synchronize belongs from the drop-down list. Note The regions that are associated with the Alibaba Cloud platform are displayed in the Cloud Service Region drop-down list. |

**cloud Management**.
You are the operations administrator of the managed Alibaba Cloud platform. The operations administrator is assigned a Resource Access Management (RAM) role to which the AdministratorAccess policy is attached.

### 5.6 Asynchronous task

You can view the progress and results of asynchronous tasks on the Asynchronous Task page.

**Background information**

On the Asynchronous Task page, you can view the information about each asynchronous task, including the task name, task type, status, creator, and creation time. The system updates the execution situation of each task in real time. This way, users can know whether the task is running as expected at any time. Asynchronous tasks are classified into the following types: batch creation of organizations and users and batch authorization of roles.

**View the information about a task**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Asynchronous Task**.
4. On the **Asynchronous Task** page, specify the **Start Date**, **End Date**, **Task Type**, and
**Task Name** parameters to search for the desired task.
5. View the task information in the task list.
6. Find the desired task and click the task name or click **View Task** in the **Actions** column.
The **Task Details** panel appears.

**Delete a task**

1. On the **Asynchronous Task** page, find the desired task and click **Delete** in the **Actions**
column.
2. In the **Delete** message, click **OK**.

> **Important:** After a task is deleted, the information about the task cannot be queried. Exercise caution when you delete a task. The information about task deletion is recorded in an operation log.

## 6 Configurations

### 6.1 Resource pool configuration

You can manage the logical inventory of cloud resources to control the maximum usage of resources.

#### 6.1.1 Service resources

##### 6.1.1.1 Configure quota items

This topic describes how to configure quota items on the Resource Pool Configuration page.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator.

**Limits**

You can add a subitem of a group quota item without adding the group quota item. When you select a group quota item, all of its subitems are selected. For more information, see Cloud services that support group quota configuration. When you add a subitem of a category quota item, the category quota item is also added. For more information, see Cloud services that support category quota configuration.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Resource Pool Configuration**.
4. Select the **Product Resources** tab.
5. In the upper part of the page, select a resource pool, a region, and a zone.

> **Note:** The resource pool drop-down list is displayed only in multi-cloud environments.
> If you select All Zones, you can manage quotas in the region. If you select the corresponding zone, you can manage quotas in the zone, and the Resource Pool Configuration page displays the services only in the zone.

6. (Optional) In the upper-right corner of the page, select **Only View Cloud Services That**
**Trigger Alerts** to display only the cloud services that trigger alerts.
7. Click the target cloud product to open the **Resource Pool Details** panel. Using Elastic
Compute Service (ECS) as an example, view configuration details displayed in the following columns: **Resource Item**, **Logical Inventory**, **Physical Inventory**, and **Total Activated**
**Resources**.
8. In the **Resource Pool Details** panel, click **Configure Quota Items** at the bottom.
9. In the **Configure Quota Items** dialog box, add or remove quota items.

> **Note:** When you configure quota items for a specific zone, you can use the **Synchronize** **Quota Items to Other Zones** switch to control quota items in other zones.

**Add quota items**: In the **Available Quota Items** list on the left side, select the quota
items that you want to add and click to add them to the **Added Quota Items** list on the right side.
**Remove quota items**: In the **Added Quota Items** list on the right side, select the
quota items that you want to remove and click to remove them.
0. Click **OK**.

##### 6.1.1.2 Create or modify a logical inventory

After configuring quota items, you can set a logical inventory for them to limit the total resource usage.

**Background information**

Resources in a resource pool are limited. You must limit the resource quotas for each organization based on its scope of responsibilities in the resource pool to ensure that each department receives a fare share of resources. The quota configuration process in a resource pool is as follows:
1. The platform administrator sets the maximum total usage of each cloud service resource
for the entire resource pool.
2. The operations administrator allocates quotas of each cloud service resource to each level-
1 organization based on the logical inventory set by the platform administrator.
3. Each organization administrator allocates quotas to subordinate organizations or resource
sets sequentially. When you activate, change configurations of, delete, or transfer ownership of a cloud service, the system directly uses the corresponding quota to validate resources and update consumption calculations for organizations and resource sets with configured quotas configured. For organizations and resource sets without configured quotas, the system traverses up the hierarchy to find the quota of a parent organization that has an ownership relationship with the current organization or resource set for validation and calculation.

**Prerequisites**

Quota items are configured. The default operator is the platform administrator.

**Limits**

When the physical inventory is unlimited, the logical inventory must not be less than the allocated inventory. When the physical inventory is limited, the default logical inventory must not be less than the used inventory and must not exceed the physical inventory.

> **Important:** When the logical inventory falls below the used inventory, the system restricts resource creation, leading to resource creation failure.
> If you need to set the logical inventory to a value greater than the physical inventory, contact technical support to disable logical inventory validation and remove the physical inventory limit.

When you configure the logical inventory of a group quota for the first time, it defaults to the sum of the logical inventory of all child items. After manual configuration, your specified value takes precedence. The sum of the logical inventory of all child items cannot exceed the logical inventory of the parent item.

> **Note:** Child items of a group quota item may share the same resource pool. Therefore, the physical inventory of a group quota item may be less than the sum of the physical inventory of its child items. This is normal.

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Resource Pool Configuration**.
4. Click the **Product Resources** tab.
5. In the upper part of the page, select a resource pool, a region, and an availability zone.

> **Note:** The resource pool is displayed only in multi-cloud scenarios.
> When you select **All Zones**, the system enforces quota management at the region level. When you select a specific availability zone, the system enforces quota management at the availability zone level, and displays only the services in that availability zone.

6. (Optional) In the upper-right corner of the page, select **Only View Cloud Services That**
**Trigger Alerts** to quickly filter cloud services that have triggered alerts.
7. Click the target cloud service to open the **Resource Pool Details** panel. Using Elastic
Compute Service (ECS) as an example, view the **Resource Item**, **Logical Inventory**,
**Physical Inventory**, and **Total Activated Resources** of the cloud service.
8. In the **Resource Pool Details** panel, click **Create Inventory** or **Modify Inventory** at the
bottom of the page.
9. Enter inventory quotas in the **Logical Inventory** column to limit the maximum usage of
resources.

> **Note:** If you do not specify a quota for a resource item, the system does not limit the resource consumption for the corresponding item.

0. Click **Save**.

##### 6.1.1.3 Cancel quotas

The resource pool configuration feature allows you to cancel configured quotas.

**Prerequisites**

You have created an inventory. The default operator is the platform administrator.

> **Note:** When the requested resource quantity plus the total provisioned resource quantity exceeds the physical inventory, you can cancel the quota to clear the quota data for the service. After you clear the quota data, the console no longer validates resources for the service during resource creation, which enables overselling.
> Canceling a quota resets the organization and logical inventory capacity data for the service to the unset status and disables quota validation. Proceed with caution.

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Resource Pool Configuration**.
4. Select the **Product Resources** tab.
5. At the top of the page, select a resource pool, a region, and an availability zone.

> **Note:** The resource pool option appears only in multi-cloud scenarios.
> When you select **All Zones**, the system manages quotas at the region level. When you select a specific availability zone, the system manages quotas at the availability zone level, and displays only the services in that availability zone.

6. (Optional) In the upper-right corner of the page, select **Only View Cloud Services That**
**Trigger Alerts** to filter services that have triggered alerts.
7. Click the target cloud service to open the **Resource Pool Details** panel. Using Elastic
Compute Service (ECS) as an example, check the **Resource Item**, **Logical Inventory**,
**Physical Inventory**, and **Total Activated Resources** of the cloud service.
8. In the **Resource Pool Details** panel, click **Cancel Quota** at the bottom.
9. In the **Cancel Quota** dialog box, select **I am aware of the risks and want to perform**
**this operation**.

> **Note:** When you cancel the quota for a specific availability zone, you can use the **Synchronize Quota Cancellation to Other Availability Zones** switch to control quotas in other availability zones.

0. Click **OK**.

**notifications**

After you configure physical inventory change notifications, the system sends SMS, email, or in-app notifications to the specified recipients at the configured time whenever the physical inventory quantity changes.

**Prerequisites**

The default operator is the platform administrator.

**Limits**

Connected public cloud resource pools do not support physical inventory change notifications.

5. At the top of the page, select a resource pool.

> **Note:** The system displays resource pools only in multi-cloud scenarios, and you can configure physical inventory change notifications only for the central cloud and secondary Apsara Stack.

6. Click **Inventory Change Notification** in the upper-right corner of the page.

**Time**.
8. Click **Save**.

##### 6.1.2.1 Set quotas

You can set token quotas for AI services on a monthly basis. The used quota will automatically reset to the initial limit on the 1st of each calendar month.

**Prerequisites**

The default operator is the platform administrator.

> **Note:** The current quota control mode is soft control. That is, when consumption exceeds the configured quota, the platform sends an alert notification but does not restrict further usage.

8. Click **Save**.

**Cloud service category**

**Descriptions of strong control, weak control, and SSO**

Strong control: The Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console hosts the creation page and list page for products. It redirects to the cloud console for product detail pages. Weak control: The Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console hosts only the list page for products. It redirects to the cloud console for both the creation page and the detail page. SSO: Redirect to the corresponding product page on the subordinate cloud by using SSO to perform resource operations. When you switch the resource pool to a subordinate cloud from the product header in the central cloud, a prompt appears to redirect you to the product page of the selected resource pool.

#### 6.2.2 Cloud platform type management

Configure and manage cloud platform types in Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console. The system presets two cloud platform types: Public Cloud and Apsara Stack. You can also define custom cloud platform types.

**Prerequisites**

You have turned on the multi-cloud switch and deployed the COMS service. The operator is the platform administrator by default.

**Limits**

You cannot operate the preset cloud platform types.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Configuration**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Native Hybrid Cloud** > **Cloud Platform Type**
**Management**.
4. Click **Add Type**.
5. In the **Add Type** dialog box, configure the cloud platform type.

| Configurati on item | Description |
|---|---|
| Type Name | Enter a name for the cloud platform type. The name can contain only letters, digits, underscores ( ), and hyphens (-). It cannot start with a digit. The name must be 2 to _ 30 characters in length. |
| Code | Enter an encoding for the cloud platform type. The encoding can be up to 15 characters in length. |
| Description | Enter a description for the cloud platform type. The description can be 1 to 150 characters in length. |
| Type | The system sets the type of the new cloud platform to Custom. |

6. Click OK.
7. Perform other related operations.

| Operation | Description |
|---|---|

| Edit cloud platform type | i. Click Edit in the Action column of the cloud platform type. ii. In the Modify Type dialog box, update the name and description of the cloud platform type. iii. Click Confirm. |
|---|---|

| Disable cloud platform type | i. Click Disable in the Action column of the cloud platform type. Note You cannot disable a cloud platform type if products exist under it. You can disable a cloud platform type only when its status is Enabled. After you disable it, its status changes to Disabled. After you disable a cloud platform type, resource pools and products under the corresponding cloud platform no longer appear. ii. Click OK. |
|---|---|
| Enable cloud platform type | i. Click Enable in the Action column of the cloud platform type. Note You can enable a cloud platform type only when its status is Disabled. After you enable it, its status changes to Enabled. |
| Delete cloud platform type | i. Click Delete in the Action column of the cloud platform type. Note You can delete a cloud platform type only when its status is Disabled. You cannot delete a cloud platform type if products exist under it. ii. In the dialog box, click OK. |

**Impact on other features**

**Multi-cloud management:** The multi-cloud management page displays items by cloud
platform type. For more information, see Multi-Cloud Management.
**Product management:** For more information, see Product management.
When you create a product, you can select a cloud platform type. The classification tree on the product list displays the newly added cloud platform types. Each cloud platform type is a root node. You cannot edit root nodes in product management.

#### 6.2.3 Export local cloud data

The configurations of the current cloud platform can be exported and used for multi-cloud configuration on another Apsara Stack platform. This way, the current cloud platform is managed by the Apsara Stack platform.

**Prerequisites**

Native Hybrid Cloud and Local Cloud Data are selected by a platform administrator. To do so, click **Configurations** in the top navigation bar. In the left-side navigation pane, choose
**Menu Settings** > **Main Menu Configuration**. On the Main Menu Configuration page,
click the **Single-cloud Menu** tab. On this tab, click **Configurations** and select Native Hybrid Cloud and Local Cloud Data. You are a platform administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Native Hybrid Cloud** > **Local Cloud Data**.
4. On the Local Cloud Data page, click **Export Local Cloud Data** to export the data of the
current Apsara Stack platform as a JSON file.

### 6.3 Security policies

You can configure login password policies, login control settings, and resource security levels.

#### 6.3.1 Set a password policy

This topic describes how to set a password policy.

**Prerequisites**

The operator is the platform administrator by default.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Security Policy**.
4. On the **Password Policy** tab, configure **Basic settings**, **Log in settings**, and **Password**
**change settings**.
5. Click **Save**.
Click **Reset** to restore default settings.

**Basic settings**

| Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|
| Password Length | Set the minimum password length. Valid values: 8 to 32 characters. |
| Required Character Types in Password | Select one or more required character types for passwords. Lowercase Letters Uppercase Letters Digits Special Characters |
| Password Validity Period (Days) | Specify the password validity period in Days. The system prompts that the password has expired when the validity period exceeds the specified value. Valid values: 0 to 1095 days. Note 0 indicates that the password never expires. The password validity period also applies to preset accounts. |

**Log in settings**

| Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|
| Login Disabled After Password Expires | Supports Yes or No. Yes: After the password expires, the system prevents users from logging in to the console. In the drop-down list, select Allow Users to Change Password or Do Not Allow Users to Change Password. Allow Users to Change Password: After the password expires, allow users to change their passwords on the log in page. They can log in after changing their passwords. Do Not Allow Users to Change Password: After the password expires, users cannot change their passwords on the log in page. Only an administrator can change the password for the user to regain access. No: After the password expires, allow users to continue logging in to the console. Important To avoid security risks that may arise from password leakage, we recommend that users change their passwords as soon as possible. They can change passwords on the log in page or notify administrators to perform the change. |
| Password Attempts | Set the maximum number of failed log in attempts allowed within one hour. The account locks temporarily when this limit is reached. Valid values: 0 to 32 attempts. Note 0 indicates the system does not enforce password retry constraints. |
| Temporary Account Lock Duration (Minutes) | Set the temporary account lock duration in Minutes. If the number of incorrect password attempts exceeds the limit, the account enters a temporary lockout period during which log in is not allowed. Valid values: 0 to 1440 minutes. Note 0 indicates the system does not enable temporary account locking. |
| Password History Check | The system ensures the new password does not match any of the previous passwords. Valid values: 0 to 24 passwords. Note 0 indicates the system does not enable password history checking. For example, if you set this value to 3, the current password cannot match any of the last three passwords used. |

**Password change settings**

| Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|
| Password Expiration Notification | Specifies whether to send a notification when the password expires. Reminder No Notification |
| Notification Method | Specifies how to send password expiration notifications. You can select multiple methods. Email DingTalk SMS Note You must configure this parameter only if you enable password expiration notifications. |
| Notification Template | Select a template for password expiration notifications. For information about how to edit templates, see Message Gateway. Note You must configure this parameter only if you enable password expiration notifications. |
| Notification Time | Specifies the number of days before password expiration to send a reminder. Valid values: 1 to 30 days. Note You must configure this parameter only if you enable password expiration notifications. |

#### 6.3.2 Configure login control

This topic describes how to configure login control settings.

**Prerequisites**

The operating user is the platform administrator by default.

**Important notes**

> **Important:** For Internet-accessible sites, the system sets session control to single-session mode by default and forces logout after 23 hours and 55 minutes.

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Configuration**.
3. On the **Security Policy** page, click the **Login Control** tab.
4. Configure login control settings according to your business requirements.

| Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|

| Session Control | Select a session mode. Single session: A user can log in from only one client at a time. Multi-session: A user can log in from multiple clients simultaneously. Region-based setting: Restrict users to single or multi-session mode based on their region. |
|---|---|
| Global MFA verification | Enable or disable global MFA verification. Enabled: All user accounts in the platform must use MFA for login authentication. After enabling global MFA verification, select the scope of user accounts to which it applies. Exclude system preset users (such as admin) All users Disabled: User accounts in the platform are not required to use MFA for login authentication. |
| MFA Binding Instructions | Configure the instructions displayed on the binding page. You can configure content in Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and English. |
| SSO User Login | Enable or disable SSO user login. Enabled: SSO users can log in to this platform. Disabled: SSO users cannot log in directly to this platform and must log in through SSO. Note Platform administrator accounts are not subject to this login restriction. |
| Login Duration During Which No Actions Occur | Set the idle timeout duration. Valid values: 5 minutes to 24 hours. If no button interaction occurs within the specified duration, the system automatically logs you out and requires you to log in again. |
| Login Duration Before Forced Logout | Set the forced logout duration. Within this time frame, the system forcibly reminds users to log out and requires re-authentication. Important The forced logout duration must be greater than or equal to the idle timeout duration. Setting both minutes and hours to zero disables this feature. |

5. Click **Save**.

#### 6.3.3 Configure security level-based authorization

**authorization**

This topic describes how to configure security level-based authorization for a resource.

**Usage notes**

> **Important:** On the Security Level Based Access tab, you can enable security level-based authorization and configure security levels for resource sets and roles. If you enable security level-based authorization, you must configure security levels for resource sets and roles. When you add an account to a resource set, the security level of the role assumed by the account must be higher than or equal to the security level of the resource set.
> After you enable security level-based authorization, you cannot disable it in the console. If you want to disable security level-based authorization, contact technical support.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Security Policies**. On the Security Policies page,
click the **Security Level Based Access** tab.
4. Configure the parameters that are described in the following table based on your business
requirements.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|

| Enable Security Level Based Authorization | Specifies whether to enable security level-based authorization. After you enable security level-based authorization, a resource set is assigned the lowest security level by default. Preset roles, except for resource set administrators and resource users, are assigned the lowest security level. Other preset roles are assigned the highest security level. The management scope of a role cannot be changed. |
|---|---|
| Security Level (from Low to High) | The security levels from top to bottom in ascending order of priority. A maximum of 10 security levels are supported. Add a security level: a. In the lower part of the Security Level Based Access tab, enter a defined security level in the text box. b. Click the square boxes next to Text Color and Text Background Color. Then, select a color from a color picker or enter a color code. c. Click Add. Delete a security level: Find the security level that you want to delete and click Delete. Change the colors of a security level: Click the square boxes next to Text Color and Text Background Color. Then, select a color from a color picker or enter a color code. |

5. Click **Save**.

### 6.4 Authentication modes

#### 6.4.1 Authentication modes

This topic describes the authentication modes. Authentication modes are classified into the token mode and the hybrid mode. You can configure an authentication mode based on your business requirements.

**Token mode**

In token mode, Resource Access Management (RAM) and Security Token Service (STS) are required. Temporary STS tokens are issued to users and cloud services to assist in permission management. In token mode, all cloud services use STS tokens to authenticate users. Cloud services that do not support STS may be affected. For example, only operations administrators and level- 1 organization administrators can log on to the console of a cloud service.

> **Note:** On the **Authentication Mode** page, you can view the cloud services that support the token mode.

After you enable the token mode, authentication of northbound APIs may be affected. For example, if you use the AccessKey pair of a RAM user to call an API operation to add, delete, modify, or query specified resources in a specified organization and resource set, and the required RAM policies are not attached to the RAM user, an error may be returned.

> **Warning:** Before you enable the token mode, we recommend that you contact Alibaba Cloud to evaluate the situation. If an error occurs when you call an API operation, disable the token mode.

**Hybrid mode**

In hybrid mode, cloud services that support RAM and STS can still authenticate users based on STS tokens. For cloud services that do not support STS, permissions are managed based on the authentication logic of Apsara Stack tenant accounts and RAM users. In hybrid mode, if you select one or more cloud services, the cloud services use STS tokens to authenticate users. Cloud services that are not selected still authenticate users in hybrid mode.

#### 6.4.2 Configure an authentication mode

You can configure an authentication mode based on the scenario.

**Prerequisites**

You have logged on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as a platform administrator.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Authentication Mode**.
4. Select **Token Mode** or **Hybrid** based on the scenario.
If you select **Hybrid**, you can control the authentication model of a cloud service by selecting or clearing the cloud service. If you select a cloud service, Security Token Service (STS)-based authentication is enabled for the cloud service.

> **Important:** After token-based authentication is enabled, the authentication mode of northbound API operations is affected. We recommend that you contact the Alibaba Cloud service team for evaluation before you enable token-based authentication. If an error occurs when an API operation is called, roll back and disable token-based authentication for the service.

5. In the lower part of the page, click **Save**.
