#### 6.5.2 Create or synchronize specifications

You can create or synchronize specifications of cloud resources.

**Prerequisites**

You have logged on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as a platform administrator.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Specifications**.
4. On the Specifications page, select a cloud service from the **Resource Specification**
**Settings** drop-down list.
5. Click the **Resource Specifications** tab.

**Create specifications**

> **Note:** You can create specifications for the following cloud services: NAT Gateway, Server Load Balancer (SLB), IPv6 Gateway, ApsaraDB RDS, Tair (Redis OSS-compatible), PolarDB-X 1.0, PolarDB-X 2.0, ApsaraDB for MongoDB, and PolarDB.

a. Click **Create Specifications**. b. In the Create Specifications dialog box, configure the parameters. For more information about the specification parameters, see Specifications. c. Click **OK**.

**Synchronize specifications**

> **Note:** The specifications of cloud services are synchronized to the current system by calling API operations. You can manually synchronize the specifications of Elastic Compute Service (ECS).

a. Click **Synchronize Specifications**. b. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

#### 6.5.3 Manage specifications

> You can enable or disable specifications of different cloud resources. This way, only enabled specifications can be configured when resources are created.

**Prerequisites**

You have logged on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as a platform administrator.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Specifications**.
i. On the Specifications page, configure the **Specification Synchronization Settings** parameter to specify the specification synchronization mechanism.

> **Important:** New specifications may be released after cloud services are updated. You can configure the specification synchronization mechanism to make sure the specifications are up-to-date.

a. Click **Edit**. Select **Maintain Current Specifications** or **Synchronize Specifications**.
**Maintain Current Specifications**: New specifications are not synchronized after
version updates.

> **Note:** Select this option if you want to retain the existing configurations after version updates.

**Synchronize Specifications**: New specifications are synchronized after version
updates.

> **Note:** We recommend that you select this option to make sure that specifications are up-to-date.

b. Click **Save**. ii. Select a cloud service from the **Resource Specification Settings** drop-down list.

| Operation | Procedure |
|---|---|
| View specification s | Click the Resource Specifications tab to view the information about resource specifications, such as the status. Click the Specifications History tab to view the information about historical specifications. Click the Existing Specifications tab to view the used specifications and the number of resources that use the specifications. |
| Disable a specification | You can disable an enabled specification. The disabled specification is unavailable when users create the corresponding resources. a. Click the Resource Specifications tab. b. Find the resource specification that you want to disable and clickD isable in the Actions column. c. In the message that appears, click OK. |
| Enable a specification | You can enable disabled specifications. a. Click the Resource Specifications tab. b. Find the resource type that you want to enable and clickE nable in the Actions column. c. In the message that appears, click OK. |
| Export specification s | You can export the specification information to your computer for backup. a. Click the Resource Specifications tab. b. Click Export above the specification list. c. Configure the storage path, enter a file name, and then clickD ownload to export specifications of the cloud service as a .csv file to your computer. |

#### 6.5.4 Examples

##### 6.5.4.1 Create an ApsaraDB RDS instance specification

**specification**

**Background information**

Company A uses ApsaraDB RDS to deploy and manage database instances. The company needs to create a new ApsaraDB RDS instance specification to meet the requirements of different departments and applications.

**Planning**

Company A analyzes the specific requirements of departments and applications and poses the following requirements on the specification: The vCPU performance must be high and content resources must be extensive to support large-scale database operations. The storage capacity and the maximum number of connections can be expanded based on business requirements. SSD storage is required. High-speed read and write performance and a low failure rate are required. Company A then plans specification configurations based on these requirements. Example: vCPU: 8 cores Memory: 16 GB Storage: 500 GB SSD Maximum number of connections: 1,000 Database engine: MySQL 8.0

> **Important:** Before you create specifications, check with cloud service technical support to make sure that the specifications are available.

**Prerequisites**

You have logged on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as a platform administrator.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Specifications**.
4. On the **Specifications** page, choose **Database Services** > **ApsaraDB RDS** from the
**Resource Specification Settings** drop-down list.
5. On the **Resource Specifications** tab, click **Create Specifications**.
6. In the **Create Specifications** dialog box, configure the parameters.
Database Engine: MySQL Minimum Storage: 500 Maximum Storage: 3000 Instance Type: rds.mysql.A Chip Type: intel Engine Version: 8.0 cpu: 8 Connections: 1,000 Memory: 16 Edition: dual_ha Storage Type: cloud_ssd
7. Click **OK**. View the specification you created in the specification list.

**Subsequent impact**

The administrator named orgA of the level-1 organization of Company A can select the created specification when orgA creates an ApsaraDB RDS instance.

##### 6.5.4.2 Disable an ApsaraDB RDS instance specification

**specification**

**Background information**

Due to changes in business, Company A needs to disable the ApsaraDB RDS instance specification rds.mysql.A. After this specification is disabled, the related departments and applications can no longer use the specification. For more information about how to create the specification rds.mysql.A, see Create an ApsaraDB RDS instance specification.

**Planning**

After the specification rds.mysql.A is disabled, it is unavailable when users create ApsaraDB RDS instances.

**Prerequisites**

You have logged on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as a platform administrator.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as the super administrator.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Specifications**.
4. On the **Specifications** page, choose **Database Services** > **ApsaraDB RDS** from the
**Resource Specification Settings** drop-down list.
5. On the **Resource Specifications** tab, find the specification rds.mysql.A and click **Disable**
in the **Actions** column.
6. In the message that appears, click **OK**. After the specification is disabled, the value in the
**Status** column of the specification changes to **Disabled**.

**Subsequent impact**

The specification rds.mysql.A is unavailable when the level-1 organization administrator orgA of Company A creates an ApsaraDB RDS instance.

### 6.6 Menu management

#### 6.6.1 Configure menus

This topic describes how to configure menus to manage and control access to services and operations.

**Background information**

You can add external links to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console for centralized management and easy access. This greatly simplifies operations, prevents frequent switching between different platforms, and improves work efficiency. In addition, to implement personalized and categorized management, you can group and name menu items that you create. This also facilitates management and search. The highly flexible and user-friendly configuration method allows you to create, edit, and organize various submenu items based on your requirements. You can categorize features into different groups so that users can quickly and accurately locate the required features. This allows the menus to better meet the requirements of different scenarios.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator.

**Menu item parameters**

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Title | The display name of the menu item. |
| URL | The URL of the menu item. |

| Console Type | The type of the console. Different consoles have different domain names. Valid values: oneconsole and other. oneconsole: You need to only enter the path in the URL field. The domain name is automatically matched. The URL starts with one.console. other: You must enter the domain name in the URL field. |
|---|---|
| Identifier | The unique identifier of the menu item in the system. This identifier can be used to indicate whether the menu item is selected in the navigation bar. The identifier cannot be changed. |
| Sort | The display order among the same-level menu items. The larger the value, the lower it is displayed. |
| Parent Level | The parent menu item to which the menu item belongs. |
| Level-1 Group | The level-1 group to which the menu item belongs. This parameter is available and required if the Parent Level parameter is set to Products. |
| Level-2 Group | Optional. The level-2 group to which the menu item belongs. |
| Open With | The method to open the page of the menu item. Valid values:D efault and New Window. Default: opens the page in the current tab. New Window: opens the page in a new tab. |
| Description | The description of the menu item. |

**Create a menu item**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Menu Settings** > **Main Menu Configuration**.
4. On the **Main Menu Configuration** page, click the **Single-cloud Menu** tab.
5. On the **Single-cloud Menu** tab, click **Create**.
6. In the **Create** dialog box, configure the parameters. For more information, see the Menu
item parameters section of this topic.
7. Click **OK**.

**Modify a menu item**

You can modify a menu item as needed.

**Limits**

The default menu items cannot be modified.
1. On the **Single-cloud Menu** tab, find the menu item that you want to modify and click **Edit**
in the **Actions** column.
2. In the **Edit** dialog box, modify the menu item information and click **OK**.

**Delete a menu item**

You can delete a menu item if you no longer need it.

**Limits**

The default menu items cannot be deleted.
1. On the **Single-cloud Menu** tab, find the menu item that you want to delete and click
**Delete** in the **Actions** column.
2. In the **Delete** message, click **OK**.

**Show or hide a menu item**

1. On the **Single-cloud Menu** tab, find the required menu item and select or clear the check
box in the **Display** column. : The menu item is displayed in the console. : The menu item is not displayed in the console.

#### 6.6.2 Creation page configuration

To let users customize the product creation page experience according to their needs, the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console provides a creation page configuration feature. This feature allows administrators to globally adjust parameters and layout for multiple product creation pages.

**Background information**

With the creation page configuration feature, users can freely choose and set whether various elements appear or remain hidden, and whether they are required or optional. For example, during the creation of a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), if a customer wants to emphasize the “Description” field, they can configure it as a required field through this feature, ensuring detailed descriptions accompany every VPC creation. Creation page configuration supports setting required fields, hidden fields, and options on product creation pages. Configure required fields: Set fields that users must fill out when creating a product. Configure hidden fields: Hide specific fields so users cannot see them on the product creation page. Configure options: Show or hide specific options within fields, make selections visible to users, and reorder options based on user habits.

**Prerequisites**

The operating user defaults to the platform administrator.

**Configure required fields**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Menu Settings** > **Creation Page Configuration**.
4. On the **Creation Page Configuration** page, locate the target product form.
You can quickly find it by using the **Product** drop-down list and **dataId** above the list.
5. Click **Required Settings** in the **Actions** column for the target form.
6. In the **Required Settings** dialog box, select the fields you want to mark as required. For
example, after selecting the **Description** field, it becomes mandatory during product creation.

> **Note:** Fields without checkboxes do not support configuration.

7. Click **Confirm**.

**Configure hidden fields**

1. Click
in the **Actions** column for the target form, then select **Hidden Item Settings**.
2. In the **Hidden Item Settings** dialog box, select the fields you want to hide. For example,
after selecting **IPv6 CIDR Block**, users will not see this field on the creation page when creating a product.

> **Note:** Fields without checkboxes do not support configuration.

3. Click **Confirm**.

**Configure options**

1. Click
in the **Actions** column for the target form, then select **Option Settings**.
2. In the **Options** dialog box, select the field whose options you want to configure, then click
**Next Step**. For example, select the **Sharing Scope** field.

> **Note:** Fields without checkboxes do not support configuration.

3. Set whether each option is **Hide**, and adjust the order of options.

> **Note:** : Indicates that option hiding is enabled. The option remains invisible to
> users on the creation page.
> : Indicates that option hiding is disabled. The option appears visible to users
> on the creation page.
> Click
> to the right of **Option**, then select **Move Up** or **Move Down** to adjust
> the option order.

4. Click **OK**.

#### 6.6.3 Redirection page configuration

You can turn on or off the switch to remove the product redirection page based on your requirements.

**Prerequisites**

The operator must be a platform administrator by default.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Configuration**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Menu Management** > **Redirection Page**
**Configuration**.
4. Configure the authorization sequence and the redirection page removal setting.
To configure the authorization sequence: Click in the **Authorization Sequence** column. Drag in front of each access mode to adjust the authorization priority. To configure redirection page removal: In the **Remove Redirection Page**
**Configuration** column, turn on or off the switch.
indicates that the redirection page removal switch is turned on. When the switch is turned on, the redirection page does not appear when you enter the product console. The floating menu in the product console displays account switching options. You can switch accounts in the floating menu.

> **Important:** When the redirection page removal switch is turned on, the system accesses the product based on the priority configured in the authorization sequence.
> If the configured priority does not exist, the system uses the second configured priority by default.
> If you set a default access mode in the account switching menu, the system ignores the priority configured in the authorization sequence.

indicates that the redirection page removal switch is turned off. When the switch is turned off, the redirection page appears before you enter the product console. You must select an organization, region, and access mode on the redirection page to proceed. The floating menu in the product console displays account switching options. You can switch accounts in the floating menu.

### 6.7 Configure the billing feature on the Billing Switch page

**on the Billing Switch page**

Billing switches control whether billing is enabled to generate resource usage bills and display cost information.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Billing Switch**.
4. In the lower part of the page, click **Edit**.
5. Configure the billing feature based on your business requirements.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Currency | The billing currency. Select a currency from the drop-down list. After you specify the currency, the currency in the system will be changed to the latest currency. If you change the currency, the amount of the generated bill will not change. |
| Monthly Billing Start Date | The start date of the monthly bill. |
| Pricing Mode | The pricing mode. Valid values: Service Metering and Cost Rate. This parameter is displayed only if you deploy multi-cloud management services. Cost-plus pricing is supported for all Alibaba Cloud services. Usage-based pricing is supported only for Alibaba Cloud services with metering data and billing rules. Service Metering: In usage-based pricing mode, prices are determined based on billing rules and pricing factors for metering data. The resale amount of Alibaba Cloud services is calculated based on the billing rules and metering data of Alibaba Cloud services. Cost Rate: In cost-plus pricing mode, the resale amount of Alibaba Cloud services is calculated based on the following formula: Resale amount of Alibaba Cloud services = Cost in the bills of Alibaba Cloud services × Price multiplier. If you set this parameter to Cost Rate, enter a price multiplier in the field next to Cost Rate. Valid values: (0,10000]. Unit: %. Important After the pricing mode is switched, it takes effect in the next billing cycle. |

| Price Inquiry Switch | Specifies whether to enable price inquiry. : enables price inquiry. : disables price inquiry. |
|---|---|
| Fee Deduction Switch | Specifies whether to enable fee deduction. : enables fee deduction. : disables fee deduction. |
| Refund Ratio | The refund ratio. The refund amount is calculated based on the refund policy for switching the billing method from subscription to pay-as-you-go, refund policy for unsubscribing from subscription instances, or refund policy for downgrading subscription instances. The usage duration is accurate to the day. The part that is less than one day is counted as one day. Refund amount = (Original order amount - Consumed amount) × Refund ratio Consumed amount = Average daily unit price × Usage duration Usage duration = Unsubscription initiation time - Order start time |
| Per-second Billing | Specifies whether to enable per-second billing for cloud services. If you enable per-second billing for a cloud service, the resource usage data is collected at the second level and bills are generated based on the second-level metering data. Important By default, the per-second billing feature is disabled. If you enable the feature for a cloud service, bills are generated based on the second-level metering data. After the per-second billing feature is enabled for a cloud service, the feature cannot be disabled. Exercise caution when you enable this feature. |

> **Note:** Monthly Billing Start Date:

> Billing starts at 00:00:00 on the selected day and ends at 00:00:00 on the same day in the following calendar month. If you set the start date to the 15th day of the month or a day before the 15th day, the billing cycle starts in the current month and ends in the following month. If you set the start date to a day after the 15th day of the month, the billing cycle starts in the previous month and ends in the current month. If you change the billing cycle, the change takes effect in the following month.
> Examples:
> If you set the start date to the 10th day of the month, the billing cycle for February starts at 00:00:00 on February 10 and ends at 00:00:00 on March 10.
> If you set the start date to the 18th day of the month, the billing cycle for February starts at 00:00:00 on January 18 and ends at 00:00:00 on February 18.
> If the date that you selected does not exist in a calendar month, the system uses the last day of the calendar month as the start date. For example, if you set the start date to the 31st day of the month, the system uses the last day of February and other 30-day months as the start date of the billing cycle. Examples:
> Billing cycle for January: 00:00:00 on December 31 to 00:00:00 on January 31
> Billing cycle for February: 00:00:00 on January 31 to 00:00:00 on February 28
> Billing cycle for March: 00:00:00 on February 28 to 00:00:00 on March 31
> Billing cycle for April: 00:00:00 on March 31 to 00:00:00 on April 30
> Billing cycle for May: 00:00:00 on April 30 to 00:00:00 on May 31
> Price Inquiry Switch: After you enable price inquiry, you can view the fees that are generated when you create (activate) services, change the configurations of (scale out) services, release (delete) services, renew services, add services to Configure, Price, Quote (CPQ), or place orders. After you disable price inquiry, fees are not displayed. If you use resources that are billed on a monthly basis and you disable price inquiry, fees cannot be calculated when you unsubscribe from the resources or change the configurations of the resources.
> Fee Deduction Switch: After you enable fee deduction, fees are deducted from the budget based on the bill. After you disable fee deduction, no fee is deducted from the budget.
> If you enable price inquiry and disable fee deduction, only bills are generated and no fee is deducted from the budget. If you enable both price inquiry and fee deduction, fees are deducted from the budget. Fees are deducted only after the fee deduction switch is turned on. Historical fees are not deducted from the budget. If historical bills are regenerated, the historical fees are deducted.

6. Click **Save**.
7. Optional. In the lower part of the Billing Switch page, click **History** to view the historical
modification records.

### 6.8 Manage announcements

You can create announcements on the platform to inform users about events such as O&M, updates, and daily operations.

**Background information**

After an announcement is published, users can view the announcement in the Announcement section of the homepage.

> **Important:** The announcements that a user can view vary based on the role of the user:
> If the user assumes a global role, the user can view all published announcements.
> If the user assumes a non-global role, the user can view the published announcements of the organization to which the user belongs and the published announcements of which the Visible for Organization parameter is set to All.
> The announcements are displayed in descending order based on the publish time.

The announcement management feature allows you to create, modify, view, edit, and delete announcements. Tenant isolation is also implemented to ensure that announcements are separately managed for each tenant.

> **Important:** When a platform administrator creates or edits an announcement, the platform administrator can set the Visible for Organization parameter to All or SystemDefaultOrganization. However, only All is a valid value. If the Visible for Organization parameter is set to SystemDefaultOrganization, an error is reported when the announcement is saved.
> Global roles can view and manage announcements of all organizations.
> Non-global roles can view only the announcements of the level-1 organization to which the current account belongs. If you create or edit an announcement by assuming a non-global role, you can select only All or the corresponding level-1 organization from the Visible for Organization drop-down list.

You can limit the visibility of announcements to specified organizations. Announcement content supports rich text. You can adjust the content style and insert images or links based on your business requirements. Announcements are automatically published or unpublished based on the specified publish or unpublish time. You can delete an announcement if you no longer need it. After the announcement is deleted, it cannot be restored.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator or operations administrator.

**Create an announcement**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Announcement Management**.
4. On the **Announcement Management** page, click **Create Announcement**.
5. On the **Create Announcement** page, configure the parameters described in the following
table.

| Section and parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Title | The title of the announcement. The title must be 2 to 120 characters in length and can contain letters, digits, and the following characters: periods (.), commas (,), semicolons (;), colons (:), single quotation marks ('), double quotation marks (''), question marks (?), angle brackets (<>), exclamation points (!), and spaces. |
| Type | The type of the announcement. Valid values: Upgrade Announcement, O&M Notifications, Security Notifications, Urgent Events, and Daily Announcement. |

| Visible for Organization | The organizations to which the announcement is visible. By default,A ll is selected. In this case, users in all organizations can view the announcement. You can also select a level-1 organization from the drop-down list. In this case, only the users in the selected level-1 organization can view the announcement. Note If you use a platform administrator account, the displayed values of the Visible for Organization parameter are All and SystemDefaultOrganization. To create the announcement, you must select All for the Visible for Organization parameter. Otherwise, the configuration is invalid. If you use an operations administrator account, you can view all level-1 organizations in the drop-down list. You can select All or a specific level-1 organization to create the announcement. If you use a custom Resource Access Management (RAM) role that has the permissions to manage announcements, take note of the following items: If you use a global RAM role, you can view all level-1 organizations in the drop-down list. You can select All or a specific level-1 organization to create the announcement. If you use a non-global RAM role, you can view only the level-1 organization to which the current account belongs in the drop-down list. You can select All or the corresponding level-1 organization to create the announcement. |
|---|---|
| Publish - Unpublish Time | The time that you want to publish and unpublish the announcement. The time is accurate to seconds. Announcements are automatically published or unpublished based on the specified publish or unpublish time. The publish time must be later than the current time, and the unpublish time must be later than the publish time. |
| Announcement content | Announcement content supports rich text. You can adjust the content style and insert images or links based on your business requirements. |

6. Click **Create**.

> **Note:** After an announcement is created and automatically published, the announcement is displayed in the Announcement section of the **homepage**. Only the users in the specified organizations can view the announcement.
> Automatic publishing and unpublishing of announcements may be delayed by 1 to 5 seconds.

**View the announcement list and details of an announcement**

After an announcement is created, you can view the created announcement in the announcement list.
1. Optional. On the **Announcements** page, enter an announcement name in the search box
to search for the announcement.
2. View the information about the announcement displayed in the following columns:
**Announcement Type**, **Announcement Name**, **Status**, **Visible Organization**, **Modified**
**At**, **Created At**, **Published At**, and **Unpublished At**.

> **Note:** Click the
> icon next to the **Status** column to filter announcements by status.
> Valid values of the Status column: **Pending**, **Published**, and **Unpublished**.
> Click the
> icon next to the **Modified At**, **Created At**, **Published At**, or
> **Unpublished At** column to sort announcements in ascending or descending order based on the corresponding time.

3. Click the name of the announcement to go to the announcement details page and view the
announcement details.

> **Note:** You can go to the details pages of only announcements in the **Published** state.

**Modify an announcement**

You can modify an announcement to reflect information changes.
1. On the **Announcement Management** page, find the announcement that you want to
modify and click **Modify** in the Actions column.
2. On the **Modify Announcement** page, modify the title, type, organizations to which the
announcement is visible, publish and unpublish time, and content based on your business requirements.
3. Click **Modify**.

**Delete an announcement**

You can delete an announcement if it is no longer needed.
1. On the **Announcement Management** page, find the announcement that you want to
delete and click **Delete** in the Actions column.
2. In the **Confirm** message, click **OK**.

### 6.10 Custom settings

#### 6.10.1 Platform settings

You can customize the logon page, platform logo, and other platform configurations on the platform based on your requirements.

**Background information**

Multiple languages are supported, including Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and English. You can select a default language for the platform. You can select a dark or light mode. You can also change the theme color of the console. You can enable and customize the page watermark. You can configure multi-language brand information in the console (including the browser ICO image, platform logo, platform name, and information displayed on the logon page). You can restore the page to factory settings. The restoration is irreversible.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Custom Configurations** > **Platform Settings**.
4. Modify the platform settings as needed. To restore factory settings, click **Restore Factory**
**Settings** at the bottom of the page. The configurations take effect the next time you log in
to the console.

| Configuration Item | Description |
|---|---|

| Platform Language | Select one or more languages supported by the platform. Valid values: Simplified Chinese Traditional Chinese English Select a default language for the platform from the supported languages. |
|---|---|
| Appearance and Theme | Appearance: Select Light Color Mode or Dark Pattern. Theme Color: Select Recommended Theme Color or Custom Swatches. ### 6.11 Third-party authentication

You can configure third-party authentication to implement single sign-on (SSO) in which the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console serves as a service provider (SP) and the system that is developed by a customer serves as an identity provider (IdP). This way, users can access the resources provided by the SP without additional authentication after they pass the authentication of the IdP.

**Terms**

SSO: allows users to log in to multiple systems with a single action of login without the need to re-enter the username and password for authentication. Single logout (SLO): allows users to log off from multiple systems with a single action of logoff. IdP: provides identity management services. SP: provide users with specific services by using the identity management services provided by IdPs. Security Assertion Markup Language 2.0 (SAML 2.0): a protocol that is designed for enterprise-level user identity authentication. SAML 2.0 is used for communication between SPs and IdPs by exchanging authentication and authorization data within security domains. Open Authorization (OAuth) 2.0: an authorization protocol that specifies the following grant types for different scenarios: authorization code, client credentials, resource owner password credentials, and implicit. The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console uses the authorization code grant type.

#### 6.11.1 User-based SSO

##### 6.11.1.1 Configure a global IdP

This topic describes how to configure a global identity provider (IdP).

**Usage notes**

> **Important:** The following section describes how to configure a global IdP, which is an enterprise system, when the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console serves as a service provider (SP). In one cloud with multiple regions scenarios, users from all regions must be authenticated by the global IdP.
> When a global IdP is configured for the cloud platform, users are authenticated by the global IdP after they click the button for authorized login on the login page of the platform.
> If a global IdP is configured for the cloud platform, you can no longer configure a local IdP. You must clear the global IdP before you configure a local IdP.
> If a local IdP is configured for the cloud platform, you can no longer configure a global IdP. You must clear the local IdP before you configure a global IdP.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Authentication by Third Party**. The User-based
SSO tab appears.
4. On the **Global IdP Settings** tab, click **Edit** and configure the parameters in the **Global**
**IdP Settings**, **Obtain Verified User Information**, and **Global Authorization Redirect**
sections.

> **Note:** The Obtain Verified User Information section is displayed only if you set the Protocol Type parameter to OAuth 2.0.

The parameters in the Obtain Verified User Information section are not required in OAuth 2.0. Configure the parameters based on your business requirements.
5. After you complete the configurations, click **Save**.

> **Important:** If you click **Restore Factory Settings**, the global IdP settings are cleared. Users are not authenticated by the global IdP when they log in to the platform. Exercise caution when you perform this operation.

##### 6.11.1.2 Configure a local IdP

This topic describes how to configure a local identity provider (IdP).

**Usage notes**

> **Important:** If a local IdP is created and bound to a level-1 organization, the button for authentication is unavailable on the login page of the platform for the users of the level-1 organization and subordinate organizations. The users are navigated to the platform only after they log in from the local IdP.
> After you create a local IdP, you can bind the IdP to a level-1 organization to implement IdP authentication at the organization level. Each level-1 organization can be bound to only one IdP including a global IdP.
> If a global IdP is configured for the cloud platform, you can no longer configure a local IdP. You must clear the global IdP before you configure a local IdP.
> If a local IdP is configured for the cloud platform, you can no longer configure a global IdP. You must clear the local IdP before you configure a global IdP.
> If a level-1 organization is bound to a local IdP, you can still configure local IdPs for other level-1 organizations.
> Before you delete a local IdP, you must unbind the local IdP from bound organizations.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Authentication by Third Party**. The User-based
SSO tab appears by default.
4. On the **Local IdP Settings** tab, click **Create Local IdP**.
5. In the **Create Local IdP** dialog box, configure parameters in the IdP Settings and Obtain
Verified User Information sections.

> **Note:** The Obtain Verified User Information section appears only if you set the Protocol Type parameter to OAuth 2.0.

The parameters in the Obtain Verified User Information section are not required in OAuth 2.0. Configure the parameters based on your business requirements.
6. Click **OK**.
7. Manage local IdPs.

| Operation | Procedure |
|---|---|

| View a local IdP | i. On the Local IdP Settings tab, view the local IdP list. The list information includes IdP Name/ID, Protocol Type, Associated Organizations, and Created At. Note After you click a number in the Associated Organizations column of an IdP, you are navigated to the Associated Organization tab. ii. Find the local IdP that you want to view and clickD etails in the Actions column. The details panel of the IdP appears. Basic Information: This tab displays the basic information about the local IdP. Note If the protocol type of the IdP isS AML 2.0, you can click Download SP Metadata File in the Basic Information section to download the metadata file. Associated Organization: This tab displays the information about organizations bound to the local IdP. The information includes Organization ID/Name, Description, and Associated At. |
|---|---|

| Modify a local IdP | i. On the Local IdP Settings tab, find the local IdP that you want to modify and click Modify in the Actions column. ii. In the Modify Local IdP dialog box, modify the parameters as required. iii. Click OK. |
|---|---|
| Delete a local IdP | i. On the Local IdP Settings tab, find the local IdP that you want to delete and click Delete in the Actions column. Note Before you delete a local IdP, you must unbind the local IdP from bound organizations. ii. In the message that appears, click Delete. |

##### 6.11.1.3 Configure a multi-cloud IdP

If a cloud platform is managed by another cloud platform, the other cloud platform acts as an identity provider (IdP) to provide unified identity authentication and this cloud platform acts as a service provider (SP) to accept identity assertion of the other cloud platform. This enables users to access resources without repeated logins. The Multi-cloud IdP Settings tab displays the configuration information about a multi-cloud IdP.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Authentication by Third Party**. The User-based
SSO tab appears by default.
4. On the **Multi-cloud IdP Settings** tab, view the details of a multi-cloud IdP. If the cloud
platform is not connected, the parameters on the tab are left empty.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| IdP Service Name | The service name of the multi-cloud IdP. |
| Protocol Type | The protocol type. Default value: SAML 2.0. Note When you configure single sign-on (SSO) on the IdP side, use the metadata provided by the Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) service provider of Apsara Stack. |
| IdP Authenticatio n Address | The URL for multi-cloud IdP authentication. Format: http://URL or https://URL . |
| IdP Certificate | The Base64-encoded third-party certificate. |
| SLO Endpoint | The URL for single logout (SLO). Format: http://URL or https://URL . Note The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console accesses this endpoint when it responds to an SLO request from the IdP. |
| SLO Request Method | The SLO request method. |

#### 6.11.2 Manage OIDC IdPs

This topic describes how to view and delete OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity providers (IdPs).

**Usage notes**

> **Important:** OIDC is an authentication protocol based on OAuth 2.0. Applications can use OIDC for authentication based on the relationship between external IdPs and Apsara Stack Resource Access Management (RAM).
> You can use the OIDC authentication feature to control API permissions on different pods that are deployed in a Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) cluster. This enables fine-grained permission control on pods and reduces security risks.
> Only ACK supports the OIDC authentication feature. You can view OIDC IdPs created by ACK clusters in the OIDC IdP list. You cannot directly create an OIDC IdP. You must contact technical support to enable the OIDC authentication feature for ACK clusters.
> After ACK clusters create OIDC IdPs, the platform administrator can view and delete the OIDC IdPs on the OIDC Authentication tab.
> After an OIDC IdP is deleted, RAM roles that reference the OIDC IdP become unavailable. This may affect cloud service authentication and cause business risks. Exercise caution when you perform this operation.

**Prerequisites**

You are a platform administrator.

**View OIDC IdPs**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Authentication by Third Party**.
4. On the **Authentication by Third Party** page, click the **OIDC Authentication** tab.
5. In the OIDC IdP list, view information about existing OIDC IdPs in the following columns: **IdP**
**Name**, **arn**, **Issuer URL**, **Client ID**, **Description**, and **Created At**.
**IdP Name**: the name of the OIDC IdP.
**arn**: the Alibaba Cloud Resource Name (ARN) of the OIDC IdP.
**Issuer URL**: the URL of the OIDC IdP. The URL is used by the client to authenticate the
source of the ID token.
**Client ID**: the ID that the OIDC IdP uses to authenticate an application.
**Description**: the description of the OIDC IdP.
**Created At**: the time when the OIDC IdP was created.

**Delete an OIDC IdP**

1. In the OIDC IdP list, find the OIDC IdP that you want to delete and click **Delete** in the
Actions column.
2. In the dialog box that appears, select **I am aware of the risks and want to delete the**
**OIDC provider**.
3. Click **OK**.

### 6.12 Message Gateway

The system sends messages to users through email, SMS, and DingTalk. You must complete the relevant configuration for each method before you send messages.

**Background information**

The system supports configuration of the email gateway, SMS gateway, DingTalk settings, Webhook, and message templates.

**Prerequisites**

By default, the operating user is the platform administrator.

**Configure the email gateway**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Message Gateway**.
4. Click the **Mail Gateway** tab.
5. Fill in the email gateway configuration items.

| Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|

| Sender email | Enter the sender email address. The system sends emails through this address. |
|---|---|
| Enable SMTP AUTH | Enable or disable SMTP AUTH. : indicates enabled. : indicates disabled. |
| Sender email password | Enter the password for the sender email account. You must enter thes ender email password if you enable SMTP AUTH. |
| SMTP Server Address | This is the outgoing mail server. It is usually smtp.xxx.com. |
| Port | Enter the SMTP server port. |
| Encryption | Select from three options: Not Encrypted, SSL, or TLS. |
| Enable | Select Enable or Disabled. |
| Email attachment | Select Enable or Disabled. |

6. Click **Submit** to complete the email configuration.
Click **Reset** to clear the email gateway configuration and reconfigure it. Click **Test email**, enter the destination email address, and test whether the email can be sent successfully.

**Configure the SMS gateway**

1. On the **Message Gateway** page, click the **SMS gateway** tab.
2. Fill in the SMS gateway configuration items.

| Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|
| SMS gateway address | Enter the API URL of the SMS gateway. |
| Receive number parameter name | Enter the parameter name that represents the recipient phone number in the SMS gateway. |
| SMS content parameter name | Enter the parameter name that represents the SMS content in the SMS gateway. |
| Request header parameters | Enter the header parameters for the request to the SMS gateway. ClickA dd to add a new request header parameter. Enter the parameter name in the first column and the parameter value in the second column. |
| Request body parameters | Click Add to add a new request body parameter. When the transfer mode is POST, both the recipient number parameter and the SMS content parameter are placed in the request body. |
| Content encoding | Select UTF-8 or GBK. |
| Transfer mode | Select GET or POST. When the transfer mode is GET, ignore the request body parameters. Append both the phone number and content using the GET method. When the transfer mode is POST, append the request body parameters, recipient number parameter, and content parameter to the request body. |
| Enable | Select Enable or Disabled. |

3. Click **Submit** to complete the SMS configuration.
Click **Reset** to clear the SMS configuration and reconfigure it. Click **Test SMS**, enter the recipient phone number, and test whether the SMS can be sent successfully.

**Configure DingTalk settings**

1. On the **Message Gateway** page, click the **DingTalk settings** tab.
2. Fill in the DingTalk configuration items.

| Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|
| Message channel enabled | Supports selecting Personal RAM user token and Global specified gateway. Personal RAM user token: The personal account token configuration takes effect. Global specified gateway: Configure to send messages to the globally specified gateway. |
| Hook address | The webhook of the custom robot. |
| Secret key | The secret key used when you select the Security Settings option Add Signature for the custom robot. To obtain the secret key, perform the following steps: i. Create a new DingTalk group chat. ii. Add an intelligent group assistant and select Custom Robot. iii. In the security settings of the robot, select Add Signature and obtain the secret key. |

3. Click **Submit** to complete the DingTalk configuration.

### 6.13 Manage service-linked roles

You can create a Resource Access Management (RAM) role to authorize cloud services in a level-1 organization to view and manage other resources in the organization.

**Prerequisites**

You have logged on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as an operations administrator, organization administrator, global organization security administrator, or organization security administrator.

**Create a service-linked role**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Service-linked Roles**.
4. On the **Service-Linked Roles** page, click **Create Service-linked Role**.
5. On the page that appears, select a service from the **Service Name** drop-down list and
select one or more organizations from the **Authorized Organization Name** drop-down list. After you select a service, the permissions of the service-linked role are displayed. You can select multiple organizations.
6. Click **OK**.

**View the details of a service-linked role**

1. On the **Service-linked Roles** page, configure the **Role Name**, **Organization Name**, and
**Service Name** parameters to filter RAM roles.
2. Find the RAM role that you want to manage and click **View Details** in the **Actions** column
to go to the details page of the RAM role.
3. On the **role details** page, view the details and policy of the RAM role.
Click the **Role Details** tab to view the name, creation time, description, and trust policy of the RAM role. Click the **Role Policy** tab to view the policy information, including the policy name, policy type, default version, description, and time when the policy is attached to the RAM role.

> **Note:** You can click **View Details** in the **Actions** column to view the policy details.

### 6.14 Configure risky operation settings

**settings**

This topic describes how to configure different identity authentication and notification methods for different risky operations. This reduces unexpected operations and ensures service security.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Limits**

If text message-based authentication and email or text message notifications are required, you must configure text message and email gateways on the platform. The valid mobile number and email address must be saved in the personal information of the user who performs risky operations. If multi-factor authentication (MFA) is enabled, you must bind a virtual MFA device to the user who performs risky operations and enable MFA when the user logs in to the platform.

4. Optional. Select a cloud service from the Product drop-down list.
5. Find the operation that you want to modify and click **Edit** in the **Actions** column.
6. In the **Edit Risky Operation Configurations** dialog box, configure the identity
authentication and notification methods.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Identity Authentica tion | The identity authentication method. Valid values: None, MFA, and Text Message. You can select only one value. |
| Notificatio n Settings | The notification method. Valid values: Email and Text Message. You can select multiple values. |

7. Click **Save**.

### 6.15 Configure log storage settings

**settings**

You can configure a storage mode for the operation logs and AccessKey logs of cloud services. This way, security administrators can query logs to check the resource usage and component status in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. Security administrators can also export operation logs as a file and download the file to a local device.

**Background information**

The log storage settings apply to the storage of operation logs and AccessKey logs of cloud services. By default, logs are stored in the underlying storage of Simple Log Service. If no Logstore exists in the sales cloud, logs are stored in the Logstore of the Apsara Infrastructure Management cluster. By default, logs are retained for seven days. The capacity required for log storage is calculated based on the following formula: 5,000,000 × Log retention period × Number of organizations/1,024/1,024/1,024. For example, if the number of organizations is 300 and the log retention period is 180 days, approximately 251.46 GB of capacity is required for log storage.

> **Note:** 5,000,000 is the estimated amount of log data generated in one day, measured in bytes. The log data includes the data generated by using Apsara Stack consoles, calling API operations, and using developer tools.
> The storage capacity is measured in GB.

**Prerequisites**

You have logged on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as an operations administrator.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

> **Note:** We recommend that you log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as the preset operations administrator. This ensures the security of created Simple Log Service projects and Logstores and prevents accidental deletion.

2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Log Storage Settings**.
4. In the lower-left part of the Log Storage Settings page, click **Edit**.
The following log storage modes are available: **Default**, **Log Storage for All**
**Organizations**, and **Log Storage for Specified Organization** .

| Storage Mode | Description |
|---|---|
| Default | The operation logs of the users of all organizations are stored in the system Logstore for seven days. Only All Events is available for the Event Type parameter. |
| Log Storage for All Organizatio ns | The operation logs of the users of all organizations are stored in the configured Logstore. You need to purchase Simple Log Service in advance. You can set the Storage Duration parameter to 30 Days, 60 Days, 90 Days, 180 Days, 360 Days, or 720 Days. The maximum storage duration is 720 days. You can set the Event Type parameter to All Events, Write Event, or Read Event. |

| Log Storage for Specified Organizatio n | The operation logs of the users of the specified organizations are stored in the configured Logstore. You need to purchase Simple Log Service in advance. You can set the Storage Duration parameter to 30 Days, 60 Days, 90 Days, 180 Days, 360 Days, or 720 Days. The maximum storage duration is 720 days. You can set the Event Type parameter to All Events, Write Event, or Read Event. In the Settings section, configure the parameters in the Organization and Log Service Configuration sections. In the Log Service Configuration section, the Log Service Region, Project Name, and Logstore Name parameters are required. You can click the icon to add more organization configurations. Important The organizations must belong to different level-1 organizations. |
|---|---|

5. Click **Save**.

### 6.16 Billing and Order Dump Configuration

**Configuration**

Configure the storage mode for orders and billing records.

**Prerequisites**

The default operator is the Operations Administrator.

**Constraints**

You cannot modify the dump mode after you set the archive mode for historical billing and order data.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Log Storage Settings**.
4. Click **Edit**.
5. Configure the log transfer mode. The system supports **Default** and **Archive Historical**
**Data** modes.
**Default**: The system stores all orders and billing records in the default database
permanently.
**Archive Historical Data**: The system archives historical data older than five years to
another storage location. You cannot query archived data. In addition, the time range available for filtering and querying orders, billing records, and data analysis is limited to the most recent five years.
**ossBucket**: Select a storage product. Configure this parameter only when you select
Archive Historical Data as the dump mode.
**path**: Enter the storage address. Configure this parameter only when you select
Archive Historical Data as the dump mode.
6. Click **Save**.
If you select the **Archive Historical Data** mode and click Save, the system displays the
**Confirm Authorization** dialog box. You must confirm authorization.

#### 6.17.2 Configure event push

The event push feature allows you to push the events in the event list to event receivers. This way, data can be efficiently communicated and forwarded.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Event Notification** > **Event Push**.
4. On the **Event Push** page, click **Create Configuration**.
5. In the **Create Configuration** dialog box, configure the parameters that are described in
the following table.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Name | The name of the event push configuration. The name must be 2 to 64 characters in length. |
| Description | The description of the event push configuration. |
| Acceptor URL | The API endpoint of the receiver. Enter a valid URL that consists of the HTTP or HTTPS protocol, domain name, and path. |
| Acceptor Parameter Name | The name of the parameter used by the receiver to receive resource changes. |

| Organization | The effective scope of event push. When a user in the selected organization performs an operation included in the event list, the event is pushed based on the configuration. |
|---|---|
| Request Header Parameters | The header names and values in the requests sent to the receiver API endpoint. The specified request headers must ensure the security, integrity, and accuracy of communication. Click Add to add more request headers. Click the icon to remove added request headers. |
| Request Body Parameters | The parameter names and values in the body of HTTP POST requests sent from a client to a server. |
| Content Code | The encoding type of the content. Valid values: UTF-8 and GBK. |
| Passing Method | The HTTP request method. Valid values: GET and POST. Important If this parameter is set to GET, the request body parameters are ignored and the receiver parameter is concatenated in GET mode. If this parameter is set to POST, the request body parameters and the receiver parameter are concatenated in the request body. |
| Enable | Specifies whether to enable the event push configuration. |

6. Click **OK**.

> **Note:** You can click **Cancel** to discard the event push configuration. You can also click **Test** to test the connectivity of the event push configuration.

7. Perform the following operations as needed.

| Operation | Description |
|---|---|

| View event push configurations | i. Optional. On the Event Push page, enter a configuration name and select an organization to search for the event push configuration that you want to view. ii. In the event push configuration list, view the information about event push configurations in the following columns: Name, Enabling Status, Acceptor URL, Acceptor Parameter Name, Effective Organization, Request Header Parameters, Request Body Parameters, Content Code, Passing Method, Description, and Created At. Note You can click the icon next to Enabling Status to filter event push configurations and display the configurations in the Enabled or Disabled state. |
|---|---|
| Modify an event push configuration | i. On the Event Push page, find the configuration that you want to modify and click Modify in the Actions column. ii. In the Modify Configuration dialog box, modify the parameters. You cannot modify the configuration name. iii. Click OK. |
| Enable an event push configuration | Note Only event push configurations in the Disabled state can be enabled. i. On the Event Push page, find the configuration that you want to enable and click Enable in the Actions column. ii. In the message that appears, click OK. |
| Disable an event push configuration | Note Only event push configurations in the Enabled state can be disabled. i. On the Event Push page, find the configuration that you want to disable and click Disable in the Actions column. ii. In the message that appears, click OK. |
| Delete an event push configuration | i. On the Event Push page, find the configuration that you want to delete and click Delete in the Actions column. ii. In the message that appears, click Delete. |

## 7 Operations

### 7.1 Resource operations

#### 7.1.1 Application forms

The Application Forms page displays service-related application forms submitted on the platform, including the application forms submitted by using a service catalog.

##### 7.1.1.1 View application forms

The Application Forms page displays a list of application forms categorized as My Application Forms, To Be Approved, Participated, Handled, and All Application Forms.

**Background information**

My Application Forms: all application forms that you created To Be Approved: application forms that require your approval Participated: application forms you have participated in, including those copied to you and all approvals automatically passed Handled: application forms that you processed, including all approval forms that you processed, transferred, or co-signed All Application Forms: all application forms within your visibility scope, including application forms that you created, processed, or participated in, as well as other application forms within your visibility scope
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Application Forms**.
4. On the **Application Forms** page, click the **My Application Forms**, **To Be Approved**,
**Participated**, **Handled**, or **All Application Forms** tab.
5. Expand **Advanced Filter**, configure the filter conditions, and then click **Search**.

| Tab | Supported filter conditions |
|---|---|

| My Application Forms | Application Form No., Process Name, Scenario, Application Form Status, and Submission Time. For Scenario, you can select Management Operations, Cloud Service Operations, Service Catalog, Service Boundary, or Custom. |
|---|---|
| To Be Approved/Partici pated/Handled | Application Form No., Process Name, Scenario, Query Type, Applicant Organization/Applicant, Include Subordinate Organizations, and Submission Time. For Scenario, you can select Management Operations, Cloud Service Operations, Service Catalog, Service Boundary, or Custom. For Query Type, you can select Query by Applicant Organization or Query by Applicant. |
| All Application Forms | Application Form No., Process Name, Scenario, Application Form Status, Query Type, Applicant Organization/Applicant, Include Subordinate Organizations, and Submission Time. For Scenario, you can select Management Operations, Cloud Service Operations, Service Catalog, Service Boundary, or Custom. For Query Type, you can select Query by Applicant Organization or Query by Applicant. |

> **Note:** **Scenario**: includes **Management Operations**, **Cloud Service Operations**, **Service Catalog**, **Service Boundary**, and **Custom**.
> **Management Operations**: The system displays this option when you select **Management Operations** for **Scenario**.
> **Cloud Service Operations**: The system displays this option when you select **Cloud Service Operations** for **Scenario**.
> **Service Catalog**: The system displays this option when you select **Service** **Catalog** for **Scenario**.
> **Cloud Service**: The system displays this option when you select **Service** **Boundary** for **Scenario**.
> **Query Type**: includes **Query by Applicant Organization** and **Query by** **Applicant**.
> **Applicant Organization** and **Include Subordinate Organizations**: The system displays these options when you select **Query by Applicant** **Organization** for **Query Type**.
> **Applicant**: The system displays this option when you select **Query by** **Applicant** for **Query Type**.
> **Submission Time**: Set the submission time of the application form.

6. View the application form list.
7. Click the application No. to go to the **Details** page.

> **Note:** The application form requirement details vary based on the scenario.
> For the Service Catalog scenario, approvers can modify the configuration. Click **Modify Configuration** in the Actions column to update the applicationform configuration. For more information, see Modify the configuration of an application form.
> Click **Detailed Parameters** in the **Actions** column to view the call parameter information in the **Detailed Parameters** panel.
> To view the application progress, click **View All** next to Approval Progress of Application Form.

##### 7.1.1.2 Withdraw an application form

The application form page allows you to withdraw an application form pending approval.

**Prerequisites**

The application form is in the **Pending Approval** status.

**Limits**

You can withdraw only the application forms created by yourself.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Application Forms**.
4. On the **Application Forms** page, click the **My Application Forms** tab.
5. Expand **Advanced Filter**, specify the **Application Form No.**, **Process Name**, **Scenario**,
**Management Operations**/**Cloud Service Operations**/**Service Catalog**/**Cloud Service**,
**Application Form Status**, and **Submission Time** conditions, and then click **Search**.

> **Note:** **Scenario**: Supports **Management Operations**, **Cloud Service Operations**, **Service Catalog**, **Service Boundary**, and **Custom**.
> **Management Operation**: Appears when you select **Management Operations** for **Scenario**.
> **Cloud Service Operations**: Appears when you select **Cloud Service** **Operations** for **Scenario**.
> **Service Catalog**: Appears when you select **Service Catalog** for **Scenario**.
> **Cloud Service**: Appears when you select **Service Boundary** for **Scenario**.
> **Submission Time**: Specifies the submission time of the application form.

6. In the application form list, click **Withdraw** in the **Actions** column of the target application
form.
7. In the dialog box, click **OK**.

##### 7.1.1.3 Modify the configuration of an application form

**form**

When an approver modifies the configuration of an application form, the approver must ensure that the product operation is connected to a service and that the relevant system preset services are listed before proceeding with configuration changes.

**Prerequisites**

The workflow bound to this application form must allow approvers to modify configurations. Approvers can successfully change configurations only if their management scope exceeds that of the initiator. The application form is in the **Under approval** state. The **Scenario** of the application form is Service Catalog.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Application Forms**.
4. On the **Application Forms** page, click the **To Be Approved** tab.
5. Expand **Advanced Filter**, configure **Application Form NO.**, **Process Name**, **Scenario**,
**Management Operation**/**Cloud Product Operation**/**Service Catalog**/**Cloud Service**,
**Query Type**, **Applicant Organization**/**Applicant**, **Include Subordinate Organizations**,
and **Submission Time**, and then click **Search**.

> **Note:** **Scenario**: includes **Management Operation**s, **Cloud Service Operations**, **Service Catalog**, **Service Boundary**, and **Custom**.
> **Management Operations**: appears when you select **Management** **Operations** for Scenario.
> **Cloud Service Operations**: appears when you select **Cloud Service** **Operations** for **Scenario**.
> **Service Catalog**: appears when you select **Service Catalog** for **Scenario**.
> **Cloud Service**: appears when you select **Service Boundary** for **Scenario**.
> **Query Type**: includes **Query by Applicant Organization** and **Query by** **Applicant**.
> **Applicant Organization** and **Include Subordinate Organizations**: appear when you select **Query by Applicant Organization** for **Query Type**.
> **Applicant**: appears when you select **Query by Applicant** for **Query Type**.
> **Submission Time**: specifies the submission time of the application form.

6. In the application form list, click the No. of the application form.
7. On the application form details page, click **Modify Configuration**.
8. On the product console page, update the configuration.
9. In the **Reason for modifying the configuration** dialog box, enter the reason.
0. Return to the application form details page and view the configuration modification history.

##### 7.1.1.4 Approve an application form

Approve an application form pending your approval.

**Background information**

When an application form requires your approval, the system sends notifications using DingTalk, in-system messages, and emails. If the applicant is also the approver of the current approval node, the system automatically approves the application form. For countersigns involving multiple approvers, the remaining approvers must approve the application form as usual.

**Prerequisites**

The application form is in the **Pending Approving** status.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Appliction Forms**.
4. On the **Appliction Forms** page, click the **To Be Approved** tab.
5. Expand **Advanced Filter**, configure the **Application Form No.**, **Process Name**,
**Scenario**, **Management Operation**s/**Cloud Service Operations**/**Service**
**Catalog**/**Cloud Service**, **Query Type**, **Applicant Organization**/**Applicant**, **Include**
**Subordinate Organizations**, and **Submission Time** conditions, and then click **Search**.

> **Note:** **Scenario**: Supports **Management Operations**, **Cloud Service Operations**, **Service Catalog**, **Service Boundary**, and **Custom**.
> **Management Operations**: Appears when you set **Scenario** to **Management** **Operations**.
> **Cloud Service Operations**: Appears when you set **Scenario** to **Cloud Service** **Operations**.
> **Service Catalog**: Appears when you set **Scenario** to **Service Catalog**.
> **Cloud Service**: Appears when you set **Scenario** to **Service Boundary**.
> **Query Type**: Supports **Query by Applicant Organization** and **Query by** **Applicant**.
> **Applicant Organization** and **Include Subordinate Organizations**: Appear when you set **Query Type** to **Query by Applicant Organization**.
> **Applicant**: Appears when you set **Query Type** to **Query by Applicant**.
> **Submission Time**: Specifies the submission time of the application form.

6. Approve a single application form or approve application forms in batches.
**Approve a single application form**:
a. In the application form list, click **Review** in the **Actions** column of the target application form. b. In the **Review** dialog box, select comments, enter a review description, and upload attachments.

> **Note:** You can set the comments to **Approve** or **Reject**.
> Click **Approval Analysis** to open Apsara Copilot, which analyzes the application form and provides approval suggestions. The approval analysis feature appears only after an operations administrator enables the intelligent assistant in **Configurations** > **Apsara Copilot** > **Custom Configuration**.

c. Click **OK**.
**Approve multiple application forms in batches**:
a. In the application form list, select multiple application forms that require approval. b. Click **Batch Approve** below the list. c. In the **Batch Approve** dialog box, select comments, enter an approval description, and upload attachments. d. Click **OK**.

#### 7.1.2 Process management

##### 7.1.2.1 Manage processes

You can create process definitions to define approval processes for different organizations and services based on the approval requirements. You can configure custom approval processes for resource applications based on existing approval processes. You can dynamically add user nodes in an approval process and specify system users as approvers. You can configure sequential signature and parallel signature approval methods, add multiple approval nodes, and specify multiple approvers. The system provides preset Start and End nodes.

**Background information**

You can manage approval processes at the operation control layer of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console to allow or reject operations that users want to perform. This way, user operations can be approved in a fine-grained manner. The process management feature is used to approve operations that users want to perform, such as creating resources. Users may perform high-risk operations in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. Before users perform high-risk operations, a role with higher or centralized permissions must approve the operations. This prevents accidental operations or unauthorized access and ensures the security, stability, and compliance of the system.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Process Management** > **Process Management**.
4. On the **Process Management** page, click **Create Process**.
5. In the Create Process wizard, configure the parameters in the **Basic Information** and
**Process Configuration** steps.
i. Configure the parameters in the Basic Information step and click **Next**. The following table describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Process Name | The name of the process. |
| Process Description | The description of the process. |
| Applicable Personnel | The organization with which the process can be associated. Valid values:A ll Organizations and Select Organization. All Organizations: The process can be associated with all organizations. Select Organization: The process can be associated only with the selected organization. |
| Select Organization | The organization with which the process can be associated. This parameter is displayed only if the Applicable Personnel parameter is set to Select Organization. Select an organization from the Select Organization drop-down list. You can select only one organization within a tenant. The process can be associated only with the selected organization. |
| Bind Sub- organization | Specifies whether the process can be associated with the subordinate organizations of the selected organization. This parameter is displayed only if the Applicable Personnel parameter is set to Select Organization. If a subordinate organization is associated with another process, the current process cannot be associated with the subordinate organization. After you select an organization from the Select Organization drop-down list, you can turn on or off the switch. : The process can be associated with the subordinate organizations of the selected organization. : The process cannot be associated with the subordinate organizations of the selected organization. |
| Select Initiator | The user or role that can initiate the process. Valid values:A ll Users and Specified Role. If you set the Applicable Personnel parameter to Select Organization and turn on Bind Sub-organization, all users or specified roles in the selected organization and its subordinate organizations can initiate the process. |
| Select Role | The role that can initiate the process. This parameter is displayed only if the Select Initiator parameter is set to Specified Role. You can select one or more roles from the Select Role drop-down list. All users who assume the selected roles can initiate the process. |

ii. Configure the process in the Process Configuration step and click **Submit**. By default, the Start and End nodes are preset when you create a process. You can add and configure approval nodes. a. Optional. Click the **Start** node. In the **Initiator Settings** panel, select or clear Allow Initiator to Add CC Recipient. Selected: allows the initiator to add carbon copy (CC) recipients.

> **Note:** The initiator can select only available users as CC recipients.

Cleared: does not allow the initiator to add CC recipients. b. Click the icon between the Start and End nodes. In the Add Objects dialog box, select **Add Approver**, **External Process Integration**, or **Conditional Branch** to add an Approved By node, an External Process Integration node, or condition nodes.

> **Note:** You can move the pointer over the
> icon in the upper-right corner of an
> added approval node and click **Delete** to remove the node.
> If you select Conditional Branch, a custom condition node and a default condition node are added by default. You can click the
> icon below the

custom condition node to add another condition node. You can add at most nine condition nodes at the same level. You do not need to configure the default condition node. If custom conditions are not met, the default conditions are met. c. Click an added node to configure the node. Approved By: For more information, see the Configure the Approved By node section of this topic. If the applicant and the approver of an approval node are the same user, the approver automatically approves the application. If multiple approvers are involved, the other approvers need to approve the applications. External Process Integration: For more information, see the Configure the External Process Integration node section of this topic. Condition nodes: For more information, see the Configure the condition nodes section of this topic. d. Optional. Click the **End** node. In the **End Node Settings** panel, specify the users who are notified of the end of the process. After the process ends, the approval results are automatically sent to the specified users. You can select one or more users from the **Specific Personnel** drop-down list. Users who are visible to the process creator are displayed.
6. After the process is created, perform the following operations based on your business
requirements.

| Operation | Procedure |
|---|---|
| View the process list and the details of a process | i. On the Process Management page, click Advanced Filter and configure filter conditions to search for processes. ii. In the process list, view the information about processes in the following columns: Process Name/ID, Workflow Type, Applicable Organizations, Include Subordinate Organizations, Applicable Personnel, Created By, Created At, Updated At, and Process Status. Note A process can be in the Initialized, Published, or Paused state. You can click the icon in the Process Status column to filter processes by status. iii. Find the process that you want to view and click its name to go to the Process Details page. iv. Click the nodes in the Settings section to view the detailed configurations of each node. |
| Modify the basic information and configurations of a process | Important Only custom processes in the Initialized or Paused state can be modified. i. On the Process Management page, find the process that you want to modify and click Modify in the Actions column. ii. In the Edit Process wizard, modify the process based on your business requirements. |

| Publish a process | Important Only custom processes in the Initialized or Paused state can be published. i. On the Process Management page, find the process that you want to publish and click Publish in the Actions column. ii. In the message that appears, click OK. After the process is published, the state of the process changes to Published. |
|---|---|
| Disable a process | Important Only custom processes in the Published state can be disabled. i. **Configure the Approved By node**

If you set the Type parameter to Specific Personnel, select one or more users from the Select Users drop-down list to specify the users as the approvers of the approval node. If you set the Type parameter to Specified Role, select a role from the Select Role drop-down list. You can select only one role. You can specify whether to allow only the role in the organization to which the initiator belongs to approve the process. If you select the check box, only the role in the organization to which the initiator belongs can approve the process. If you clear the check box, all users assigned the selected role in the level-1 organization can approve the process. |
