Only supervisors of the selected level can approve the process. Valid values of the Initiator parameter include Direct Supervisor, Second Level Supervisor, Third Level Supervisor, Fourth Level Supervisor, and Fifth Level Supervisor. You can select only one supervisor level. Note Supervisors are the organization administrators of organizations of each level. If you select Direct Supervisor, the approver is the organization administrator of the organization to which the initiator belongs. If you select Second Level Supervisor, the approver is the organization administrator of the parent organization to which the initiator belongs. You can select a supervisor of up to the fifth level. If no supervisor can be found, the process is automatically approved. After you configure continuous multi-level supervisors, the supervisors at different levels can approve the process in turn. If you set the Type parameter to Continuous Multi-level Supervisor, select a value from the Approval Endpoint drop-down list to specify the highest supervisor level. The process is approved in turn by supervisors from the lowest level to the highest level. Supervisors of multiple levels may be involved as the approvers of the approval node. Valid values of the Approval Endpoint parameter include Direct Supervisor, Second Level Supervisor, Third Level Supervisor, Fourth Level Supervisor, and Fifth Level Supervisor. You can select only one supervisor level. Note If you select Direct Supervisor, the final approver is the organization administrator of the organization to which the initiator belongs. If you select Second Level Supervisor, the final approver is the organization administrator of the parent organization to which the initiator belongs. You can select a supervisor of up to the fifth level. If no supervisor can be found, the process is automatically approved. **Configure the External Process Integration node**

To transfer application forms from the process system of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console to a third-party approval node, you must complete the following connection configurations to notify the third-party process system and start the approval process in the third-party process system. After you complete the configurations, click
**Connectivity Test** to check the connectivity between the two parties.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Request Method | The request method. Default value: POST. |
| Request URL | The request URL of the notification operation provided by the third-party process system. Important The request URL must be an external cloud URL. To enable access to the URL, contact Apsara Stack technical support. The involved server role is unimanager- workflow.flow#. |
| Access Token | The access token of the notification operation. Access tokens are a security mechanism used for identity authentication and authorization. When a request is made, an access token is inserted into headers in the format of {"Authorization": " bearer <Access token>"} to prove the identity of the requester and obtain access permissions. |

| Process Access Configuratio n | The custom parameters to be included in the request. You can clickA dd One Row to add a custom parameter. You can add at most 20 parameters, one per row. For more information, see the Request parameters section of this topic. In each parameter row, enter the parameter name in the Request Parameter Name field and the parameter value in the Field Name field. When the third-party notification operation is called, the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console generates a set of key-value pairs based on the specified parameters, encapsulates them into a JSONObject, and then passes the JSONObject to the third-party process system. |
|---|---|

**Request parameters**

The parameters to be included in requests from the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console to the third-party notification operation are defined as paramJson. paramJson consists of required data and custom data.

**Required data**

For more information, see lines 35 to 37 in the Pseudocode for constructing request parameters section of this topic. Required data is passed by default. You do not need to add required data in the **Process**
**Access Configuration** section. The following table describes the required data.

> **Important:** If you add a parameter with the same name as a required parameter in the **Process** **Access Configuration** section, the added parameter does not take effect.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| callbackParams | Map<String, Object> | The parameters required for callbacks. After the third-party process system completes the approval, it notifies the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console with the parameters. |

**Custom data**

In each parameter row in the **Process Access Configuration** section, the parameter name is defined as paramKey and the parameter value is defined as paramValue. Parameter values support preset and non-preset values.

**Preset values**

For more information, see lines 24 to 27 in the Pseudocode for constructing request parameters section of this topic. If the value of a custom parameter is a preset value, the console dynamically obtains the corresponding information of the application form based on the definition of the preset value, and encapsulates the parameter name and dynamic information as a new keyvalue pair into paramJson. **Pseudocode for constructing request parameters**

The following pseudocode is provided to help you better understand how parameters are constructed.

ement Console for calling the third-party notification operation as paramJson.

        if (preSetInfoList.containsKey(paramValue)) {
            paramJson.put(paramKey, "Dynamic data of the application form obtained
based on paramValue");

##### 7.1.2.2 Workflow binding

Configure the association between workflows and business operations to meet configuration requirements for multiple scenarios. The system supports dynamically binding resource application methods with approval processes. Multiple types of resources can share the same workflow.

**Background information**

Establish a binding relationship between workflows and business operations. The system intercepts the requester’s operation based on specific business requirements and workflow settings. The system executes the related operation only after approval. This approach provides better control over workflow execution and ensures compliance and accuracy of business activities. Create, modify, and delete workflow binding relationships.

**Prerequisites**

Before you create a workflow binding relationship, make sure that you have created the workflow and that the workflow is in the **Published** state. By default, the operating user is the operations administrator.

**Limits**

A single workflow can have only one binding relationship with a business scenario. If the selected workflow already has a binding relationship, the corresponding business scenario becomes grayed out and cannot be bound again.

**Create a workflow binding relationship**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operation** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Process Management** > **Bind Process**.
4. At the top of the page, click **Bind Process**.
5. On the **Bind Process** page, complete the following binding configuration.

| Configuratio n item | Description |
|---|---|
| Process name | From the process name drop-down list, select the workflow to bind. You can only select workflows with the status Published. |
| Business scenario | The workflow supports binding to one of the following business scenarios: Management Operations, Cloud Service Operations, or Service Catalog. Single selection only. |

| Managemen t Operations | Business scenario is set to Management Operations. Configure this item. You can select multiple management operations. When you perform the selected management operations, the system requires workflow approval. Examples include managing organizations and managing resource sets. |
|---|---|

| Cloud Service Operations | Business scenario is set to Cloud Service Operations. Configure this item. You can select multiple cloud resources and their operations. When you perform the selected cloud service operations, the system requires workflow approval. Examples include starting or stopping an ECS instance under Elastic Compute Service (ECS), or creating, modifying, or deleting a VPC under Virtual Private Cloud (VPC). Note In multi-cloud scenarios, a unified approval process is supported. For public cloud services, permission points are limited to those cloud services already integrated into the service catalog. Currently supported public cloud services include ECS, VPC, Server Load Balancer (SLB), and Elastic IP Address (EIP). |
|---|---|
| Service Catalog | Business scenario is set to Service Catalog. Configure this item. You can select multiple service catalogs. After you select a service type, the corresponding service catalog appears. In the Actions column of the service catalog list, select the relevant operations. Examples include create and change configuration. |

6. Click **Submit**.
Before submission, you can select **No permissions are required for the initiator.** This allows the initiator to submit the workflow form even if they lack permissions for the approval operations within the workflow.
7. After you complete the workflow binding, perform other related operations as needed.

| Operation | Description |
|---|---|
|   | i. On the Bind Process page, expand Advanced filtering. You can quickly find the target workflow by using filters such as Process name, Applicable Personnel, and Business Scenarios. Note Business Scenarios include Management Operations, Cloud Product Catalog, and Service Catalog. After you select a specific scenario, you can further filter by specific business operations under Management Operations, Cloud Service Operations, or Service Catalog. ii. In the binding list, view information such as Process Name/ID, Process Status, Process Description, Applicable Organizations, Include Subordinate Organizations, Applicable Personnel, Business Scenarios, Business Operations, Created At, and Update Time. Click the workflow name to go to the workflow details page. Note Click cards in the configuration information section to view detailed configurations for each workflow node. |

| View the workflow binding list | Click View in the Actions column to view workflow binding details. Example of management operation binding details: Example of cloud service operation binding details: Example of service catalog binding details: |
|---|---|

| Edit the workflow binding relationship | Note When you edit a workflow binding relationship, you can only modify the specific management operation, cloud service operation, or service catalog operation. You cannot modify other configurations. i. In the binding list, click Edit in the Actions column of the workflow binding. ii. Update the business operations to bind based on your actual business needs. |
|---|---|
| Delete the workflow binding relationship | i. In the binding list, click Delete in the Actions column of the workflow binding. ii. Click Confirm. |

**Submit additional information for the workflow**

After you bind a business scenario to a workflow, the workflow management system intercepts related operations. You must provide additional information to complete the submission and generate a workflow order.

> **Note:** You can add CC recipients only if the workflow is configured to allow the initiator to add them. When adding CC recipients, you can select only users visible to the initiator.

#### 7.1.3 Quota management

##### 7.1.3.1 Products that support resource quotas

Organization administrators and users can create resources within the quota limits of each product in their organization. When the quota for a product is exhausted, they cannot create additional resources for that product. To continue creating resources, they must first increase the product quota in the organization. If no quota is configured, the system does not limit resource creation.

> **Note:** For disk, memory, and capacity quotas, the minimum calculation unit is **GB**. The system rounds decimal values to the nearest integer. For example, when calculating the quota, the system rounds 0.8 GB up to 1 GB and 0.2 GB down to 0 GB.

###### 7.1.3.1.1 Elastic computing

###### 7.1.3.1.1.1 ECS

This topic describes the quotas that you can configure for Elastic Compute Service (ECS), calculation methods of quota usage, and inventory source.

**Quotas**

| Quota |   | Description |
|---|---|---|
| CPU Quota (Cores) |   | The total number of CPU cores that you can configure for ECS. |
| GPU Quota (GPUs) |   | The total number of GPUs that you can configure for ECS. |
| Memory Quota (GiB) |   | The total memory capacity that you can configure for ECS. |
| Disk Quota (GiB) | SSD (GiB) | The total capacity of SSDs that you can configure for ECS. |
|   | Ultra Disk (GiB) | The total capacity of ultra disks that you can configure for ECS. |
|   | Premium Performance Disk (GiB) | The total capacity of premium performance disks that you can configure for ECS. |
|   | Standard Performance Disk (GiB) | The total capacity of standard performance disks that you can configure for ECS. |
| Security Group Quota (Units) |   | The total number of security groups that you can create for ECS. |
| Custom Image Quota (Units) |   | The total number of custom images that you can create for ECS. |
| ENI Quota (Units) |   | The total number of elastic network interfaces (ENIs) that you can create for ECS. |
| Instance type quota |   | The number of instances that can be created for an instance type. |

**Calculation methods of quota usage**

The usage of CPU cores, memory, GPUs, and disk capacity of a single ECS instance is calculated based on the following formulas: CPU core usage = instanceTypeId.cpu Memory usage = instanceTypeId.mem GPU usage = instanceTypeId.gpu Disk capacity usage= ∑ (System disks and attached disks) Instance type usage = Number of created instances of the instance type

> **Note:** The usage of CPU cores, memory, and GPUs of a single ECS instance is obtained the information defined in the instance type.
> instanceTypeId.cpu indicates the number of CPU cores defined in the selected instance type.
> instanceTypeId.mem indicates the memory size defined in the selected instance type.
> instanceTypeId.gpu indicates the number of GPUs defined in the selected instance type.
> The disk capacity usage of an instance is calculated by accumulating the size of the system disks and the size of the attached disks.

The usage of security groups, custom images, and ENIs is calculated based on the following formulas: Security group usage = Number of created security groups Custom image usage = Number of created custom images ENI usage = Number of created ENIs

> **Note:** The usage of security groups, custom images, and ENIs is the number of created resource instances.

**Inventory source**

The data is collected by the Capacity module of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.

> **Important:** Some Elastic Block Storage (EBS) clusters can share disks of multiple types. When you configure logical inventories, make sure that the sum of the logical inventories of the disk quota items does not exceed the physical inventory. For example, if an IO15 cluster has a physical inventory of 1,000 GiB and can share premium performance disks and standard SSDs, the physical inventory of both premium performance disks and standard SSDs is increased by 1,000 GiB. When you configure logical inventories, you need to check whether disk sharing is enabled for the EBS cluster and make sure that logical inventories do not exceed 1,000 GiB.

|   | ACK Cluster Computing Power Quota (TFLOPS) | The computing power of container clusters that you can create for BMCP. |
|   | Computing Power Quota (TFLOPS) | The computing power of super computing clusters that you can create for BMCP. |
| GPU memory quotas | Bare Metal Cluster GPU Memory Quota (GiB) | The total memory capacity of GPUs of bare metal clusters that you can create for BMCP. |
|   | ACK Cluster GPU Memory Quota (GiB) | The total memory capacity of GPUs of container clusters that you can create for BMCP. |
|   | E-HPC GPU Memory Quota (GiB) | The total memory capacity of GPUs of super computing clusters that you can create for BMCP. |
| GPU type |   | The GPU type is reported by BMCP. This quota is counted by the number of GPUs. You must configure the quota items based on the supported GPU types. Example: XG310 (4SG1) (Units). |

**Calculation method of quota usage**

The quota usage of a single cluster is calculated based on the following formulas: CPU core usage = Cluster.CpuCount = sum(Node.CpuCount) Memory usage = Cluster.MemCount = sum(Node.MemCount) Computing power usage = Cluster.FlopsCount = sum(Node.FlopsCount) GPU memory usage = Cluster.VideoMemCount = sum(Node.VideoMemCount)

> **Note:** Cluster.CpuCount indicates the number of CPU cores of the selected cluster.
> Node.CpuCount indicates the number of CPU cores of a node in the selected cluster.
> Cluster.MemCount indicates the memory of the selected cluster.
> Node.MemCount indicates the memory of a node in the selected cluster.
> Cluster.FlopsCount indicates the computing power of the selected cluster.
> Node.FlopsCount indicates the computing power of a node in the selected cluster.
> Cluster.VideoMemCount indicates the GPU memory of the selected cluster.
> Node.VideoMemCount indicates the GPU memory of a node in the selected cluster.

**Inventory source**

The data is collected by the Capacity module of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.

> **Important:** Bare metal clusters and container clusters share the physical inventory. When you configure logical inventories, make sure that the sum of the logical inventories of a quota item of the two types of clusters cannot be exceed the physical inventory. For example, if the physical CPU inventory of both bare metal clusters and container clusters is five cores, the sum of the logical CPU inventories of bare metal clusters and container clusters must be equal to or smaller than five cores.

###### 7.1.3.1.4 Database services

###### 7.1.3.1.4.1 AnalyticDB for PostgreSQL

This topic describes the quotas that you can configure for AnalyticDB for PostgreSQL, calculation method of quota usage, and inventory source.

**Quotas**

| Quota | Description |
|---|---|
| CPU Quota (Cores) | The total number of CPU cores that you can configure for AnalyticDB for PostgreSQL. |
| Memory Quota (GiB) | The total memory capacity that you can configure for AnalyticDB for PostgreSQL. |
| Disk Quota (GiB) | The total storage capacity that you can configure for AnalyticDB for PostgreSQL. |

**Calculation method of quota usage**

**Integrated storage mode**

CPU quota usage = cpuCore × DBInstanceGroupCount Memory quota usage = memory × DBInstanceGroupCount Disk quota usage = disk × DBInstanceGroupCount × Number of replicas

> **Note:** The quota usage of AnalyticDB for PostgreSQL instances of the integrated storage mode is calculated based on the instance type, the number of compute nodes, and the number of replicas.
> cpuCore indicates the number of CPU cores of the selected instance type.
> DBInstanceGroupCount indicates the number of compute nodes.
> memory indicates the memory capacity of the selected instance type.
> disk indicates the disk size of the selected instance type.
> By default, the number of replicas is 2.

**Reserved storage mode**

CPU quota usage = cpuCore × (SegNum + MasterNum + Number of replicas) Memory quota usage = memory × (SegNum + MasterNum + Number of replicas) Disk quota usage = disk × (SegNum × 2 + MasterNum + Number of replicas)

> **Note:** The quota usage of AnalyticDB for PostgreSQL instances of the reserved storage mode is calculated based on the instance type, the number of compute nodes, the number of master nodes, and the number of replicas. The fixed ratio of CPU cores, memory capacity, and disk capacity of an instance is 1:8:80.
> cpuCore indicates the number of CPU cores of the selected instance type.
> memory indicates the memory capacity of the selected instance type.
> disk indicates the disk size of the selected instance type.
> SegNum indicates the number of compute nodes.
> MasterNum indicates the number of master nodes.
> By default, the number of replicas is 1.

**Inventory source**

The data is collected by the Capacity module of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.

> **Note:** Shared AnalyticDB for PostgreSQL instances share physical resources with each other without being limited by the physical inventory. The shared physical resources include the memory capacity and CPU cores. Therefore, the physical inventory of the memory capacity and CPU cores may not indicate the saleable memory capacity and CPU cores. The saleable memory capacity and CPU cores may be greater than the physical inventory.

###### 7.1.3.1.4.2 ApsaraDB for MongoDB

This topic describes the quotas that you can configure for ApsaraDB for MongoDB, calculation methods of quota usage, and inventory source.

**Quotas**

| Quota | Description |
|---|---|
| CPU Quota (Cores) | The total number of CPU cores that you can configure for ApsaraDB for MongoDB. |
| Memory Quota (GiB) | The total memory capacity that you can configure for ApsaraDB for MongoDB. |
| Disk Quota (GiB) | The total storage capacity that you can configure for ApsaraDB for MongoDB. |

**Calculation methods of quota usage**

**Replica set instance**

CPU quota usage = DBInstanceClass.cpu × Number of primary and secondary nodes Memory quota usage = DBInstanceClass.mem × Number of primary and secondary nodes Disk quota usage = DBInstanceStorage × Number of primary and secondary nodes

> **Note:** The quota usage is calculated based on the instance specifications and the number of primary and secondary nodes.
> DBInstanceClass.cpu: the number of CPU cores of the selected instance specifications.
> DBInstanceClass.mem: the memory capacity of the selected instance specifications.
> DBInstanceStorage: the storage capacity of the selected instance specifications.
> By default, the number of primary and secondary nodes is 3.

**Sharded cluster instance**

CPU quota usage = mongosSpec.cpu × mongosCount + shardSpec.cpu × shardCount × Number of replicas + configserverSpec.cpu × configserverCount × Number of replicas Memory quota usage = mongosSpec.mem × mongosCount + shardSpec.mem × shardCount × Number of replicas + configserverSpec.mem × configserverCount × Number of replicas Disk quota usage = shardStorage × shardCount × Number of replicas + configserverStorage × configserverCount × Number of replicas

> **Note:** The quota usage of mongos nodes, shard nodes, and Configserver nodes is calculated.
> The quota usage of mongos nodes is calculated based on the node specifications and the number of mongos nodes.
> mongosSpec.cpu: the number of CPU cores of the selected mongos node specifications.
> mongosCount: the number of mongos nodes.
> The quota usage of shard nodes is calculated based on the node specifications, number of shard nodes, and number of replicas.
> shardSpec.cpu: the number of CPU cores of the selected shard node specifications.
> shardSpec.mem: the memory capacity of the selected shard node specifications.
> shardStorage: the storage capacity of the selected shard node specifications.
> shardCount: the number of shard nodes.
> By default, the number of replicas is 3.
> The quota usage of Configserver nodes is calculated based on the node specifications, number of Configserver nodes, and number of replicas.
> configserverSpec.cpu: the number of CPU cores of the selected Configserver node specifications.
> configserverSpec.mem: the memory capacity of the selected Configserver node specifications.
> configserverStorage: the storage capacity of the selected Configserver node specifications.
> configserverCount: the number of Configserver nodes.
> By default, the number of replicas is 3.

**Inventory source**

The data is collected by the Capacity module of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.

> **Note:** Shared ApsaraDB for MongoDB instances share physical resources with each other without being limited by the physical inventory. The shared physical resources include the memory capacity and CPU cores. Therefore, the physical inventory of the memory capacity and CPU cores may not indicate the saleable memory capacity and CPU cores. The saleable memory capacity and CPU cores may be greater than the physical inventory.

###### 7.1.3.1.4.3 PolarDB-X 2.0

This topic describes the quotas that you can configure for PolarDB-X 2.0, calculation methods of quota usage, and inventory source.

**Quotas**

| Quota | Description |
|---|---|
| Memory Quota (GiB) | The total amount of memory that can be configured for PolarDB-X 2.0. |
| CPU Quota (Cores) | The total number of CPU cores that can be configured for PolarDB-X 2.0. |
| Disk Quota (GiB) | The total disk capacity that can be configured for PolarDB-X 2.0. |
| License Core Quota (Core) | The total number of License cores that can be configured for PolarDB-X 2.0. |

**Calculation methods of quota usage**

**CPU**

Standard Edition: CPU usage = CPU specification of a data node + CPU specification of a data node + 2 Enterprise Edition: CPU usage of compute nodes = Number of compute nodes × CPU specification of a compute node CPU usage of data nodes = Number of data nodes × (CPU specification of a data node + CPU specification of a data node + 2) CPU usage of Global Meta Service (GMS) nodes = CPU specification of a data node + CPU specification of a data node + 2 CPU usage of Change Data Capture (CDC) nodes = 2 × 4 Total CPU usage = CPU usage of compute nodes + CPU usage of data nodes + CPU usage of GMS nodes + CPU usage of CDC nodes

**Memory**

Standard Edition: Memory usage = Memory specification of a data node + Memory specification of a data node + 4 Enterprise Edition: Memory usage of compute nodes = Number of compute nodes × Memory specification of a compute node Memory usage of data nodes = Number of data nodes × (Memory specification of a data node + Memory specification of a data node + 4) Memory usage of GMS nodes = Memory specification of a data node + Memory specification of a data node + 4 Memory usage of CDC nodes = 2 × 16 Total memory usage = Memory usage of compute nodes + Memory usage of data nodes + Memory usage of GMS nodes + Memory usage of CDC nodes

**Disk**

Standard Edition: Disk usage = User-specified capacity × 2 Enterprise Edition: Disk usage of compute nodes = Number of compute nodes × 300 Disk usage of data nodes = Number of data nodes × 2 × User-specified capacity Disk usage of GMS nodes = 2 × 50 Disk usage of CDC nodes = 200 Total disk usage = Disk usage of compute nodes + Disk usage of data nodes + Disk usage of GMS nodes + Disk usage of CDC nodes

**License core**

Standard Edition: Dedicated: License core usage = CPU usage General-purpose: License core usage = CPU usage/2 Enterprise Edition: Dedicated: License core usage = Total CPU usage General-purpose: License core usage = Total CPU usage/2

**Inventory source**

The data is collected by the Capacity module of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.

###### 7.1.3.1.4.4 ApsaraDB RDS

This topic describes the quotas that you can configure for ApsaraDB RDS, calculation methods of quota usage, and inventory source.

**Database engines**

ApsaraDB RDS supports the following database engines: MySQL, PostgreSQL, PolarDB, and SQL Server. You can configure quotas for different database engines.

**Quotas**

| Quota | Description |
|---|---|
| CPU Quota (Cores) | The total number of CPU cores that you can configure for ApsaraDB RDS. |
| Memory Quota (GiB) | The total memory capacity that you can configure for ApsaraDB RDS. |
| Disk Quota (GiB) | The total storage capacity that you can configure for ApsaraDB RDS. |

**Calculation methods of quota usage**

**High-availability Edition**

CPU quota usage = dbInstanceClass.cpu × Number of nodes Memory quota usage = dbInstanceClass.mem × Number of nodes Disk quota usage = DBInstanceStorage × Number of nodes

> **Note:** The quota usage is calculated based on the instance specifications and the number of nodes.
> dbInstanceClass.cpu: the number of CPU cores of the selected instance specifications.
> dbInstanceClass.mem: the memory capacity of the selected instance specifications.
> DBInstanceStorage: the storage capacity of the selected instance specifications.
> By default, the number of nodes is 2.

**Enterprise Edition**

CPU quota usage = dbInstanceClass.cpu × Number of regular nodes + Fixed CPU overhead of replica nodes Memory quota usage = dbInstanceClass.mem × Number of regular nodes + Fixed memory overhead of replica nodes Disk quota usage = DBInstanceStorage × Number of regular nodes + Fixed storage overhead of replica nodes

> **Note:** The CPU quota usage is calculated based on the instance specifications, the number of regular nodes, and the fixed resource overhead of replica nodes.
> dbInstanceClass.cpu: the number of CPU cores of the selected instance specifications.
> By default, the number of regular nodes is 2.
> The CPU overhead of replica nodes is fixed to 2 GiB.
> The memory quota usage is calculated based on the instance specifications, number of regular nodes, and fixed resource overhead of replica nodes.
> dbInstanceClass.mem: the memory capacity of the selected instance specifications.
> By default, the number of regular nodes is 2.
> The memory overhead of replica nodes is fixed to 4 GiB.
> The disk quota usage is calculated based on the instance specifications, number of regular nodes, and fixed resource overhead of replica nodes.
> DBInstanceStorage: the storage capacity of the selected instance specifications.
> By default, the number of regular nodes is 2.
> The storage overhead of replica nodes is fixed to 50 GiB.

**Inventory source**

The data is collected by the Capacity module of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.

> **Note:** ApsaraDB RDS for MySQL instances and PolarDB for MySQL clusters that use local disks share the inventory.
> Shared ApsaraDB RDS instances share physical resources with each other without being limited by the physical inventory. The shared physical resources include the memory capacity and CPU cores. Therefore, the physical inventory of the memory capacity and CPU cores may not indicate the saleable memory capacity and CPU cores. The saleable memory capacity and CPU cores may be greater than the physical inventory.

###### 7.1.3.1.4.5 Tair (Redis OSS-compatible)

This topic describes the quota that you can configure for Tair (Redis OSS-compatible), calculation methods of quota usage, and inventory source.

**Quota**

| Quota | Description |
|---|---|
| Memory Quota (GiB) | The total memory capacity that can be configured for Tair (Redis OSS- compatible). |

**Calculation method of quota usage**

**Standard Edition (Master-replica)**

Memory usage = instanceClass.mem × Number of replicas The preceding formula is used to calculate the memory usage of a standard instance.

> instanceClass.mem indicates the memory size that is defined in the instance type.
> The number of replicas is fixed to 2.

**Cluster Edition**

Memory usage = instanceClass.mem × Number of replicas + Proxy node overhead + CS node overhead

> **Note:** The preceding formula is used to calculate the memory usage of a cluster instance.
> instanceClass.mem indicates the memory size that is defined in the instance type.
> The number of replicas is fixed to 2.
> You can calculate the corresponding proxy node overhead based on the number of proxy nodes. You can obtain the number of proxy nodes by checking the number before "proxy" in the InstanceClass field. For example, if an instance is of the redis.logic.sharding.8g.8db.0rodb.8proxy.default class, the number of proxy nodes of the instance is 8.
> The CS node overhead is fixed to 1 GiB.

**Read/write Splitting**

Memory usage = instanceClass.mem × (2 + Number of read-only nodes) + Proxy node overhead + CS node overhead

> **Note:** The preceding formula is used to calculate the memory usage of a read/write splitting instance.
> instanceClass.mem indicates the memory size that is defined in the instance type.
> You can select one or three read-only nodes when you select a node type.
> You can calculate the corresponding proxy node overhead based on the number of proxy nodes. You can obtain the number of proxy nodes by checking the number before "proxy" in the InstanceClass field. For example, if an instance is of the redis.logic.sharding.8g.8db.0rodb.8proxy.default class, the number of proxy nodes of the instance is 8.
> The CS node overhead is fixed to 1 GiB.

The following table describes the relationships between the number of proxy nodes and the proxy node overhead.

| Number of proxy nodes | Proxy node overhead |
|---|---|
| 4 | 20 GiB |
| 6 | 30 GiB |
| 8 | 40 GiB |
| 12 | 40 GiB |
| 16 | 60 GiB |

| 24 | 80 GiB |
|---|---|
| 32 | 120 GiB |
| 48 | 180 GiB |
| 64 | 240 GiB |
| 96 | 320 GiB |
| 128 | 480 GiB |
| 192 | 480 GiB |
| 256 | 480 GiB |
| 384 | 960 GiB |
| 512 | 1,280 GiB |
| 768 | 1,920 GiB |
| 1024 | 2,560 GiB |

**Inventory source**

The data is collected by the Capacity module of the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.

> **Note:** The memory of a shared Tair (Redis OSS-compatible) instance can be shared. The shared Tair (Redis OSS-compatible) instance shares physical resources with other shared Tair (Redis OSS-compatible) instances without being limited by the physical inventory. Therefore, the physical inventory data of the memory size may not indicate the saleable memory size. The saleable memory size may be greater than the physical inventory.

###### 7.1.3.1.4.6 PolarDB

This topic describes the quotas that you can configure for PolarDB, calculation methods of quota usage, and inventory source.

**Quotas**

| Quota | Description |
|---|---|
| CPU Quota (Cores) | The total number of CPU cores that can be configured for PolarDB. |
| Memory Quota (GiB) | The total size of memory that can be configured for PolarDB. |
| Disk Quota (GiB) | The total storage capacity that can be configured for PolarDB. |

**Calculation methods of quota usage**

CPU quota usage = DBNodeClass.cpu × DBNodeNum + CPU overhead of hot standby storage clusters + CPU overhead of PolarProxy Memory quota usage = DBNodeClass.mem × DBNodeNum + Memory overhead of hot standby storage clusters + Memory overhead of PolarProxy Disk quota usage = StorageSpace + Disk overhead of hot standby storage clusters

> **Note:** DBNodeClass.cpu: the number of CPU cores defined in the selected node specifications.
> DBNodeNum: the number of selected nodes. If you select **1 Read/Write + 1** **Read-only**, the number of nodes is 2. If you select **1 Read/Write**, the number of nodes is 1.
> DBNodeClass.mem: the memory size defined in the selected node specifications.
> StorageSpace: the size of the selected storage space.
> CPU overhead of hot standby storage clusters: You can enable or disable the hot standby storage cluster feature.
> If the hot standby storage cluster feature is disabled, the CPU overhead of hot standby storage clusters is 0.
> If the hot standby storage cluster feature is enabled, the CPU overhead is equal to the number of CPU cores defined in the selected node specifications.
> CPU overhead of PolarProxy: You can enable or disable the PolarProxy feature.
> If the PolarProxy feature is disabled, the CPU overhead of PolarProxy is 0.
> If the PolarProxy feature is enabled, the CPU overhead is calculated based on the following formulas:
> MySQL and PostgreSQL: CPU overhead of PolarProxy = Number of CPU cores defined in the selected cluster specifications.
> Oracle: CPU overhead of PolarProxy = Number of CPU cores defined in the selected cluster specifications × 2. By default, two replicas are used.
> Memory overhead of hot standby storage clusters: You can enable or disable the hot standby storage cluster feature.

> If the hot standby storage cluster feature is disabled, the memory overhead of hot standby storage clusters is 0.
> If the hot standby storage cluster feature is enabled, the memory overhead is equal to the memory size defined in the selected node specifications.
> Memory overhead of PolarProxy: You can enable or disable the PolarProxy feature.
> If the PolarProxy feature is disabled, the memory overhead of PolarProxy is 0.
> If the PolarProxy feature is enabled, the memory overhead is calculated based on the following formulas:
> MySQL and PostgreSQL: Memory overhead of PolarProxy = 4 GiB. This is a fixed value.
> Oracle: Memory overhead of PolarProxy = Memory size defined in the selected cluster specifications × 2. By default, two replicas are used.
> Disk overhead of hot standby storage clusters: You can enable or disable the hot standby storage cluster feature.
> If the hot standby storage cluster feature is disabled, the disk overhead of hot standby storage clusters is 0.
> If the hot standby storage cluster feature is enabled, the disk overhead is equal to the size of the selected storage space.

**Inventory source**

No inventory is involved. By default, the inventory is unlimited.

**Calculation methods of quota usage**

CU quota usage = Number of CUs that are configured for the current instance Disk quota usage = Used disk capacity of the current instance

###### 7.1.3.1.5.2 Elasticsearch on Kubernetes

This topic describes the quotas that you can configure for Elasticsearch on Kubernetes, calculation methods of quota usage, and inventory source.

**Quotas**

| Quota | Description |
|---|---|
| CPU Quota (Cores) | The total number of CPU cores that can be configured for Elasticsearch on Kubernetes. |
| Memory Quota (GiB) | The total size of memory that can be configured for Elasticsearch on Kubernetes. |
| Disk Quota (GiB) | The total storage capacity that can be configured for Elasticsearch on Kubernetes. |

**Calculation methods of quota usage**

Elasticsearch on Kubernetes includes the following types of nodes: data node, Kibana node, dedicated master node, and client node. The CPU and memory quota usage is calculated based on the number of nodes and specification-based overhead. The disk quota usage is calculated based on the number of nodes and the storage capacity of nodes. CPU or memory quota usage = nodeSpec.spec × nodeAmount + kibanaConfiguration.spec × kibanaConfiguration.amount + masterConfiguration.spec × masterConfiguration.amount + clientNodeConfiguration.spec × clientNodeConfiguration.amout Disk quota usage = nodeSpec.disk × nodeAmount + kibanaConfiguration.disk × kibanaConfiguration.amount + masterConfiguration.disk × masterConfiguration.amount + clientNodeConfiguration.disk × clientNodeConfiguration.amout

> **Note:** The specifications of a node include the number of CPU cores and the memory size. The number of CPU cores is used to calculate the CPU quota usage and the memory size is used to calculate the memory quota usage.
> nodeSpec.spec: the selected data node specifications.
> nodeAmount: the number of data nodes.
> kibanaConfiguration.spec: the selected Kibana node specifications.
> kibanaConfiguration.amount: the number of Kibana nodes.
> masterConfiguration.spec: the selected dedicated master node specifications.
> masterConfiguration.amount: the number of dedicated master nodes.
> clientNodeConfiguration.spec: the selected client node specifications.
> clientNodeConfiguration.amout: the number of client nodes.
> nodeSpec.disk: the storage capacity of the selected data node specifications.
> kibanaConfiguration.disk: the storage capacity of the selected Kibana node specifications.
> masterConfiguration.disk: the storage capacity of the selected dedicated master node specifications.
> clientNodeConfiguration.disk: the storage capacity of the selected client node specifications.

**Inventory source**

No inventory is involved. By default, the inventory is unlimited.

##### 7.1.3.3 Manage quotas

###### 7.1.3.3.1 Service resources

###### 7.1.3.3.1.1 Cloud services supported by multi-cloud quotas

**cloud quotas**

In a multi-cloud scenario, operations managers can manage resource quotas for subordinate clouds from the central cloud.

> **Important:** When you set quotas by resource pool in the central cloud console, you can only configure quotas for bound level-1 organizations in the subordinate cloud. After setting subordinate cloud quotas, the system updates them to the subordinate cloud. To manage resource set quotas for the subordinate cloud, you must configure them in the subordinate cloud console.
> When you set quotas in the subordinate cloud console, it includes quotas for managed level-1 organizations. After the subordinate cloud updates level-1 organization quotas, the central cloud displays them in real time.

**Cloud services with quota support in Apsara Stack**

When the subordinate cloud is Apsara Stack, the supported cloud services for quota configuration include all cloud services that support quotas in that Apsara Stack.

**Cloud services with quota support in Alibaba Public Cloud**

When the subordinate cloud is Alibaba Public Cloud, the supported cloud services for quota configuration are as follows.

> **Note:** The quota usage for instance count is calculated based on the actual number of instances used. The quota usage for CPU, memory, disk, and other resources is calculated by summing the corresponding fields returned by the API.

**Compute**

| Cloud service | Quota item |
|---|---|
| Elastic Compute Service (ECS) | Disk quota, basic disk, ultra disk, shared ultra disk, shared SSD, cloud SSD, I/O-intensive local disk, throughput-intensive local disk, local disk, local SSD, ESSD, high-performance disk, standard performance disk, ESSD AutoPL, ESSD Entry, elastic ephemeral disk - standard edition, custom image quota, CPU quota, security group quota, GPU quota, elastic network interface quota, memory quota |

###### 7.1.3.3.1.2 Cloud services that support group quota configuration

**quota configuration**

This topic describes the rules for group quota configuration and the cloud services that support group quota configuration.

**Configuration rules**

Group quotas are configured top-down. A parent organization must have a quota configured before you can configure quotas for its subordinate organizations. A group quota must be configured before individual quotas can be configured within that group. You can configure a group quota for a subordinate organization only after the parent organization has its group quota configured. You can configure individual quotas within a group for a subordinate organization only after the parent organization has its corresponding group quota and individual quotas configured. A group quota must be greater than or equal to the sum of its configured individual quotas. This example demonstrates disk quota configuration for Elastic Compute Service (ECS). In this example, Organization B is subordinate to Organization A. If no disk quota is configured for Organization A, you cannot configure individual quotas for SSDs, ultra disks, premium performance disks, or standard performance disks in Organization A. If no disk quota is configured for Organization A, you cannot configure a disk quota for Organization B. If no individual disk quotas are configured for SSDs, ultra disks, premium performance disks, or standard performance disks in Organization A, you cannot configure corresponding quotas in Organization B. When you configure individual disk quotas in Organization A, the sum of the quotas for SSDs, ultra disks, premium performance disks, and standard performance disks cannot exceed the total configured disk quota of Organization A.

**Supported cloud services**

Only ECS supports group quotas, specifically for disks.

| Parent resource item | Child resource item |
|---|---|
| Disk quota (GiB) | SSD (GiB) |
|   | Ultra disk (GiB) |
|   | Premium performance disk (GiB) |
|   | Standard performance disk (GiB) |

###### 7.1.3.3.1.3 Cloud services that support category quota configuration

**quota configuration**

This topic describes the rules for category quota configuration and the cloud services that support category quota configuration.

**Configuration rules**

Category quotas are configured top-down. A parent organization must have a quota configured before you can configure quotas for its subordinate organizations. You can configure individual quotas within a category for a subordinate organization only after the parent organization has its corresponding category quota and individual quotas configured. This example demonstrates category quota configuration for Bare Metal Computing Platform (BMCP). In this example, Organization B is subordinate to Organization A. If no quotas are configured for basic intelligent computing clusters such as machineA and machineB in Organization A, you cannot configure quotas for the corresponding clusters in Organization B.

**Supported cloud services**

Only Elastic Compute Service (ECS) and BMCP support category quota configuration.

**ECS**

| Parent resource item | Child resource item |
|---|---|
| Instance type | Specifications supported by the instance type. Example: ecs.sn2ne.xlarge. |

**BMCP**

| Parent resource item | Child resource item |
|---|---|
| High- performance Network Cluster | Specifications supported for a high-performance network cluster. |
| Managed Cluster | Specifications supported for a managed cluster. |
| High- performance Computing Network Cluster | Specifications supported for a high-performance computing network cluster. |
| Basic Cluster | Specifications supported for a basic cluster. |

This topic describes the cloud services that support zone-level resource quotas. When you configure a resource quota, you can select a zone. If you select all zones, you can configure resource quotas at the region level. If you select a zone, you can configure resource quotas for the zone, and the console displays only cloud services in the current zone.

| Cloud service | Resource item |

| ECS | Disk quota, SSD, ultra disk, premium performance disk, standard performance disk, memory quota, CPU quota, GPU quota, Elastic Network Interface (ENI) quota, and specification quota. |

| NAS | NAS usage, performance disk capacity, capacity disk capacity, and NAS quota. |
|---|---|

###### 7.1.3.3.1.5 Set or modify quotas for a single cloud service

**service**

Resources in a resource pool are limited. You must restrict the number of resources for each organization based on its scope of responsibilities. Quota management allows you to set or modify quotas for each cloud service in organizations and resource sets.

**Prerequisites**

Before setting quotas, ensure that the platform administrator (super) has completed the resource pool configuration. For more information, see Resource pool configuration. By default, the operations administrator and organization administrator can perform this operation. Users with custom roles require the Operate Quotas permission under Quota Management, as well as the Quota Management > Quota Management menu permission.

**Limits**

You must set the quota of the parent organization before setting the quota of a subordinate organization. Quotas must be allocated level by level. Skipping levels is not allowed. Quotas support two settings: limited and unlimited. If a quota is not explicitly set, it defaults to unlimited, allowing an organization to use all available quota from its parent organization. Resource sets and subordinate organizations under the same organization share the quota of that organization. When you set group quotas, the general rule is that you cannot set a subordinate quota unless the parent quota is set. For the specific cloud services that support group quotas, see Cloud services that support group quota configuration. You can set quota items within a group only after the group quota item is set. You can set the group quota item of a subordinate organization only after the group quota item of the parent organization is set. You can set quota items within a group of a subordinate organization only after the quota items within the group of the parent organization are set. The group quota value must be greater than or equal to the sum of the configured values of quota items within the group. When setting category quotas, the general rule is that you cannot set a subordinate quota unless the parent quota is set. You can set category quota items of a subordinate organization only after the category quota items of the parent organization are set. For the specific cloud services that support category quotas, see Cloud services that support category quota configuration. The operations administrator can set quotas for all organizations and resource sets. The organization administrator can set quotas for subordinate organizations, including resource set quotas. Setting a quota for the current organization is treated as a quota application to the parent organization. The application takes effect after approval.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top menu bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Quotas** > **Quotas**.
4. Click the **Product Resources** tab.
5. Above the organization structure on the left side of the page, select a resource pool.

> **Note:** The resource pool option appears only in multi-cloud scenarios.

6. Above the product list on the right side, set the region and zone, and select Only View
Cloud Services That Trigger Alerts.

> **Note:** If you select All Zones, you can configure quotas at the region level. If you select a zone, you can configure quotas for the zone, and the console displays only cloud services in the current zone.
> If you select **View Only Cloud Services That Have Triggered Alerts** , only the cloud services that trigger alerts are displayed.

7. In the left-side organization structure of the Quotas page, select the organization or
resource set whose resources you want to manage.
8. Click the target service (ECS in this example) to open the Quota Details panel. For more
information about the resource quotas of each cloud service, see Products that support resource quotas.
9. In the Quota Details panel, configure the quotas.

**Quota**.

###### 7.1.3.3.1.6 Set quotas in batches

The quota management feature allows you to set quotas for multiple cloud services in batches.

**Prerequisites**

Before you set quotas, make sure that the platform administrator (super) has configured the resource pool. For more information, see the **Resource pool configuration** section. By default, only operations administrators and organization administrators can perform this operation. Users with custom roles must have the Operate Quotas permission under Quota Management and the Quotas > Quotas menu permission.

**Limits**

You must set the quotas for a parent organization first before configuring quotas for its subordinate organizations. You can allocate quotas only hierarchically and cannot skip levels. Quotas support two modes: limited and unlimited. If you do not set a quota, the quota is unlimited, and the organization can consume all available quotas of its parent organization. Resource sets and subordinate organizations under the same organization share the quota of that organization. When you configure group quotas, the general rule is that you cannot configure a subordinate quota unless the parent quota is configured. For the specific cloud services that support group quotas, see Cloud services that support group quota configuration. You can configure quota items within a group only after configuring the group quota item. You can configure a subordinate group quota item only after configuring the parent group quota item. You can configure a subordinate quota item within a group only after configuring the parent quota item within the group. The group quota value must be greater than or equal to the sum of all quota item values within the group. When you configure category quotas, the general rule is that you cannot configure a subordinate quota unless the parent quota is configured. You can configure a subordinate quota item within a category only after configuring the parent quota item within the category. For the specific cloud services that support category quotas, see Cloud services that support category quota configuration. Operations administrators can set quotas for all organizations and resource sets. Organization administrators can set quotas for subordinate organizations, including resource set quotas. Setting a quota for the current organization is equivalent to applying for a quota from the parent organization. The application succeeds after approval.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Quotas** > **Quotas**.
4. Click the **Product Resources** tab.
5. Above the organization hierarchy on the left, select a resource pool.

> **Note:** The resource pool option appears only in multi-cloud scenarios.

6. Above the product list on the right, set the region, available zone, and the option to only
view cloud services that trigger alerts.

> **Note:** If you select **All Zones**, the system applies quota management at the region level. If you select a specific available zone, the system applies quota management at the available zone level and displays only the products in that zone.
> Select **Only View Cloud Services That Trigger Alerts** to quickly filter cloud services that have triggered alerts.

7. In the organization hierarchy on the left, click the target organization or resource set.
8. Set quotas in batches.
To set quotas for a subordinate organization or resource set, click **Configure Quotas**. To set quotas for the current organization, click **Apply for Quotas in Batches**.
9. In the **Configure Quotas**/**Apply for Quotas in Batches** panel, click **Add Service**.
0. In the cloud service selector, select the cloud services that you want to add.

> **Note:** After you add a cloud service, click
> next to the cloud service to switch to
> another cloud service.
> After you add a cloud service, click
> next to the cloud service to remove the
> added cloud service.

1. In the **Set Total Quota** column, enter a quota value to set the quota for each added cloud
service.
**Set Total Quota**: If left empty, the system does not set this item, which means
the quota is unlimited.
**Existing Quota**: Displays the current quota settings.
**Quota Change**: Displays the specific adjustment between the new total quota
and the original quota.

> Click
> before a resource item to expand its sub-resource items.
> Use a quota template to set quotas quickly.
> In the **Quota Template** drop-down list, select a quota template. The system clears existing configurations, calculates values based on the template rules, and fills in the new configurations If a resource item is not set in the quota template, the system retains the existing configuration for that item.
> Click **Restore** next to **Quota Template** to revert to the configuration before applying the quota template.

2. Click **OK**.
3. In the **Do you want to save the content?** dialog box, click **OK**.
4. (Optional) When applying for quotas for the current organization, you must also submit the
application for approval. i. After you save the quota application for the current organization, complete the information in the **Process Information Supplement** dialog box.
**Execution Method After Approval**: Select **Automatic Execution** or **Manual**
**Execution**.
**Automatic Execution**: The system automatically performs the service operation
after approval.
**Manual Execution**: After approval, you must go to the application form details page
and manually perform the service operation.
**Operation Reason**: Enter the reason for the operation.
ii. Click **Submit for Approval**. iii. In the **Operation Succeeded** dialog box, click **Close** or **Application Form Details**.

##### 7.1.3.4 Quota alert management

###### 7.1.3.4.1 Create a quota alert rule

The system provides a default alert rule for each product service. The rule is named after the product code, applies to all organizations and resource sets, and belongs to the root organization. You can create a new alert rule when the preset alert rule does not meet your requirements. Quota alerts support notifications. When the quota of an organization or resource set reaches the preset threshold, the system notifies the organization administrator or resource set administrator. The system sends the notification once a day upon the first trigger of each day.

**Prerequisites**

The default operator is the operations administrator or organization administrator.

**Limits**

You cannot create a new alert rule for the current organization or resource set if an enabled alert rule already exists. A newly created alert rule takes effect immediately and disables all other alert rules within its effective scope.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the menu bar, select **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Quotas** > **Quota Alerts**.
4. On the **Quota Alerts** page, click **Create Alert Rule**.
5. In the **Create Alert Rule** dialog box, complete the configuration.

| Configuration item |   | Description |
|---|---|---|
|   | Resource Pool | Select the resource pool where the current quota alert rule takes effect. Note The resource pool drop-down list appears only in multi-cloud scenarios. |
|   | Rule Type | Select Product Resources or AI Service Token. |
|   | Organizatio n/Resource Set | Select the organization or resource set where the current quota alert rule takes effect. |

| Alert Rule Informatio n |   |   |
|---|---|---|
|   | Include Child Organizatio ns | Enable or disable the option to include subordinate organizations. When enabled, the effective scope of the alert rule covers the current organization and all subordinate organizations, as well as all resource sets within the scope. This option appears only when you select an organization for Organization/Resource Set. : Include subordinate organizations. : Do not include subordinate organizations. |
|   | Region | Select the region where the current quota alert rule takes effect. |
|   | Cloud Service | Select the cloud service for which you want to create the alert rule. Important You can select only cloud services that have quotas in the current organization or resource set. |
| Alert Informatio n | Alert Rule Name | Enter a name for the current quota alert rule. |
|   | Alert Type | Used Amount: The system triggers an alert when the used quota exceeds the configured alert threshold. Remaining Available Quota: The system triggers an alert when the remaining quota falls below the configured alert threshold. |
|   | Alert Threshold | Resource Type: The default value is the resource item that has a configured quota for the selected cloud service. Used Amount/Quota: The default values are the used quota and the quota of the cloud service in the selected organization and resource set. Threshold: You can select No, Percentage, or Number. Alert Threshold: Set the alert threshold value. The system generates an alert when the used quota exceeds the alert threshold or the remaining quota falls below the alert threshold. When you set Threshold to No, the default value for this item is No Alerts. |

6. Click **OK**.

In the Modify Quota Alert Rule dialog box, modify the configurations of the quota alert rule. #### 7.1.4 Tag management

##### 7.1.4.1 Manage tags

Tags are used to classify and manage resources from different dimensions. You can add tags to cloud resources to manage the resources in a finer-grained and more intelligent manner.

**Background information**

Each tag consists of a tag key and a tag value. A tag key is the core identification part of a tag. It is used to define the resource category or describe resource attributes. In most cases, the tag key is a short and descriptive string. Each tag key added to a resource must be unique. A tag value refers to the content that is associated with a tag key and provides more details of a resource. Administrators can define various types of tags based on business requirements and add multiple tag keys and corresponding tag values to cloud resources. This way, you can classify and retrieve resources from different dimensions. This helps you quickly find the resources that you require from a large amount of resources and facilitates cloud resource management.

**Limits**

You can create at most 20 tags at a time and add the tags to resources. You can select at most 50 resource instances at a time when you add tags to resources.

**Create or select tags and add the tags to resources**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Tags** > **Tag**.
4. On the **Tag** page, click **Create or Select Tags and Add Them to Resources**.
5. In the **Create or Select Tags and Add Them to Resources** dialog box, configure
parameters in the following steps as prompted. i. **Create or Select Tags** Select an existing tag key or create a tag key, enter a tag value in the **Tag Value** field, and then click **Next**.

> **Note:** In the Create or Select Tags step, you can create multiple tags at a time.
> You can click **Add** to create or select more tags.
> You can click the
> icon that corresponds to a tag to delete or remove the tag.

ii. **Select a Resource** Select the organization and resource set to which the resources belong, region, and cloud services, and click **Next**. iii. **Confirmation Information** Confirm the information about the tags and resources and click **Confirm**.

**View resources to which tags are added**

1. In the left-side **Tag Key** pane of the **Tag** page, find the tag key that you want to view.
You can click the icon next to Tag Key to specify filter conditions in the **Filter**
**Conditions** dialog box. The filter conditions include the organization and resource set to
which resources belong, the region in which resources reside, and keyword.

> **Note:** The number next to Tag Key indicates the total number of tag keys.
> In the tag key list, the number next to each tag key indicates the number of tag values that correspond to the tag key.

2. Click the tag key that you want to view. In the right-side Tag Key section, view the tag
values that correspond to the tag key and the cloud services to which the tag is added.

> **Note:** In the right-side Tag Key section, you can click **Add Tag Value** to add one or more tag values to the tag key.
> In the tag value list, you can view the number of cloud services to which each tag is added.

3. View the resources to which a tag is added.
i. Find the tag value that you want to view and click the icon next to the tag value to view the cloud services to which the tag is added. ii. Find the cloud service resource type that you want to view and click the number next to it to view the resources to which the tag is added. Alternatively, click **View Resources** in the **Actions** column of the tag value. In the panel that appears, select a cloud service to view the resources to which the tag is added.

> **Note:** You can select multiple resource instances and click **Unbind Current Tags** or **Bind** **Multiple Tags** below the resource instance list to unbind the current tags from or bind other tags to the resource instances at a time.

4. Optional. In the tag value list, find the tag value that you want to manage and click **Bind**
**Resources** in the **Actions** column. In the panel that appears, select the resources to which
you want to add the tag and click **Submit**.

##### 7.1.4.2 Policy library

A tag policy defines standardized tag rules to ensure that all tags added to resources meet unified requirements. The tag policy can be applied to organizations, resource sets, cloud services, or instances. It can define the valid tag keys and tag values.

###### 7.1.4.2.1 Create a tag policy

When creating a tag policy, you can restrict the effective scope of the policy by resource type, resource set, excluded resource ID, region, and tag scope.

**Prerequisites**

By default, the operations administrator and organization administrator can perform this operation. Users with custom organization-scoped roles must have the Create Tag Policy permission under Tag Management and the Tag Management > Policy Library menu permission.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Tags** > **Policy Library**.
4. Click **Create Tag Policy**.
5. On the **Create Tag Policy** page, configure the tag policy.

| Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|

| Basi c Info rma tion | Organ izatio n | Select the organization to which the tag policy belongs. |
|---|---|---|
|   | Policy Name | Enter a name for the tag policy. The policy name can contain digits, letters, and underscores ( ), and must be 1 to 128 characters in length. _ |
|   | Policy Descri ption | Enter a description for the tag policy. The description must be 0 to 512 characters in length. |
| Poli cy Info rma tion | Quick Entry | Under Resources Automatically Inherit Tags from Resource Sets, select a policy scenario, and then specify the tag key and resource scope. Select Policy Scenario: The system currently supports the Resources Automatically Inherit Tags from Resource Sets and Add Tag with Specified Tag Value to Resources scenarios. Resources Automatically Inherit Tags from Resource Sets: When a resource set binds to a specified tag, the resources in the set automatically inherit that tag from the resource set. Add Tag with Specified Tag Value to Resources: The system automatically binds the specified tag to the resources within the resource scope. Tag Key: Select a tag key from the Tag Key drop-down list. You can select only one tag key. If you select Resources Automatically Inherit Tags from Resource Sets as the policy scenario: After you select a tag key, clickV iew Resource Sets Bound to This Tag Key to view the resource sets that already bind to this tag key. Note When a resource set binds to this tag key (including resource sets that bind to this tag key after the policy takes effect), the resources in the resource set automatically inherit the tag from the resource set and follow any subsequent changes to the tag. When a resource set unbinds from this tag, the system does not automatically delete the tags that the resources have already inherited. If you select Add Tag with Specified Tag Value to Resources as the policy scenario: After you select a tag key, add tag values under Specify Allowed Tag Values. This tag key allows only the specified values. You can use one wildcard character (*) per tag value, for example, *e***@mail.com. Resource Scope: Set the resource scope for this tag policy. Specify Resource Types to Be Checked for Tag Key: The tag policy checks only the specified resource types. If you do not select any resource type, the policy checks all resource types by default. Specify Resource Set Scope: Set the resource sets that inherit tag values for this tag key. You can select only resource sets that already bind to this tag key. |

|   |   | Specify IDs of Resources to Be Excluded: The specified resource IDs are excluded from the policy and do not inherit this tag key from the resource set. You can specify up to 20 resource IDs. Specify Region Scope: Set the region scope to check for this tag key. If you do not select any region, the policy checks all regions by default. You can specify up to 20 regions. Specify Tag Scope: Set the tag scope to check for this tag key. Multiple tags use the AND logical relationship. You can specify up to 20 tags. Automatically Correct: Specify a tag key for remediation. The system applies the corresponding specified tag to the non-compliant resources detected during the check. Note This option is available only when you select Add Tag with Specified Tag Value to Resources as the policy scenario. |
|---|---|---|

6. Click **Create**.

###### 7.1.4.2.2 View tag policies

On the Policy Library page, you can view tag policies and the details of each tag policy.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator, a resource auditor, an organization administrator, or an organization resource auditor. If you are assigned a custom role that is authorized to manage organizations, the custom role must be granted permissions to view tag policies and access the Policy Library page in the Tags module.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Tags** > **Policy Library**.
4. View information about existing tag policies. You can quickly search for tag policies by
organization, policy ID, policy name, and tag key.
5. Find the tag policy that you want to view and click its name or **Details** in the **Actions**
column to go to the policy details page. Then, view the details of the tag policy.
6. Optional. Click **View Effective Policy and Check Tasks** on the details page of the tag
policy to go to the details page of the effective policy. You can perform this step if the tag policy is enabled. For more information, see Effective policies.

###### 7.1.4.2.3 Edit a tag policy

You can modify a tag policy when the policy changes.

**Prerequisites**

The tag policy is in the **Disabled** status. By default, only the operations administrators and organization administrators can perform this operation. Users with custom organization-scoped roles require the Edit and Delete Tag Policies permission under Tag Management and the Tags > Policy Library menu permission.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Tags** > **Policy Library**.
4. In the list, click **Modify** in the **Actions** column of the target policy.
5. On the **Modify Tag Policy** page, update the policy configuration. For more information on
the configuration items, see Create a tag policy.
6. Click **Modify**.

###### 7.1.4.2.4 Enable a tag policy

After a disabled tag policy is enabled, the system checks the compliance of resource tags and automatically executes related rules based on the tag policy. When you enable a tag policy, the effective policy with the same policy type and tag key as the tag policy is updated. If no such effective policy exists in the current organization, a new effective policy is created.

**Prerequisites**

The tag policy is in the **Paused** state. You are an operations administrator or an organization administrator. If you are assigned a custom role that is authorized to manage organizations, the custom role must be granted permissions to modify and delete tag policies and access the Policy Library page in the Tags module.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Tags** > **Policy Library**.
4. On the Policy Library page, find the tag policy that you want to enable and click **Enable** in
the **Actions** column.
5. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

> **Note:** After you enable a tag policy, the tag policy applies to resources within the specified scope.
> The tag configured in the tag policy is automatically added to new resources after they are created.
> The tag configured in the tag policy is automatically added to existing resources.

###### 7.1.4.2.5 Disable a tag policy

After an enabled tag policy is disabled, the system no longer checks the compliance of resource tags or automatically executes related rules based on the tag policy. When you disable a tag policy, the effective policy with the same policy type and tag key as the tag policy is updated. If the tag policy is the only one associated with the effective policy, the effective policy is deleted after the tag policy is disabled.

**Prerequisites**

The tag policy is in the **Enabled** state. You are an operations administrator or an organization administrator. If you are assigned a custom role that is authorized to manage organizations, the custom role must be granted permissions to modify and delete tag policies and access the Policy Library page in the Tags module.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Tags** > **Policy Library**.
4. On the Policy Library page, find the tag policy that you want to disable and click **Disable** in
the **Actions** column.
5. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

###### 7.1.4.2.6 Delete a tag policy

You can delete tag policies that you no longer require.

**Prerequisites**

The tag policy is in the **Paused** state. You are an operations administrator or an organization administrator. If you are assigned a custom role that is authorized to manage organizations, the custom role must be granted permissions to modify and delete tag policies and access the Policy Library page in the Tags module.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Tags** > **Policy Library**.
4. On the Policy Library page, find the tag policy that you want to delete and click **Delete** in
the **Actions** column.
5. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

##### 7.1.4.3 Effective policies

An effective policy is obtained by aggregating multiple tag policies.

###### 7.1.4.3.1 View effective policies

After tag policies are enabled, they are aggregated by tag key and policy type and displayed on the Effective Policy page. If multiple tag policies of the same policy type share a tag key, the effective scope of the effective policy depends on the order in which the tag policies are enabled. If the effective scopes of the tag policies conflict, the effective scope of the earliest enabled tag policy prevails.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator, a resource auditor, an organization administrator, or an organization resource auditor. If you are assigned a custom role that is authorized to manage organizations, the custom role must be granted permissions to view effective policies and access the Effective Policy page in the Tags module.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Tags** > **Effective Policy**.
4. View effective policies on the Effective Policy page. You can quickly search for effective
policies by tag key and policy type.
5. Find the effective policy that you want to view and click **Details** in the **Actions** column to
go to the details page of the effective policy. Then, view the details of the effective policy.
**Basic Information**: View the basic information about the tag policy whose binding order
is 1.
**Relevant Policies**: On the **Relevant Policies** tab, view the information about the tag
policies that are associated with the effective policy in the following columns: **Policy ID**,
**Policy Name**, **Binding Order**, and **Bound At**.

> **Note:** You can find the tag policy that you want to view and click its ID or **Details** in the **Actions** column to go to the details page of the tag policy.
> You can find the tag policy that you want to modify and click **Modify** in the **Actions** column to go to the **Modify Tag Policy** page. On the Modify Tag Policy page, you can update the tag policy.

**Detection Results**: On the **Detection Results** tab, view the detection results and fix
tags of non-compliant resources. You can view the detection results in the following sections: **Detected Resources**, **Compliant Resources**, **Non-compliant Resources**,
**Inapplicable Resources**, and **Non-compliant Resources/Percentage**.

> **Note:** **Compliant**: The specified tag keys are added to the resources and resource sets to which the resources belong.

**Non-compliant**: The specified tag keys are not added to the resources. Tags
of non-compliant resources can be manually fixed. For more information, see Manage effective policies.

> **Inapplicable**: The specified tag keys are not added to the resource sets to which the resources belong. For example, the specified tags are removed from a resource set.

**Fix Records**: On the **Fix Records** tab, view the details of the automatic fix records.

###### 7.1.4.3.2 Manage effective policies

You can manually fix the tags of non-compliant resources.

**Prerequisites**

Resources are in the **Non-compliance** state. You are an operations administrator or an organization administrator. If you are assigned a custom role that is authorized to manage organizations, the custom role must be granted permissions to manage effective policies and access the Effective Policy page in the Tags module.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Tags** > **Effective Policy**.
4. On the Effective Policy page, find the effective policy that you want to manage and click
**Details** in the **Actions** column.
5. On the details page of the effective policy, click the **Detection Results** tab. On the
Detection Results tab, manually fix non-compliant resources in the **Fix Non-compliant**
**Resources** section. You can select **Non-compliance** from the Compliance Status drop-
down list to search for non-compliant resources.

| Operat ion | Procedure |
|---|---|
| Fix the tags of a single non- compli ant resour ce | i. Find the non-compliant resource whose tags you want to fix and clickF ix in the Actions column. ii. In the Fix Tags dialog box, enter a new tag value in the tag value field and clickO K. iii. After the resource tags are fixed, click OK. |

| Fix the tags of multipl e resour ces at a time | i. In the resource list, select multiple non-compliant resources. ii. Click Batch Fix below the resource list. iii. In the Fix Tags dialog box, enter a new tag value in the tag value field and clickO K. iv. After the resource tags are fixed, click OK. |
|---|---|
