#### 7.1.5 Metering management

##### 7.1.5.1 Metering configuration management

###### 7.1.5.1.1 Create a metering table

This topic describes how to create a metering table for a cloud service. You can customize metering rules and metering fields in a metering table to generate new metering data in order to meet operations needs.

**Prerequisites**

The switch controlling metering table creation is turned on. Contact O&M personnel if you need to turn on this switch. You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Metering** > **Metering Configuration**
**Management**.
4. On the **Metering Configuration Management** page, select cloud product resources from
the **Resources** drop-down list.
5. Then, click the card of the resource to go to metering configuration details page.
6. On the **Metering table** tab, click **Create Metering Table**.
7. In the **Create Metering Table** panel, configure the metering parameters.

| Parameter |   | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Basic Informa tion | Metering Table Name | Enter the name of the metering table. |
|   | Metering Table Description | Enter the description of the metering table. |
|   | Metering Cycle | Select the cycle of metering data generation. You can select Hours, Days, Month, or Year. The metering cycle must be greater than or equal to the push cycle. Hours: A metering data entry is generated every hour. Days: A metering data entry is generated every day. Month: A metering data entry is generated every month. Year: A metering data entry is generated every year. |
|   | Push Cycle | The cycle of metering data pushes. By default, the push cycle is same as that of the predefined metering table and cannot be modified. |
| Document Ve | rsion: 20260902 64 |   |

|   | Metering Dimension | Select a metering dimension. You can select Instance or Resource Set. |
|---|---|---|
| Metering Field |   | Add metering fields: a. Click Add Metering Field above the metering field list. b. In the Add Field panel, configure metering fields. For more information, see Configure metering fields. c. Click OK. View metering fields: a. In the metering field list, you can view predefined and custom metering fields. b. Click View in the Operations column of a metering field to open the View Details panel. In the panel, you can view the basic information, metering information, and metering rules of the metering field. Modify a metering field: Important You cannot modify predefined metering fields. If the metering table is enabled, you cannot modify the metering fields in the table. a. In the metering field list, click Modify in the Operations column of a custom metering field. b. In the Edit Field panel, modify the metering field configuration. For more information, see Configure metering fields. c. Click OK. Delete a metering field: Important You cannot delete predefined metering fields. If the metering table is enabled, you cannot delete the metering fields in the table. a. In the metering field list, find click Delete in the Operations column of a custom metering field. b. In the message that appears, click OK. |

8. Click **OK**.

**Configure metering fields**

###### 7.1.5.1.2 Modify a metering table

This topic describes how to modify the basic information and metering fields of a metering table.

**Prerequisites**

You have logged in to the console as an operations administrator. The status of the custom metering table to be modified is **Draft**.

**Limits**

You can modify only custom metering tables.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Metering** > **Metering Configuration**
**Management**.
4. On the **Metering Configuration Management** page, select cloud product resources from
the **Resources** drop-down list.
5. Then, click the card of the resource to go to metering configuration details page.
6. On the **Draft** tab of the **Metering Table** page, click **Configure** in the **Operations** column
of a custom metering table.
7. In the **Modify Metering Table** panel, modify the basic information and metering fields of
the metering table.
8. Click **OK**.

###### 7.1.5.1.3 View metering tables

View preset or custom metering tables for product metering resources. Metering tables created by third-party products in product management also appear here.

**Prerequisites**

The operating user defaults to the Operations Administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the menu, select **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Metering** > **Metering Configuration**
**Management**.
4. On the **Metering Configuration Management** page, from the **Resource** drop-down list,
select a cloud service resource.
5. Click a resource card to enter its metering configuration details.
6. Under **Metering Table**, on the **Published** or **Draft** tab, click **View** in the **Actions** column.

> **Note:** The Published tab displays published metering tables. Preset metering tables are **Enabled** by default and appear under the **Published** tab.
> The Draft tab displays draft metering tables.

7. In the **Meter Details** panel, view the detailed information of this metering table.

###### 7.1.5.1.4 Enable a metering table

After you enable a metering table in the Draft state, the enabled metering table generates corresponding metering tasks based on the metering cycle.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator. The custom-type metering table is in the **Draft** or **Disable** state.

**Limits**

Only custom-type metering tables can be enabled. Under the same product metering resource, only one custom-type metering table can be enabled.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Metering Management** > **Metering**
**Configuration Management**.
4. On the **Metering Configuration Management** page, select cloud product resources from
the **Resources** drop-down list.
5. Click the resource card to go to the metering configuration details page of the resource.
6. On the **Published** or **Draft** tab of the **Metering Table** tab, find the meter table that you
want to manage and click **Enable** in the **Operations** column.
7. In the dialog box that appears, click **OK**.

###### 7.1.5.1.5 Disable a metering table

You can disable an enabled metering table. A disabled metering table does not trigger metering tasks for the next metering cycle but does not affect existing tasks.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator. The custom-type metering table is in the **Enable** state.

**Limits**

Only custom-type metering tables can be disabled.

**Usage notes**

> **Important:** After a metering table is disabled, if it is later enabled again, some metering data may be missing and cannot be replenished.

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Metering Management** > **Metering**
**Configuration Management**.
4. On the **Metering Configuration Management** page, select cloud product resources from
the **Resources** drop-down list.
5. Click the resource card to go to the metering configuration details page of the resource.
6. On the **Published** tab of the **Metering Table** tab, find the meter table that you want to
manage and click **Disable** in the **Operations** column.
7. In the dialog box that appears, click **OK**.

###### 7.1.5.1.6 Clone a metering table

By cloning an existing metering table, you can quickly create a new metering table, which significantly improves efficiency and reduces repetitive work.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator. The custom-type metering table is in the **Enable** or **Disable** state.

**Limits**

Only custom-type metering tables can be cloned.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Metering Management** > **Metering**
**Configuration Management**.
4. On the **Metering Configuration Management** page, select cloud product resources from
the **Resources** drop-down list.
5. Click the resource card to go to the metering configuration details page of the resource.
6. On the **Published** tab of the **Metering Table** tab, find the meter table that you want to
manage and click **Clone** in the **Operations** column.
7. In the **Clone** panel, update the basic information and metering fields of the metering table.
8. Click **OK**. After the metering table is cloned, it is in the Draft state by default and is
displayed in the list on the Draft tab.

###### 7.1.5.1.7 Delete a metering table

This topic describes how to delete a custom metering table.

**Prerequisites**

You have logged in to the console as an operations administrator. The status of the custom metering table to be deleted is **Draft**.

**Limits**

You can delete only custom metering tables.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Metering** > **Metering Configuration**
**Management**.
4. On the **Metering Configuration Management** page, select cloud product resources from
the **Resources** drop-down list.
5. Then, click the card of the resource to go to metering configuration details page.
6. On the **Draft** tab of the **Metering Table** page, find the metering table that you want to
delete and click **Delete** in the **Operations** column.
7. Click **OK**.

###### 7.1.5.1.8 Create a draft based on an existing metering table

**metering table**

You can create a metering table in the Draft state based on an existing metering table. This creates a new version of the metering table. If the draft is enabled, a new version of the metering table is generated.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator. The custom-type metering table is in the **Enable** or **Disable** state.

**Limits**

Only custom-type metering tables support creating drafts.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Metering Management** > **Metering**
**Configuration Management**.
4. On the **Metering Configuration Management** page, select cloud product resources from
the **Resources** drop-down list.
5. Click the resource card to go to the metering configuration details page of the resource.
6. On the **Published** tab of the **Metering Table** tab, find the meter table that you want to
manage and click **Create Draft** in the **Operations** column.
7. In the **Create Draft** dialog box, enter a description.
8. Click **OK**. After the draft is created, the new version of the metering table is displayed in
the list on the Draft tab.

###### 7.1.5.1.9 View published version records of a metering table

**metering table**

You can view the published version records of a metering table to understand its historical changes, which helps troubleshoot issues.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator. The custom-type metering table is in the **Enable** or **Disable** state.

**Limits**

You can view version records only for custom-type metering tables.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Metering Management** > **Metering**
**Configuration Management**.
4. On the **Metering Configuration Management** page, select cloud product resources from
the **Resources** drop-down list.
5. Click the resource card to go to the metering configuration details page of the resource.
6. On the **Published** tab of the **Metering Table** tab, find the meter table that you want to
manage and click **Versions** in the **Operations** column.
7. In the **Published Versions** panel, view the version record information of the metering
table. The latest version is displayed at the top.

| Related operations | Description |
|---|---|
| View details of a specific version of a metering table | Click View in the Operations column of the version records list. |

| Create a draft based on a specific version of a metering table | i. Click Create Draft in the Operations column of the version records list. ii. In the Create Draft dialog box, enter a description. iii. Click OK. |
|---|---|
| Clone a specific version of a metering table | i. Click Clone in the Operations column of the version records list. ii. In the Clone dialog box, update the basic information and metering fields. iii. Click OK. |

###### 7.1.5.1.10 View metering data push

This topic describes how to view the metering data push in each metering cycle of a cloud service.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Metering** > **Metering Configuration**
**Management**.
4. On the **Metering Configuration Management** page, select a cloud service resource from
the **Resources** drop-down list.
5. Click the card of the resource to go to the metering configuration details page.
6. Click the **Metering Data Push** tab.
7. View the details of metering data push in each metering cycle.

> **Note:** The total number of abnormal metering cycles to be processed is displayed above the list.
> You can configure the **Status** and **Metering Cycle** parameters above the list to find metering data push records.
> For records in the **Uncompleted** state, you can click **View Details**, **Retry**, or **Cancel** in the Actions column.
> For records in the **Processing** state, no operation is supported.
> For records in the **Completed** or **Canceled** state, you can click **View** **Details** in the Actions column.

8. Click **View Details** in the **Actions** column of a metering cycle to view the metering data
push details.

| Section | Description |
|---|---|
| Basic Informa tion | The Basic Information section displays the following metering data push information: Product, Resources, Status, Description, and Metering Cycle. |
| Meterin g Data Push Progres s | The metering data push progress includes Obtain Metering Data and Audit Metering Data. Obtain Metering Data: If metering data is obtained, click the icon to show metering data push details. You can view metering details by Organization, Resource Set, Region, and Instance ID. Audit Metering Data: If the metering data audit fails, click the icon to view Affected Data Example. |

###### 7.1.5.1.11 View alert records of metering data

The Alert Records tab displays the alert rules and alert records of cloud service metering data.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Metering** > **Metering Configuration**
**Management**.
4. On the **Metering Configuration Management** page, select a cloud service resource from
the **Resources** drop-down list.
5. Click the card of the resource to go to the metering configuration details page.
6. Click the **Alert Records** tab.
7. View alert records. Alert records are displayed in reverse chronological order. The latest
alert record is displayed at the top.
8. Optional. Click **Alert Rules** to view the details of the alert rules.

###### 7.1.5.2.2 View and export usage statistics details

On the Metering Details page, you can view resource usage statistics. The information and metering changes of resource instances are recorded at a granularity of one hour or one second. This topic describes how to view and export the details of resource usage statistics.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Metering** > **Metering Details**.
4. On the Metering Details page, click the **Hourly Details** or **Second-level Details** tab.
**Hourly Details**: Resource usage statistics are recorded at a granularity of one hour.
**Second-level Details**: Resource usage statistics are recorded at a granularity of one
second.
5. On the **Hourly Details** or **Second-level Details** tab, click Advanced Filter, configure filter
conditions such as **Cloud Platform**, **Organization**, **Resource Set**, **Resources**, **Metering**
**Table**, **Region**, **Time: (UTC±HH:MM)**, and **Instance ID**, and then click **Search**.

> **Note:** The Cloud Platform parameter is displayed in filter conditions and the metering details list only in multi-cloud environments. Based on the cloud platform that you select, the metering details list displays the resource usage statistics of cloud services in Apsara Stack Multi-Enterprise Cloud Edition and the Alibaba Cloud public cloud.
> The Metering Table parameter is displayed only on the Hourly Details tab.

6. View the details of resource usage statistics in the list.

**Hourly Details**

**Second-level Details**

7. Click the
icon in the upper-right corner to export the resource usage statistics as an
**.xlsx** file to your computer.

> **Note:** You can view or export up to 1,000 entries of resource usage statistics in the console. If you want to view or export more resource usage statistics, you can call the MeteringQuery operation.

#### 7.1.6 Product management

##### 7.1.6.1 Product management

The product management feature supports centralized access to custom services and provides service operations capabilities in internal operations control and resale scenarios.

###### 7.1.6.1.1 Add product category

The top-level product category represents the cloud platform type. It includes system-preset and custom types. System-preset top-level categories include "Apsara Stack" and "Public Cloud". Platform administrators can add custom top-level categories in Configuration > Native Hybrid Cloud > Cloud Platform Type Management. When you add a product category, you can create level 1 and level 2 categories under the top-level category. These correspond to the two-tier menu for products.

**Prerequisites**

By default, the operating user is an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager management console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Product Management** > **Product Management**.
4. On the **Product Management** page, click **Add Category**.
5. In the **Add Category** dialog box, configure the product category.

| Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|

| Product Parent Class | You can select a top-level category or a level 1 category as the parent class. If you select a top-level category as the parent class, the system adds a level 1 category under this category. If you select a level 1 category as the parent class, the system adds a level 2 category under this category. |
|---|---|
| Product Category Name | Enter the name of the product category that you want to add. |

6. Click **Confirm**.

###### 7.1.6.1.2 Edit product category

Update the name when a custom product category changes.

**Prerequisites**

The operating user is an operations administrator by default.

**Limits**

You can edit only the names of custom level 1 and level 2 categories. You cannot edit preset product categories. Top-level categories represent cloud platform types. You cannot edit them on the Product Management page. For more information, see Cloud platform type management.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Product Management** > **Product Management**.
4. On the **Product Management** page, move the pointer over the product category name
and click .

> **Note:** Enter a category name in the search box above the product category structure to quickly find the category.

5. In the **Edit Category** dialog box, update the product category name.

> **Note:** When you update the name of a level 1 or level 2 category, the parent category information appears and you cannot edit it.

6. Click **Confirm**.

###### 7.1.6.1.3 Delete a product category

You can delete a custom product category when it is no longer needed.

**Prerequisites**

No products exist under the custom product category. The current user must be an operations administrator by default.

**Limits**

You cannot delete preset product categories. Top-level categories represent cloud platform types. You cannot edit them on the product management page. For more information, see Cloud platform type management.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Product Management** > **Product Management**.
4. On the **Product Management** page, hover over the name of the custom product category
and click .

> **Note:** Enter a category name in the search box above the category tree to quickly locate the category.
> Before you delete a product category, delete its child categories first, then delete the parent category.

5. Click OK.

###### 7.1.6.1.4 Add a product

After you complete adding service categories, you can add services under secondary service categories.

**Prerequisites**

The current user must be an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Product Management** > **Product Management**.
4. On the **Product Management** page, click **Add Products** above the list.
5. In the **Add Products** dialog box, configure the service.

| Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|
| Product category | Select the category to which the service belongs. You can selectS oftware Products, Hardware Products, or Offline Products. |
| Category | Select the category to which the service belongs. The first column indicates the cloud platform type (that is, the top-level category). The second column indicates the name of the secondary category. |
| Service provider | Select the service provider to which the service belongs. |
| Product code (unique code) | Enter a product code. The code must be 2 to 20 characters in length and can contain lowercase letters and hyphens (-). It must start and end with a letter. Do not start your input with "custom-". The system automatically prepends "custom-" after the service is created. |
| Product display name | Enter a display name for the service. The name must be 2 to 30 characters in length. It must start with a letter and end with a letter or digit. It can contain underscores ( ) and hyphens (-). _ |

| Product description | Enter a description for the product. |
|---|---|

6. Click **OK**.

###### 7.1.6.1.5 Edit service

Update the service information when it changes.

**Prerequisites**

The service is in the **Not put on shelves** state. The operating user defaults to an Operations Administrator.

**Constraints**

You cannot edit preset services.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Service Management** > **Service Management**.
4. On the **Service Management** page, click a service category on the left.
5. Under the selected category, click **Edit** in the **Actions** column for the target service.

> **Note:** To quickly find a service, enter its name in the search box above the service list.

6. In the **Edit Product** dialog box, update the service configuration.

> **Note:** You cannot modify the service provider or service code when updating the configuration.

7. Click **OK**.

###### 7.1.6.1.6 Publish a service

This topic describes how to publish a service. You can use a service only after it is published.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Limits**

The resource type for a service must be published before you publish the service. After the resource type is published, the service is automatically published. For more information about how to publish a resource type, see Publish a resource type.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Product Management** > **Product Management**.
4. Publish a service.

| Operati on | Description |

| psara Uni-ma |   |   |

For example, the structure of a single Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) instance information is as follows (simplified version): Set the attribute recognition location of the VPC name to VpcName. Set the attribute recognition location of the IPv6 CIDR block to Ipv6CidrBlocks.Ipv6CidrBlock[*].Ipv6Isp. Set the attribute recognition location of the associated vSwitch to VSwitchIds.VSwitchId. { "VpcName": "test", "Ipv6CidrBlocks": { "Ipv6CidrBlock": [ { "Ipv6Isp": "BGP", "Ipv6CidrBlock": "****:****:2:48::/61" } ] }, "Description": "", "CidrBlock": "172.*.*.*/12", "Status": "Available", "VSwitchIds": { "VSwitchId": [ "vsw-pb4a3h8dx2q9e4f1r****", "vsw-pb4g86up0q0f9jcoq****", "vsw-pb48jvsg77a2cjnyf****" ] } } |
|---|---|
| Display Control | Select the display control format for the attribute. When Field Type is set to Character type, select Single line text or Multi- line text as the display control. When Field Type is set to Numerical, select Single line text as the display control. When the Field Type is set to Enumerated type, select Multi-select or Single-select as the display control. When the Field Type is set to Boolean, select Switch as the display control. |

| Attribute value source | When Field Type is set to Enumerated type, you must configure the source of attribute values. You can select Custom enumeration values, Interface, or Resource list. You can add entries, delete entries, and adjust the order of entries. **Quota management**

On the **Quota Management** page, integrate quotas and configure quota information.

| Configuration item |   | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Quota Settings | Enable quota managemen t | Specify whether to enable quota management. Once it is disabled, the system assumes that this resource type does not require quota management, and inventory management has no limits by default. |
|   | Inventory Acquisition Rules | After you enable quota management, configure this parameter. You can select Interface acquisition or Manual configuration. |
|   | Interface call key | When you select Interface acquisition for Inventory Acquisition Rules, enter the authentication key for calling the inventory interface. |
|   | Interface call address | When you select Interface acquisition for Inventory Acquisition Rules, enter the address for calling the inventory interface. |
| Interface parameter configuration |   | When you select Interface acquisition for Inventory Acquisition Rules, configure this item. This specifies the request parameters when you call the interface. |

| Quota Item Configuration | After you enable quota management, configure settings related to quota items. Interface parameter mapping and configuration change parameter mapping are optional. All other items are required. Resource type allows you to select all resource types under the product of the current operation. Quotas may require cross- resource type validation. Quota items support all custom resource items and resource items configured in specifications for the selected resource type. The system manages these items as quota items. Quota unit indicates the unit of a quota item. Interface parameter mapping indicates the filter condition in the inventory interface response that corresponds to this quota item. For example, if the current quota item is Cpu and the inventory interface returns the following inventory data, where "cpu type" _ represents the physical inventory of Cpu, set this item to cpu type. _ [{"metric":"cpu type","total":100}, _ {"metric":"disk","total":1000}] If you select Manual configuration for Inventory Acquisition Rules or the quota item cannot obtain inventory information from the interface, you can directly enter an integer as its physical inventory. You can also leave it blank to indicate no physical inventory limit. If multiple resources configure this quota item and all configure interface parameter mapping, the system retrieves physical inventory multiple times. The final displayed physical inventory is the cumulative value. Creation parameter mapping indicates the parameter name of this quota item in the create interface request. For example, if the current quota item is Cpu and the create interface request is as follows, where "CpuCost" represents the Cpu cost, set this item to CpuCost. {"CpuCost":100, "Description":"test"} Configuration change parameter mapping indicates the parameter name of this quota item after configuration change in the configuration change interface request. For example, if the current quota item is Cpu and the configuration change interface request is as follows, where "NewCpuCost" represents the cost of Cpu after the configuration change, configure this item as NewCpuCost. {"NewCpuCost":100, "Description":"test"} Deduction parameter mapping indicates the parameter name of this quota item in the list interface response. For example, if the current quota item is Cpu and the list interface response is as follows, where "CpuCount" represents the cost of Cpu, configure this item as CpuCount. {"CpuCount":100, "Description":"test", "InstanceId":"xxx"} |
|---|---|

The quota management operations and horizontal capabilities for third-party products integrated with quotas are consistent with those of preset products. You can manage thirdparty products integrated with quotas on the Resource pool configuration, Quota management, Quota alert management, and Quota alert history pages.

###### 7.1.6.1.17 Third-party product management integration

**integration**

To enable management of external cloud products in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, make sure that the relevant systems and network environment meet the basic conditions. This solution is based on the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console and relies on its ability to call the management APIs of external cloud products. At the same time, the external clouds must provide standardized APIs to support cross-cloud resource management. Stable and secure two-way network connectivity must be established between the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console and external cloud API gateways to ensure the reliability of service calls and the security of data transmission. As the major caller, the Apsara Unimanager Management Console must maintain continuously available network connections with the external cloud API gateways to ensure the efficient execution of cross-cloud resource management processes. On this basis, the third-party products must provide complete functional support, including instance management features such as resource creation, deletion, modification and query, status change feedback, and execution result feedback. These capabilities ensure that the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console can efficiently call the APIs of external cloud services, test resource management processes in a multi-cloud environment, and reduce the integration complexity and testing costs of cross-cloud systems.

###### 7.1.6.1.17.1 Integration solution

The integration solution includes Service Provider Interface (SPI) integration for instance management, instance status update triggering by third-party products, and metering data pushing by third-party products. Instance management SPI integration This topic describes the interface specifications and integration steps for instance management SPI integration.

**Interface specifications**

Instance management is a core function of cloud service lifecycle management. It covers operations such as creating, querying, modifying, and deleting resources like ECS and RDS instances. To support unified management of instances by the Alibaba Cloud Apsara Unimanager Management Console, external clouds must provide standardized RESTful API interfaces to enable full lifecycle control over instances. The following table lists the specific operation types, request URLs, methods, and parameter descriptions.

> **Note:** All interfaces require POST requests over HTTPS with Content-Type set to application/json; charset=utf-8.

**CreateInstance**

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| action | true | String | Static field: createInstance. |
| aliUid | true | String | The Alibaba Cloud user ID that triggers the request. |
| params | true | JSONString | The request parameters for the API. The system fills in all declared parameters. |
| token | true | Security Token | A JWT security token for service provider validation. |
| traceId | false | String | The EagleEye ID. Service providers can record this ID for traceability purposes. |
| productCode | false | String | The product code. Service providers can record this code, which is assigned during product integration. |
| resourceTypeCod e | false | String | The resource type. Service providers can record this code, which is assigned during resource integration. |

| organizationId | false | Integer | The organization ID. Service providers can record the organization ID passed during instance creation. |
|---|---|---|---|
| resourceSetId | false | Integer | The resource set ID. Service providers can record the organization ID passed during instance creation. |

**Return value**

|---|---|---|---|
| code | true | Integer | The status code. 2XX: The call is successful. Other values: The call fails. |
| insntanceId | false. You must return either this parameter or taskId. | String | The ID of the unique key instance. |
| detail | true | Json | The detailed response information. |
| taskId | false. You must return either this parameter or insntanceId. | String | If the actual API of the service provider is asynchronous, you can return this field. The system uses this field to query the task execution status later. |

**GetTask for asynchronous task query**

If the SPI involves an asynchronous operation, you must provide an SPI interface to query the execution result of the asynchronous task. When an asynchronous task is triggered by a creation interface and completes, the query response must return the instanceId. Polling interval: 5 minutes. Parameters

| Parameter | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| action | true | String | The static field: getTask. |
| token | true | String | The JWT security token for service provider verification. |
| taskId | true | String | The ID of the task to query. |
| aliUid | false | String | The Alibaba Cloud user identifier that triggered the request. |
| traceId | false | String | The trace ID. Service providers can record this ID for troubleshooting purposes. |
| productCode | false | String | The product code. Service providers can record this code, which is assigned during product onboarding. |

| resourceTypeCod e | false | String | The resource type. Service providers can record this code, which is assigned during resource onboarding. |
|---|---|---|---|

Return values

| Parameter | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| code | true | Integer | The status code. 2XX: The call is successful. Other values: The call fails. |
| execStatus | true | String | WAITING: The task is waiting. RUNNING: The task is running. SUCCESS: The task succeeded. FAIL: The task failed. |
| instanceId | false | String | If the asynchronous task is triggered by a create instance interface and succeeds, this interface must return the instanceId parameter. |

**Integration steps**

1. Create an instance. The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console calls the API to trigger
an instance creation request. The SPI returns the generated instance ID and its current status. If the third-party product uses asynchronous API calls, return a taskId so that the cloud service can later query the task progress. After the task completes, return the instanceId. The cloud service retrieves the instance details by calling the GetInstanceDetail API and then stores them in the database.
2. Delete an instance. The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console sends a request to
trigger the deletion operation. The SPI deletes the instance corresponding to the provided instance ID and updates the instance status. If the third-party product uses asynchronous API calls, return a taskId so that the cloud service can later query the task progress. After the task completes, the cloud service deletes the record from the database.
3. Query an instance. The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console retrieves instance
details through the API. The SPI returns the detailed information for the instance corresponding to the specified instance ID.
4. Change the specification. The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console calls the API to
update the instance's specification. The SPI performs the modification and returns the result. If the third-party product uses asynchronous API calls, return a taskId so that the cloud service can later query the task progress. After the task completes, the cloud service retrieves the updated instance details by calling the GetInstanceDetail API and updates the database.
5. Get specifications. If the third-party product needs to support dynamic specification
retrieval, configure this API. The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console calls this API to obtain the currently supported specifications in real time.
6. Get inventory. If the third-party product needs to support inventory retrieval, configure this
API. Update the status of third-party product instances If a third-party product instance is managed by the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console and its status or information changes on the third-party platform, the third-party platform can call the CloudUpdateResource operation to notify the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console to query the real-time information about the instance by calling the GetInstanceDetail operation. CloudUpdateResource information:

**Basic information**

Operation: CloudUpdateResource Version: 2019-05-10 Request method: POST Product: Apsara Uni-manager Management Console Supported account: the tenant accounts granted the permission to synchronize resource information Call method: POP SDK

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Requ ired | Open | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| resourceType | String | true | true | The resource type of the third-party product to be accessed. |
| resourceId | String | true | true | The ID of the resource instance. |

If true is returned for the success parameter, the instance status is updated. `{`

    "success": true,
    "message": ""

**Basic information**

Operation: PutMeteringData Version: 2019-05-10 Request method: POST Product: Apsara Uni-manager Management Console Supported account: the tenant accounts granted the permission to upload metering data Call method: POP SDK Request parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| productCode | String | Yes | The resource type of the third- party product to be accessed. |
| data | String | Yes | The metering data in the JSON format. Take note of the following items: 1. The metering data of at most 100 instances can be pushed per request. 2. Except for the ResourceGId , ResourceGName , OrgId , OrgName , RegionId , and TableVersion fields, all the other fields in the metering data must be pushed. 3. The instance ID in the metering data must be managed in the resource management module. InsId indicates the instance ID in the resource management module. 4. The values of StartTime and EndTime in the metering data must be on the hour, and the start time is one hour earlier than the end time. Unit: seconds. In addition, the StartTime and EndTime of all instances in a request must be in the same metering cycle. |

|---|---|---|---|

Third-party product resource push A third-party product uses the ImportUnclaimedInstance API to actively push instances. If you need to directly store instances in Resource Management, a single operation must not exceed 10 instances. The ImportUnclaimedInstance API information is as follows:

**Basic information**

API: ImportUnclaimedInstance Path: /ascm/basic/marketInstance/importUnclaimedInstance Version: 2019-05-10 Method: POST Product: ascm Supported account: Tenant account (you must have the creation permission for the corresponding product to call this API). Calling method: Call by using POP SDK.

**Request parameters**

| Parameter | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| productUid | true | String | The UID of the accessed product. |
| resourceTypeUid | true | String | The UID of the accessed resource type. |
| platformCode | true | String | The platform code. The default value is default. |
| instanceDetails | true | JsonArr ay | The information about the imported instance. |

**Description of fields in instanceDetails**

| Parameter | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| instanceId | true | String | The ID of the instance. |
| instanceName | false | String | The name of the instance. |
| detail | false | String | The details of the instance. |
| shareType | false | String | The sharing scope of the instance. Default value: 0. 0: The current resource set. 1: The current organization and its subordinate organizations. 2: The current organization. |

| resourceSetId | false Note When you push resources directly into resource management, you must specify one of resourceSetId, resourceSetUuid, or resourceSetPath. If you specify all three, the system uses them in the following priority: resourceSetId > resourceSetUuid > resourceSetPath. | String | The ID of the target resource set to which the instance belongs. |
|---|---|---|---|
| resourceSetUuid | false | String | The UUID of the target resource set to which the instance belongs. |
| resourceSetPath | false | String | The path of the resource set to which the instance belongs. Start naming from the root organization. Example: "root/level-1 organization/level-2 organization/resource set"; root/ascm-tester/ResourceSet(ascm- tester). Note If you have customized the root name, use the custom name. |
| regionId | false Note This parameter is required when you push resources directly into resource management. | String | The region ID to which the instance belongs. |

| instanceCreateTi me | true | String | The time when the instance was created. Format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss. Example: 2025-12-15 17:39:31 |
|---|---|---|---|
| instanceCreateU ser | false | String | The user who created the instance. |

**Response Parameter**

If success=true, the update succeeded.

```json
{"code":"200","message":"success"}
```

A JSON Web Key (JWK) can be at most 4,096 characters in length. You can generate a JWK at https://mkjwk.org/. You can use the information displayed in the left card in the following figure to generate a JWK. The information displayed in the right card is used to generate a public key, which is used to verify JWT tokens. For more information, see the Verify a JWT token section of this topic.

    private String generateJwtToken(JSONObject requestBody, String secret) {
        try {
            PrivateKey privateKey = RSAKey.parse(secret).toPrivateKey();
            // Header
            Map<String, Object> header = new HashMap<>();
            header.put("alg", "RS256");
            header.put("typ", "JWT");
            // Payload
            // exp 15 minutes
            Map<String, Object> claims = new HashMap<>(requestBody);
            // Identify the request source as Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
            claims.put("iss", "ascm");
            claims.put("iat", System.currentTimeMillis() / 1000);
            claims.put("exp", (System.currentTimeMillis() / 1000) + 900);
            return Jwts.builder()
                    .setHeader(header)
                    .setClaims(claims)
                    .signWith(privateKey, SignatureAlgorithm.RS256)
                    .compact();
        } catch (Exception e) {
            throw new CommonException(500, SPI_TOKEN_GENERATE_FAILED);
```

nce is created.

@PostMapping("/create") public String createInstance(@RequestBody Map<String, Object> map) {
    String token = (String) map.get("token");
    String expiredTimeStr = (String) map.get("expiredTime");
    String params = (String) map.get("params");
    String spec = JSONObject.parseObject(params).getString("spec");
    // Verify the token.
    validateToken(token);
    // Parse the time string.
    Date expiredTime = parseDate(expiredTimeStr);
    // Implement the logic to create the instance.
    return instanceManager.createInstance(spec, expiredTime);
```

`}`

@PostMapping("/delete") public String deleteInstance(@RequestBody Map<String, Object> map) {
    String instanceId = (String) map.get("instanceId");
    String token = (String) map.get("token");
    // Verify the token.
    validateToken(token);
    // Implement the logic to delete the instance.
    return instanceManager.deleteInstance(instanceId);

##### 7.1.6.2 Service provider management

The service provider management feature allows you to manage the service providers of custom services in a centralized manner.

###### 7.1.6.2.1 Add a service provider

Before you add a custom service, you must add the service provider to which the service belongs.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Product Management** > **Service Provider**
**Management**.
4. On the **Service Provider Management** page, click **Add Service Provider**.
5. In the **Add Service Provider** dialog box, configure the parameters. The following table
describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|

| Service Provider Display Name | The display name of the service provider. The display name must be 2 to 30 characters in length and can contain underscores ( ) and hyphens (-). It must _ start with a letter and end with a letter or digit. |
|---|---|
| Service Provider Description | The description of the service provider. The description can be up to 200 characters in length and can contain common characters and punctuations. |
| Contact | The contact information of the service provider. The contact information must be 2 to 30 characters in length and must start and end with a letter. |
| Phone Number | The phone number of the service provider. |

6. Click **OK**.

###### 7.1.6.2.2 Modify a service provider

This topic describes how to modify a service provider when the service provider information changes.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Limits**

The built-in system service providers cannot be modified.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Product Management** > **Service Provider**
**Management**.
4. On the **Service Provider Management** page, find the service provider that you want to
modify and click **Edit** in the **Operation** column.

> **Note:** You can specify the Service Provider Display Name and Source parameters above the service provider list to quickly find a service provider.

5. In the **Edit Service Provider** dialog box, configure the parameters. The following table
describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Service Provider Display Name | The display name of the service provider. |
| Service Provider Description | The description of the service provider. |
| Contact | The contact information of the service provider. |
| Phone Number | The phone number of the service provider. |

6. Click **OK**.

###### 7.1.6.2.3 Remove a service provider

You can remove a service provider if you no longer need it.

**Prerequisites**

The service provider has no services. You are an operations administrator.

**Limits**

The built-in system service providers cannot be removed.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Product Management** > **Service Provider**
**Management**.
4. On the **Service Provider Management** page, find the service provider that you want to
remove and click **Delete** in the **Operation** column.

> **Note:** You can specify the Service Provider Display Name and Source parameters above the service provider list to quickly find a service provider.

5. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

#### 7.1.7 Examples

##### 7.1.7.1 Example: Manage the memory quota of ECS

###### ECS

This topic describes how to manage the memory quota of Elastic Compute Service (ECS).

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or organization administrator. Quotas are configured for the parent organization.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the main menu, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Quotas** > **Quotas**.
4. In the left-side organizational structure of the Quotas page, select the organization or
resource set whose resources you want to manage.
5. In the upper-right corner of the page, select a region.
6. Click the **Elastic Compute Service** card to view the quota details.
7. In the **Quota Details** panel, view the resource items, quotas, amount and percentage of
allocated quotas, and amount and percentage of activated resources.

> **Note:** **Quota**: If you do not specify a quota for a resource item, no quota is configured for the resource item. The system does not limit the usage of the corresponding resources.
> **Allocated Quota (Percentage/Allocated Amount)**: displays the quotas that are allocated to each resource item in the specified organization and its sub- organizations. You can view the amount and percentage of allocated quotas.
> **Activated Resources (Percentage/Activated Amount)**: displays the resources that are activated in the specified organization and its sub- organizations. You can view the amount and percentage of the activated resources.

8. In the lower part of the **Quota Details** panel, click **Create Quotas** or **Modify Quota**.
9. In the **Quota** column of the **Memory Quota(GB)** field, enter the quota that you want to
set. Example: 500.
0. Click **Save**.

##### 7.1.7.2 Create an alert rule for the memory quota of ECS

**of ECS**

This topic describes how to create an alert rule for the memory quota of Elastic Compute Service (ECS).

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or organization administrator. The memory quota of ECS is configured.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the main menu, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Quotas** > **Quota Alerts**.
4. On the Quota Alerts page, click **Create Alert**.
5. In the **Create Quota Alert** dialog box, configure the parameters in the Alert Object
Information and Alert Information sections. In the Alert Object Information section, select an organization or a resource set and a region. Select **Elastic Compute Service** from the Cloud Service Category drop-down list. In the Alert Information section, configure the Alert Name, Alarm Standard, and Alert Threshold parameters. For example, you can set the name of the alert rule to ECS_memory, select Used for the Alarm Standard parameter, select Number from the drop-down list in the Threshold column of the Memory Quota(GB) field, and set the threshold to 180. This way, an alert is triggered when the used memory of ECS exceeds 180 GB in size.
6. Click **OK**.

##### 7.1.7.3 Example: Create and publish a process

This topic provides an example on how to create and publish a process.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Process Management** > **Process Management**.
4. On the **Process Management** page, click **Create Process**.
5. Configure the basic information and click **Next**.
**Process Name**: Enter a name for the process. Example: Process for baseservicetest.
**Process Description**: Enter a description for the process. Example: The process is used
for the baseservicetest organization.
**Applicable Personnel**: Select **All Organizations** or **Select Organization**. Example:
Select **Select Organization** and select baseservicetest from the **Select Organization** drop-down list.

> **Note:** If you turn off **Bind Sub-organization**, the process cannot be associated with the sub-organizations of the selected organization. If you need to associate sub- organizations with the process, turn on **Bind Sub-organization**.

**Select Initiator**: Select **All Users** or **Specified Role**. Example: Select **All Users**.
6. In the **Process Configuration** step, configure the process nodes, including the start,
approver, and end information. After the configuration is complete, click **Submit**.
**Start**: Click the **Start** card. In the **Initiator Settings** panel, select or clear **Allow**
**Initiator to Add CC Recipient**. Example: Clear **Allow Initiator to Add CC Recipient**.
In this case, the initiator is not allowed to add CC recipients.
**Approved By**: Click the
icon. In the **Approval Node Settings** panel, configure the approval node.
**Approved By**: specify the approver type. Example: Set the **Type** parameter to
**Specific Personnel** and select **admin(admin)** from the **Specific Personnel** drop-
down list.
**Approval Method**: Select **Parallel Signature(Requires Approval by One)** or
**Sequential Signature(Requires Approval by All)** for **When multiple approvers**
**are specified**. You have specified admin as the approver. Keep the default setting.
Select or clear **Allow the approver to specify additional signatories** . Only the current approver can add signatories. Multiple signatories can be specified. Example: Select **Allow the approver to specify additional signatories** . In this case, the admin user is allowed to add signatories.
**Add CC Recipient**: You can select CC recipients from the **Specific Personnel** drop-
down list. Example: Leave the **Specific Personnel** parameter empty.
**End**: Click the **End** card. In the **End Node Settings** panel, you can specify the users who
are notified of the end of the process. After the process ends, the approval results are automatically sent to the specified users. Example: Leave the **Specific Personnel** parameter empty.

> **Note:** If you need to notify other users, select the users from the **Specific Personnel** drop- down list. The selected users must be visible to the process creator.

7. After the process is created, view the process in the process list.
8. Click **Publish** in the **Operations** column of the process. After the process is published, the
status of the process changes to **Published**. You can associate a process with a business scenario only when the process is in the **Published** state.

##### 7.1.7.4 Example: Associate a process with management operations

**management operations**

This topic provides an example on how to associate a process with management operations (creating and deleting organizations).

**Prerequisites**

A process is created and published. For more information, see Example: Create and publish a process. You are an operations administrator.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Resource Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Process Management** > **Process Binding**.
4. On the **Process Binding** page, click **Process Binding**.
5. Configure the parameters for process association and click **Submit**.
**Process Name**: For example, select the process created and published in Example:
Create and publish a process.
**Scenario**: For example, select **Management Operations**.
**Management Operations**: For example, find and click Organization Management in the
left-side pane and then select **Create and delete organizations**.
6. After you submit the process association, the process association is displayed in the
process list.

**Impacts**

When a user in the baseservicetest organization attempts to create or delete an organization, the operation is reviewed by using the process management feature before the operation can be performed. Before you initiate a process, you must provide supplementary information. After the application is submitted for approval, a process application form is generated. You can create or delete an organization only after the approver approves the application.

### 7.2 Service operations

#### 7.2.1 Shopping cart

You can add the cloud services for which you want to apply to the shopping cart and apply for multiple cloud services of different types at a time on the Shopping Cart page.

**Background information**

You can add multiple cloud services for which you want to apply to the shopping cart, confirm the information on the Shopping Cart page, and then submit multiple applications at a time. This improves the usage efficiency. You can add a service to the shopping cart on the service configuration page. After a service is added to the shopping cart, you can remove and modify the configurations of the service on the Shopping Cart page. After an application is submitted, a service order is generated.

**Add a service to the shopping cart**

In this example, Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) is used.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Networking** > **Cloud Network** > **Virtual**
**Private Cloud**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Virtual Private Clouds**.
4. On the Virtual Private Clouds page, click **Create VPC**.
5. On the Create VPC page, configure the parameters. For more information, see the user
guide of VPC.
6. Click **Add to Cart** in the lower part of the page

**View services in the shopping cart**

1. In the lower-right corner of the console, click the
icon to show the floating menu and click the icon to go to the Shopping Cart page.

> **Note:** After you add a service to the shopping cart on the service configuration page, you are automatically navigated to the Shopping Cart page.
> The number in the upper-right corner of the Shopping Cart icon indicates the number of services added to the shopping cart.

2. On the Shopping Cart page, view the information about the cloud services that are added to
the shopping cart in the following columns: **Service**, **Specifications**, **Billing Method**,
**Quantity**, **Duration**, and **Fee**.

> **Note:** Fees are displayed only after you enable price inquiry.

**Remove one or more services from the shopping cart**

**Remove a single service**

i. On the Shopping Cart page, find the service that you want to remove and click **Remove** in the **Actions** column. ii. In the message that appears, click **OK**. After the service is removed, it is no longer displayed in the shopping cart.

**Remove multiple services at a time**

i. On the Shopping Cart page, select the services that you want to remove. ii. Click **Batch Remove** in the lower part of the page. iii. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

**Modify service configurations in the shopping cart**

1. On the Shopping Cart page, find the service whose configurations you want to modify and
click **Change Specifications** in the **Actions** column.
2. Modify the configurations based on your business requirements by referring to the user
guide of the cloud service.

**Submit service applications**

1. On the Shopping Cart page, select the services for which you want to apply.
2. In the lower part of the page, click **Apply Now**.
3. On the **Confirm Order** page, click **Create Now**.

##### 7.2.2.2 Service management

The Service Management page displays all services that you can manage. You can create custom services, publish services, and authorize specific users to access services.

**Background information**

The service management feature is used to manage and control specific specifications of specific services that belong to an enterprise or organization. For example, enterprises or organizations require employees to go through an approval process before the employees purchase Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances with high specifications, or authorize only a specific user or users in a specific organization to purchase high-specification ECS instances. In this case, enterprises or organizations can configure the specifications and specify users by using the service management feature. After a service is published, the authorized users or organizations can select only the specifications that they are authorized to access. If they create resources with high specifications, they must go through an approval process. This way, enterprises or organizations can impose limits on resource users and manage specifications in a fine-grained manner.

###### 7.2.2.2.1.2 Create a service

Create a new service. Configure the associated product, authorization scope, form, pricing, and other information for the service. Create a service from a custom source.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or an organization administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the menu, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Service Catalog** > **Service Management**.
4. On the **Product Service** tab, click **Create a service**.
i. **Basic information**: Configure the users who can use the service and the approval process.

| Parameter |   | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Service type | Type | You can select Service or Specify URL. |
|   | Resource Pool | Select the resource pool to which the service belongs. This parameter appears only in multi-cloud scenarios. This parameter appears when you set Type to Service. |
|   | Product | Select the product whose resource items you want to restrict. This parameter appears when you set Type to Service. |
| Service informati on | Service name | Enter a service name. The name must be 3 to 25 characters in length and must be unique. |
|   | Icon | Click to open the Select an icon dialog box. Select an icon from the icon library or upload a local icon, and then click OK. Note When you upload a local icon, the following limits apply to the format, size, and resolution: Format: PNG, JPG, and JPEG are supported. Size: The image size must not exceed 200 KB. Resolution: The resolution must be 200 × 200 pixels. |
|   | Category | When Type is set to Service, this field is not editable. The category of the selected service will be displayed. When Type is set to Specify URL, specify a custom category for the service. |
|   | Provider | When Type is set to Service, this field is not editable. The provider of the selected service will be displayed. When Type is set to Specify URL, specify a custom provider for the service. |
|   | Service Descriptio n | Enter a description for the service. The description appears in your service catalog and must be 2 to 100 characters in length. |

| Configur ation method | Service configurat ion method | The default configuration method is Specify URL. This parameter appears when you set Type to Specify URL. |
|---|---|---|
|   | Activation address | Enter the activation URL of the service. The URL must start with http:// or https://. This parameter appears when you set Type to Specify URL. |

| Billing Method | Billing Method Configurat ion | Set the billing method for the service. The system displays this billing method when you activate the service. When you configure the billing method, you can select Pay-as-you-go or Subscription. The available billing methods vary by resource. Pay-as-you-go: This billing method charges you after you use resources based on actual resource usage. Subscription: This billing method requires upfront payment based on a subscription period, such as one month. Note When you create a service, the system displays billing methods based on the following rules: First-party services: Public cloud resources: When the billing switch uses the pay-as-you-go pricing mode, the system displays only Pay-as-you-go. When the billing switch uses the cost rate mode, the system displays billing methods that the corresponding service resources support. Apsara Stack resources: When custom metering and billing management is disabled, the system displays billing methods that metering and pricing support. When custom metering and billing management is enabled, the system displays only Pay-as-you-go. Third-party services: Public cloud resources: When the billing switch uses the pay-as-you-go pricing mode, the system does not display any billing method. When the billing switch uses the cost rate mode, the system displays billing methods that the corresponding service resources support. Apsara Stack resources: When no rule template is configured, the system does not display any billing method. When a rule template is configured, the system displays the billing method that the rule template specifies. |
|---|---|---|

| Service Authoriza tion | Authorizat ion type | The authorization types include: Global scope: Allows all users in all organizations to access the service. Specify organization: Allows all users in a specified organization to access the service. Specify user: Allows specified users to access the service. |
|---|---|---|
|   | Authorized organizati on | When you set Authorization type to Specify organization, you must specify the authorized organization. |
|   | Authorized User | When you set Authorization type to Specify user, you must specify the authorized user. Click Add user, select an organization and a username, and authorize the user. After you add the user, you can click Delete in the Actions column to remove the user from the authorized user list. |

ii. **Form Field Settings**: Based on the original form of the product resource, you can add custom fields for different business scenarios. The fields that you add appear at the end of the original form by default.

> **Note:** You do not need to configure this item when you set **Type** of the service to **Specify** **URL**.

|---|---|

Select: Includes Drop-down list, Radio button, and Checkbox. Time: Includes Date and Date range. Other: Includes Attachment. |

| Component configurati on | In the Form Design area, select a component and configure its settings. Click Preview the complete form at the top to preview the complete form, including the existing standard form and the custom form. |

Click Add to add multiple specification pools. Move the pointer over the specification pool name and click to modify the specification pool name. You cannot modify the default specification pool. Move the pointer over the specification pool name and click to delete the specification pool. You cannot delete the default specification pool. Preview the complete form: Preview all configuration items that appear when you create the corresponding cloud service resource through the standard process. Note The service catalog at the upper level controls the specification configuration of the specification pool. If the parameter configurations at the lower level conflict with those at the upper level, the validation fails. |
| Form field | Click Select attribute fields and select the fields that you want to specify in the expanded panel. The system generates a field specification configuration based on the selected fields. Configure the field specifications in the corresponding field area. Service management retrieves different field trees based on the selected service type. These field trees are relationship trees composed based on the dependencies among fields. All resources require detailed information about the organization and resource set when you activate, modify, or release them in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. Therefore, the Organization and Resource Set fields appear by default. |

iv. **Pricing configuration**: Preview the pricing configuration.

> **Note:** You do not need to configure this item when you set **Type** of the service to **Specify URL**.
> If billing information exists, click **View details** to go to the billing configuration details page.

###### 7.2.2.2.1.5 Publish a service

You must publish a service before users can use it. The system initializes all preset services in the **To be put on shelves** status by default.

**Prerequisites**

The service is in the **To be put on shelves** or **Removed** status. The default operator is the operations administrator or organization administrator.

**Limits**

You cannot publish **custom services** of the legacy custom configuration type. If necessary, go to Product Management to create a custom product, and then create a new service based on the custom product.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Service Catalog** > **Service Management**.
4. On the **Product Service** tab, publish a single service or multiple services in batches.

**Publish a single service**

a. In the service list, click **Shelf** in the **Action** column of the target service. b. Click **OK**. After publishing the service, the system changes its status to **Put on**
**shelves**.

**Publish multiple services in batches**

a. In the service list, select the services that you want to publish. b. Click **Publish** at the bottom of the list. c. Click **OK**. After publishing the services, the system changes their status to **Put on**
**shelves**.

###### 7.2.2.2.1.6 Unpublish a service

Unpublish a service that is already published.

**Prerequisites**

The service is in the **Put on shelves** status. The default operator is the operations administrator or organization administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Service Catalog** > **Service Management**.
4. On the **Product Service** tab, unpublish a single service or multiple services in batches.

**Unpublish a single service**

a. In the service list, click **Lower shelf** in the **Actions** column of the target service. b. Click **OK**. After unpublishing the service, the system changes its status to **Removed**.

**Unpublish multiple services in batches**

a. In the service list, select the services that you want to unpublish. b. Click **Unpublish** below the list. c. Click **OK**. After unpublishing the services, the system changes their status to
**Unpublished**.
