##### 7.2.2.3 Operation examples

###### 7.2.2.3.1 Example: Create an ECS instance service

This topic describes how to create an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance service.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or an organization administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Service Catalog** > **Service Management**.
4. On the **Service Management** page, click **Create a service**.
5. In the Basic information step, configure the parameters and click **Next Step**.

**Service type**

**Type**: Select **Service**.
**Cloud Platform**: Select a cloud platform. The Cloud Platform parameter is displayed
only in multi-cloud scenarios.
**Product**: Select **Elastic Compute Service** of the **Elastic Computing** category from
the first drop-down list and **ECS Instance** from the second drop-down list.

**Service information**

**Service name**: Enter the name of the service. Example: ECS instance service.
**Icon**: Select the icon of the service.
**Service Description**: Enter the description of the service. Example: Set restrictions on
the instance types, disks, and the number of ECS instances for when users in the baseservicetest organization create ECS instances.

**Billing Method**

Select the billing method of the service. Valid values: **Pay-as-you-go** and **Subscription**. When users create ECS instances, the billing method that you configure for this parameter is displayed.

**Service Authorization**

Specify which users of which organizations can access the service. For example, if you select **Specify organization** and select the baseservicetest organization from the
**Authorized organization** drop-down list, only users of this organization can access the
service.
6. In the Form Field Settings step, configure form fields and configuration instructions, and
click **Next Step**. For example, click Create Instance on the left, drag the Input box component in the Component section to the Form Design section. Then, configure the component in the Component configuration section on the right. Set the name of the field group to Custom Form and the name of the input box to Reason for Application.
7. In the Form parameter configuration step, select attribute fields, configure their values, and
then click **Next Step**. Example: Click Select attribute fields. In the panel that appears, select **Instance Type** in the
**Instance** category, **System Disk** and **Data Disk** in the **Storage** category, and **Number**
**of Instances** in the **Management Configuration** category. Then, click OK.
In the **Data Disk** section, click Add specifications and configure parameters such as the instance type, system disk type and capacity, and data disk type and capacity. If you set the **Number of Instances** parameter to 1 to 5, users can create a maximum of five ECS instances at a time.
8. In the Pricing configuration step, confirm the pricing rules and click **Submit**.
9. In the service list, find the service and click **Shelf** in the Actions column to publish the
service.

**Impacts**

When users in the baseservicetest organization select the preceding service catalog when they create ECS instances, the ECS instances are subject to the service catalog restrictions.

**Restrictions on instance types**

**Restrictions on the types and capacities of the system disk and data disk**

**Restrictions on the number of ECS instances**

**Custom forms**

#### 7.2.3 Order management

##### 7.2.3.1 Orders

On the Orders page, you can view the order history, including order status, date, and cost, and track the progress of orders.

###### 7.2.3.1.1 View orders

The Orders page displays order information categorized as My Orders, Orders to Be Handled, To Be Claimed, All Orders, and Abnormal Orders.

**Background information**

Orders include orders for activation, configuration change, unsubscription, renewal, and billing method change. The following scenarios generate orders. Activation: You activate a cloud service for the first time or create an instance in the cloud product console. Configuration change: You change the configuration of cloud product resources, such as scaling in, scaling out, upgrading, or downgrading. Unsubscription: You release the corresponding cloud service or cloud product resources. Renewal: You renew a resource order that uses the subscription billing method. Subscription to pay-as-you-go: You change the billing method of a resource from subscription to pay-as-you-go. Pay-as-you-go to subscription: You change the billing method of a resource from pay-asyou-go to subscription. Each cloud service generates one main order, and each cloud product resource generates one sub-order. If no cloud product corresponds to the service, the service generates one main order. By default, the system does not display sub-order information in the order details. Instead, the system displays it as instance information. My Orders: orders that you created Orders to Be Handled: orders that need to be handled To Be Claimed: orders pending claim. Administrators can also assign these orders. All Orders: all orders within your permission scope Abnormal Orders: orders that have billing exceptions, uncreated resources, or inconsistent statuses
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top menu bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Orders** > **Orders**.
4. On the **Orders** page, click the **My Orders**, **Orders to Be Handled**, **To Be Claimed**, **All**
**Orders**, or **Abnormal Orders** tab.
5. Expand **Advanced Filter**, configure the filter conditions, and then click **Search**.

> **Note:** **Resource Pool**: Filter orders by resource pool. This option is available only in multi-cloud scenarios.

**Organization**: When you filter orders by organization, the system does not
include order data from subordinate organizations.

> **Type**: You can select **Purchase**, **Change Configuration**, **Unsubscribe**, **Renew**, **Switch to Pay-as-you-go**, or **Switch to Subscription**.

**Billing Method**: You can select **Pay-as-you-go** or **Subscription**.
**Resource Item**: Select a cloud product before you select a resource item.
6. View the order list on the corresponding tab.

> **Note:** Move the pointer over
> next to **Specification details** to view the detailed
> specification information.
> **Quantity**: the number of resources in the order
> **Duration**: For the pay-as-you-go billing method, charges are based on the actual usage, and this column displays a hyphen (-). For the subscription billing method, this column displays the actual duration of new purchases, renewals, or the remaining duration after configuration changes based on the order type. For the unsubscription, this column displays a hyphen (-).
> **Fees**: the fee information of the order. For the pay-as-you-go billing method, this column displays the unit price. For the subscription billing method, this column displays the total cost. If the resource does not support billing or the fee is zero, this column displays a hyphen (-).
> **Purchase**: the unit price or the total cost for the newly purchased resources
> **Renewal**: the total renewal cost for the resources
> **Change Configuration**: the unit price of the resources after the configuration change or the price difference for this configuration change. A positive price difference indicates an upgrade and represents the additional fee that you must pay. A negative price difference indicates a downgrade and represents the refund amount.
> **Unsubscribe**: the total refund amount upon the unsubscription
> **Switch to Pay-as-you-go**: the total refund amount when you change the billing method from subscription to pay-as-you-go
> **Switch to Subscription**: the additional fee that you must pay when you change the billing method from pay-as-you-go to subscription

7. Click **Details** in the **Actions** column of an order, or click the order ID to go to the order
details page.

| Item | Description |
|---|---|
| Basic informatio n | Displays information about the order, including the organization, resource set, region, creator, creation time, order type, billing method, and total expenses. |
|   | Displays service configuration information and instance details provisioned by this order. Service information represents sub-order details. The status of the main order correlates with the provisioning status of instances in sub-orders. Service configuration: Displays the service name, configuration specifications, billing method, subscription duration, and fees. |

| Service informatio n | Note Click View Details to open the Expense Details dialog box and view detailed billing information. Original Price: the sum of the original prices of all billing items Discount Price: the sum of the discounted prices of all billing items Discounted price = Total price × Discount rate The discounted price is automatically truncated at the seventh decimal place. Any amount beyond the seventh decimal place is excluded from the final discounted price. Under the discounted price, each billing item and its |
|---|---|
|   | corresponding discounted price are displayed. For example, in Expense Details, Priced by specification and Priced by storage capacity both represent billing items. A price difference may exist when you change the service configurations. For the pay-as-you-go billing method, the price difference represents the difference in unit price before and after the configuration change. For the subscription billing method, a positive price difference indicates the additional amount that you must pay, and a negative price difference indicates the refund amount. A refund may be issued when you unsubscribe from a service. The refundable amount is automatically truncated at the third decimal place. The used duration is calculated in exact days, and any partial day is rounded up to one full day. Request Configuration Change Records: The system displays configuration change records when the service configuration has been modified. Instance details: Displays detailed information about instances associated with the order. The information shown is a snapshot taken when the order was completed. If the instance changes later, the snapshot remains unchanged. Overall provisioning status: Total quantity: the total number of resources in the order |
| Execution Progress | Completed: the number of successfully provisioned resources Displays the overall execution progress of the order. Failed: the number of failed resources. If failures occur, you can click Rerun or Cancel execution on the page. |
| Coupon Informatio n | Canceled: the number of canceled resources DisplayUs pthdea tceo Tuipmoen: dtehde utcimtioen o rfe tchoer dlass ot fu tphdea oterd, einrc.luding operations triggered by reruns or cancellations |
| Instance details list: Displays detailed information about instances in the order. |   |

###### 7.2.3.1.2 Reorder

This topic describes how to generate an identical or a similar order based on an existing order. This way, the configurations of the existing order can be reused to avoid reconfiguration.

**Prerequisites**

The order type is **Purchase**.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top menu bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Orders** > **Orders**.
4. On the **Orders** page, click the **My Orders**, **Order to Be Handled**, or **All Orders** tab.

> **Note:** **My Orders**: displays the orders that you created.
> **Orders to Be Handled**: displays the orders that need to be handled by you.
> **All Orders**: displays all orders within your permission scope.

5. Expand **Advanced Filter**, configure the filter conditions, such as **Order No.**,
**Organization**, **Creation Time (UTC±HH:MM)**, **Created by**, **Resource Pool**, **Service**,
**Product**, **Resource Item**, **Type**, **Instance ID**, **Instance Name**, **Billing Method**, and
**Status**, and click **Search**.

> **Note:** **Resource Pool**: Filter orders by resource pool. This condition is available only in multi-cloud scenarios.

**Organization**: If you filter orders by organization, the order data of subordinate
organizations is excluded.

> **Type**: You can select**Purchase**,**Change Configuration**,**Unsubscribe**, **Renew**, **Switch to Pay-as-you-go**, or **Switch to Subscription**.

**Billing Method**: You can select **Pay-as-you-go** or **Subscription**.
**Resource Item**: Select a cloud product before you select a resource item.
6. On the order list, find the new purchase order that you want to reorder.
7. Click **Re-order** in the **Actions** column of the order. Alternatively, go to the **Order Details**
page and click **Re-order**.
8. On the displayed resource creation page, adjust the configuration parameters as needed,
and then submit the order.

###### 7.2.3.1.3 Cancel an order

The order submitter and users with the order delivery processing permission can cancel an order.

**Prerequisites**

The order is in the **Rejected**, **Approving**, **Pending**, or **Processing Failed** status.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Orders** > **Orders**.
4. On the **Orders** page, click the **My Orders** or **All Orders** tab.

> **Note:** **My Orders**: Displays the orders that you created.
> **All Orders**: Displays all orders within your permission scope.

5. Expand **Advanced Filter**, configure the **Order No.**, **Organization**, **Creation time**
**(UTC±08:00)**, **Created by**, **Resource Pool**, **Service**, **Product**, **Resource Item**, **Type**,
**Instance ID**, **Instance Name**, **Billing Method**, and **Status** conditions, and then click
**Search**.

> **Note:** **Resource Pool**: Filters orders by resource pool. This condition is available only in multi-cloud scenarios.

**Organization**: When you filter orders by organization, the results do not include
order data from subordinate organizations.

> **Type**: Supports **Purchase**, **Change** **Configuration**, **Unsubscribe**, **Renew**, **Switch to Pay-as-you-go**, and **Switch to Subscription**.
> **Billing Method**: Supports **Pay-as-you-go** and **Subscription**.

**Resource Item**: select a cloud product before you select a resource item.
6. Find the target order in the order list, and cancel the order or cancel the execution of the
resource operation as needed.

| Operation | Description |
|---|---|

| Cancel an order | i. Click Cancel in the Actions column of the order. Alternatively, go to the Order Details page and click Cancel. ii. In the Confirm Operation dialog box, click OK. |
|---|---|
| Cancel the execution of a resource operation | i. Click the order ID to go to the order details page. ii. In the instance details section, click Cancel execution. Note Only orders in the processing failed status support Cancel execution. Click Rerun to retry a failed order. iii. Click OK. |

###### 7.2.3.1.4 Execute delivery

On the **Orders to Be Handled** tab, set a delivery time for a custom service order in the pending status. The system automatically executes the delivery when the specified time arrives.

**Prerequisites**

The order status is **Processing**.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Orders** > **Orders**.
4. On the **Orders** page, click the **Orders to Be Handled** tab.
5. Expand **Advanced Filter**, set the **Order No.**, **Organization**, **Creation time**
**(UTC±08:00)**, **Created by**, **Resource Pool**, **Service**, **Product**, **Resource Item**, **Type**,
**Instance ID**, **Instance Name**, **Billing Method**, and **Status** conditions, and then click
**Search**.

> **Note:** **Resource Pool**: Filters orders by resource pool. This option appears only in multi-cloud scenarios.

**Organization**: When you filter orders by organization, the results do not include
order data from subordinate organizations.

> **Type**: Supports **Purchase**, **Change Configuration**, **Unsubscrbe**, **Renew**, **Switch to Pay-as-you-go**, and **Switch to Subscription**.

**Billing Method**: Supports **Pay-as-you-go** and **Subscription**. Custom services
support only the pay-as-you-go method, so the system delivers only pay-as-yougo services.
**Resource Item**: Select a cloud service before you select a resource item.
6. In the order list, find the order that you want to process.
7. Click **Perform delivery** in the **Actions** column of the order. Alternatively, go to the **Order**
**Details** page, click **More**, and then select **Perform delivery**.
8. In the **Service delivery confirmation** dialog box, enter the **Instance Details Address**,
**Delivery time**, and **Description**.
You can select a past time as the delivery time. The earliest selectable time is 15 days before the current time.
9. Click **OK**.

##### 7.2.3.2 Renewal management

###### 7.2.3.2.1 View organization renewal resources

The Renewal Management page displays resources that users activated with the subscription billing method.

**Prerequisites**

By default, authorized users include Operations Administrator, Resource Auditor, Organization Administrator, Organization Resource Auditor, Organization Security Administrator, Global Organization Security Administrator, Platform Security Administrator, and Platform Security Configuration Administrator. Custom roles must have the permission “View organization renewal resources” under “Order Management” and menu access to “Renewal Management”.

**Constraints**

Operations Administrator, Resource Auditor, Global Organization Security Administrator, Platform Security Administrator, and Platform Security Configuration Administrator have permissions across all organizations. Organization Administrator, Organization Resource Auditor, and Organization Security Administrator have permissions for their own organization and subordinate organizations.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Order Management** > **Renewal**.
4. On the **Renewal** page, expand **Advanced Filter**, set conditions for **Instance ID**, **Instance**
**Name**, **Organization**, **Resource Set**, **Resource Pool**, **Product**, **Resource**, and
**Expiration time (UTC±HH:MM)**, then click **Search** to quickly locate resources.

> **Note:** **Resource Pool**: Filter resources by resource pool. This option appears only in multi-cloud scenarios.
> Select an organization before selecting a resource set.

5. View resource instances activated within the organization.

> **Note:** Click
> next to **Expiration Time** to sort resources in ascending or descending
> order.
> Click an instance ID to navigate to the corresponding resource console and view instance details.
> Resources configured for **Manual Renewal** change status to **Expired** upon expiration and are billed on a pay-as-you-go basis. If you renew an expired resource, the system charges on a pay-as-you-go basis for the renewal day and switches to subscription billing from the next day.
> Automatic renewal takes effect the day after configuration. The system deducts the renewal fee at 08:00, nine days before resource expiration.
> If deduction fails, the system retries daily until successful or until one day before expiration.
> If a resource expires tomorrow, automatic renewal does not apply. You must manually renew it.

###### 7.2.3.2.2 Set the renewal method

Renewal management allows you to manage resource renewal methods.

**Prerequisites**

By default, users with the following roles can perform this operation: Operations Administrator, Resource Auditor, Organization Administrator, Organization Resource Auditor, Resource Set Administrator, Resource User, Organization Security Administrator, Global Organization Security Administrator, Platform Security Administrator, and Platform Security Auditor. For custom roles, you must grant the "Set Renewal Method" permission under "Order Management" and the "Renewal Management" menu permission.

**Limits**

The permission scope for Operations Administrators, Resource Auditors, Global Organization Security Administrators, Platform Security Administrators, and Platform Security Configuration Administrators covers all organizations. The permission scope for Organization Administrators, Organization Resource Auditors, and Organization Security Administrators covers their own organization and subordinate organizations. The permission scope for Resource Set Administrators and Resource Users covers their own resource sets. You cannot set the renewal method for resources that are undergoing changes.

**Change manual renewal resources to automatic renewal**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Order Management** > **Renewal**.
4. On the **Renewal** page, click **Enable Auto Renewal** in the **Actions** column of a resource
configured with manual renewal.
5. In the **Automatic Renewal Management** dialog box, select a value for **Subscription**
**Duration**.

> **Note:** Valid values: **1 Month**, **2 Months**, **3 Months**, **4 Months**, and **More Durations**.
> If you select **More Durations**, you can customize the subscription duration by specifying a value from 5 to 60 in the **Subscription Duration (Months)** field.
> The automatic renewal setting takes effect the next day. The system deducts the quota at 08:00 nine days before the resource expires.
> If the deduction fails, the system retries daily until the deduction succeeds or one day before expiration.
> If the resource expires tomorrow, automatic renewal does not apply. You must manually renew the resource.

6. Click OK. After the setting is successful, the renewal method of the resource changes from
**Manual Renewal** to **Automatic Renewal**.

**Change automatic renewal resources to manual renewal**

1. On the **Renewal** page, click **Resume Manual Renewal** in the **Actions** column of a
resource configured with automatic renewal.
2. In the **Operation Confirmation** dialog box, click **Confirm**. After the setting is successful,
the renewal method of the resource changes from **Automatic Renewal** to **Manual**
**Renewal**.

**Set the subscription duration for automatic renewal**

1. On the **Renewal** page, click **Modify Automatic Renewal** in the **Actions** column of a
resource configured with automatic renewal.
2. In the **Automatic Renewal Management** dialog box, select a value for **Subscription**
**Duration**.

> **Note:** Valid values: **1 Month**, **2 Months**, **3 Months**, **4 Months**, and **More Durations**.
> If you select **More Durations**, you can customize the subscription duration by specifying a value from 5 to 60 in the **Subscription Duration (Months)** field.

3. Click OK.

###### 7.2.3.2.3 Manual renewal

The renewal management feature supports manual renewal of resources.

**Prerequisites**

By default, users with the following roles can perform this operation: Operations Administrator, Resource Auditor, Organization Administrator, Organization Resource Auditor, Resource Set Administrator, Resource User, Organization Security Administrator, Global Organization Security Administrator, Platform Security Administrator, and Platform Security Auditor. Custom roles must have the “Manual Renewal” permission under “Order Management” and access to the “Renewal Management” menu.

**Constraints**

Users with the roles of Operations Administrator, Resource Auditor, Global Organization Security Administrator, Platform Security Administrator, and Platform Security Configuration Administrator have permissions across all organizations. Users with the roles of Organization Administrator, Organization Resource Auditor, and Organization Security Administrator have permissions for their own organization and subordinate organizations. Users with the roles of Resource Set Administrator and Resource User have permissions limited to their assigned resource sets. You cannot renew resources that are currently undergoing modification.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Orders**> **Renewal**.
4. On the **Renewal** page, click **Renew** in the **Actions** column for the target resource.
5. In the **Manual Renewal** dialog box, select **Subscription Duration**.

> **Note:** Available durations include **1 month**, **2 months**, **3 months**, **4 months**, and **More Durations**.
> If you select **More Durations**, you can customize the subscription duration in **Subscription Duration (Months)**. The valid range is 5 to 60 months.
> After successful manual renewal, the expiration date of the resource extends by the number of months you selected.
> When a resource renewed via **Manual Renewal** expires, its status changes to **Expired**, and billing switches to the Pay-As-You-Go method. If you renew an expired resource, the system charges on a Pay-As-You-Go basis for the day of renewal and switches to Subscription billing starting the next day.

6. Click **OK**.

Perform AI analysis on renewal resources.

**Prerequisites**

The operations administrator has enabled the display of the intelligent assistant in
**Configurations** > **Apsara Copilot** > **Custom Settings**.
Make sure that you have enabled the **Intelligent Operations Expert** on the expert management page of Apsara Copilot.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Orders** > **Renewal**.
4. On the **Renewal** page, click **AI Analysis** in the upper-right corner.
5. View the idle resource ratio analysis report.

Custom role users must be granted the permission "View instances eligible for billing method conversion" under "Order Management" and access to the "Switch Billing Method" menu.

2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Service Operations**.

###### 7.2.3.3.2 Switch from subscription to pay-as-you-go

**go**

You can switch the billing method of an instance from subscription to pay-as-you-go. After you change the billing method, you are charged based on the actual usage. The fee for the remaining subscription is refunded. This helps you reduce costs and flexibly manage resources.

**Prerequisites**

The current billing method of the instance is subscription. You are an operations administrator, a resource auditor, an organization administrator, an organization resource auditor, an organization security administrator, a global organization security administrator, a platform security administrator, or a platform security configuration administrator. If you are using a custom role, the role must be granted the View Organization Resource Renewals management permission and the Renewal menu permission.

**Limits**

The payment method of an instance can be changed only once within a calendar day. The operations administrator, resource auditor, global organization security administrator, platform security administrator, and platform security configuration administrator have permissions on all organizations. The organization administrator, organization resource auditor, and organization security administrator have permissions on the organization to which they belong and the subordinate organizations.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Orders** > **Switch Billing Method**.
4. Find the instance for which you want to change the billing method and click **Change to**
**Pay-as-you-go** in the **Actions** column.
5. In the **Change to Pay-as-you-go** dialog box, view the instance information and refund
fees.

> **Note:** Click the instance ID to go to the Instance Details page to view the instance details.
> Move the pointer over **View details** in the Change to Pay-as-you-go dialog box to view the billing details.
> Refundable fee = (Original order amount -Charged fee) × Refund percentage.

6. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

###### 7.2.3.3.3 Switch from Pay-As-You-Go to Subscription Billing

**Subscription Billing**

After you switch a Pay-As-You-Go instance to Subscription Billing, the system bills you based on the selected subscription duration and resource configuration.

**Prerequisites**

The current billing method of the instance is Pay-As-You-Go. By default, only users with the following roles can perform this operation: Operations Administrator, Resource Auditor, Organization Administrator, Organization Resource Auditor, Organization Security Administrator, Global Organization Security Administrator, Platform Security Administrator, and Platform Security Configuration Administrator. Custom role users must be granted the "Switch Billing Method" permission under "Order Management" and access to the "Switch Billing Method" menu.

**Limits**

You can switch the billing method for the same instance only once per calendar day. Only Pay-As-You-Go instances of cloud services that support Subscription Billing can be switched to Subscription Billing. Operations Administrators, Resource Auditors, Global Organization Security Administrators, Platform Security Administrators, and Platform Security Configuration Administrators manage all organizations. Organization Administrators, Organization Resource Auditors, and Organization Security Administrators manage their own organization and subordinate organizations.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Orders** > **Switch Billing Method**.
4. Click **Change to Subscription** in the **Actions** column of the target instance.
5. In the **Change to Subscription** dialog box, set the subscription duration and whether to
enable auto-renewal.

> **Note:** Click the instance ID to go to the instance details page and view detailed information about the instance.
> Available subscription durations are **1 month**, **2 months**, **3 months**, **4 months**, and **More Durations**. If you select **More Durations**, you can specify a custom duration in the **Subscription Duration (Months)** field. Valid values range from 5 to 60 months.
> Hover over **View Details** to expand the cost breakdown.

6. Click **OK**.

##### 7.2.4.1 Product bill overview

###### 7.2.4.1.1 View the product bill overview

The Bill Overview tab of the Product Bill Overview page displays the bill overview of products.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator, a resource auditor, an organization administrator, or an organization resource auditor.

**Limits**

The operations administrator and resource auditor have permissions on all organizations. The organization administrator and organization resource auditor have permissions only on the organization to which they belong and the subordinate organizations.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Bills** > **Product Bill Overview**.
4. On the **Bill Overview** tab, select an accounting period from the **Accounting Period** drop-
down list. If the selected accounting period has unprocessed issues, the bill data displayed may be inaccurate. In this case, you can click **Pending Bill Issues** as an operations administrator or a resource auditor to go to the **Bill Audit Issues** page for troubleshooting.
**Bill Overview of Resource Items**: displays the **number of activated resource**
**items**, **number of resource items for which fees are charged in the selected**
**month**, **total fees in the selected month** , and **total fees of the year**.

> **Note:** Move the pointer over the number corresponding to **Resource Items that** **Incur Fees This Month** and view details.
> Click the amount corresponding to **Total Fees of This Month** to go to the **Overview of Monthly Bill** tab.

**Consumption Trend of Resource Items . Last 6 Months** : displays the consumption
trend of each resource item in the selected month and the previous five months. Click **Top 5** or **Top 10** in the upper-right corner to display the top 5 or top 10 resource items for which the most fees are charged each month. Click the or icon to display the consumption trend of resource items in a column chart or a line chart.

and percentage of the fees that are charged for the top 5 or top 10 resource items in the selected month.

**Consumption Details of All Resource Items** : displays the fees that are charged for all
resource items in each organization in the selected month.

> **Note:** In the upper-right corner of the section, you can select **Sort by Fee in** **Descending Order** or **Sort by Fee in Ascending Order** .
> You can click an amount in the **Fees** column to go to the **Overview of** **Monthly Bill** tab. On this tab, the accounting period, resource item, and organization are selected as the filter conditions by default.

**Settings** page of the **Apsara Copilot** module in **Configurations**.

**Product Bill Overview** page.

down list. If the selected accounting period has unprocessed issues, the bill data displayed may be inaccurate. In this case, you can click **Pending Bill Issues** as an operations administrator or a resource auditor to go to the **Bill Audit** page for troubleshooting.
5. Click **AI Diagnostics** in the upper-right corner to perform intelligent analysis on the
overview data and generate a bill analysis report.

> **Note:** The Bill Fluctuation Analysis feature supports the analysis of bill changes from multiple dimensions, such as cloud service, organization, resource set, and tag.
> The Trend Analysis and Forecast feature provides bill trend prediction for cloud services, organizations, resource sets, tags, cost centers, and resource instances.

You can ask questions based on analysis results by using Apsara Copilot.

###### 7.2.4.2.4 Settle monthly bills for organizations

After monthly bills are settled, the quotas of independent accounts and allocation accounts in budgets are deducted based on the actual bill amount of the current month, and the frozen quota is unfrozen.

**Usage notes**

> **Important:** After the bills in an accounting period are settled, the bill amount is frozen and cannot be adjusted or regenerated. Be sure to confirm the bill information before settlement.
> If the billing rules, discount deductions, bill adjustments, and cost center rules for the accounting period are adjusted, the bill regeneration feature must be used to ensure that the configurations and rules are applied to historical bills.
> If you want to adjust the bill amount after the bills are settled, make supplements and corrections in the bills next month.

**Prerequisites**

In the budget settings, the **Budget account creation dimension** parameter in **global**
**settings** is set to **By organization**.
You are an operations administrator.

**Limits**

You can settle monthly bills only if all check items are in the **Successful** state.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Bills** > **Organization Bill Overview**.
4. Click **Monthly Bill Settlement** in the upper-right corner.
5. In the **Monthly Bill Settlement** dialog box, configure the **Billing Cycle** parameter and
view the status of check items.

| Param eter | Description |
|---|---|

| Billing Cycle | The accounting period involved in the settlement. |
|---|---|
| Check Item | The fee deduction switch is turned on.: checks whether the fee deduction switch is turned on. If not, turn on the switch before settlement. The billing period has ended.: checks whether the accounting period has ended. Settlement can be made only after two days from the end date of the accounting period. The bill for the billing period is not generated.: checks whether the bills of the selected accounting period are settled. Settlement is not supported if the bills have been settled. All freezing tasks of the budget account in the billing period are normal.: checks whether all freezing tasks of the budget account in the current accounting period are normal. If not, contact O&M engineers to handle abnormalities before settlement. The latest independent account balance matches the account statement.: checks whether the latest balance of the independent account is consistent with the account statement. If not, contact O&M engineers to handle abnormalities before settlement. The latest balance of the independent account is the same as the balance of the allocation account.: checks whether the latest balance of the independent account is the same as the balance of the allocation account. If not, contact O&M engineers to handle abnormalities before settlement. No running bill regeneration task, cost center relabeling task, or bill adjustment task exists in the current billing period.: checks whether the accounting period has any bill regeneration tasks, cost center relabeling tasks, or bill adjustment tasks that are running. If yes, wait until the tasks are complete before settlement. No pending audit issues exist during the billing period.: checks whether the accounting period has any unprocessed audit issues. If yes, go to the Bill Audit page to troubleshoot issues before settlement. Reconciliation rules in the billing period have taken effect.: checks whether the adjustment rules are effective during the accounting period. If the adjustment is not complete, make the adjustment records effective or void. After the adjustment records take effect, you need to regenerate bills. |

6. Select **You confirm that the billing data in the billing period is accurate.** and click
**Confirm**.

then click **Search**. If you do not select an organization, the system displays all monthly bills within your permission scope by default.

> before the

If a selected organization has subordinate organizations, click

> organization name to expand its subordinate organization monthly bills.

|---|---|---|

The system displays different time zones based on the deployment location. The format is: Accounting period (UTC±HH:MM). For example, Accounting period (UTC+08:00). |

##### 7.2.4.4 Overview of public cloud bills

The Public Cloud Bill Overview page provides a comprehensive bill comparison across public cloud services.

###### 7.2.4.4.1 View the overview of public cloud bills

The Public Cloud Bill Overview page provides an overview of public cloud bills.

**Prerequisites**

The multi-cloud management feature is enabled, and the Alibaba Cloud public cloud platform is configured. This allows you to view bill data. You are an operations administrator or a resource auditor.

**Usage notes**

> **Important:** Public cloud subscription resources are not billed based on orders, but are billed based on the total list price on public cloud bills.

> Newly purchased, configurations upgraded, renewed, and billing method changed from pay-as-you-go to subscription: Total list price × Price multiplier × Discount
> Unsubscribed, configurations downgraded, and billing method changed from subscription to pay-as-you-go: Total list price × Price multiplier × Discount × Refund ratio

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Bills** > **Overview of Public Cloud Billing** to go to
the **Public Cloud Bill Overview** page.
4. On the **Bill Overview** tab, select an accounting period from the **Account Period** drop-
down list. If the selected accounting period has unprocessed issues, the bill data displayed may be inaccurate. In this case, you can click **Bill problem pending** as an operations administrator or a resource auditor to go to the **Bill Audit** page for troubleshooting.
**Resource Item Bill Overview**: displays the following items: **Products in Selected**
**Accounting Period**, **Charged Resources**, **Total Public Cloud Cost in This Month** ,
**Total Resale Revenue of Public Cloud in This Month** , **Total Profit in This Month**,
and **Total Profit in This Year**.
**Trend and Distribution**: displays the resale revenue trends and resource profit
distribution in the previous six months. You can switch between the top 5 and top 10 resources.
**Resale Revenue Trends in Last 6 Months** : displays the trends of resale revenue in
the current month and the previous five months in the selected accounting period. You can click the drop-down list in the upper-right corner of the chart to select a cloud service.
**Resource Profit Distribution**: displays the profit distribution of the resources in the
selected accounting period.
**Organization Ranking by Profit**: displays the profit information of all organizations in
the current month of the selected accounting period.

> **Note:** **Public Cloud Cost**: the payable amount of public cloud bills.
> **Resale Revenue**: the amount payable in cloud service bills.
> **Profit** = **Resale Revenue** - **Public Cloud Cost**.
> You can click the
> icon next to the Public Cloud Cost, Resale Revenue, or
> Profit field to sort data by amount in ascending or descending order.

###### 7.2.4.4.2 View the monthly bills of public cloud services

**services**

The Monthly Product Bill Overview tab displays the monthly bills of public cloud services.

**Prerequisites**

The multi-cloud management feature is enabled, and the Alibaba Cloud public cloud platform is configured. This allows you to view bill data. You are an operations administrator or a resource auditor.

**Usage notes**

> **Important:** Public cloud subscription resources are not billed based on orders, but are billed based on the total list price on public cloud bills.
> Newly purchased, configurations upgraded, renewed, and billing method changed from pay-as-you-go to subscription: Total list price × Price multiplier × Discount
> Unsubscribed, configurations downgraded, and billing method changed from subscription to pay-as-you-go: Total list price × Price multiplier × Discount × Refund ratio

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Bills** > **Overview of Public Cloud Billing** to go to
the **Public Cloud Bill Overview** page.
4. Click the **Monthly Product Bill Overview** tab.
5. Configure the **Account Period** and **Resources** filter conditions to filter bills.
6. View the monthly bills of public cloud services in the list.

> **Note:** **Public Cloud Cost**: the payable amount of public cloud bills.
> **Resale Revenue**: the amount payable in cloud service bills.
> **Profit** = **Resale Revenue** - **Public Cloud Cost**.
> You can click the
> icon next to the Public Cloud Cost, Resale Revenue, or Profit
> field to sort data by amount in ascending or descending order.

The permission scope for Operations Administrators and Resource Auditors covers all organizations and all cost centers. When the data scope is set by organization, the permission scope for Organization Administrators and Organization Resource Auditors includes their own organization and subordinate organizations. When the data scope is set by cost center, the permission scope for Organization Administrators and Organization Resource Auditors includes authorized cost centers at their level and child cost centers.

###### 7.2.4.5.7 Regenerate bills

If a bill is abnormal or needs to be updated, you can regenerate the bill based on the latest data and rules. This ensures the accuracy and timeliness of the bill.

**Prerequisites**

**q**

You are an operations administrator.

**Limits**

For accounting periods whose bills are settled, bill regeneration is not supported.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Bills** > **Bill Details** to go to the **Bill Details** page.
4. Click **Generate bills again** in the upper-right corner.
5. In the **Generate bills again** dialog box, configure the following parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Output Type | Valid values: Basic Bill, Bill Adjustment, Bill Split, and Cost Unit. Basic Bill: applies to scenarios in which the billing, discount, or reduction rules are adjusted. If you select this option, the cost center bills are updated. Bill Adjustment: applies to scenarios in which the bill adjustment records are added, enabled, or canceled. Bill Split: applies to scenarios in which bills are split based on the split rule. Cost Unit: applies to scenarios in which the cost center data or allocation rules are adjusted. |
| Product | The products for which you want to regenerate bills. You can select multiple products at a time. You can also search for a product by name. After you select products, click OK at the bottom of the Product drop-down list. |
| Resources | The resources for which you want to regenerate bills. You can select all or specific resources. |
| Account period(UTC ±HH:MM) | The accounting period of the bills to be regenerated. If you select Basic Bill, Bill Split, or Cost Unit as the output type, you can select only one month as the accounting period. If you select Bill Adjustment as the output type, you can select at most six consecutive months as the accounting period. |
| Billing Date | The time range of the bills to be regenerated. This parameter is supported only when you select Basic Bill, Bill Split, or Cost Unit as the output type. |

6. Click **OK**.
7. After bills are regenerated, click **Rebuild records** in the upper-right corner of the **Bill**
**Details** page to view the detailed generation records.

> **Note:** If a record displayed as Failed to generate exists on the **Bill Adjustment**, **Bill** **Split**, or **Cost Center** tab, contact the O&M engineers for troubleshooting.
> A failed record on the **Basic Bill** tab indicates that an audit issue exists. In this case, go to the Bill Audit Issues page for troubleshooting.
> If a record is not generated within 1 hour, you can click **Stop** in the Actions column of the record to stop the regeneration. After you stop the regeneration, you can resume it.

##### 7.2.4.6 Bill adjustment

###### 7.2.4.6.1 Add a reconciliation record

When bill amounts are incorrect, you can use the bill reconciliation feature to increase or decrease them for each instance. After you enable a reconciliation record, you must click Generate bills again on the Bill Details page to regenerate bills. Bill details and reconciliation amounts are then added.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Limits**

You cannot add reconciliation records to settled accounting periods.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Bills** > **Bill Reconciliation**.
4. In the upper part of the page, click **Add Transfer Records**.
5. In the **Add Transfer Records** panel, configure the parameters that are described in the
following table.

| Parameter |   | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Dat e | Acco unt Perio d | The accounting period of the reconciliation record. Only one month is supported. |
|   | Date Rang e | The specific date range in the accounting period. If you select multiple days, the bill adjustment details are generated each day during the period. |
| Attr ibut ion and Sco pe | Reso urce Scop e | Specify resource filter conditions in the Product, Resources, Organization, Resource Set, and Cost Unit drop-down lists. Select one or more instances in the resource instance list. |
|   | Tran sfer Type | The reconciliation type. Valid values: Chong Zheng and Supplement. Chong Zheng: A reconciliation record is added to decrease the amount of an existing bill, and a negative number is generated. The decreased amount is displayed as a negative number in red. Supplement: A reconciliation record is added to increase the amount of an existing bill, and a positive number is generated. The increased amount is displayed as a positive number in blue. |

| Am oun t |   |   |
|---|---|---|
|   | Adju stme nt Amo unt | The amount to be reconciled. Daily amounts of each instance within the accounting period will be reconciled. |
|   | Total | The total reconciled amount. |
|   | Desc ripti on | The description of the reconciliation. |

6. Click **OK**. By default, the new reconciliation record is in the To take effect state.

###### 7.2.4.6.2 View reconciliation records

This topic describes how to view reconciliation records on the Bill Reconciliation page.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or a resource auditor.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Bills** > **Bill Reconciliation**.

**Name**, **Product**, **Resources**, **Organization**, **Resource Set**, and **Status**, and then click
**Search**.

Description of the Adjustment Amount column: A negative amount is generated if a reconciliation record is added to decrease the amount of an existing bill. A positive amount is generated if a reconciliation record is added to increase the amount of an existing bill.
6. Click a record ID. The **Bill Adjustment Record Details** panel appears.

###### 7.2.4.6.3 Enable a reconciliation record

After a reconciliation record changes from the To take effect state to the In effect state, the reconciliation record is enabled. After you enable a reconciliation record, you must click Generate bills again on the Bill Details page to regenerate bills. Bill details and reconciliation amounts are then added.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or resource auditor. The reconciliation record is in the To take effect state.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Bills** > **Bill Reconciliation**.
4. Click **Advanced Filter**, configure the **ID**, **Instance ID**, **Instance Name**, **Product**,
**Resources**, **Organization**, **Resource Set**, and **Status** parameters, and then click
**Search**.
5. Find the reconciliation record that you want to enable and click **Effective** in the **Actions**
column.
6. In the message that appears, click **OK**.
After the reconciliation record is enabled, it changes to the In effect state.

###### 7.2.4.6.4 Disable a reconciliation record

You can disable a reconciliation record. After you disable a reconciliation record, you must click Generate bills again on the Bill Details page to regenerate bills. Bill details and reconciliation amounts are then added.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator. The reconciliation record is in the To take effect or In effect state.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Bills** > **Bill Reconciliation**.
4. Click **Advanced Filter**, configure the **ID**, **Instance ID**, **Instance Name**, **Product**,
**Resources**, **Organization**, **Resource Set**, and **Status** parameters, and then click
**Search**.
5. Find the reconciliation record that you want to disable and click **Void** in the **Actions**
column.
6. In the **Confirm void** message, click **OK**.
After the reconciliation record is disabled, it changes to the Invalidated state.

##### 7.2.4.7 Bill split management

###### 7.2.4.7.1 Create a split rule

This topic describes how to create a split rule to allocate unowned resource sets or shared costs to the correct owner based on the rule.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Bills** > **Bill Split Management**.
4. On the **Bill Split Management** page, click **Create A Rule**.
5. In the **Create Split Rule** dialog box, configure the following parameters.

| Section and parameter |   | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Basi c Info rma tion | Rule Name | The name for the split rule. The name can be up to 128 characters in length. |
|   | Plan Priorit y | The priority of the split rule. Valid values: 0 to 99. If you click the input field, the existing priorities are displayed. You cannot enter an existing priority. Bill split rules are matched from the highest priority to the lowest priority. |
|   | Effecti ve Time( UTC± HH:M M) | The effective time of the split rule. Bills within the effective period are split based on the corresponding rules. For historical bills, go to the bill details to update them by regenerating bills. |
| Rul e Con diti ons | Condit ions | The conditions for the split rule. You can configure multiple conditions with the Or or And combination. Add a condition or a condition group: a. Click Add Condition or Add Group. b. Configure a specific condition rule in the condition line. Delete a condition or a condition group: Click the icon on the right side of the condition or condition group. |
|   | Cost Alloca tion | Configure the resource set to which the cost belongs and the allocation proportion. You can configure multiple resource sets for bill splitting at the same time, and the allocation proportions cannot exceed 100% in total. Add a resource set: a. Click Add Resource Set. b. Select a resource set from the Resource Set drop-down list and set the allocation proportion of each resource set in the Allocation Proportion field. Delete a resource set: Click the icon in the row of a resource set and its allocation proportion. |

6. Click **OK**.

###### 7.2.4.7.2 View the split rule list and the details of a split rule

**a split rule**

This topic describes how to view the split rule list and the details of a split rule.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or resource auditor.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Bills** > **Bill Split Management**.
4. On the **Bill Split Management** page, view the created split rules.

> **Note:** You can configure the Rule Effective Date and Rule Name parameters to quickly find a specific rule.

5. Click the name of the rule that you want to view. In the **Rule Details** dialog box, view the
details of the rule.

###### 7.2.4.7.3 Modify a split rule

This topic describes how to modify a spit rule when the rule changes.

**Prerequisites**

The split rule is not deprecated. You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Bills** > **Bill Split Management**.
4. On the **Bill Split Management** page, find the rule that you want to modify and click **Edit**
in the **Actions** column.

> **Note:** You can configure the Rule Effective Date and Rule Name parameters to quickly find a specific rule.

5. In the **Modify Split Rule** dialog box, modify the rule configuration. For more information

###### 7.2.4.7.4 Enable a split rule

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Bills** > **Bill Split Management**.
4. On the **Bill Split Management** page, find the rule that you want to enable and click

> **Note:** You can configure the Rule Effective Date and Rule Name parameters to quickly find a specific rule.

##### 7.2.4.8 Bill audit

You can check and handle metering, billing, and bill generation issues.

###### 7.2.4.8.1 View bill audit issues

This topic describes how to view the overview of bill audit issues and details of each bill audit issue on the Bill Audit Issues page.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or resource auditor.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Bills** > **Bill Audit**.
4. View overview data.

| Item | Description |
|---|---|
| Abnormal Bill Days | The number of unique billing dates involving issues in the Pending Review state. |
| Total Issues | The total number of issues in all states. The states includeP ending Review, Processed, and Closed. |
| Pending | The number of issues in the Pending Review state. |
| Processed | The number of issues in the Processed state. |

5. Click **Advanced Filter**, configure the **Billing Period**, **Bill Date**, **Issue Type**, **Status**,
**Service**, **Resource Item**, and **Detected At** parameters, and then click **Search**.

> **Note:** Valid values of the **Issue Type** parameter: **An error occurred in the bill** **generation system.** and **An error occurred in the business** **configurations.**
> Before you select a resource item, select a cloud service first.

6. View bill audit issues. The information is displayed in the following columns: **Issue ID**,
**Detected At**, **Billing Date**, **Billing Period**, **Service**, **Resource Item**, **Issue Type**,
**Status**, **Cause**, and **Suggestion**.
7. Contact on-site O&M engineers to handle the issues based on the suggestions.
Alternatively, click **View Details** in the **Actions** column of an issue. In the **Error Message** panel, view the details of the issue and the solution.

> **Note:** In the Error Message panel of an issue, if "The price of the specifications is not specified." is displayed in the Issue column of the Details section, the specifications for which prices are not specified are displayed in the Content column. You can go to the Rule Settings page, find a billing configuration that is effective on the billing date, and then go to its details page. On the details page of the billing configuration, find the service that you want to manage and click Pricing Configuration in the Actions column. In the Price Settings step of the Pricing Configuration panel, set prices for the specifications.

###### 7.2.4.8.2 Close a bill audit issue

This topic describes how to close a bill audit issue that does not need to be processed on the Bill Audit Issues page.

**Prerequisites**

The issue is in the Pending Review state. You are an operations administrator.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Bills** > **Bill Audit**.
4. Click **Advanced Filter**, configure the **Billing Period**, **Bill Date**, **Issue Type**, **Status**,
**Service**, **Resource Item**, and **Detected At** parameters, and then click **Search**.

> **Note:** Valid values of the **Issue Type** parameter: **An error occurred in the bill** **generation system.** and **An error occurred in the business** **configurations.**
> Before you select a resource item, select a cloud service first.

5. View bill audit issues. The information is displayed in the following columns: **Issue ID**,
**Detected At**, **Billing Date**, **Billing Period**, **Service**, **Resource Item**, **Issue Type**,
**Status**, **Cause**, and **Suggestion**.
6. Find the issue that you want to manage, confirm that the issue does not need to be
processed, and then click **Close** in the **Actions** column.
7. In the **Confirm** message, click **Close**. After the issue is closed, the issue changes to the
Closed state.

###### 7.2.4.8.3 AI analysis of bill audit

The system provides bill audit capabilities based on AI analysis.

**Prerequisites**

The operations administrator has enabled the display of the intelligent assistant in
**Configurations** > **Apsara Copilot** > **Custom Settings**.
Ensure that you have enabled **Intelligent Operations Expert** on the expert management page of Apsara Copilot.

###### 7.2.4.9.4 Create an allocation rule

After you create a cost center, you can configure rules based on the actual financial cost structure to reaggregate resource bills. Resources are matched to different cost centers in ascending order in which global rules take effect. A resource belongs to only one cost center. After a bill is generated on the next day, you can view the resource ownership in the bill details.

**Prerequisites**

A cost center is created. You are assigned the operations administrator role.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Bills** > **Cost Centers**.
4. On the Cost Centers page, select the cost center that you want to manage in the **Financial**
**unit settings** section in the left-side pane. Enter the name of a cost center in the search
box to quickly find the cost center.
5. On the right side of the Cost Centers page, click the **Rule list** tab. On the Rule list tab, click
**Create a rule**.
6. In the **Create allocation rules** dialog box, configure the parameters that are required to
create the allocation rule.

| Section and parameter |   | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Basic informat ion | Rule name | The name of the allocation rule. |
|   | Financial unit | The cost center to which the allocation rule belongs. |
|   | Effective order | The priority value of the allocation rule. A smaller value specifies a higher priority. Select a reference allocation rule from the Reference location drop- down list, and then select Before or After from the Sequence drop- down list. If no allocation rule is available, the Effective order parameter is not displayed. |
|   | Effective time | The time range of the bills to which the allocation rule applies. |
| Rule conditions |   | The conditions based on which the allocation rule is triggered. The allocation rule is triggered only if the conditions are met. For more information, see the Rule conditions section of this topic. |

7. Click **OK**.

**Rule conditions**

**Items in rule conditions**

| Item | Condition type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Organization | Only this organization is included Organizations and subordinate organizations | In the organization tree, find an organization and click the name of the organization. |
| Resource set | Equal Not equal | Select a resource set from the drop-down list. |
| Resource set name | Equal Not equal Include Not included Start... | Enter a condition value in the field. |

| Cloud products | Equal Not equal | Select a cloud service from the drop-down list. |
|---|---|---|
| Resource Item | Equal Not equal | Select a resource item from the drop-down list. |
| Instance ID | Equal Not equal Include Not included Start... | Enter a condition value in the field. |
| Region | Equal Not equal | Select a region from the drop-down list. |
| Label | Contains any one All | Select one or more tags from the dialog box. |

**Operators**

Conditions are connected by using the **And** or **Or** operator.
**And**: All conditions must be met.
**Or**: At least one of the conditions must be met.
A condition group is a set of conditions that need to be met.

**Add or remove a condition or condition group**

At least one condition must be retained in the rule conditions. Up to five levels of rule conditions are supported. To add a condition, click **Add condition** in the rule conditions. To add a condition group, click **Add condition Group** in the rule conditions. To delete a condition, find the condition and click the icon that corresponds to the condition in the rule conditions. To delete a condition group, find the condition group and click the icon that corresponds to the condition group in the rule conditions.
