#### 7.2.5 Budget management

##### 7.2.5.1 Configure budget settings

Budget management can be used to limit the available quotas for organizations or cost centers. You can configure budget accounts, budget control settings, and budget alert settings based on your business requirements.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator. If you are assigned a custom role, the custom role is granted the permissions to access the Budgets module and the permissions to configure global settings and budget alert settings.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Budgets**.
4. In the upper-right corner of the **Budgets** page, click **Budget settings**.
5. In the **Budget settings** panel, configure global settings and budget alert settings.

**Global Settings**

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Budget account creation dimension | Valid values: By organization and By financial unit. By organization: configures budget accounts based on the organization architecture. By financial unit: configures budget accounts based on the cost center architecture. If you select By financial unit, you must configure cost centers and allocation rules. Note You can configure the Budget account creation dimension parameter only if you enter the Budgets module for the first time and you have not completed the initial setup. You cannot modify this parameter after it is configured. Proceed with caution. |

| Insufficient budget control settings | Valid values: If the budget is insufficient, you can apply for new resources. and Insufficient budget does not allow new resource applications. Note If the budget is insufficient, you can apply for new resources.: The system does not limit resource allocation by budget management. The account balance can be deducted to a negative value. Insufficient budget does not allow new resource applications: The system controls resource allocation based on orders. Subscription services do not accept resource applications if the account balance is less than the order payment. Pay-as-you-go services do not accept resource applications if the account balance is zero or less than zero. |
|---|---|

**Budget alert**

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Alarm switch | Specifies whether to enable budget alert. Valid values: Open and Close. |
| Alert Threshold | The alert threshold. The system checks the available quotas of the allocation accounts at 09:00 every day. If a quota is lower than the specified threshold, an alert notification is sent. |
| Alert object | The alert contact. Valid values: Organization Administrator/financial unit authorized user and Operations Administrator. You can select both options. |

6. Click **Save**.

##### 7.2.5.2 View independent accounts

You can view the list of independent accounts on the Budgets page.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or resource auditor. If you are assigned a custom role, the custom role is granted the permissions to access the Budgets module and the permissions to view independent accounts.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Budgets**.
4. On the **Budgets** page, click **Independent account list** in the left-side **Budget Overview**
section.
5. View independent accounts. You can filter or search for specific accounts by configuring the
**Account name** and **Includes deleted accounts** parameters.

> **Note:** An independent account is the master account of a level-1 organization or cost center. You can increase or reduce the budget for an independent account.
> An allocation account is used to control the quota of an organization or cost center. The quotas of allocation accounts are allocated from the independent account level by level.
> The account list displays only independent accounts. This helps you view the overall quota information about each level-1 organization or cost center.

##### 7.2.5.3 View the income and expenditure details of all accounts

**of all accounts**

This topic describes how to view the income and expenditure details of all accounts on the Budgets page.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or a resource auditor. If you are assigned a custom role, the custom role must be granted the permissions to view the income and expenditure details of all accounts and access the Budgets module.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Budgets**.
4. On the **Budgets** page, click **Income and expenditure details** in the **Budget Overview**
section in the left-side pane.
5. In the upper part of the **Budget Account** section, select one or all cloud platforms.

> **Note:** The cloud platform drop-down list is displayed only in multi-cloud environments and only if budgets are configured by organization.
> If you select **All**, you can view the income and expenditure details of accounts on all cloud platforms.

6. View the income and expenditure details of accounts. In the **Advanced Filter** section
above the list of income and expenditure details, configure filter conditions such as **Assign**
**Accounts**, **Independent Account**, **Operator**, **Serial Number**, **Revenue and**
**Expenditure Type**, **Flow Type**, **Account Period**, and **Billing Date** to filter data or
search for specific data.

> **Note:** **Flow Type**: You can select **Quota adjustment**, **Quota Allocation**, **Freeze**, **Freeze** **release**, or **Deduction**.
> **Quota adjustment**: You can increase or reduce the quota of an independent account.
> **Quota Allocation**: You can increase or reduce the quota of an allocation account.
> **Freeze**: The system suspends the available quota based on the cloud service bill on a daily basis, or suspends the available quota when the system regenerates a bill.
> **Freeze release**: The quota suspended in a month is released when the system generates the monthly bill.
> **Deduction**: When the system generates a monthly bill, the system deducts the bill amount from the available quota and adds the bill amount to the used quota.

##### 7.2.5.4 View account details of a node

You can view the account details of a node on the Budgets page.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or an organization administrator. If you are assigned a custom role, the custom role must be granted the permissions to access the Budgets module and view account details.

**Limits**

An operations administrator can view all nodes. If budget accounts are configured based on the organization architecture, you can view only the organization to which you belong and its subordinate organizations. If budget accounts are configured based on the cost center architecture, you can view only the cost center for which you are authorized and its subordinate cost centers.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Budgets**.
4. In the **Budget Account** section of the Budgets page, select a cloud platform or All from the
cloud platform drop-down list.

> **Note:** The cloud platform drop-down list is displayed only in multi-cloud environments and when budget accounts are configured based on the organization architecture.

5. In the **Budget Account** section, select the node that you want to view.

> **Note:** You can select **Show Deleted Accounts** to display the deleted nodes.

6. On the right side of the Budgets page, click the **Account details** tab.
7. View the account details.

**Independent account details**

> **Note:** By default, independent accounts are enabled and cannot be disabled.

An independent account is the master account of a level-1 organization or cost center. You can increase or reduce the quota of an independent account. In single-cloud environments, select a level-1 node to view the independent account details of the node. In multi-cloud environments, select **All** from the cloud platform drop-down list, select a level-1 node, and then view the independent account details of the node.

| Section | Description |
|---|---|
| Independent account | Displays the total budget quota within the level-1 node. You can adjust the account quota. Available quota = Total quota - Used quota - Frozen quota Frozen quota: The amount of the frozen quota is calculated based on the daily bill amount. Used quota: After a monthly bill is settled, the actual bill amount of the current month is the used quota. The used quota is deducted from the total quota, and the frozen quota is unfrozen. |
| Budget allocation details | By default, the available budget of the current level-1 node is the quota of the independent account. After budgets are allocated to subordinate nodes, the budget quota of the current node is reduced accordingly. Current & Subordinate: the overall quota information about the current node and its subordinate nodes. Current Budget Quota: The actual available quota for resource allocation at the current node is the sum of its allocation account quota and the quotas of its subordinate nodes for which the allocation accounts are disabled. Current Allocation Account: the allocation account quota of the current node. Subordinate Allocation Account: the total quotas allocated from the current node to the subordinate nodes for which the allocation accounts are disabled. The quota is allocated to the subordinate account.: the quotas allocated to the subordinate nodes for which the allocation accounts are enabled. |

**Allocation account details**

> **Note:** In single-cloud environments, the accounts of the level-2 and lower nodes on a specific cloud platform are allocation accounts.
> In multi-cloud environments, if you select **All** from the cloud platform drop- down list, the accounts of the level-2 and lower nodes on the selected cloud platforms are allocation accounts. If you select a cloud platform from the cloud platform drop-down list, the accounts of all the nodes (including level-1 nodes) on the selected cloud platform are allocation accounts. In addition, the parent node of a node on the selected cloud platform is its corresponding same-level node found under the **All** selection. If this corresponding node is disabled, the system searches upwards for the next active parent. For example, Level-1 Node A (independent account) under the **All** selection is the parent node of Level-1 Node A (allocation account) on a specific cloud platform. Level-2 Node B (allocation account) under the **All** selection is the parent node of Level-2 Node B (allocation account) on a specific cloud platform.

| Scenario | Description |
|---|---|

| Allocation accounts in single-cloud environments or allocation accounts of level-2 and lower nodes if you select All from the cloud platform drop-down list in multi-cloud environments | If quota allocation is disabled for the allocation account of a node, the allocation account shares the budget quota of the parent node of the node. Parent Budget Quota: the quota of the nearest parent node for which quota allocation is enabled. Current Allocation Account: the quota information about the current account. If quota allocation is enabled for the allocation account of a node, the allocation account uses the budget quota of the node. Current & Subordinate: the overall quota information about the current node and its subordinate nodes. Current Budget Quota: The actual available quota for resource allocation at the current node is the sum of its allocation account quota and the quotas of its subordinate nodes for which the allocation accounts are disabled. Current Allocation Account: the allocation account quota of the current node. Subordinate Allocation Account: the total quotas allocated from the current node to the subordinate nodes for which the allocation accounts are disabled. The quota is allocated to the subordinate account.: the quotas allocated to the subordinate nodes for which the allocation accounts are enabled. |
|---|---|

| Allocation accounts of the nodes on the cloud platform selected from the cloud platform drop-down list in multi-cloud environments | If quota allocation is disabled for the allocation account of a node on the cloud platform selected from the cloud platform drop-down list, the allocation account shares the budget quota of the parent node of the node. If quota allocation is enabled for the allocation account of a node on the cloud platform selected from the cloud platform drop-down list, the allocation account uses the budget quota of the node. |
|---|---|

##### 7.2.5.5 View the transaction details of a node

You can view the transaction details of a node on the Budgets page.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator, organization administrator, or organization resource auditor. If you are assigned a custom role, the custom role must be granted the permissions to access the Budgets module and view account details.

**Limits**

An operations administrator can view all nodes. If budget accounts are configured based on the organization architecture, you can view only the organization to which you belong and its subordinate organizations. If budget accounts are configured based on the cost center architecture, you can view only the cost center for which you are authorized and its subordinate cost centers.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Budgets**.
4. In the **Budget Account** section of the Budgets page, select a cloud platform from the cloud
platform drop-down list.

> **Note:** The cloud platform drop-down list is displayed only in multi-cloud environments and when budget accounts are configured based on the organization architecture.

5. In the **Budget Account** section, select the node that you want to view.

> **Note:** You can select **Show Deleted Accounts** to display the deleted nodes.
> In multi-cloud environments, if you select **All** from the cloud platform drop-down list, the accounts of the level-2 and lower nodes on the selected cloud platforms are allocation accounts. If you select a cloud platform from the cloud platform drop-down list, the accounts of all the nodes (including level-1 nodes) on the selected cloud platform are allocation accounts. In addition, the parent node of a node on the selected cloud platform is its corresponding same-level node found under the **All** selection. If this corresponding node is disabled, the system searches upwards for the next active parent. For example, Level-1 Node A (independent account) under the **All** selection is the parent node of Level-1 Node A (allocation account) on a specific cloud platform. Level-2 Node B (allocation account) under the **All** selection is the parent node of Level-2 Node B (allocation account) on a specific cloud platform.

6. On the right side of the Budgets page, click the **Income and expenditure details** tab.
7. Click Advanced Filter and configure the following parameters to filter or search for specific
transaction details: **Operator**, **Serial Number**, **Revenue and Expenditure Type** , **Flow**
**Type**, **Account Period(UTC+08:00)**, and **Billing Date(UTC+08:00)**.
8. View the transaction details of the node.

> **Note:** If the current node is a level-1 node, the transactions within the independent account of the node are displayed. In multi-cloud environments, if you select a cloud platform from the cloud platform drop-down list and select a level-1 node, the transactions within the allocation account of the node are displayed.
> If the current node is a level-2 or lower node, the transactions within the allocation account of the node are displayed. In multi-cloud environments, if you select a cloud platform from the cloud platform drop-down list and select a node, the transactions within the allocation account of the node are displayed.
> Valid values of the **Flow Type** parameter are **Quota adjustment**, **Quota** **Allocation**, **Freeze**, **Freeze release**, **Deduction**, and **Refund**.
> **Quota adjustment**: You can increase or reduce the quota of an independent account.
> **Quota Allocation**: You can increase or reduce the quota of an allocation account.
> **Freeze**: The system suspends the available quota based on the service bill on a daily basis, or suspends the available quota when the system regenerates a bill.
> **Freeze release**: The quota suspended in the month is released when the system generates the monthly bill.
> **Deduction**: When the system generates a monthly bill, the system deducts the bill amount from the available quota and adds the bill amount to the used quota.
> **Refund**: Refunds may be involved when users enable reversing reconciliation records, change the specifications of subscription resources, and unsubscribe from resources.

##### 7.2.5.6 Enable quota allocation

You can enable quota allocation for allocation accounts. After quota allocation is enabled for the allocation account of a node, you can allocate the quota to the allocation account and use the quota as the separate budget of the node and its subordinate nodes. For more information about how to allocate quotas, see Allocate quotas.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or an organization administrator. If you are assigned a custom role, the custom role must be granted the permissions to access the Budgets module and allocate quotas. Quota allocation is disabled for an allocation account.

**Limits**

> **Note:** By default, quota allocation is disabled for allocation accounts. If quota allocation is disabled for the allocation account of a node, the allocation account shares the budget quota of the parent node of the node.
> If you want to manage the budget quota of a subordinate node in a more fine- grained manner, you can enable quota allocation for the node and allocate the available quota to the node.

You can enable quota allocation only for allocation accounts. An operations administrator can enable quota allocation for all allocation accounts. Users can enable quota allocation for the subordinate nodes within their organization or their authorized cost center, and then allocate quotas to the subordinate nodes. Before you enable quota allocation for the allocation account of a node, you must enable quota allocation for the parent node of the node.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Budgets**.
4. In the **Budget Account** section of the Budgets page, select a cloud platform or All from the
cloud platform drop-down list.

> **Note:** The cloud platform drop-down list is displayed only in multi-cloud environments and when budget accounts are configured based on the organization architecture.

5. In the **Budget Account** section, select the node to which the allocation account belongs.

> **Note:** In multi-cloud environments, if you select **All** from the cloud platform drop-down list, the accounts of the level-2 and lower nodes on the selected cloud platforms are allocation accounts. If you select a cloud platform from the cloud platform drop-down list, the accounts of all the nodes (including level-1 nodes) on the selected cloud platform are allocation accounts. In addition, the parent node of a node on the selected cloud platform is its corresponding same-level node found under the **All** selection. If this corresponding node is disabled, the system searches upwards for the next active parent. For example, Level-1 Node A (independent account) under the **All** selection is the parent node of Level-1 Node A (allocation account) on a specific cloud platform. Level-2 Node B (allocation account) under the **All** selection is the parent node of Level-2 Node B (allocation account) on a specific cloud platform.

6. On the right-side section of the Budgets page, click the **Account details** tab.
7. On the **Account details** tab, click **Enable** in the upper-right corner of the Assign accounts
section.
8. In the **Operation confirmation** message, click **Enable**.

##### 7.2.5.7 Disable quota allocation

You can disable quota allocation for allocation accounts. If quota allocation is disabled for the allocation account of a node, the allocation account shares the budget quota of the parent node of the node.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or an organization administrator. If you are assigned a custom role, the custom role must be granted the permissions to access the Budgets module and allocate quotas. Quota allocation is enabled for an allocation account.

**Limits**

An operations administrator can disable quota allocation for all allocation accounts. Users can disable quota allocation for the subordinate nodes within their organization or their authorized cost center. Before you disable quota allocation for a node, you must disable quota allocation for all its subordinate nodes and withdraw the quota allocated to the node. In this case, the total quota of the node is 0.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Budgets**.
4. In the **Budget Account** section of the Budgets page, select a cloud platform or All from the
cloud platform drop-down list.

> **Note:** The cloud platform drop-down list is displayed only in multi-cloud environments and when budget accounts are configured based on the organization architecture.

5. In the **Budget Account** section, select the node to which the allocation account belongs.

> **Note:** In multi-cloud environments, if you select **All** from the cloud platform drop-down list, the accounts of the level-2 and lower nodes on the selected cloud platforms are allocation accounts. If you select a cloud platform from the cloud platform drop-down list, the accounts of all the nodes (including level-1 nodes) on the selected cloud platform are allocation accounts. In addition, the parent node of a node on the selected cloud platform is its corresponding same-level node found under the **All** selection. If this corresponding node is disabled, the system searches upwards for the next active parent. For example, Level-1 Node A (independent account) under the **All** selection is the parent node of Level-1 Node A (allocation account) on a specific cloud platform. Level-2 Node B (allocation account) under the **All** selection is the parent node of Level-2 Node B (allocation account) on a specific cloud platform.

6. On the right-side section of the Budgets page, click the **Account details** tab.
7. On the **Account details** tab, click **Disable** in the upper-right corner of the Assign accounts
section.
8. In the **Operation confirmation** message, click **Disable**.

##### 7.2.5.8 Adjust quotas

You can adjust quotas for the independent accounts of level-1 nodes based on your business requirements.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator. If you are assigned a custom role, the custom role must be granted the permissions to access the Budgets module and adjust quotas.

**Limits**

You can adjust quotas only for independent accounts.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Budgets**.
4. In the **Budget Account** section of the Budgets page, select All from the cloud platform
drop-down list.

> **Note:** The cloud platform drop-down list is displayed only in multi-cloud environments and when budget accounts are configured based on the organization architecture. In multi-cloud environments, if you want to adjust the quota for an independent account, select **All** from the cloud platform drop-down list.
> In multi-cloud environments, if you select **All** from the cloud platform drop-down list, the accounts of the level-2 and lower nodes on the selected cloud platforms are allocation accounts. If you select a cloud platform from the cloud platform drop-down list, the accounts of all the nodes (including level-1 nodes) on the selected cloud platform are allocation accounts. In addition, the parent node of a node on the selected cloud platform is its corresponding same-level node found under the **All** selection. If this corresponding node is disabled, the system searches upwards for the next active parent. For example, Level-1 Node A (independent account) under the **All** selection is the parent node of Level-1 Node A (allocation account) on a specific cloud platform. Level-2 Node B (allocation account) under the **All** selection is the parent node of Level-2 Node B (allocation account) on a specific cloud platform.

5. In the **Budget Account** section, select the level-1 node that you want to view.
6. On the right side of the Budgets page, click the **Account details** tab.
7. On the **Account details** tab, click **Adjustment quota** in the upper-right corner.
8. In the **Adjustment quota** dialog box, configure the parameters to adjust the quota.

| Paramete r | Description |
|---|---|
| Adjustm ent type | The adjustment type of the quota. Valid values: Increase or Decrease. |
| Quota | The quota that you want to increase or decrease. The quota that you want to decrease cannot be greater than the total quota. |
| Remarks | The description of the adjustment. |

9. Click **OK**.

##### 7.2.5.9 Allocate quotas

After the quota allocation feature is enabled for the allocation account of a node, you can allocate quotas to the node. This topic describes how to allocate quotas to a node.

**Prerequisites**

The quota allocation feature is enabled for the allocation account of a node. You are an operations administrator or an organization administrator. If you are assigned a custom role, the custom role must be granted the permissions to allocate quotas and access the Budgets module.

**Limits**

When you configure budgets by organization, you can allocate budget quotas only to the subordinate organizations of the organization to which you belong, but not to the organization itself. When you configure budgets by cost center, you can allocate budget quotas only to the subordinate cost centers of the cost center that you are authorized to access, but not to the cost center itself.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Budgets**.
4. On the Budgets page, select a cloud platform in the **Budget Account** section.

> **Note:** You need to select a cloud platform only in multi-cloud environments and when budgets are configured by organization.

5. In the **Budget Account** section, select the node to which the allocation account belongs.

> **Note:** In multi-cloud environments, **all** nodes of level 2 and lower on the central cloud platform are allocation accounts, and all nodes of managed cloud platforms, including level-1 nodes, are allocation accounts. In addition, the parent nodes of the nodes on the managed cloud platforms refer to **all** nodes of the same level on the central cloud platform. If nodes of the same level on the central cloud platform are disabled, nodes of next higher level are used. For example, **all** level-1 nodes A (independent accounts) of the central cloud platform are the parent nodes of level-1 nodes A (allocation accounts) of the managed cloud platforms, and **all** level-2 nodes B (allocation accounts) of the central cloud platform are the parent nodes of level-2 nodes B (allocation accounts) of the managed cloud platforms.

6. On the right-side section of the Budgets page, click the **Account details** tab.
7. On the **Account details** tab, click **Allocation quota** in the upper-right corner.
8. In the **Allocation quota** dialog box, configure the parameters to allocate quotas. The
following table describes the parameters.

| Parameter |   | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Superior budget | Superior allocation account | The allocation account of the parent node. |
|   | Superior available quota | The quota available to the parent node. |
| Current account status | Cloud Platform | The cloud platform to which the allocation account belongs. This parameter is displayed only when the quota is allocated to the allocation account of a node on the managed cloud platform in multi-cloud environments. |
|   | Total budget quota at this level | The total budget quota of the current node. |
|   | Available budget quota at this level | The budget quota available to the current node. |
| Allocation quota | Adjustme nt type | The adjustment type of the quota. Valid values: Increase and Decrease. |
|   | Quota | The quota that you want to increase or decrease. The quota that you want to increase cannot be greater than the quota available to the parent node. The quota that you want to decrease cannot be greater than the total budget quota available to the current node. |
|   | Remarks | The description of the adjustment. |

9. Click **OK**.

##### 7.2.6.2 Configure an alert rule for quotas of Alibaba Cloud platform accounts

#### Alibaba Cloud platform accounts

After you configure an alert rule for quotas of Alibaba Cloud platform accounts, if the available quota of an Alibaba Cloud platform account is less than the specified threshold, an alert notification is sent to the specified contacts. This topic describes how to configure an alert rule for quotas of Alibaba Cloud platform accounts.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Public Cloud Account**.
4. On the **Public Cloud Account** page, click **Alert Settings** in the upper-right corner.
5. In the **Alert Settings** panel, configure the parameters. The following table describes the
parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|

| Alarm Switch | Specifies whether to enable alerting. Valid values: Open and Close. |
|---|---|
| Alert Threshold | The alert threshold. If the available quota of an Alibaba Cloud platform account is less than the specified threshold, an alert notification is sent to the specified contacts. The system checks the available quota of Alibaba Cloud platform accounts at 9:00 every day. |
| Alert Object | The alert recipient. Valid values: Organization Administrator/Cost Unit Authorized User and Operations Administrator. You can select both options. |

6. Click **Save**.

##### 7.2.7.1 Create a contract

You can create a custom contract and configure the basic information and billing information about the contract. This topic describes how to create a contract.

**Prerequisites**

The Contract Management module is displayed. By default, the Contract Management module is hidden. To show the Contract Management module, log in to the Apsara Unimanager Management Console as a platform administrator. In the top navigation bar, click
**Configurations**. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Menu Settings** > **Main Menu**
**Configuration**. On the **Single-cloud Menu** tab, choose **Operations** > **Service**
**Operations** and select **Contract Management**.
You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Contract Management**.
4. On the **Contract Management** page, click **Create Contract**.
5. In the **Create Contract** panel, configure the parameters. The following table describes the
parameters.

| Parameter |   | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Basic Infor matio n | Contract Name | The name of the contract. The name can be at most 128 characters in length. |
|   | Contract Number | The contract number. It must be 3 to 60 characters in length. |
|   | Organizatio n | The organization to which the contract belongs. You can select only one organization. |
|   | Validity Period(UTC +08:00) | The start and end dates of the validity period of the contract. Only one contract can take effect on the same day for an organization. The validity periods of contracts cannot overlap. |
|   | Contract Attachment | The file related to the contract. To upload a file, click Upload File and then select the file that you want to upload. The file must be in the PDF format and cannot exceed 5 MB in size. |

| Billing Infor matio n | Bind Discount Rule | The discount rule to be bound to the contract. Add discount rules a. Click Add Discount. b. In the Add Discount dialog box, select one or more discount rules. Note You can find the discount rule that you want to view and click Details in the Actions column to go to the details page of the discount rule. Then, you can view the details of the discount rule. c. Click OK. Remove discount rules: In the added discount rule list, find the discount rule that you want to remove and click the icon on the right side of the discount rule. Note You can find the discount rule that you want to view and click the icon on the right side of the discount rule to go to the details page of the discount rule. Then, you can view the details of the discount rule. |

##### 7.2.7.2 View contracts

This topic describes how to view information about contracts.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator, a resource auditor, an organization administrator, or an organization resource auditor.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Contract Management**.
4. On the **Contract Management** page, click **Advanced Filter**, configure the **Contract**
**Number**, **Organization**, **Validity Period(UTC+08:00**), and **Status** parameters, and then
click **Search** to search for contracts.
5. In the contract list, view the information about the contracts.
6. Find the contract that you want to view and click its name or **Details** in the **Actions**
column to go to the **Contract Details** page.

##### 7.2.7.3 Modify a contract

This topic describes how to modify a contract.

**Prerequisites**

A contract is in the **Disable** state. You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Contract Management**.
4. On the **Contract Management** page, click **Advanced Filter**, configure the **Contract**
**Number**, **Organization**, **Validity Period(UTC+08:00**), and **Status** parameters, and then
click **Search** to search for contracts.
5. In the contract list, view the information about the contracts.
6. Find the contract that you want to modify and click **Edit** in the **Actions** column.
7. In the **Modify Contract** panel, modify the parameter settings of the contract. For more
information about the parameters of a contract, see Create a contract.
8. Click **OK**.

##### 7.2.7.4 Enable a contract

This topic describes how to enable a contract in the Disable state.

**Prerequisites**

A contract is in the **Disable** state. You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Contract Management**.
4. On the **Contract Management** page, click **Advanced Filter**, configure the **Contract**
**Number**, **Organization**, **Validity Period(UTC+08:00**), and **Status** parameters, and then
click **Search** to search for contracts.
5. In the contract list, view the information about the contracts.
6. Find the contract that you want to enable and click **Enable** in the **Actions** column.
7. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

##### 7.2.7.5 Disable a contract

This topic describes how to disable a contract that is in the Enable state but remains ineffective.

**Prerequisites**

A contract is in the **Enable** state and the current date is earlier than the start date of the validity period of the contract. You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Contract Management**.
4. On the **Contract Management** page, click **Advanced Filter**, configure the **Contract**
**Number**, **Organization**, **Validity Period(UTC+08:00**), and **Status** parameters, and then
click **Search** to search for contracts.
5. In the contract list, view the information about the contracts.
6. Find the contract that you want to disable and click **Disable** in the **Actions** column.
7. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

##### 7.2.7.6 Terminate a contract

This topic describes how to terminate an effective contract in the Enable state.

**Prerequisites**

A contract is in the **Enable** state and the current date is later than the start date but earlier than the end date of the validity period of the contract. You are an operations administrator.

**Limits**

You can terminate a contract only once.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Contract Management**.
4. On the **Contract Management** page, click **Advanced Filter**, configure the **Contract**
**Number**, **Organization**, **Validity Period(UTC+08:00**), and **Status** parameters, and then
click **Search** to search for contracts.
5. In the contract list, view the information about the contracts.
6. Find the contract that you want to terminate, move the pointer over the
icon in the
**Actions** column, and then select **Terminate**.
7. In the **Terminate Contract** dialog box, specify the date when the contract ends.
8. Click **OK**.

##### 7.2.7.7 Delete a contract

This topic describes how to delete a contract that is no longer required.

**Prerequisites**

A contract is in the **Disable** state. You are an operations administrator.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Contract Management**.
4. On the **Contract Management** page, click **Advanced Filter**, configure the **Contract**
**Number**, **Organization**, **Validity Period(UTC+08:00**), and **Status** parameters, and then
click **Search** to search for contracts.

The price calculator calculates the estimated costs based on cloud service configurations in the deployment cloud environment and region, and allows you to add items to a configuration list.

You can enable price inquiry as a platform administrator. To do so, you can perform the following operations: Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as a platform administrator. In the top navigation bar, click **Configurations**. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Billing Switch**.

##### 7.2.8.2 Billing configuration overview

On the Rule Overview page, you can view the timeline of each billing configuration in the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. The timeline displays the validity period of the billing configuration.

**Background information**

On the Rule Overview page, each billing configuration is displayed in a timeline, which displays the validity period of the billing configuration. This helps you trace the historical billing configuration changes. You can also view billing configurations by day, week, month, quarter, and year. This helps enterprises more clearly and efficiently understand their costs and implement fine-grained operations and cost optimization.

**Prerequisites**

Billing configurations are created.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Pricing** > **Rules**.
4. On the **Rule Overview** page, view the validity period of each billing configuration in the
Gantt chart.

> **Note:** By default, billing configurations are displayed by month. The name of a billing configuration contains the validity period of the billing configuration.

**Change the time span of the Gantt chart** : Click **Day View** in the upper-right corner
and select **Week View**, **Month View**, **Quarter View**, or **Year View** from the drop-down list.
**Search for billing configurations**: In the navigation tree, enter a keyword in the
search box above the billing configuration list.
**View the details of a billing configuration**: In the navigation tree, find the billing
configuration that you want to view and click its name. The **Billing Configuration**
**Detail** page appears On the **Billing Configuration Detail** page, view the details of the
billing configuration.

###### 7.2.8.3.2 Cloud services that support price inquiries

**inquiries**

After you turn on the price inquiry switch, the system displays cost information during service usage when you create (activate), reconfigure (scale up), unsubscribe (delete or release), renew, use the CPQ, or view orders.

**Enable the pricing inquiry switch**

The platform administrator turns on the price inquiry switch in **Configuration** > **Billing**
**Switch**. For detailed operations, see Configure the billing feature on the Billing Switch page.

**Cost description**

For cloud services that support the pay-as-you-go billing method, the system displays cost information during new purchase, configuration change (if supported), CPQ, and order processing. The displayed cost represents the unit price of the product. FFor cloud services that support the subscription billing method, the system displays cost information during new purchase, configuration change (if supported), unsubscription, renewal, CPQ, and order processing. The displayed cost represents the total amount payable for the product. Date calculation rules New purchase: The purchase day is not billed. If you activate and unsubscribe on the same day, no fee applies. For example, if you purchase a one-month subscription on January 1, 2024, the billing cycle runs from 00:00:00 on January 2, 2024 to 00:00:00 on February 2, 2024. Configuration change: On the day of the change, the system bills based on the previous specification. Starting the next day, the system bills based on the new specification. Renewal: The renewal period starts from the day after the instance expires. Unsubscription: The system bills for the day of unsubscription. Use the following formulas to calculate payable amounts during configuration change, unsubscription, and renewal: Payable amount for configuration change or unsubscription (monthly billing) = Unused fee - (Paid fee - Consumed fee)

> **Note:** Consumed fee: the fee consumed by this instance during the past period
> Paid fee: The total fee already paid for this instance during the past period. This includes fees paid during initial purchase, each configuration change, and each renewal.
> Unused fee: The fee required for future usage. The future specification may be the new specification or the current specification.

Payable amount for renewal (monthly billing) = Number of renewal months x Monthly unit price

**Cloud services that support price inquiry in Enterprise Edition**

In multi-cloud scenarios, Enterprise Edition supports price inquiry for all cloud services available in the corresponding edition (excluding custom services).

**Fee display examples**

> **Note:** Configuration cost: shows the unit price or payable amount for a resource item.
> If the resource has associated resources, their costs also appear. For example, when you purchase a new ECS instance, the system also displays the cost of its associated disks**.** ECS disk (EBS) cost: shows the unit price of the ECS disk resource item associated with the ECS instance.
> Cost details/View details: Move the pointer over this link to view the original and discounted prices for the resource item. If associated resources exist, their details also appear. For example, under ECS cost details, the system also displays cost details for the associated ECS disk (EBS) resource item.
> Original price: the sum of the original prices for all billable items
> Discounted price: the sum of the discounted prices for all billable items
> Discounted price = Total price × Discount rate
> The system automatically truncates any amount beyond the seventh decimal place and excludes it from the discounted price.
> Under the discounted price, the system displays each billable item and its corresponding discounted price.

For example, in the Elasticsearch cost details, items such as "Pricing by primary node CPU", "Pricing by primary node memory", and "Pricing by data node CPU" represent billable items.

> Coupon: If a coupon is used for a resource, the system also displays the coupon amount.

When you change the configuration of a service, a price difference may occur. For pay-as-you-go billing, the price difference represents the difference between the unit prices before and after the configuration change. For subscription billing, a positive number indicates the amount the user must pay to cover the difference, while a negative number indicates the amount to refund to the user. When you unsubscribe from a service, you may receive a refund. The system automatically truncates any amount beyond the third decimal place in the calculated refund. The used duration is calculated in full days, and any partial day counts as one full day.

**Purchase an ECS instance (pay-as-you-go)**

**Purchase an Elasticsearch instance (pay-as-you-go)**

**Purchase an ECS instance (subscription)**

**Change the configuration of an ECS instance (pay-as-you-go)**

**Change the configuration of an ECS instance (subscription)**

**Renew an ECS instance (subscription)**

**Unsubscribe from an ECS instance (subscription)**

> **Note:** When you cancel a subscription, the configuration details show the refund amount for each monthly-billed instance.

**CPQ cost display**

> **Note:** At the bottom of the CPQ page, the system displays the total cost for all services.
> If all services use the subscription billing, the system displays the total monthly discounted cost.
> If all services use the pay-as-you-go billing, the system displays the total hourly discounted cost for all resources and their units. The unit display rule matches the rule used during new purchase quotation. If multiple billable items have different units, the system displays "/hour".
> If services use both the subscription and pay-as-you-go billing, the total at the bottom shows the subscription cost and the pay-as-you-go cost separately. The pay-as-you-go cost includes its unit, following the same display rule as new purchase quotation. If multiple billable items have different units, the system displays "/hour".

**Order list cost display**

For detailed information about the cost display in the order list and order details, see Orders.

###### 7.2.8.3.3 Public cloud product pricing mode description

**description**

The billing switch supports usage-based pricing and cost rate. The cost rate applies to all integrated public cloud products. The usage-based pricing applies only to public cloud products that have metering data and billing rules.

> **Note:** Usage-based pricing: The system prices resources based on billing rules and pricing factors from metering data. It calculates the resale amount for public cloud services by applying billing rules to public cloud metering data.
> Price multiplier pricing: The resale amount for public cloud services equals the cost amount on the public cloud bill multiplied by the price multiplier.
> When you set the pricing mode to usage-based pricing, the system cannot generate bills for cloud services that support only the cost rate.

###### 7.2.8.3.4 Create a billing configuration

This topic describes how to create a billing configuration on the Billing Rules page.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

**Limits**

When you create a billing configuration, the service list displays the services and specifications that support and use the billing configuration. If additional services and specifications are added later, **Pending Configuration** is displayed in the billing configuration list and on the details pages of billing configurations, which prompts you to complete the billing configuration.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Pricing** > **Billing Rules**.
4. On the **Billing Rules** page, click **Create Billing Configuration**.
5. On the Create Billing Configuration page, configure parameters in the **Basic Information**
step, and then click **Next: Billing Configuration**. The following table describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|

| Billing Configuratio n Name | The unique name of the billing configuration. |
|---|---|
| Effective Time(UTC+0 8:00) | The start and end dates of the validity period of the billing configuration. The effective time is accurate to the date and excludes the specified end date. For example, if you set the start date to August 13, 2024 and the end date to August 15, 2024, the billing configuration takes effect at 00:00:00 on August 13, 2024 and expires after 00:00:00 on August 15, 2024. |
| Billing Method | The billing method. Valid values: Pay-as-you-go and Subscription. Pay-as-you-go: Users use services before fees are generated based on the actual amount of used resources. This billing method is suitable for scenarios in which resource usage frequently fluctuates or is difficult to predict. It allows users to flexibly utilize resources based on actual needs, preventing resource waste. Subscription: Users directly subscribe to resources for a fixed period, and the cost is generated based on the subscribed quantity and duration. No additional fees are charged during subsequent usage. This billing method is suitable for scenarios in which resource usage is relatively stable. Users can plan resource usage and estimate resource requirements to prevent the impact on business due to insufficient resources. |
| Plan Priority | The priority of the billing configuration. Set the value to a unique number. Note A larger number indicates a higher priority. This priority determines the sequence in which billing configurations are displayed. After a billing configuration is created, its display order is adjusted based on its priority. |
| Applicable Organization s | The organization to which the billing configuration applies. Only level-1 organizations are supported. If you select root, the billing configuration applies to all organizations. |
| Remarks | The description of the billing configuration. The description must be 1 to 256 characters in length. |

6. In the **Billing Configurations** step, configure pricing configurations for services, and then
click **Next: Billing Configuration Verification** . For more information, see Manage pricing configurations.
7. In the **Billing Configuration Verification** step, preview the pricing configurations, and
then click **Save**. The following table describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Product | The name of the cloud service. |
| Product Category | The category to which the cloud service belongs. |
| Instance Type Configuratio n Ratio | The proportion of cloud service specifications whose prices have been set to a number greater than 0. |
| Price Verification | Indicates whether the configuration ratio is 100%. Note If the configuration ratio of a service is smaller than 100%, Rejected is displayed. The parameter value is for reference only. You can create the billing configuration even if the configuration ratios of specific services are smaller than 100%. |

###### 7.2.8.3.7 Manage pricing configurations

You can manage pricing configurations when you create billing configurations or manage existing billing configurations.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Pricing** > **Billing Rules**.
4. Go to the **Pricing Configuration** panel.
**When you create a billing configuration**:
a. In the **Billing Configurations** step of the **Create Billing Configuration** page, select a cloud service from the **Product Details** drop-down list to quickly find the cloud service. b. Click **Pricing Configuration** in the **Actions** column.
**When you manage an existing billing configuration**:
a. Find the billing configuration that you want to manage and click **Edit** in the **Actions** column. b. On the **Billing Configuration Detail** page, select a cloud service from the **Product**
**Details** drop-down list to quickly find the cloud service.
c. Click **Pricing Configuration** in the **Actions** column.
5. In the Pricing Configuration panel, configure the parameters in the **Billable Item**
**Configuration** and **Price Settings** steps.
i. In the **Billable Item Configuration** step, configure the billable items and price type of the cloud service and the filter condition type for fine-grained cost management.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Product | The name of the cloud service for which you want to configure the pricing configuration. The current cloud service is selected by default and cannot be changed. |
| Billing Method | The billing method of the cloud service. The current billing method of the cloud service is selected by default and cannot be changed. |
| Configure Filtering Condition | The filter condition type. Valid values: Exact Match and Conditional Match. For more information, see the Filter conditions section of this topic. |
| Metering Table | The metering table associated with the cloud service. |
| Billing Cycle | The billing cycle of metering table. |
| Price Type | The type of the unit price that you want to use for the pricing configuration. Valid values: Monthly Price, Daily Price, and Hourly Price. For more information, see the Price types section of this topic. |
| Billing Item Management | You can modify existing billable items and create or delete billable items based on your business requirements. For more information, see the Billable item management section of this topic. |

ii. In the **Price Settings** step, configure the prices of billable items and click **OK**.

> **Note:** If you turn on **Display Only Unpriced Items** in the upper-right corner of the panel, the billable items for which you have not configured prices are automatically displayed.
> Click **AllHide** or **AllShow** in the upper-right corner to collapse or expand all priced and unpriced billable items.

**Billable item configurations**

**Filter conditions**

You can set the Configure Filtering Condition parameter to **Exact Match** or **Conditional**
**Match**.
**Exact Match**: All metering data is included in the billing and used for bill generation.
**Conditional Match**: Only metering data that meets the specified filter conditions is
included in the billing. The filter condition consists of the **Field** and **Value** parameters. If the value of a field in the metering data is the same as the specified value of the Value parameter, the metering data meets the filter condition.

> **Note:** To add a filter condition, you can click **Add Filtering Condition**. You can add multiple filter conditions.
> You can click **Delete** in the **Actions** column of a filter condition to delete the filter condition. If you set the Configure Filtering Condition parameter to Conditional Match, at least one filter condition must be retained.

If you select **And**, a bill is generated only if the metering data meets all the filter conditions that you specified. If you select **Or**, a bill is generated if the metering data meets at least one of the filter conditions.

**Price types**

> **Important:** If the decimal cannot be completely divided, the amount after the seventh decimal place is automatically rounded off and not included in the unit price. If the pay-as- you-go billing method is used, bills are generated based on the hourly price. We recommend that you set the price type to hourly price if the pay-as-you-go billing method is used.

30 indicates the number of days in a calendar month. You need to replace it with the actual number of days in the current month based on the actual situation. You can select **Monthly Price**, **Daily Price**, or **Hourly Price** from the Price Type drop-down list. If you select **Monthly Price** as the price type, bills are generated for the billable item by month. You can use the following formulas to calculate the hourly price, daily price, and annual price: Hourly price = Monthly price/30/24 Daily price = Monthly price/30 Annual price = Monthly price × 12 If you select **Daily Price** as the price type, bills are generated for the billable item on a daily basis. You can use the following formulas to calculate the hourly price, monthly price, and annual price: Hourly price = Daily price/24 Monthly price = Daily price × 30 Annual price = Monthly price × 12 If you select **Hourly Price** as the price type, bills are generated for the billable item on an hourly basis. You can use the following formulas to calculate the daily price, monthly price, and annual price: Daily price = Hourly price × 24 Monthly price = Daily price × 30 Annual price = Monthly price × 12

**Billable item management**

**Billable item**

A billable item defines how to price and charge a type of service. For example, ApsaraDB RDS is charged based on specifications and storage. In this case, the specifications and storage are two billable items. Each billable item defines the billing method and unit price of a type of service.

**Pricing**

The logic for determining the price of a particular feature of a cloud service per unit quantity is categorized into three types: **metered pricing**, **fixed pricing**, and **tiered pricing**.
**Metered pricing**: You are charged based on the service specifications and attribute
values. For example, Elastic Compute Service (ECS) provides a variety of instance types at different prices. Metering fields and values can be found in the metering data. The billing module obtains the values of specific metering fields from the metering data to determine the unit price of an instance. In addition, prices of specific services are not determined based only on specifications, and prices of instances with the same specifications may vary based on their regions. Therefore, in metered pricing mode, multiple metering fields are required for pricing.
**Fixed pricing**: You are charged at a fixed rate that does not change with variables within a
unit quantity. For example, you are charged for the storage capability based only on the amount of data because the storage capability does not involve specifications. In this case, the unit price is fixed.
**Tiered pricing**: You are charged different prices based on the service usage. You can
customize one or more usage ranges and specify a price for each range. If you configure tiered unit prices for a service capability, only metered quantities are supported.

**Quantity settings**

A quantity indicates the usage or a declared number of a resource. The following quantity types are supported:
**Fixed quantity**: The number of instances is fixed in each metered data record.
For example, you are charged for ECS instances based on specifications, and each metered data record is generated for one instance. In this case, the instance quantity is fixed to 1.
**Metered quantity**: The billing module uses the value of a specific numeric field in the
metered data as the quantity for billing. For example, the value of the Storage field in the metering data for Object Storage Service (OSS) indicates the storage usage. If you want to charge users for OSS based on the storage usage, you can configure the Storage field as the quantity. The unit used to measure metering data may not be the same as that used to determine the price. For example, OSS is billed per GB. However, the unit of the Storage field in the metering data may be Byte. Therefore, when you define a quantity, you need to specify a conversion factor to convert the value of a specific parameter in the metering data to a value in the unit of the price. For example, 1 GB is equal to 1,073,741,824 bytes. In this case, you need to set the conversion factor to 1073741824.

**Manage billable items**

1. In the Billable Item Configuration step of the **Pricing Configuration** panel, click **Create**
**Billable Item** in the **Billing Item Management** section.
2. In the **Create Billable Item** dialog box, configure the billable item.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|

| Billable Item Name | The name of the billable item. |
|---|---|
| Billing Method | The billing method of the billable item. By default, the billing method is the same as that in the billing configuration. |
| Unit Price Settings | The pricing model. Valid values: Quantity-based Price, Fixed Price, and Stepwise Pricing. If you select Quantity-based Price, you must configure the primary price of the cloud service and upload a pricing file. If secondary prices are supported for the cloud service, you can also add one or more secondary prices for the cloud service. To upload a pricing file, download a pricing template, specify the unit price in the pricing template, and then click Upload Price File to upload the pricing file. If you select Fixed Price, enter a fixed price. If you select Stepwise Pricing, configure the Match Mode and Stepwise Pricing Configuration parameters. |

|   | Match Mode: Select Graduated Pricing or Volume-based Pricing. Note You can specify pricing factors, such as primary and secondary prices. If you select a pricing factor, the Specified Price column is not displayed in the Stepwise Pricing Configuration table. Instead, the Download detailed pricing Template button is displayed. You must upload a pricing file. Graduated Pricing: The total cost is calculated by applying the unit price of the tier corresponding to the total usage Example: The unit price is USD 0.2 if the total used disk space falls into the 0 to 40 GB tier and USD 0.1 if the total used disk space exceeds 40 GB. In this case, if 50 GB of disk space is used, the fee is calculated based on the following formula: 50 × 0.1 = 5. Volume-based Pricing: The total cost is calculated by applying the corresponding unit price to the usage within each tier and summing the results. Example: The unit price is USD 0 if the used disk space falls into the 0 to 40 GB tier and USD 0.1 if the total used disk space exceeds 40 GB. In this case, if 50 GB of disk space is used, the fee is calculated based on the following formula: 40 × 0 + (50 - 40) × 0.1 = 1. Stepwise Pricing Configuration: Specify a tier and a price for the tier. Note You can click Add Interval to add more tiers and prices. You can click Delete in the Actions column to delete the tier and price. You can click Upload Price File to upload a pricing file. To upload a pricing file, download a pricing template, specify the prices in the pricing template, and then click Upload Price File to upload the pricing file. |
|---|---|

| Quantity Settings | A quantity indicates the usage or a declared number of a resource. Quantities are classified into fixed quantity and metered quantity. If the Quantity Type parameter is set to Quantity, the value of the Quantity parameter is set to a specification field used for metering. If you select Stepwise Pricing in the Unit Price Settings section, you can set the Quantity Type parameter only to Quantity, and only one entry can be configured in the Quantity Settings section. If the Quantity Type parameter is set to Fixed Quantity, the value of the Quantity parameter can be set to a custom value. Note You can click Add Quantity Settings to configure multiple entries. You can click Delete in the Actions column of an entry to delete the entry. At least one entry must be retained. |
|---|---|
| Billable item | If you set the Unit Price Settings parameter toQ uantity-based Price, the billable items are displayed based on the unit price settings and quantity settings. The billable item names are also displayed in other pricing models. |

3. Modify or delete the billable item based on your business requirements.
Modify a billable item. a. In the billable item list of the **Billing Item Management** section, find the billable item that you want to modify and click **Edit** in the **Actions** column. b. In the **Billing Item Details** dialog box, modify the billable item configurations. c. Click **OK**. Delete a billable item. a. In the billable item list of the **Billing Item Management** section, find the billable item that you want to delete and click **Delete** in the **Actions** column. b. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

A billing configuration is disabled. You are an operations administrator.

**Limits**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Pricing** > **Billing Rules**.
4. Go to the **Billing Configuration Detail** page of a billing configuration.
On the **Billing Rules** page, find the billing configuration that you want to enable and click its name. On the **Billing Rules** page, find the billing configuration that you want to enable and click
**Edit** in the **Actions** column.
5. In the upper-right corner of the **Billing Configuration Detail** page, click
next to Enable Configuration.
6. In the **Enable Configuration** message, click **OK**.

###### 7.2.8.3.12 Disable a billing configuration

You can disable an enabled billing configuration.

**Prerequisites**

The billing configuration is in the enabled status. The default operator is the operations administrator.

**Limits**

You cannot disable a preset pay-as-you-go billing configuration.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Pricing** > **Billing Rules**.
4. Go to the **Billing Configuration Detail** page.
On the **Billing Rules** page, click the name of the target billing configuration. On the **Billing Rules** page, click **Edit** in the **Actions** column of the target billing configuration.
5. In the upper-right corner of the **Billing Configuration Detail** page, click
next to
**Enable Configuration**.

> **Note:** To disable the last subscription billing configuration:
> If published subscription services exist, unpublish the services or change the billing method before you disable the configuration.
> If you disable the scubscription billing configuration while running subscription service instances exist, unexpired subscription resources automatically transitions to pay-as-you-go billing upon expiration.

6. In the **Disable configuration** dialog box, click **OK**.

###### 7.2.8.3.13 Export a price list

You can export the price list of a billing configuration if you want to save the pricing configurations of cloud services to your computer. This topic describes how to export a price list.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Pricing** > **Billing Rules**.
4. Go to the **Billing Configuration Detail** page of a billing configuration.
On the **Billing Rules** page, find the billing configuration for which you want to export a price list and click its name. On the **Billing Rules** page, find the billing configuration for which you want to export a price list and click **Edit** in the **Actions** column.
5. On the **Billing Configuration Detail** page, click **Export Price List** above the service
details list.

> **Note:** The price list of a billing configuration is exported as an **XLS** file.
> The price list file contains the organization, export time, start and end time of the billing configuration, and pricing configurations of each service. The pricing configurations include the service type, service name, billing method, pricing method, billable item description, billing field, specifications, prices, counting method, counting field, unit, and conversion factor.

###### 7.2.8.3.14 Clone a billing configuration

You can clone an existing billing configuration to create a similar billing configuration.

You are an operations administrator.

**Limits**

The billing method of the cloned billing configuration is the same as that of the original billing configuration and cannot be modified.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Pricing** > **Billing Rules**.

configuration. For more information about the parameters, see Create a billing configuration.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Pricing** > **Billing Rules**.

##### 7.2.8.4 Manage discount rules

You can manage discount rules for specified organizations or products.

**Discount rule permissions in different states**

> **Note:** Discount rules may be in the following states. Different operations can be performed in different states. In the following table, √ indicates that the operation is supported. × indicates that the operation is not supported.

| Status/Operation | Detai ls | Edit | Enab le | Disa ble | Dele te | Can cel | Request details |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enable | ✓ | X | X | ✓ | X | X | X |
| Disable | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | X | ✓ | X | X |
| Enable (being approved for disabling) | ✓ | X | X | X | X | ✓ | ✓ |
| Enable (approval for disabling rejected) | ✓ | ✓ | X | ✓ | X | X | ✓ |
| Enable (failed to disable) | ✓ | ✓ | X | ✓ | X | X | X |
| Disable (being approved for enabling) | ✓ | X | X | X | X | ✓ | ✓ |
| Disable (approval for enabling rejected) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | X | ✓ | X | ✓ |
| Disable (failed to enable) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | X | ✓ | X | X |

**Prerequisites**

You have logged on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console as an operations administrator.

**Create a discount rule**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Pricing** > **Discount Management**.
4. On the **Discount Management** page, click **Create Discount Rule**.
5. In the **Create Discount Rule** panel, configure parameters in the **Basic Configuration**
and **Discount Configuration** step. i. **Basic Configuration**

| Parameter |   | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Basic Informatio n | Rule Name | The name of the discount rule. The name must be 2 to 128 characters in length. It cannot start or end with a space. |
|   | Description | The description of the discount rule. |
| Rule Configurati on | Effective Scope | The organizations for which the discount rule takes effect. Valid values: Global and Specified Organization. |
|   | Specified Organizatio n | This parameter is displayed only if the Effective Scope parameter is set to Specified Organization. Select an organization from the drop-down list. You can select multiple organizations. |
|   | Effective Time | The time when the discount rule takes effect. |
|   | Priority | The priority of the discount rule. Valid values: 0 to 99. Click the text box to display the existing priority values. Note You must enter a new priority value. |

ii. **Discount Configuration**
**Unified Discount**: By default, a unified discount is applied to all products. Enter a
positive integer less than or equal to 1000 in the test box. Unit: %.
**Specified Product**: The unified discount text box is not displayed. You must enter a
positive integer less than or equal to 1000 (unit: %) next to each product.

> **Note:** If a product is added to the cloud platform, the product is added to the discount rule with the 100% discount by default.

iii. Click **Submit**.

**View discount rules**

and **Organization** to filter discount rules.

**Description**, **Effective Scope**, **Effective Time**, **Priority**, **Status**, **Operator**, and **Update**
**Time**.

information in the **Basic Information** and **Rule Details** sections.

column.
2. In the **Edit Discount Rule** panel, modify the settings of the discount rule. For more
information about the configuration items, see Create a discount rule.

**Enable a discount rule**

1. On the **Discount Management** page, find the discount rule and click **Enable** in the
**Actions** column.
2. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

**Disable a discount rule**

> **Important:** A discount rule will not be used in cost calculations after it is disabled.

1. On the **Discount Management** page, find the discount rule and click **Enable** in the
**Actions** column.
2. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

**Delete a discount rule**

1. On the **Discount Management** page, find the discount rule and click **Enable** in the
**Actions** column.
2. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

**Revoke a discount rule**

1. On the **Discount Management** page, find the discount rule, click
in the **Actions** column, and select **Revoke**.
2. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

**View the approval details of a discount rule**

> **Important:** Only after approval is enabled, you can view the approval details of the discount rules in the Being Approved or Approval Rejected state. For more information about how to create an approval process and how to bind an approval process to an operation, see Process approval.

1. On the **Discount Management** page, find the discount rule, click
in the **Actions** column, and select **Approval Details**.

##### 7.2.8.5 Deduction management

You can deduct billable usage and fees for resources based on your business requirements.

###### 7.2.8.5.1 Create a deduction rule

This topic describes how to create a deduction rule on the Deductions page.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Pricing** > **Deductions**.
4. On the Deductions page, click **Create Deduction Rule**.
5. In the **Create Deduction Rule** panel, configure the parameters in the Basic Configurations
step. The following table describes the parameters.

| Parameter |   | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Basic Informati on | Rule Name | The name of the deduction rule. |
|   | Descripti on | The description of the deduction rule. |
| Rule Configur ation | Effective Scope | The effective scope of the deduction rule. Valid values: Global, Specified Organization, and Specified Resource Set. |
|   | Specified Organizat ion | This parameter is displayed only if the Effective Scope parameter is set to Specified Organization. You can select one or more organizations from the drop-down list. |
|   | Resource Set | This parameter is displayed only if the Effective Scope parameter is set to Specified Resource Set. You can select one or more resource sets from the drop-down list. |
|   | Effective At | The start and end time of the validity period of the deduction rule. |

6. Click **Next**.
7. In the Deduction Configuration step, click **Add Deduction Rule**.

> **Note:** You can add multiple deduction rules.
> After a deduction rule is added, you can click **Edit** or **Delete** in the **Actions** column to modify or delete the deduction rule.

8. In the **Add Deduction Rule** dialog box, configure the parameters that are described in the
following table.

| Paramete r | Description |
|---|---|
| Deducte d Services | The cloud service and resource item to which the deduction rule applies. You need to select a cloud service first before you can select a resource item. |

| Deductio n Scope | The effective scope of the deduction rule. Valid values: All, By Instance, and By Condition. If you set the Deduction Scope parameter to By Instance, you must enter one or more instance IDs in the Instance ID field. Separate multiple instance IDs with commas (,) or line feeds. If you set the Deduction Scope parameter to By Condition, you must specify the filter condition. The deduction rule takes effect only if the specified filter condition is met. A filter condition consists of the Field and Value parameters. If the value of a field in the metering data is the same as the specified value of the Value parameter, the metering data meets the filter condition. Note You can click Add Filter Condition to add a filter condition. You can add multiple filter conditions. You can click Delete in the Actions column of a filter condition to delete the filter condition. If you set the Deduction Scope parameter to By Condition, at least one filter condition must be retained. If you select And, the deduction rule takes effect only if all the specified filter conditions are met. If you select Or, the deduction rule takes effect if one of the specified filter conditions is met. |
|---|---|
| Deductio n Content | The billable items to which the deduction rule applies. Valid values:A ll or By Billable Item. If you set the Deduction Content parameter to By Billable Item, you must configure the Metering Table and Billable Item parameters and enter a specific deduction amount in the Deduction Amount field. |
| Effective Period | The validity period of the deduction rule. Valid values: Effective Period of Current Rule and Since Instance Creation. You can select Since Instance Creation only for specific services. If you select Since Instance Creation, you must configure the Duration parameter to specify the validity period of the deduction rule. Unit: day or month. |

9. Click **OK**.
0. Click **Submit**.
