##### 7.2.8.6 Rule template configuration

###### 7.2.8.6.1 Billing rule templates

###### 7.2.8.6.1.1 Create a billing rule template

You can create billing rule templates based on your business requirements. This topic describes how to create a billing rule template.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Pricing** > **Rule Template Configuration**.
4. Optional. Configure the **Cloud Services**, **Resource Item**, and **Status** parameters and
click **Search** to filter billing rule templates.

> **Note:** The following options are available in the **Status** drop-down list: **Not Configured**, **Configured**, **Delete Service**, and **Unpublish Service**.

5. Find and click the resource card that you require to go to the **Rule Template** page.
6. On the **Billing Rule Template** tab, click **Create Rule**.
7. Configure the parameters in the **Basic Information**, **Rule Settings**, and **Price Query**
**Settings** steps as prompted.

> **Note:** The Price Query Settings step is displayed only for third-party custom cloud services. After price query settings are configured for a cloud service, prices can be displayed on the activation, configuration change, purchase, and Configure, Price, Quote (CPQ) and pricing (price calculator, configuration list, and service pricing) pages of the service.

**Basic Information**

In the **Basic Information** step, configure the metering table, billing cycle, and billing field settings of the billing rule template.

| Paramet er | Description |
|---|---|
| Meteri ng Table | The metering table to be associated with the billing rule template. Select a metering table from the Metering Table drop-down list. |
| Billing Cycle | The billing cycle for the selected metering table. |
| Billing Field Setting s | Click Add Field. Configure the parameters, including Billing Field, Field Type, Usage Unit for Billing, and Conversion Factor. Note The system automatically configures the fields of the Specifications type with data of the configured service specifications. Find the billing field that you want to remove and clickR emove in the Actions column to remove the billing field. |

**Rule Settings**

You need to add billing rules, including the billable item configuration and price settings.
1. In the **Rule Settings** step, click **Create Billing Rule**.
2. In the **Pricing Template Configuration** panel, configure the parameters in the **Billable**
**Item Configuration** and **Price Settings** steps. For more information about billable item
configuration and pricing settings, see Manage pricing configurations.

**Price Query Settings**

In the **Price Query Settings** step, configure price query settings. You can select Field Mapping Configuration or Code Configuration.

**Field Mapping Configuration**

You can complete price query settings by configuring field mapping.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Required Fields for Price Query by Using Form | From the Form Fields drop-down list, select the fields for price query by using a form. The organizationId and regionId fields are required. |

| Billing Field Mapping Configurat ion | Configure the mapping between billing fields and form fields. You can add or remove fields. If you select No Mapped Form Field in the Form Fields column, you can select Integer, Boolean Value, String, or Empty in the Default Value column. Set Billing Field to a fixed value. The value can be a Boolean value, a numeric value, or a character. If Empty is selected in the Default Value column, the value of the configured billing field is calculated based on the extended rule. The system saves the form fields in the context. Groovy expressions are supported. Scenario 1: Unit conversion. The billing rule charges for the systemDisk field. The unit in the context is GB. However, the billing rule charges for this field based on the unit of MB. Therefore, you need to configure the following expression in the corresponding extended rule: systemDisk × 1024 . Note Other unit conversions follow the same principle. To perform quantity operations, you must first confirm the field types in the context. Only fields of the integer type can be used for quantity operations. If a field is not of the integer type, you must first convert the field type by using relevant Groovy syntax. Scenario 2: String processing. The billing rule charges for the spec field. The value of the spec field in the context is small. However, all enumerated fields configured for the spec field in the billing rule contain the ecs prefix. For example, the price of the ecs-small specification is 2. In this case, to concatenate the ecs string for the spec field, you need to configure "ecs-" + spec in the extended rule. Scenario 3: Context field computing The billing rule charges for the total disk size. The total disk size is calculated based on the systemDisk, dataDisk, and dataNum fields. Total disk size = System disk size + Data disk size × Number of data disks. Configure systemDisk + dataDisk × dataNum in the extended rule. |
|---|---|

| Instance Informatio n Mapping | Instance information mapping must be configured only in the configuration change, unsubscription, or renewal scenarios. This way, you can query the billing amount from the instance details. In the configuration change scenario, instance information mappings are first used to query the price before the change, and then used to calculate the price difference before and after the configuration change. In the unsubscription or renewal scenario, instance information mappings are used to query the monthly price of the instance, and then calculate the refund amount of the unsubscription or the renewal fee. To configure the instance information mapping, you must query the instance to obtain the instance details. Then, enter the details field as the configuration input. For more information about how to obtain the instance details, see Configure price query settings. |
|---|---|

**Code Configuration**

In the code editor, you can write code for price query settings. The code configuration method provides a more customized and comprehensive price query capability and allows you to configure mappings by using code. The price query settings are used to convert the parameters in forms or instance details into the corresponding billing field data and obtain a price based on billing rules. Therefore, to write the code for price query settings, you must parse the data in forms or instance details. For more information about code configuration, see Configure price query settings. ###### 7.2.8.6.1.2 View the details of a billing rule template

**template**

This topic describes how to view the details of a billing rule template.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Pricing** > **Rule Template Configuration**.
4. Optional. Specify **Cloud Services**, **Resource Item**, and **Status** and click **Search** to filter
rule templates.

> **Note:** The following options are available in the **Status** drop-down list: **Not Configured**, **Configured**, **Delete Service**, and **Unpublish Service**.

5. Click a resource card to go to the **Rule Template** page.
6. On the **Billing Rule Template** tab, view the billing rule templates of the service.
7. Find the billing rule template that you want to view, and click **Details** in the Actions
column.
8. On the **Rule Template Details** page, view the detailed configurations.

###### 7.2.8.6.1.3 Modify a billing rule template

You can modify the settings of a billing rule template based on your business requirements.

**Prerequisites**

Billing rule templates are in the **Disable** state. You are an operations administrator.

**Limits**

Preset billing rule templates cannot be modified.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Pricing** > **Rule Template Configuration**.
4. Optional. Configure the **Cloud Services**, **Resource Item**, and **Status** parameters as filter
conditions and click **Search**.

> **Note:** Valid values of the **Status** parameter: **Not Configured**, **Configured**, **Delete Service**, and **Unpublish Service**.

5. Find and click the card for the resource type that you want to manage to go to the **Rule**
**Template** page.
6. On the **Billing Rule Template** tab, find the template that you want to modify and click
**Modify** in the Actions column.
7. On the **Modify Rule Template** page, modify the settings of the billing rule template. For
more information about the parameters, see Create a billing rule template.

###### 7.2.8.6.1.4 Enable a billing rule template

You can enable a disabled billing rule template. After a billing rule template is enabled, you can use it for billing rule configuration.

**Prerequisites**

Billing rule templates are in the **Disable** state. Metering tables associated with billing rule templates are in the **Enable** state. You are an operations administrator.

**Limits**

You can enable only one custom billing rule template for the billing rule configuration of a single resource type. If both an enabled custom billing rule template and a preset billing rule template are used for the billing rule configuration of a single resource type, the custom billing rule template takes precedence over the preset billing rule template.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Pricing** > **Rule Template Configuration**.
4. Optional. Configure the **Cloud Services**, **Resource Item**, and **Status** parameters as filter
conditions and click **Search**.

> **Note:** Valid values of the **Status** parameter: **Not Configured**, **Configured**, **Delete Service**, and **Unpublish Service**.

5. Find and click the card for the resource type that you want to manage to go to the **Rule**
**Template** page.
6. On the **Billing Rule Template** tab, find the template that you want to enable and click
**Enable** in the Actions column.
7. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

###### 7.2.8.6.1.5 Disable a billing rule template

You can disable an enabled billing rule template. After a billing rule template is disabled, you can no longer use it for billing rule configuration.

**Prerequisites**

Billing rule templates are in the **Enable** state. You are an operations administrator.

**Limits**

Preset billing rule templates cannot be disabled.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Pricing** > **Rule Template Configuration**.
4. Optional. Configure the **Cloud Services**, **Resource Item**, and **Status** parameters as filter
conditions and click **Search**.

> **Note:** Valid values of the **Status** parameter: **Not Configured**, **Configured**, **Delete Service**, and **Unpublish Service**.

5. Find and click the card for the resource type that you want to manage to go to the **Rule**
**Template** page.
6. On the **Billing Rule Template** tab, find the template that you want to disable and click
**Disable** in the Actions column.
7. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

###### 7.2.8.6.1.6 Configure price query settings

This topic describes how to configure price query settings in billing rule templates.

**Field mapping configurations**

**Instance information mappings**

The configuration of instance information mappings is required only in scenarios that involve configuration changes, unsubscription, or renewal. Instance information mappings can be used to query the corresponding billing amount from instance details. In a configuration change scenario, instance information mappings are first used to query the price before the change, and then used to calculate the price difference before and after the configuration change. In an unsubscription or renewal scenario, instance information mappings are first used to query the monthly subscription price of an instance, and then used to calculate the refund for the unsubscription or the fee for the renewal.

**Obtaining of instance details**

Unlike directly obtaining form fields from an frontend page as the input, the configuration of instance information mappings requires querying the relevant instance to retrieve instance details, and then using the instance details fields as the input. The system calls the `CloudSearchResources` operation to query instance details, and places the instance details fields into the context. When you configure instance information mappings in the console, specify the instance details fields in the Instance Field column. For example, the following response is returned if the system calls the CloudSearchResources operation to query a third-party cloud service instance: `{`

`}` The following code shows the fields in the returned `detail` parameter after JSON serialization. These fields are the instance details fields that you can specify in the Instance Field column when you configure instance information mappings in the console. In this example, instance details fields include `organizationId, instanceId, regionId,` `resourceSetId, spec, systemDisk, dataDisk, dataNum, and instanceUrl` . If additional operations are required on the details data, the operations can be configured in extension rules. `{`


`}`

**Extension rules**

Extension rules support Groovy expressions. The context variables of Groovy expressions can be form fields or instance details fields. When the data source for a price query is a form on a frontend page, such as billing field mappings for a new purchase or configuration change, the Groovy expression context includes all form fields. When the data source for a price query is instance details, such as instance information mappings for a configuration change, unsubscription, or renewal, the Groovy expression context consists of instance details fields. For example, the context variables include the following fields: `{`

```json
  "organizationId": "3",
  "instanceId": "31313123313",
  "regionId": "cn-wulan-env***-d01",
  "resourceSetId": 2,
  "spec": "small",
  "systemDisk": 10,
  "dataDisk": 15,
  "dataNum": 2,
  "instanceUrl":
"https://one.console.con.shuguang.com/test/console/instance/detail/info? InstanceId=31313123313"
```

`}`

**Scenario 1: Unit conversion**

A billing rule involves charges for the systemDisk field. The unit in the context is GB, but the billing rule requires charging based on the unit of MB. Therefore, the following expression is configured in the corresponding extension rule: `systemDisk * 1024` .

> **Note:** Other unit conversions follow the same principle.
> To perform quantity operations, you must first confirm the field types in the context. Only integers can be used for quantity operations. If a field is not of an integer type, you must first convert the field type by using relevant Groovy syntax.

**Scenario 2: String processing**

|   | spec |
|---|---|
| spec |   |

A billing rule involves charges for the `spec` field. The value of the `spec` field in the context is small. However, all enumeration fields configured for `spec` in the billing rule include the ecs prefix. For example, the price for the ecs-small specification is 2. In this

| tring for | spec , |
|---|---|
| "ecs-" + spec |   |

corresponding extension rule: `"ecs-" + spec` .

**Scenario 3: Context field calculation**

A billing rule involves charges for the total disk size, which requires the combination of the `systemDisk, dataDisk, and dataNum` fields for billing. The total disk size is calculated by using the following formula: Total disk size = System disk size + Data disk size × Number of data disks. Therefore, the following expression is configured in the corresponding extension rule: `systemDisk + dataDisk * dataNum` .

**Code configurations**

Code configurations offer more customizable and comprehensive price query capabilities, allowing you to configure mappings by using pure code. The essence of price query settings is to convert fields from forms or instance details into corresponding billing field data, which is then used by billing rules to obtain a price. Therefore, price query settings require the parsing of form data or instance details data.

**product**

Required. The billable item code of the cloud service in price query settings. If the cloud service is provided by a third party, this field specifies the cloud service code generated when the cloud service was created. The billable item code for such a cloud service is consistent with the cloud service code. If the cloud service is provided by Apsara Stack, this field specifies the billable item code of the cloud service in the corresponding preset billing rule. Alternatively, you can configure and submit field mappings in price query settings. After the configurations are saved, you can obtain the value of the `productPriceQueryConfigForAll.product` field. Then, you can configure code in price query settings.

**resourceType**

Required. The resource type of the cloud service in price query settings. If the cloud service is provided by a third party, this field specifies the unique identifier generated when the resource type was created. If the cloud service is provided by Apsara Stack, this field specifies the resource type code after the number sign (#) in the value of the

| CatalogConfig.resourceType _ |   | field obtai |
|---|---|---|
| example, the value is |   |   |

`_CatalogConfig.resourceType` field obtained from the form fields for new purchases. In this example, the value is `ecs#ecs_instance` , and `ecs_instance` after the number sign (#) is the resource type code. Alternatively, you can configure and submit field mappings in price query settings. After the configurations are saved, you can obtain the value of the `productPriceQueryConfigForAll.resourceType` field. Then, you can configure code in price query settings.

**type**

Required. The configuration type of price query settings. For code configurations, set the value to `JSON` .

**priceQueryForNew.departmentIdKey**

Optional. The key of the organization ID field in the new purchase form. If no value is specified, Department or organizationId is used. If a value other than Department and organizationId is used in some new purchase forms, such as department, you must analyze and confirm the value.

**priceQueryForNew.regionIdKey**

Optional. The key of the region ID field in the new purchase form. If no value is specified, RegionId or regionId is used. If a value other than RegionId and regionId is used in some new purchase forms, such as _regionId, you must analyze and confirm the value.

**priceQueryForNew.priceQueryRequiredFields**

Required. The basic price query fields. A price query is initiated only if the values of these fields are not empty. If the `priceQueryRequiredFieldsAny` field is specified, the specified fields are also required. You must select at least the form fields that specify the organization ID and region ID. A detailed analysis of the billing fields and the new purchase page is required to determine the specific basic price query fields.

**priceQueryForNew.priceQueryRequiredFieldsAny**

Optional. The incremental price query fields, which are designed for dynamic scenarios involving required fields. The value of this field is a two-dimensional array. A price query is initiated when the form fields include both the basic price query fields and one of incremental price query fields. Example: Elastic Compute Service (ECS) has the `OSType` and `OSNameEn` billing fields, which are obtained based on the image ID selected on the relevant page. However, the key of the image ID field in the new purchase form changes dynamically based on the image type ( `_imageType` ) selected in the form: If `_imageType = "system"` is specified, the key of the image ID field is `ImageId` . If `_imageType = "self"` is specified, the key of the image ID field is `customImage` . If `_imageType = "others"` is specified, the key of the image ID field is `shareImage` . If `_imageType = "others2"` is specified, the key of the image ID field is `publicImage` . In this case, four incremental price query fields are required for price queries involving dynamic scenarios.

**priceQueryForNew.priceQueryAgainForValueChangedFields**

Required. The fields for re-initiating a price query. This indicates that a price query must be re-initiated if the value corresponding to one of these fields changes. A detailed analysis of the billing fields and the new purchase page is required to determine the fields for re-initiating a price query. When the values of these fields in the new purchase form change, the price query results are affected and a price query must be re-initiated.

**priceQueryForNew.priceQueryProducts**

Required. The expressions for mapping form fields to billing fields for a price query of a billable resource. The system uses the defined methods to calculate the values of the corresponding fields from form fields. This list of values is then passed to the billing rule involved to obtain the actual price. product: required. The billable item code for which a price query is requested in a billing rule. billingFields: a list. Each element in the list represents the method for obtaining the value of a billing field. Each element consists of four fields: key, valueExpression, valueExpressionType, and defaultValue. You need to specify only one of the `billingFields` and `billingFieldExpression` fields. key: the corresponding billing field. valueExpression: the value expression. The system supports the direct mapping of context fields or complex operations by using Groovy expressions. valueExpressionType: the type of the value expression. This field can be left empty if the `valueExpression` field specifies the direct mapping of context fields. If a Groovy operation is required, set this field to GROOVY_EXPRESSION. defaultValue: the default value to use if the corresponding value cannot be obtained by using the value expression specified by the `valueExpression` field. billingFieldExpression: Use this field in the following cases: when the billingFields field cannot meet your price query requirements, when the billing fields cannot be obtained by using mapping or calculation, and when multiple price queries are to be performed and the results need to be summed up. You need to specify only one of the `billingFields` and `billingFieldExpression` fields. For example, the new purchase page for an ECS instance allows you to select multiple data disks of different specifications. In this case, multiple price queries are performed and the prices are summed up.

**Examples of using billingFields**

**When the billing data is consistent with the data of a form field**

Scenario: The billing data required by the billing rule involved is consistent with the data of a form field. Examples: ECS specifications: Both the relevant field in the new purchase form and the billing field are InstanceType. ApsaraDB RDS specifications: The relevant field in the new purchase form is DBInstanceClass, and the billing field is ClassCode. Configurations: `{`

```json
    "key": "InstanceType",
    "valueExpression": "InstanceType"
```

`}` `{`

```json
    "key": "ClassCode",
    "valueExpression": "DBInstanceClass"
```

`}`

**When the billing data needs to be calculated from form fields**

Scenario: The billing data required by the billing rule involved cannot be obtained directly from form fields and requires logic operations. In this case, a Groovy expression is needed. Examples: VPN specifications: The relevant field in the new purchase form is Bandwidth, and the billing field is Spec. The value of the Bandwidth field is a number, such as 5. However, the Spec field in the billing rule requires a unit, such as M. Therefore, the value of the Bandwidth field needs to be converted. In this case, a Groovy expression is required, and the value expression is set to "Bandwidth + \"M\"". ECS operating system type: The billing field is OSType, which can be found in the Image list under the Images field in the new purchase form. In this case, a Groovy expression is required, and the value expression is set to "Images.Image[0].OSType". Configurations: `{`

```json
  "key": "Spec",
  "valueExpression": "Bandwidth + \"M\"",
  "valueExpressionType": "GROOVY_EXPRESSION"
```

`}` `{`

```json
  "key": "OSType",
  "valueExpression": "Images.Image[0].OSType",
  "valueExpressionType": "GROOVY_EXPRESSION"
```

`}`

**When the billing data is a fixed value**

Scenario: The billing data for an item is not obtained from a form, but needs to be set to a fixed value. Examples: Flink used core-hours: The billing field is CpuUsed. For a new purchase, no used corehours are involved and a unit quantity needs to be displayed. Therefore, the default value is set to a unit quantity. Take note that the corresponding conversion factor for the billing field must be considered. If the conversion factor is 3, the default value is set to 3. ECS GPU specifications: The billing field is GPUSpec. However, ECS does not have GPU specifications. Therefore, the default value is set to ASCM_SPEC_EMPTY, indicating no charge for the specifications. Configurations: `{`

```json
  "key": "CpuUsed",
  "defaultValue": 1
```

`}` `{`

```json
  "key": "GPUSpec",
  "defaultValue": "ASCM_SPEC_EMPTY"
```

`}`

**Examples of using billingFieldExpression**

Scenario: Billing field mappings are highly complex and cannot be complete with simple configurations. In this case, an expression is required to directly generate the list of price query fields. For example, for an ECS disk price query during a new purchase, the system disk field is required and only one specification option is available. However, you can specify multiple data disks with different specifications for the data disk field. A single mapping cannot generate the full list of billing fields required to complete the entire price query. Therefore, a Groovy expression can be used to directly generate multiple sets of billing fields, perform multiple price queries, and then aggregate the results at the framework layer. Configurations:

```json
// Define the system disk information. def SystemDiskNew = [
    "DiskCategory": SystemDisk.Category,
    "DiskSize": SystemDisk.Size
```

`]`

```python

If the variable exists, a ssign values. Otherwise, use an empty list. if (binding.variables.containsKey("DataDisk")) {
    DataDiskList = DataDisk ?: []
```

`}`

```json
        def num = disk.Num

```


###### 7.2.8.6.1.7 Edit the billing origin of a rule template

**template**

Edit the billing origin for third-party products.

**Prerequisites**

Only non-Alibaba public cloud products that are integrated through product management support editing the billing origin.

**Operator**

By default, the operator is the operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Service Pricing** > **Rule Template Management**.
4. (Optional) Set the **Cloud Service**, **Resource Item**, and **Status** filter conditions, then click
**Search**.

> **Note:** **Status** includes **Not configured**, **Configured, Product deleted**, and **Unpublish** **Service**.

5. Click a resource card to go to the **Rule Template** page.
6. In the **Basic information** section, click **Edit**.
7. On the **Edit Rule Template** page, update the billing origin.

> **Note:** The billing origin supports **System Generated** and **External Import**.
> **System Generated**: The system generates billing data based on metering data.
> **External Import**: Obtain billing data through an API. If the billing origin is external import, the bill audit does not perform verification. Resources with external import do not generate billing data according to billing rules.

8. Click **OK**.

###### 7.2.8.6.2 Alibaba Cloud mapping configurations

###### 7.2.8.6.2.1 Configure mappings to Alibaba Cloud multiplier pricing

**multiplier pricing**

This topic describes how to configure mappings to Alibaba Cloud multiplier pricing.

**Purpose of multiplier pricing mappings**

Multiplier pricing mappings associate the billing resources of Alibaba Cloud with Apsara Stack resources. This enables resale pricing based on original Alibaba Cloud bills by applying a configured multiplier.

**How the mappings work**

A resource type of Apsara Stack can be mapped to a group of billable items on Alibaba Cloud. After the mappings are configured, the system synchronizes the original Alibaba Cloud bills every day. Based on the mappings, the system applies the configured multiplier to the billable items on Alibaba Cloud and generates bills that belong to the mapped resource type. Take note of the following rules when you configure the mappings:
1. In most cases, a resource type is mapped to one or more billable items of a single Alibaba
Cloud service (with a specific pipCode value). For example, for the resource type "XX resale resource", you can map all billable items of Alibaba Cloud Function Compute to this resource type.
2. The mappings configured for a resource type consist of multiple mapping rules. Each
mapping rule contains three fields: Service Code, Product Code, and Billable Item Code. The smallest granularity is Billable Item Code.
3. Each mapping rule can be configured in one of the following forms:
Service Code: AA. Product Code: BB. Billable Item Code: CC. This is exact mapping. When an exact mapping rule is applied, the system maps the bills of only specified billable items to the mapped resource type. Service Code: AA. Product Code: *. Billable Item Code: *. This is fuzzy mapping. When a fuzzy mapping rule is applied, the system maps the bills of all billable items of the Alibaba Cloud service AA to the mapped resource type. Fuzzy mapping simplifies configuration and allows you to efficiently map the bills of an Alibaba Cloud service to a resource type.

**Source of fields for multiplier pricing mappings**

Log in to the Alibaba Cloud Management Console. Go to the **Expenses and Costs** console and choose **Billing** > **Bill Details**. In the bill list, check the Product Code, Commodity Code, and Billable Item Code fields, which can be used for configuring multiplier pricing mappings. If you want to map all billable items of a specific Alibaba Cloud service to a resource type of Apsara Stack, obtain the value of the Product Code field from the bill details on Alibaba Cloud and specify it as the value of the Service Code field in the billing rule template of the resource type on Apsara Stack. In addition, set both the Product Code and Billable Item Code fields to an asterisk (*) on Apsara Stack.

> **Note:** If the bills of an Alibaba Cloud service fail to be synchronized, go to the Bill Details page in the Alibaba Cloud Management Console, click **Back to Old Version** in the upper-right corner, and then obtain the value of the Product Code field for configuring multiplier pricing mappings.

###### 7.2.8.6.2.2 Modify mappings

You can configure mappings between the billing resources of Alibaba Cloud and Apsara Stack resources. After you configure the mappings, you can apply the service multiplier pricing method of Alibaba Cloud to Apsara Stack resources.

**Prerequisites**

A third-party custom cloud service is hosted on Alibaba Cloud. You are an operations administrator.

**Limits**

If a cloud service has preset Alibaba Cloud mapping configurations, you cannot modify those mappings.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Pricing** > **Rule Template Configuration**.
4. Optional. Configure the **Cloud Services**, **Resource Item**, and **Status** parameters as filter
conditions and click **Search**.

> **Note:** Valid values of the **Status** parameter: **Not Configured**, **Configured**, **Delete Service**, and **Unpublish Service**.

5. Find and click the card for the resource type that you want to manage to go to the **Rule**
**Template** page.
6. On the **Public Cloud Mapping Configuration** tab, click **Modify Mapping**.
7. In the **Public Cloud Mapping Configuration** panel, click **Add**. Enter values in the
**Service Code**, **Product Code**, and **Billable Item Code** fields to configure mappings.

| Para met er | Description |
|---|---|
| Serv ice Cod e | The code of the Alibaba Cloud service to map to. Example: ecs. |
| Prod uct Cod e | The code of the service resource to map to. Examples: * and snapshot. A value of an asterisk (*) indicates all resources. |
| Billa ble Item Cod e | The code of the billable item to map to. Examples: * and SystemDiskSize. A value of an asterisk (*) indicates all billable items. |

Mapping configuration examples:

> **Important:** Exact and fuzzy mapping rules are mutually exclusive.
> If the billable items of an Alibaba Cloud service are mapped to a resource type of Apsara Stack by using an exact mapping rule, no fuzzy mapping rules can be configured to map the billable items of this Alibaba Cloud service.
> If the billable items of an Alibaba Cloud service are mapped to a resource type of Apsara Stack by using a fuzzy mapping rule, no exact mapping rules can be configured to map the billable items of this Alibaba Cloud service.
> The combination of Service Code, Product Code, and Billable Item Code in each exact mapping rule must be unique. If a combination of Service Code, Product Code, and Billable Item Code is configured as an exact mapping rule for a resource type of Apsara Stack, this combination cannot be configured as an exact mapping rule for another resource type of Apsara Stack.
> When you configure exact mapping rules, make sure that all billable item codes that exist on the site are covered by the configured mappings.

To map all billable items of Alibaba Cloud Elastic Compute Service (ECS) to a resource type of Apsara Stack, enter ecs in the **Service Code** field, * in the **Product Code** field, and * in the **Billable Item Code** field. This is fuzzy mapping. To map the Size billable item of snapshots of Alibaba Cloud ECS to a resource type of Apsara Stack, enter ecs in the **Service Code** field, snapshot in the **Product Code** field, and Size in the **Billable Item Code** field.

###### 7.2.8.6.2.3 View Alibaba Cloud mapping configurations

## configurations

**Prerequisites**

5. Find and click the card for the resource type that you want to manage to go to the **Rule**
**Template** page.
6. On the **Public Cloud Mapping Configuration** tab, view the preset and custom Alibaba
Cloud mapping configurations.

#### 7.2.9 Coupon

##### 7.2.9.1 Coupon management

The system provides manageable coupon campaigns. You can create, manage, and distribute coupons.

###### 7.2.9.1.1 Create a coupon

Create a coupon, including its basic information and rule configuration.

**Prerequisites**

The operating user defaults to the Operations Administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Coupon** > **Coupon Management**.
4. Click **Create Coupon**.
5. In the **Create Coupon** panel, configure the basic information and rule settings for the
coupon.

| Configuration item |   | Description |
|---|---|---|
|   | Coupon Name | Enter the name of the coupon. |
|   | Coupon Type | Select the type of coupon. Currently, only the Voucher type is supported. |

| sara Uni-mana |   |   |
|---|---|---|
| Basic Informatio n |   |   |
|   | Description | Enter a description for the coupon. |
|   | Coupon Validity Period | Set the start and end dates for the coupon validity period. |
| Rule Configurat ion | Total Issued Amount | Enter the total number of coupons to issue. |
|   | Single Coupon Amount | Enter the discount amount per coupon. |
|   | Applicable Resources | Select the resources to which the coupon applies. You can choose All resources, Applicable to Specified Resources, or Inapplicable to Specified Resources. |
|   | Resource | This setting is required if you select Applicable to Specified Resources or Inapplicable to Specified Resources. Specify the exact resources that can or cannot use the coupon. |
|   | Applicable Organization | Select the organizations to which the coupon applies. You can choose All organizations or Specify Organization. |
|   | Amount Limit | Set the spending threshold for using the coupon. You can choose No Minimum Spend or Available when spending exceeds XX. If a threshold is set, the coupon becomes usable only when the order or bill amount exceeds this limit. |
|   | Validity Period | Set the usage validity period for the coupon. You can choose Same as Coupon Validity Period, Immediately Effective upon Issuance, or Effective after XX days from issuance, valid for XX days. Same as Coupon Validity Period: The expiration time of each generated coupon matches the overall coupon validity period. Immediately Effective upon Issuance: Validity is calculated in calendar days. For example, if you set immediate effect with 2-day validity and the user claims the coupon at 14:00 on May 21, the coupon is valid from 14:00:00 on May 21 to 23:59:59 on May 22. Effective after XX days from issuance, valid for XX days: Both activation and validity are calculated in calendar days. For example, if you set 2-day activation delay and 2- day validity, and the user claims the coupon at 14:00 on May 21, the coupon is valid from 00:00:00 on May 23 to 23:59:59 on May 24. |

6. Click OK.

###### 7.2.9.1.10 Coupon redemption rules

This topic describes coupon redemption rules.

> **Note:** Public Cloud Subscription Billing (Multiplier Pricing): The system redeems coupons based on bills.
> A coupon supports multiple uses. You can apply one coupon per order or bill.
> In CPQ, one coupon can associate with only one service configuration.

**Apply at order confirmation**

When you purchase subscription resources (such as Subscription ECS instances), the system matches available coupons based on product and amount attributes of the order. The system automatically filters and displays applicable coupons on the submission page. You can manually select one coupon for deduction. Usage quantity: You can apply one coupon per order. A single coupon can offset multiple orders within its validity period until its balance is exhausted. Automatic matching recommendation: If multiple coupons are available, the system recommends or prioritizes usage in the following order: i. Prioritize coupons with larger remaining balances. ii. Prioritize coupons with earlier expiration dates. iii. Prioritize coupons issued earlier. Refund upon exception: The system redeems coupons in successfully created orders. To refund and reuse a coupon, you must first cancel the unsuccessful order. After order cancellation, the coupon returns to the "Available" status. Renewal coupon usage: When you manually renew a resource, the renewal payment page displays applicable coupons. You can choose whether to use them. When you enable autorenewal, the system automatically selects and applies an applicable coupon according to predefined rules. Budget deduction: If the order amount remains after all coupons are applied, the system deducts the remaining amount from your budget.

**Automatic deduction after bill generation**

For Pay-As-You-Go resources, the system automatically applies active coupons during Bill Generation. Automatic matching: The system prioritizes coupons nearing expiration. If expiration dates are identical, the system prioritizes coupons with larger remaining balances. Multi-coupon deduction: If the balance of a single coupon is insufficient to cover the entire bill, the system automatically applies the next available voucher to continue deduction until the bill amount is fully offset or all applicable coupons are exhausted. Budget deduction: If the bill amount remains after all coupons are applied, the system deducts the remaining amount from your budget.

##### 7.2.9.2 Coupon details

The coupon details page displays all coupons and allows you to view detailed usage information for each coupon.

**Constraints**

When issuing coupons, you can select only level-1 organizations. Therefore, the coupon details page displays coupons that belong to level-1 organizations. Users of a level-1 organization who have the permission to view coupons can view coupons that belong to their level-1 organization on the coupon details page. Users of subordinate organizations cannot view available coupons.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operation** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Coupon** > **Coupon Details**.
4. View existing coupons in the list.
Click a coupon ID to expand the **Basic Information** panel. Click **Usage Details** in the **Actions** column of a coupon to view its detailed usage information.

Manage tenant blacklists. The system supports blacklist control by level-1 organization dimension to restrict permissions for coupon claiming and redemption.

**Prerequisites**

The operating user defaults to the operations administrator.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Coupon** > **Blacklist Management**.

5. In the **Add to Blacklist** panel, configure blacklist information.

| Configuration Item | Description |
|---|---|
| Organization | Add a level-1 organization to the blacklist. The system supports single selection only. |
| Limit Type | Defaults to Disallow Issuance and Disallow Use. Modification is not supported. |
| Reason | Enter the reason for adding to the blacklist. |

6. Click **Confirm**.
7. Manage the blacklist.

| Action | Description |
|---|---|
| Edit blacklist | i. In the blacklist list, click Actions column’s Edit. ii. In the Edit Blacklist panel, update the reason for adding to the blacklist. iii. Click Confirm. |
| Delete blacklist | i. In the blacklist list, click Actions column’s Delete. ii. Click Confirm. |

Configure the credit conversion rules, version specifications, and pricing rules for token plans.

###### 7.2.10.3.1 Enable the unified metering standard by credit

**by credit**

After enabling the unified metering standard, the system uses credits as the unified metering unit and converts tokens in quota management based on conversion rules.

**Prerequisites**

The default operator is the operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Token Plan Management** > **Token Plan**
**Configuration**.
4. Click
on the right side of the **Unified Metering Standard Credit** card.
5. In the dialog box, click **Confirm**.

> **Note:** You cannot disable this feature after enabling it. The system converts the corresponding quotas to the credit standard for management.

###### 7.2.10.3.2 Edit Token Plan configuration

After you enable Unified Metering Standard by Credit, you can edit the Token Plan Configurations.

**Prerequisites**

The default user role is Operations Administrator. You have enabled Unified Metering Standard by Credit.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top menu bar, choose **Operations** > **Service Operations**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Token Plan Management** > **Token Plan**
**Configurations**.
4. Click **Modify** on the right side of the **Unified Metering Standard by Credit** card.
5. Complete **Credits Conversion Settings**, **Token Plan Configurations**, and **Price**
**Management** in sequence.
i. **Credits Conversion Settings**: Click **Configure** in the Actions column of a model, set the conversion coefficient, and click **Save**.

> **Note:** If no conversion coefficient is configured for a new model, the system converts credits based on the following default ratios:
> Input Token: 1000 : 0.2
> Output Token: 1000 : 1.2
> Cache Token: 1000 : 0.02
> After you update the conversion coefficient, the existing metering data remains unchanged. The new coefficient applies only to metering data generated after the update.

ii. **Token Plan Configurations**: Configure the specifications and benefits for each version of the Token Plan.

| Action | Description |
|---|---|
| Add a version | a. Click Create Version above the version list. b. In the dialog box, set Version Name, Credit Quota, and Custom Description Field. c. Click Save. |
| Enable or disable a version | Click or in the Enabling Status column of a version. indicates that the version is enabled. indicates that the version is disabled. |
| Edit a version | a. Click Modify in the Actions column of a version. b. In the Modify Version dialog box, update the version information. c. Click Save. |
| Delete a version | a. Click Delete Version in the Actions column of a version. b. In the dialog box, click Delete Version. |
| Configure a shared usage plan | In the Shared Usage Plan section, configure the Minimum Credits per Order, Increment Step Size (Credits), and Maximum Credits per Order. |

iii. **Pricing Management**: Manage the pricing rules for each version and specification. Click
**Configure** in the **Actions** column of an associated rule. In the **Pricing Configurations**
panel, set the prices.
6. Click **OK**.

##### 7.3.1.1 Data analysis

The Data Analysis page provides platform and organization administrators with platformbased operations data analytics, self-service analytics, and scenario-specific operations report capabilities.

###### 7.3.1.1.1 View data table

to the corresponding type of data table.

| Data table type | Description |
|---|---|
| Product statistics | Displays the corresponding resource reports and quota reports based on the selected cloud service. |
|   | Supports statistical reports, resource reports, cost reports, compute resource reports, idle analysis, and storage resource reports. Statistical reports Number of instances in region (daily) Number of instances in region (monthly) Number of instances in region (weekly) Number of instances under resource (daily) Number of instances under resource (monthly) Number of instances under resource (weekly) Number of instances under tag (daily) Number of instances under tag (monthly) Number of instances under tag (weekly) |

|   | Usage statistics report (daily) Number of instances under region (daily) Number of instances under region (monthly) |
|---|---|
| Organizati on statistics | Number of instances under region (weekly) Resource reports Full resource instance table Resource count statistics table Cost reports Monthly bill statistics by organization Monthly service bill statistics by organization Monthly service bills of organizations by tag Monthly organization bills by tag Annual service bill statistics by organization Monthly bill statistics by service Annual bill statistics by service Monthly bill statistics by resource set Monthly service bill statistics by resource set Monthly service bills of resource sets by tag Monthly resource set bills by tag Compute resource reports Compute-type product instance table Compute resource statistics table by organization Compute resource statistics table by resource set Idle analysis Resource health Organization health Resource set health Organization and sub-organization health Idle resource analysis Idle resource analysis of organization Idle resource analysis of resource set Idle resource analysis of all organizations Storage resource reports Storage resource statistics table by organization Storage resource statistics table by resource set Storage-type product instance table |

Filter: Click **Filter** above the list, add entries, and set filter conditions to quickly find the required data. You can also click after a field in the data table column to set filter conditions.

> **Note:** The organization and resource set fields support multiple selections.

Sort: Click **Sort** above the list, add entries, and set sorting conditions to arrange data in ascending or descending order. Only one field can be sorted at a time. You can also click after a sortable field in the data table column to sort directly by that field. Show/hide fields: Click **Field** above the list, select or clear fields to show or hide them and their data. Drag before a field to adjust the display order of fields. Scenario analysis: In the data table column, click after a field that supports scenario analysis, select a scenario, and you will be redirected to the custom chart page. If you want to download the data in a data report to your local machine, you can export the data.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Custom Analysis** > **Data Analysis**.
4. On the Data Analysis page, click the **Product**, **Organization**, or **My** tab to display the
corresponding list of tables.
5. On the **Product**, **Organization**, or **My** tab, click the table that you want to view.
6. Optional. Configure the Filter, Sort, or Field settings based on your business requirements.
7. Export all data or selected data. When you export data, the data that meets the filter
conditions is exported.

**Export selected data**

a. In the data list section, select the data that you want to export and click **Export Data** in the upper-right corner. b. In the **Export Data** dialog box, configure the **Export Scope** and **Task Name** parameters, and click **Yes**.

> **Note:** You can select **All** or **Selected** for the Export Scope parameter based on your business requirements.
> If you select **All** for the Export Scope parameter, you are navigated to the **Report Download** page to view the report export task.
> If you select **Selected** for the Export Scope parameter, the exported data is directly saved to your local machine in the **.xlsx** format.

**Export all data**

a. On the **Data Analysis** page, click **Export Data** above the data list. b. In the **Export Data** dialog box, configure the **Task Name** parameter, and click **Yes**.

> **Note:** By default, **All** is selected for the **Export Scope** parameter.
> After the data is exported, you are navigated to the **Report Download** page to view the report export task.

###### 7.3.1.1.4 Export the data of multiple tables

You can select multiple tables at a time for data export.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Data Analysis**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Custom Analysis** > **Data Analysis**.
4. On the Data Analysis page, click the **Product**, **Organization**, or **My** tab to display the
corresponding list of tables.
5. On the **Product**, **Organization**, or **My** tab, click the table that you want to view.
6. Optional. Configure the Filter, Sort, or Field settings based on your business requirements.
7. Click **Export Multiple Tables** in the upper-right corner.
8. In the **Export Multiple Tables** dialog box, configure the **Task Name**, **Report Type**, and
**Reports** parameters.

> **Note:** You can select multiple reports.
> When you download multiple reports, the following filter conditions are retained: organization, resource set, region, creation time, and tag. Other filter conditions do not take effect.

9. Click **Yes**. After a report export task is created, a dialog box appears. In this dialog box, you
can click **Go to Download Report Page** to view the report export task.

0. Click **OK**.

**Configure data**

**Filter data**

You can click Data Filtering to configure filter conditions. This way, only data that meets the filter conditions is displayed.
1. On the **Data Configuration** tab, click **Data Filtering**.
2. In the **Set Filter Condition** dialog box, add entries and configure filter conditions.

> **Note:** Each entry consists of a filter field, filter condition, and filter value. If the value of a filter field in data is the same as the specified filter value, the data meets the filter condition entry.
> You can add multiple entries. Multiple entries can be connected by using the **And** or **Or** operator.
> **And**: Data is displayed only if it meets all the filter conditions.
> **Or**: Data is displayed if it meets one of the filter conditions.

3. Click **OK**.

**Field details**

The **Dimensions** and **Metrics** sections are displayed in the Field Details section of the Data Configuration tab. You can drag a field to the X Axis and Y Axis sections based on your business requirements.
**Dimensions**: optional data fields for parent dimensions.
**Metrics**: data fields for metrics. Numeric values are supported.

**Chart types**

**Column chart**

A column chart uses vertical bars to represent the values of categorical data.

**Line chart**

A line chart uses lines to display data changes within a period of time.

**Pie chart**

A pie chart is a statistical chart that displays the proportion of categorical data. It uses the area or angle of each sector to represent the proportion of each part to the whole.

**Metric card**

A metric card is a simple and card-style chart that is used to display metric information.

**Nested pie chart**

A nested pie chart displays hierarchical data by nesting one or more smaller pie charts within a main pie chart.

**Table**

A table is used to display detailed data.

##### 7.3.1.3 Intelligent analysis

This feature provides intelligent question answering and data insight capabilities under AIpowered intelligent analysis scenarios.

**Prerequisites**

When you deploy Apsara Copilot, an operations administrator has enabled the display of the intelligent assistant in **Configuration** > **Apsara Copilot** > **Personalized Configuration**. By default, authorized users include Operations Administrators, Organization Administrators, Resource Set Administrators, Resource Users, Resource Auditors, and Organization Resource Auditors. Users with custom roles require authorization for the Data Analysis > Custom Analysis > Intelligent Analysis menu.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Data Analysis**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Custom Analysis** > **Intelligent Analysis**.
4. In the **Intelligent Analysis** dialog box, select a domain.

> **Note:** You can select **All**, **Cost Analysis Domain**, **Cloud Optimization Domain**, or **Resource Analysis Domain** as the domain scope for intelligent analysis.

| Domain | Description |
|---|---|

| All | This domain integrates operations data across all dimensions and supports comprehensive analysis such as billing management, resource utilization tracking, and security compliance configuration to deliver full-spectrum operational insights. |
|---|---|
| Cost Analysis Domain | This domain contains billing-related data and supports cost breakdown and trend analysis across multiple dimensions such as organizational structure, financial unit, and products. It provides month-over-month (MoM) and year-over-year (YoY) analysis capabilities, allowing you to view the cost fluctuation curve over the last 12 months and accurately identify cost change patterns. When you select Cost Analysis Domain as the query scope, you can select a billing table at the top of the dialog box. The system then displays the key metrics and aggregation dimensions of the billing table for quick selection. |
| Cloud Optimizatio n Domain | This domain contains cloud resource optimization data and diagnoses the health status of the cloud environment based on a health status evaluation system that combines resource utilization and security scores. It supports instance-level performance analysis across organizations, resource sets, and products to precisely identify idle resources and performance bottlenecks. Additionally, it evaluates security compliance by identifying configuration defects through a security scoring mechanism, thereby strengthening your cloud security posture. When you select Cloud Optimization Domain as the query scope, you can select the health status, idle resource analysis, or bottleneck analysis table at the top of the dialog box. The system then displays the key metrics and aggregation dimensions of the selected table for quick selection. |
| Resource Analysis Domain | This domain contains cloud resource data and provides statistics on total instance counts and instance type distribution. It supports in-depth analysis of core metrics such as CPU load, memory usage, and disk usage by instance type to provide robust data support for resource inventory and efficiency evaluation. When you select Resource Analysis Domain as the query scope, you can select a resource data table at the top of the dialog box. The system then displays the key metrics and aggregation dimensions of the resource table for quick selection. |

5. Enter your question in the dialog box and click
.

> **Note:** Intelligent analysis supports multiple models. You can switch between different models to ask questions.
> Enter "/" in the input box to add a slot, and then select the corresponding slot value based on the slot type.

Intelligent analysis provides different types of recommended questions. You can trigger them with one click as needed.

> New conversation: Click
> in the upper-left corner to start a new conversation.
> Conversation history: Click
> in the upper-left corner to expand the conversation
> history. In the conversation history panel, click
> to pin the conversation history
> list.

6. After intelligent analysis provides an answer, perform the following operations.
: Thumbs up to indicate that you approve of the answer. : Thumbs down to indicate that you disapprove of the answer. : Copy the answer content. : Export the generated answer to a PDF file.

##### 7.3.2.1 View health analysis data

The health analysis feature allows you to analyze the health status of cloud resources based on core metrics such as resource usage efficiency and security. This helps you understand the health status of resources, continuously improve overall resource governance, and optimize resource allocation policies.

**Background information**

The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console displays health analysis data by organization, resource set, and resource. Health analysis on organizations: collects the health status of all resource sets of each organization. By default, the health status of subordinate organizations is not included. You can select Aggregate Sub-organizations to calculate the average health score of an organization and its subordinate organizations. Health analysis on resource sets: collects the health status of all resources of each resource set and displays the scoring details of all resources in each resource set. Health analysis on resources: collects the data metrics that are related to the utilization and security of each resource and displays the scoring details of each resource. Different health scores indicate different health status. If a health score is greater than or equal to 90, the health status is excellent. If a health score is greater than or equal to 70 but less than 90, the health status is good. If a health score is greater than or equal to 50 but less than 70, the health status is fair. If a health score is less than 50, the health status is poor. You can view the health details based on metrics such as the usage rate score and security score. You can also view the algorithm rules, scoring reasons, and optimization suggestions.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Data Analysis**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Cloud Resource Optimization** > **Overall Health**
**Score**.
4. View the health scores, health score trends, health analysis data of organizations, resource
sets, and resources. For more information, see the View the health analysis data of organizations, View the health analysis data of resource sets, and View the health analysis data of resources sections of this topic.

**View the health analysis data of organizations**

On the **Organization** tab of the **Overall Health Score** page, view the health analysis data of organizations.

**Top 10 organizations with the highest health scores and top 10**

**organizations with the lowest health scores**

**Top 10 High Health Scores**: displays the top 10 organizations with the highest health
scores and their scores.
**Top 10 Low Health Scores**: displays the top 10 organizations with the lowest health
scores and their scores.

**Health analysis data of organizations**

Switch between the resource tabs to view the health status of different resources in organizations. View the health analysis data by **day**, **week**, or **month**. Click **From High to Low** or **From Low to High** to view health scores in descending or ascending order. Click the icon to display the resource list. You can drag and drop resources to adjust the display order of resources. Click the icon to display the resource selection dialog box. In the resource selection dialog box, add or remove one or more resources and click **OK** to show or hide the corresponding resource tabs.

**Health details of organizations**

In the Organization Health Details section, view the details of the health status of organizations. You can configure the following parameters to filter data: **Scoring Date**,
**Organization**, **Organization Health**, **Usage Rate Score**, **Security Score**, **Product**
**Categories**, and **Cloud Services**.
Select **Aggregate Sub-organizations** above the list to calculate the average health score of an organization and its subordinate organizations. Click the icon above the list to export and save the data to your local device. Find the organization whose data is to be exported, click **Export Data** in the **Actions** column, and then select **Resource Set Scoring Details**, **Resource Scoring Details**, or
**Governance Details**. In the message that appears, click **OK**.
Find the organization whose scoring details are to be viewed and click **Scoring Details** in the **Actions** column. On the Scoring Details Table page, view the scoring details of all resources in the organization. Select **Show Sub-organization Resources** in the upper-right corner of the Scoring Details Table page to view the scoring details of the resources in subordinate organizations. On the **Scoring Details Table** page, find the resource whose scoring details are to be viewed and click **Scoring Details** in the **Actions** column. On the page that appears, view the scoring details of the resource.

**View the health analysis data of resource sets**

On the **Resource Set** tab of the **Overall Health Score** page, view the health analysis data of resource sets.

**Top 10 resource sets with the highest health scores and top 10**

**resource sets with the lowest health scores**

**Top 10 High Health Scores**: displays the top 10 resource sets with the highest health
scores and their scores.
**Top 10 Low Health Scores**: displays the top 10 resource sets with the lowest health
scores and their scores.

**Health analysis data of resource sets**

Switch between the resource tabs to view the health status of different resources in resource sets. View the health analysis data by **day**, **week**, or **month**. Click **From High to Low** or **From Low to High** to view health scores in descending or ascending order. Click the icon to display the resource list. You can drag and drop resources to adjust the display order of resources. Click the icon to display the resource selection dialog box. In the resource selection dialog box, add or remove one or more resources and click **OK** to show or hide the corresponding resource tabs.

**Health details of resource sets**

In the Resource Set Health Details section, view the details of the health status of resource sets. You can configure the following parameters to filter data: **Scoring Date**,
**Organization**, **Resource Set**, **Resource Set Health**, **Usage Rate Score**, **Security**
**Score**, **Product Categories**, and **Cloud Services**.
Click the icon above the list to export and save the data to your local device. In the Resource Set Health Details section, find the resource set whose scoring details are to be viewed and click **Scoring Details** in the **Actions** column. On the Scoring Details page, view the scoring details of all resources in the resource set. Configure the following parameters to filter data: **Scoring Date**, **Resource Type**,
**Instance ID**, **Instance Name**, **Resource Health**, **Usage Rate Score**, and **Security**
**Score**.
On the **Scoring Details** page, find the resource whose scoring details are to be viewed and click **Scoring Details** in the **Actions** column. On the page that appears, view the scoring details of the resource.

**View the health analysis data of resources**

On the **Resource** tab of the **Overall Health Score** page, view the health analysis data of resources.

**Top 10 resources with the highest health scores and top 10**

**resources with the lowest health scores**

**Top 10 High Health Scores**: displays the top 10 resources with the highest health scores
and their scores.
**Top 10 Low Health Scores**: displays the top 10 resources with the lowest health scores
and their scores.

**Health analysis data of resources**

Switch between the resource tabs to view the health status of different resources. View the health analysis data by **day**, **week**, or **month**. Click **From High to Low** or **From Low to High** to view health scores in descending or ascending order. Click the icon to display the resource list. You can drag and drop resources to adjust the display order of resources. Click the icon to display the resource selection dialog box. In the resource selection dialog box, add or remove one or more resources and click **OK** to show or hide the corresponding resource tabs.

**Health details of resources**

In the Resource Health Details section, view the details of the health status of resources. You can configure the following parameters to filter data: **Scoring Date**, **Resource Type**,
**Instance ID**, **Instance Name**, **Organization**, **Resource Set**, **Region**, **Resource Health**,
**Usage Rate Score**, and **Security Score**.
Click the icon above the list to export and save the data to your local device. In the Resource Health Details section, find the resource whose scoring details are to be viewed and click **Scoring Details** in the **Actions** column. On the page that appears, view the scoring details of the resource.

##### 7.3.2.4 View security compliance analysis data

The security compliance analysis feature allows you to analyze the overall resource security based on resource security metrics, This helps you identify potential security risks and noncompliant configurations.

**Background information**

The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console displays security compliance data by organization, resource set, and resource. Security compliance analysis on organizations: collects the security compliance data of all resource sets of each organization. By default, the security compliance data of suborganizations is not included. You can select Aggregate Sub-organizations to calculate the average security scores of an organization and its sub-organizations. Security compliance analysis on resource sets: collects the security compliance data of all resources of each resource set and displays the scoring details of all resources in each resource set. Security compliance analysis on resources: collects the data metrics that are related to the security of each resource and displays the scoring details of each resource. Different security scores indicate different security status. If a security score is greater than or equal to 90, the security status is excellent. If a security score is greater than or equal to 70 but less than 90, the security status is good. If a security score is greater than or equal to 50 but less than 70, the security status is fair. If a security score is less than 50, the security status is poor.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Data Analysis**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Cloud Resource Optimization** > **Security**
**Compliance Analytics**.
4. View the security score overview, security score trends, and security compliance analysis
data of organizations, resource sets, and resources. For more information, see the View the security compliance analysis data of organizations, View the security compliance analysis data of resource sets, and View the security compliance analysis data of resources sections of this topic.

**View the security compliance analysis data of organizations**

On the **Organization** tab of the **Security Compliance Analytics** page, view the security compliance analysis data of organizations.

**Top 10 organizations with the highest security scores and top**

**10 organizations with the lowest security scores**

**10 Organization with the Highest Security Scores** : displays the top 10 organizations
with the highest security scores and their scores.
**10 Organizations with the Lowest Security Scores** : displays the top 10 organizations
with the lowest security scores and their scores.

**Security score distribution of organizations**

##### 7.3.2.5 Resource optimization settings

The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console provides the rule configuration feature for health analysis, idle resource and bottleneck analysis, and security compliance analysis of cloud resources, and allows you to flexibly modify rules and parameters based on your business requirements.

###### 7.3.2.5.1 Default rule

The default rule is built in the system and applies to all organizations by default. The default rule cannot be modified or deleted and has the lowest priority. You can create custom rules. For more information, see Create and manage custom rules.

**Supported cloud services and rule details**

> **Note:** By default, rule weights are evenly configured based on the number of displayed rules.
> Rules of undeployed services are not displayed.
> The system executes rules at 05:00 every day.

###### 7.3.2.5.2 Create and manage custom rules

If the default rule built in the system fails to meet your business requirements, you can create a custom rule based on your business requirements.

**Prerequisites**

You are assigned the operations administrator role.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Data Analysis**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Cloud Resource Optimization** > **Resource**
**Optimization Settings**.
4. On the Resource Optimization Settings page, click **Create Policy**.
5. On the **Create Rule** page, configure the parameters in the **Basic Information** and **Select**
**Rule** steps.

> **Note:** The system executes rules at 05:00 every day.

i. Configure parameters in the Basic Information step.

| Section and parameter |   | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Basic Informati on | Rule Name | The name of the custom rule. |
|   | Descriptio n | The description of the custom rule. |
| Applicable Scope | Organizati on | The organization to which the custom rule applies. You can select only one organization. If a rule is already applied to the selected organization, you cannot apply the custom rule to the organization. |
|   | Region | The region to which the custom rule applies. If you do not select a region, the custom rule applies to all regions. |

ii. Configure parameters in the Select Rule step. a. In the left-side section, click the name of a cloud resource to quickly locate its rules. b. In the right-side section, select one or more rules of the cloud resource.

> **Note:** You can select **Default** from the Select a template drop-down list to select all rules of the Security & Compliance type.
> You can enter a keyword in the search box to search for a rule in fuzzy search mode.
> You can click **Select All** in the upper part of the right-side section to select all cloud resource rules.
> You can click **Clear** in the upper part of the right-side section to clear the selected rules.
> You can select **Show Selected Actions Only** in the upper part of the right- side section to display only the selected rules.

c. Enter the weight of each rule in the **Weight** column.

> **Note:** After rules are selected, the system automatically assigns equal weight to each rule. You can modify the weight of each rule based on your business requirements.

d. Optional. Find a rule of the **Utilization** type and click **Rule Configuration** in the
**Weight** column. In the Rule Configuration panel, modify the parameters of the rule.

> **Note:** The rule parameters vary based on cloud resources.

| Section and parameter |   | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Basic Informatio n | Name | The name of the resource optimization setting. You cannot modify the parameter. |
|   | Description | The description of the resource optimization setting. The description must be 1 to 300 characters in length. |
|   | Resource Type | The cloud service to which the resource belongs. You cannot modify the parameter. |
| Time Range | Duration | The duration of the resource optimization. Valid values: 1 Day, 1 Week, 2 Weeks, and 30 Days. |
| Valid Values | Hourly Usage | The hourly usage of the cloud service. Valid values: Average, Maximum Value, and Minimum Value. |
|   | Daily Usage | The daily usage of the cloud service. Valid values: All and Duration. Note If you select Duration, you must add new entries to configure the Time Range and Weight parameters. You can add multiple entries. |
| Set Threshold | Idle Rules | Configure a threshold for the idle rules of the resource optimization setting. |
| Recommen ded Solution | Recommende d Solution | The suggestions for fixing the resource optimization setting. The suggestions must be 0 to 300 characters in length. |

6. View the custom rule. By default, a custom rule takes effect after it is created. On the
Resource Optimization Settings page, you can view the created custom rule by configuring the **Status** and **Rule Name** parameters.

> **Note:** You can select **Effective** or **Paused** from the Status drop-down list.
> In the Rule Name search box, you can enter a keyword to search for a rule in fuzzy search mode.

7. Perform other operations on the custom rule based on your business requirements. The
following table describes the supported operations.

| Operation | Description |
|---|---|
| View the details of a rule | Click Details on the card of the rule to go to the Rule Details page. |
| Disable a rule | i. Click Disable on the card of the rule in the Effective state. ii. In the Disable Rule message, click OK. After the rule is disabled, the state of the rule changes to Paused. |
| Enable a rule | i. Click Enabled on the card of the rule in the Paused state. ii. In the Enable Rule message, click OK. After the rule is enabled, the state of the rule changes to Effective. |

#### 7.3.3 Download and delivery

##### 7.3.3.1 Report download

You can create a download task to download multiple data records. After the task is created, data is asynchronously exported in the background. After the data is exported, you can download the report.

###### 7.3.3.1.1 Report results

On the report results tab, create a download task. After you successfully create the task, export and download the report.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Data Analysis**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Download and Deliver** > **Report Download**.
4. On the **Report Results** tab, click **Create Download Task**.
5. In the **Create Download Task** dialog box, configure the report download information. For
more information, see Report types.
6. Click **OK**.
7. Expand **Advanced Filtering**, set conditions for **Report Name**, **Report Type**, **Cloud**
**Service**, **Report Generation Status**, and **Time Range**, then click **Search** to quickly
locate reports.
8. On the **Report Results** tab, perform the following operations.

| Task | Procedure |
|---|---|
| Download a report | Click Download Report in the Actions column of the target report. Note If the report status is Failed or Canceled, click Retry to retry the task. When the report status changes to Completed, you can click Download Report to download it. |
| Delete a report | Delete one report a. Click Delete in the Actions column of the report. b. In the Delete Task dialog box, click OK. Delete multiple reports a. Select the check boxes before the report names. b. At the bottom of the list, click Delete, then click OK. |

**Report types**

The following report types are currently supported: **Metering Report**, **Second-level**
**Metering Report**, **Resource Report**, **Quota Report**, **Organization report**, **Resource set**
**report**, **Access policy report**, **User report**, **User group report**, **Role report**, **Detailed**
**Billing Report**, **Monthly Billing Report of Service**, **Monthly Billing Report of**
**Resource Set**, **Monthly Billing Report of Organization**, and **Monthly Billing Report of**
**Cost Unit**.

> **Note:** For billing reports, the billing period and start/end times refer to the time zone of the server deployment location. The time zone varies based on the deployment location and follows this format: Billing Period (UTC±HH:MM), Start/End Time (UTC±HH:MM). For example: Billing Period (UTC+08:00), Start/End Time (UTC+08:00), Start/End Time (UTC+04:00).
> Billing reports support online download only.
> The **Email** delivery method appears only when you enable the email feature switch. To use this delivery method, ensure that an email gateway is configured in the Message Gateway.
