###### 7.3.3.1.2 Scheduled job

On the Scheduled Job tab, create a scheduled job. After you create the job successfully, the system pushes the report periodically according to the configured time period.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Data Analysis**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Download and Deliver** > **Report Download**.
4. On the **Scheduled Tasks** tab, click **Create Scheduled Task**.
5. In the **Create Scheduled Task** dialog box, configure the scheduled task. For more
information, see Report types.
6. Click **OK**.
7. Expand **Advanced Filtering**, set conditions for **Task Name**, **Report Type**, and **Push**
**Cycle**, then click **Search** to quickly find scheduled tasks.
8. On the **Scheduled Tasks** tab, perform related operations.

| Task operation | Procedure |
|---|---|
| View a task | i. Click View in the Actions column of the task. ii. In the View Scheduled Tasks dialog box, view the configuration of the scheduled task. |

| Edit a task | i. Click Edit in the Actions column of the task. ii. In the Modify Scheduled Task dialog box, update the scheduled task configuration. iii. Click OK. |
|---|---|
| Delete a task | i. Click Delete in the Actions column of the task. ii. In the dialog box, click OK. |

##### 7.3.3.2 Manage the push rules of daily operations reports

**reports**

The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console provides the report subscription feature that allows you to configure the push rules of daily operations reports. You can specify the scheduled time to send reports and the desired content of reports. The system automatically generates operations reports and sends them to your email address based on the rules that you configure. This helps you keep track of the resource usage and facilitates monitoring and alerting.

**Background information**

You can configure up to 10 push rules for each of your role. The system generates report files in the .xlsx format based on the content settings that you configure in a rule and sends the report files to your email address based on the scheduled time that you specify. The reports contain enterprise, operations, and cloud service statistics, which can be accessed by the role corresponding to the rule.

**Create a push rule of daily operations reports**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Data Analysis**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Download and Deliver** > **Daily Operations**
**Report Delivery**.
4. On the **Daily Operations Report Delivery** page, click **Create Rule**.

| Step | Paramete r | Description |
|---|---|---|
|   | Rule Name | The name of the rule. The name must be 2 to 64 characters in length and can contain letters, digits, hyphens (-), and underscores ( ). _ |

| sara Uni-manag | er User Guide·Operation |   |
|---|---|---|
| Basic Settings |   |   |
|   | Rule Descriptio n | The description of the rule. |
|   | Report Name | The name of the generated reports, which are attached in the emails sent to your email address. |
|   | Push At | The interval at which reports are generated and sent. Valid values: Every Day and Every Week. |
|   | Scheduled Time | The point in time at which reports are generated and sent. Note If you set the Push At parameter to Every Week, you must configure the Days parameter to specify the days of the week on which reports are generated and sent. |
| Content Settings |   | In this step, you can specify the following content of the reports: Enterprise statistics: the numbers of and changes in users, roles, organizations, and resource sets. Operations statistics: the usage and alerts of quotas. Cloud service statistics: the changes in the numbers of resources and alerts. Note The reports contain only the statistics of the resources that can be accessed by the current role. |
| Push Preview |   | In this step, you can preview a demo report. The report is generated based on the content settings that you configure in the previous step. |

5. Preview the report and click **Create**. The system sends reports to your email address based
on the scheduled time that you specify.
6. Optional. After you create a push rule of daily operations reports, you can manage the rule
on the Daily Operations Report Delivery page. Click **Details** in the Actions column to view the details and push history of the rule. You can also modify the report content settings on the rule details page.

> **Note:** On the rule details page, click **Edit** in the Rule Content section to modify the report content settings.
> On the rule details page, find the push task that you want to download in the Push History section and click **Download** in the Actions column to save the report pushed by the push task as an **.xlsx** file to your local machine.

Click **Modify Attributes** in the Actions column to modify the configurations of the rule, such as the rule name, rule description, report name, push cycle, and scheduled time. You can modify the report content settings only on the rule details page. Click **Enabled** or **Disabled** in the Actions column to enable or disable the rule. If the rule is disabled, no push task is triggered.

> **Note:** A disabled rule is still counted as one rule. If the number of rules created for a role reaches 10, you cannot create more rules for the role.

Move the pointer over the More icon in the Actions column and select **Push History** to view the push tasks that were triggered by the rule. You can also download historical reports. Move the pointer over the More icon in the Actions column and select **Delete** to delete the push rule. If the number of existing push rules reaches the upper limit, you can delete the rules that you no longer need.

### 7.4 Portal management

#### 7.4.1 Site management

You can manage all sites on the Sites page, including creating sites, configuring site navigations, publishing or unpublishing sites, and viewing all pages of sites.

**Background information**

A site is an independent web portal. An operations administrator can build an independent service portal by using the portal management feature to provide users with an all-in-one web portal to manage cloud services. A site displays multi-aspect information including column navigation and page content. This way, the internal and external organization service information can be managed and published in a centralized manner, the users of a cloud platform can experience the service capabilities and view the operations information about the cloud platform, and the efficiency of information communication is improved.
1. Create a site: Configure the domain name and navigation settings of a site when you create
the site. This ensures that a page can be directly associated with a site navigation when you create the page.
2. Build pages: Create pages, associate the pages with site navigations, configure the
components and uploaded materials and data to complete the page building, and then publish the pages.
3. Publish the site: Check whether the site navigations are associated with pages on the Sites
page, preview the display effects of the site, and then publish the site. After the site is published, check the display effects of the site to ensure that the site works as expected.

##### 7.4.1.1 Create a site

Create a new site and configure its basic information. This ensures you can directly associate the site when creating a page.

**Prerequisites**

The operating user is an operations administrator by default.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Operations Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Sites**.
4. On the **Sites** page, click **Create Site**.
5. In the **Create Site** dialog box, configure Basic information, Theme color configuration,
Brand configuration, Footer configuration, and Navigation configuration.
6. Click **OK**.

**Basic information**

| Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|
| Site Template | Select a site template. You can quickly create a site based on a site template. If you use a site template, the system imports basic site information, configuration information, and associated pages by default. |
| Site Name | Enter a custom name for the site. The name must be 1 to 60 characters in length and cannot be the same as the name of an existing site. |

| ID | Enter an ID. The ID must be 1 to 30 characters in length and can contain lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens (-). It must start with a lowercase letter and cannot be the same as the ID of an existing site. You cannot modify the ID after the site is created. |
|---|---|
| Description | Enter the description of the site. The description must be 1 to 200 characters in length. |
| URL Token | You can enable or disable this feature. Important After you disable URL token, tokens are not displayed in page URLs. This may cause page leakage. Proceed with caution. |

**Theme color configuration**

| Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|
| One-click Gray | Use this feature on national days of mourning or major disaster days. This feature takes effect only for the service portal. : indicates that One-click Gray is enabled. : indicates that One-click Gray is disabled. |

| Appearance | You can select Light Mode or Dark Mode. Note You can configure Appearance only when One-click Gray is disabled. |
|---|---|
| Theme Color | Configure the theme color for the site. You can select aR ecommended Theme Color or use a Custom Palette. Note You can configure the site theme color only when One-click Gray is disabled. |

**Brand configuration**

| Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|

| Browser Icon | Click Upload Icon to upload the browser icon. We recommend that you use an image with a 1:1 aspect ratio (for example, 32 pixels × 32 pixels). The image format must be GIF, PNG, JPG, or JPEG. The image size cannot exceed 2 MB. |
|---|---|
| Show Logo | : indicates that the logo is displayed. : indicates that the logo is hidden. |
| Platform Logo | Configure this item only when Show Logo is enabled. Click Upload Logo to upload the platform logo. The logo appears in the upper- left corner of the site navigation. We recommend that you use an image with a resolution of 160 pixels × 36 pixels. The image format must be GIF, PNG, JPG, or JPEG. The image size cannot exceed 2 MB. |
| Logo Redirect URL | Configure this item only when Show Logo is enabled. Enter the redirect URL for the platform logo. |

**Footer configuration**

**Custom configuration disabled**

| Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|
| Enable Footer | Configure whether to display the footer. : indicates that the footer is displayed. : indicates that the footer is hidden. |
| Background Color | You can configure this item only when custom configuration is disabled. Set the footer color in the text box (for example, #FFFFFF). You can also click the color picker next to the text box to select a color. |
| Version Information | You can configure this item only when custom configuration is disabled. Enter version information. The version information appears in the footer and must be 1 to 40 characters in length. |
| Copyright Notice | You can configure this item only when custom configuration is disabled. Enter copyright notice. The copyright notice appears in the footer and must be 1 to 80 characters in length. |

| Bottom Information Configuration | You can configure this item only when custom configuration is disabled. The bottom information configuration includes settings for the Friendship Link, Solution, Documentation and tools, and Contact Us modules. Each module allows you to enable or disable the module, set the title text color, set the copy text color, customize the module title, and manage submodules. Module enablement: Enable or disable the module. : indicates that the module is enabled. : indicates that the module is disabled. Title text color: Set the title text color in the text box (for example, #FFFFFF). You can also click the color picker next to the text box to select a color. Copy text color: Set the copy text color in the text box (for example, #FFFFFF). You can also click the color picker next to the text box to select a color. Module title: Customize the module title as needed. Submodule management: Click Add sub-modules to add a submodule. Click before a submodule to expand its options and configure its name, description, and link based on your needs. Click in the row of a submodule to drag and adjust its display order. Click in the row of a submodule to delete the submodule. Preview: After you complete the module settings, click Preview to preview the effect. Note Friendship Link: Configure footer text and links. You can add up to three submodules. Solution: Configure footer text and links. You can add up to two submodules. Documentation and tools: Configure footer text and links. You can add up to five submodules. Contact Us: Configure images such as QR codes and enterprise logos. You can add up to four submodules. |
|---|---|

**Custom configuration enabled**

| Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|
| Enable Footer | Configure whether to display the footer. : indicates that the footer is displayed. : indicates that the footer is hidden. |
| Custom Configuration | Enable or disable custom configuration. : indicates that custom configuration is enabled. : indicates that custom configuration is disabled. |

| Footer Configuration | You can configure this item only when custom configuration is enabled. Customize the footer information. |
|---|---|

Module configuration: Click Add sub-modules to add a submodule. You can add up to eight submodules. Click before a submodule to expand its options and configure its name, link, and opening method based on your needs. Click in the row of a submodule to drag and adjust its display order. Click in the row of a submodule to delete the submodule. |

##### 7.4.1.2 View sites

On the Sites page, you can view the site list and the details of a site.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Sites**.
4. On the Sites page, view all created sites.
You can enter a site name in the search box above the site list and click the Search icon to efficiently filter sites by site name. You can click the icon next to the **Status** field to filter sites by status. You can click the icon next to the **Launch Time** field to sort sites in ascending or descending order.
5. Click the name of a site to go to the site details page.
6. On the site details page, view the basic information, navigations, and associated pages of
the site.
**Site Information**: displays the name, status, URL, description, platform logo, theme
color, and browser icon of the site and the status of the footer feature.
**Navigation Configuration**: displays the navigation configurations of the site. For more
information about how to configure a site navigation, see Configure a site navigation.
**Page List**: displays the pages associated with the site. For more information about how
to configure a site page, see Configure a site page.

##### 7.4.1.3 Modify the information and homepage of a site

**site**

After a site is created, you can modify the site information based on your business requirements.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Sites**.
4. On the Sites page, find the site that you want to manage and click **Edit** in the Operation
column. Alternatively, go to the site details page and click **Edit** in the upper-right corner.
5. In the **Edit Site** dialog box, modify the site information such as basic information, theme
color configurations, and brand configurations based on your business requirements. For more information about the parameters, see Create a site.

> **Note:** When you modify a site, you can configure the Home Page parameter in the Basic Information section to select a page as the site homepage based on your business requirements. Before you select a page as the homepage, make sure that the page is created.

6. Click **OK**.

##### 7.4.1.4 Configure a site navigation

After a site is created, you can configure navigations for the site.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Sites**.
4. On the Sites page, find the site that you want to manage and click **Configure Navigation**
in the Operation column.
5. On the **Navigation Configuration** tab of the site details page, click **Add Navigation**.
6. In the **Add Navigation** dialog box, configure the parameters and click **OK**. The following
table describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Navigation Name | Enter a name for the navigation. |
| Parent Navigation | Select the parent navigation to which the navigation belongs. |
| Sort | Specify the order in which the navigation is displayed. A smaller value indicates a higher priority. |
| Navigation Type | Select the type of the navigation. Valid values:P arent Navigation Group, Page Navigation, and Third-party Link. |
| Associated page | Specify the page with which the navigation is associated. This parameter is displayed only if you set the Navigation Type parameter to Page Navigation. If no option is available in the drop-down list, create a page first. |

| Third-party Link | Enter the URL of the third-party page with which the navigation is associated. This parameter is displayed only if you set the Navigation Type parameter to Third-party Link. |
|---|---|
| Open Mode | Select the method for going to the page with which the navigation is associated. This parameter is displayed only if you set the Navigation Type parameter to Page Navigation. Valid values: New Window Opens and The Current Window Opens. |
| Show or Not | Specify whether to display the navigation and its child navigations. If you set the value to No, the navigation and its child navigations are not displayed. |
| Display time | Valid values: Instant Display and Scheduled Display. Instant Display: The navigation is displayed on the portal immediately after you submit the configurations. Scheduled Display: The navigation is displayed on the portal at the specified time. |
| Time setting | This parameter is displayed only if you set the Display time parameter to Scheduled Display. Select a start time and an end time. The time is accurate to the second. The start time is required. If the start time is earlier than the current time, the system displays the navigation immediately after you submit the configurations. The end time is optional. If you do not specify an end time, the navigation remains displayed. |

7. On the Navigation Configuration tab, manage the navigation based on your business
requirements. To modify the site navigation, click **Edit** in the Operation column. To add a child navigation, click **Add Sub-navigation** in the Operation column. To delete the site navigation, click **Delete** in the Operation column.

##### 7.4.1.5 Configure site pages

After you create a site, configure its pages.

**Prerequisites**

By default, the operating user is an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Sites**.
4. On the sites list, click the site name to go to the site details page.
5. On the **Pages** tab, click **Create Page**.
6. In the **Create Page** dialog box, configure the page settings and click **Confirm**.

| Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|
| Page Template | Select a page template. You can quickly create a page based on a template. If you use a template, the system automatically applies the basic page information and layout configuration. |
| Page Name | Enter a custom page name. The name must be 1 to 30 characters in length and cannot duplicate an existing page name. |

| ID | Enter an English identifier for the page. The identifier must be 1 to 30 characters in length, start with a lowercase letter, and can contain only lowercase letters, digits, underscores ( ), and hyphens (-). It cannot duplicate _ an existing page identifier. Changing the identifier affects the page URL. If other pages reference this URL, update those references accordingly. |
|---|---|
| Page Type | You can select only Low code build. |
| Site | The system displays the site name by default. |
| Page Description | Enter a description for the site page. The description must be 1 to 200 characters in length. |

7. After you configure the site page, you can modify, remove, build content for, or preview the
page as needed. Click **Edit** in the Actions column to modify the basic page configuration. Click **View Page** in the Actions column to view the published page. Click **Page Building** in the Actions column to create or update the page layout and content. Click
**Version Management** in the Actions column to go to the page history
versions. You can view and restore historical versions. Click
**Remove** in the Actions column to remove the page from the site. After removal,
the site becomes empty.

##### 7.4.1.6 Customize the style of a site

If the preset site styles do not meet your business requirements, you can configure custom site styles. Page-level styles take precedence over global site styles. If no conflicts are involved, both the configured site styles and page styles take effect.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Sites**.
4. Click the name of a site to go to the site details page.
5. On the site details page, click **Style Settings** in the upper-right corner.
6. In the **Page Style** dialog box, enter the CSS code for configuring the style.
Example:

```
body { background-color: black;
```

`}`
7. Click **OK**. After the site style is saved, it takes effect immediately.

##### 7.4.1.7 Preview a site

After you configure the homepage, navigations, and pages of a site, you can preview the site and check the display effects of the site to ensure that the site works as expected.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Sites**.
4. On the Sites page, find the site that you want to manage and click **Preview** in the
Operation column. Alternatively, go to the site details page and click **Preview** in the upper-right corner.
5. On the page that appears, view the display effects of the site.

##### 7.4.1.8 Publish a site

Before you publish a site, make sure that all navigations are associated with pages and the associated pages are published. You can preview the display effects of the site to ensure that the site works as expected before it is published.

**Prerequisites**

Sites are in the **Offline** state. You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Sites**.
4. On the Sites page, find the site that you want to manage, move the pointer over the
icon in the Operation column, and then select **Online**. Alternatively, go to the site details page and click **Online** in the upper-right corner.
5. In the dialog box that appears, enter a description and click **OK**.

##### 7.4.1.9 Unpublish a site

You can unpublish a site based on your business requirements. After a site is unpublished, users cannot view the site.

**Prerequisites**

Sites are in the **Online** state. You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Sites**.
4. On the Sites page, find the site that you want to manage, move the pointer over the
icon in the Operation column, and then select **Offline**. Alternatively, go to the site details page and click **Offline** in the upper-right corner.
5. In the dialog box that appears, enter a description and click **OK**.

##### 7.4.1.10 Delete a site

You can delete a site that you no longer use.

**Prerequisites**

Sites are in the **Offline** state. You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Sites**.
4. On the Sites page, find the site that you want to manage, move the pointer over the
icon in the Operation column, and then select **Delete**. Alternatively, go to the site details page and click **Delete** in the upper-right corner.

##### 7.4.1.11 How users access a site

This topic describes how users access a site. After you publish a site, you can obtain its endpoint on the site details page. Users can visit the site by using this endpoint. The endpoint format is:

```
 https://${sitekey}.operation.${internet.domain}/coms/protal/${token} .
```

> **Note:** ${sitekey}: The custom identifier that you set when creating the site.
> ${internet.domain}: The root domain of the tenant.
> /coms/portal/${token}: The path to the site homepage. You can view the specific path in the page list. When you disable the **URL Token** feature, the endpoint does not include ${token}.

#### 7.4.2 Page management

##### 7.4.2.1 Pages

During the lifecycle of a site, you can perform operations such as maintaining, updating, and optimizing the content and structure of the site pages based on your business requirements. This ensures the efficiency and accuracy of site information and good user experience.

**Background information**

Pages are the important components of a site. Each page carries specific information or features to provide services. You can specify a page as the homepage of a site or associate a page with a site navigation based on your business requirements.

**Permissions on pages in different states**

> **Note:** Pages may be in the states described in the following table. Different operations can be performed on pages in different states. In the following table, ✓ indicates that the operation is supported, and × indicates that the operation is not supported.

| State/Operation | Mod ify a pag e | Pre vie w a pag e | Buil d a pag e | Save a page (with updates) | Pub lish a pag e | Dele te a page | Revo ke the publ ishin g of a page | View the revie w detai ls of a page |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | × |
| To be published as scheduled | × | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | × | ✓ | × |
| Draft (being reviewed for publishing) | × | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | × | ✓ | ✓ |
| Draft (review rejected) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | ✓ |
| Draft (publishing failed) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | × |
| Published | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | ✓ | × | × |
| Published (modifications to be published) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | × |
| Published (modifications to be published as scheduled) | × | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | × | ✓ | × |
| Published (being reviewed for publishing modifications) | × | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | × | ✓ | ✓ |
| Published (review for publishing modifications rejected) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | ✓ |

| Published (failed to publish modifications) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | × |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

###### 7.4.2.1.1 Create a page

| Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|

| Page Name | Enter a custom name for the page. The name must be 1 to 60 characters in length and cannot duplicate an existing page name. |

| ID | Enter an English identifier for the page. This identifier generates the page path. It must be 1 to 30 characters long, start with a lowercase letter, and contain only lowercase letters, digits, underscores ( ), or hyphens (-). It cannot _ duplicate an existing page identifier. Changing the English identifier affects the page’s URL. If other pages reference this URL, update those references accordingly. |
|---|---|

**Published (Modification publishing approval rejected)**, or **Published (Modification**
**publishing failed)**.
The operator must be an Operations Administrator by default.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Page Management** > **Page List**.

###### 7.4.2.1.4 Page building

Use page building to configure page content and architecture.

**Prerequisites**

By default, the operating user is an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Portal management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Page management** > **Page list**.
4. On the **Page List** page, click **Page Building** in the Actions column.
5. On the **Page Building** page, add components and materials as needed to build the page.
Left side: displays the outline, components, and versions. Outline: displays components that you have added to the page. You can manage these components, including moving, cloning, and deleting them. Components: supported component categories include Navigation, Card, Image and text, Display card, Display component, and Others. Add components to the page as needed. Versions: displays historical version information of the page. You can specify a time range to quickly find a version. You can view or restore a historical version as needed. Middle: displays components that you have added. After you select a component, you can move it up, move it down, clone it, or delete it. Right side: provides settings for the page and components. Page settings: include theme style, background color, background material, and footer display settings. Theme style: configure CSS style code for the page. Page styles take precedence over global site styles. If no style conflicts exist, both site and page styles take effect. Background color: enter a color code (such as #d0021b) in the input box or click the color picker to select a color. Background material: supports **Local Upload** or **Material Center**. Format requirements: JPG or PNG. Size requirements: width 3840 pixels, height customizable. Display footer: footer content is displayed based on the footer configuration of the associated site. If the site does not enable the footer, the footer cannot be displayed. Component settings: configuration items vary by component. You can perform personalized configurations as needed. After you select a target component in the middle section, the right section displays component-related configurations. You can configure the component as needed.
6. After you complete page building, click **Save** in the upper-right corner.

> **Note:** Click **Undo** or **Recovery** to quickly adjust the page during page building.
> Click **Preview** to preview the display effect of the page during page building.
> Click **Publish** to publish the built page.
> Click **View Page** to view the content displayed on the published page. This operation is available only for pages in the Published state.

###### 7.4.2.1.5 Publish page

You can publish a page multiple times. Each publication generates a version that records the current content of the page.

**Prerequisites**

The page is in one of the following states: **Draft**, **Draft (publishing approval rejected)**,
**Draft (publishing failed)**, **Published (modified, pending publication)**, **Published**
**(modified, publishing approval rejected)**, or **Published (modified, publishing**
**failed)**.
By default, the operating user is an Operations Administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Page Management** > **Page list**.
4. Publish the page.
**Publish a single page**: On the **Page list** page, click
in the Actions column and select **Publish**. Alternatively, enter the page builder, complete and save the page content, then click **Publish** in the upper-right corner.
**Batch publish pages**: On the **Page list** page, select multiple pages you want to
publish, then click **Batch Publish** at the bottom of the list.
5. In the **Page Publishing** dialog box, select a publishing time. You can choose **Publish now**
or **Scheduled release**.
**Publish now**: The page updates immediately after you confirm publication.
**Scheduled release**: After selecting scheduled release, set the time below. The page
content will update at the specified time. After scheduling a release, if you need to modify the time, you must first cancel the scheduled release and then republish.
6. Click **OK**.

icon in the Operation column, and then select **Revoke Publishing**.

#### 7.4.3 Material center

You can upload, modify, and delete site materials such as images and videos as needed.

**Background information**

The material center manages the material resources required by the site, including images and videos, so that administrators can quickly find and use them when managing the site.

**Prerequisites**

The operating user is an operations administrator by default.

**Upload images and videos**

Upload the image and video materials required by the site to the material center.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Material Center**.
4. On the **Material Center** page, click **Upload Material**.
5. In the **Upload Material** dialog box, enter the **Material Name**, select the **Material Type**
(image or video), and then click **Upload Material** to add a file.

> **Important:** Image format and size requirements:
> The system supports gif, png, jpg, jpeg, and GIF formats.
> The image size must not exceed 6 MB.
> Video format, resolution, and size requirements:
> The system supports common video formats. We recommend using mp4, mkv, or mov formats.
> The resolution must be 360p (640 pixels × 360 pixels) or higher.
> The video file size must not exceed 5 GB.

6. Click OK.

**Preview materials**

After you upload materials, you can preview the uploaded images and videos.
1. At the top of the **Material Center** page, search for materials by material name, material
type (All, Image, or Video), group, or associated page.
2. The material card displays the material type, format, and latest update time. Hover over
the material card and click **Preview** to preview the material.

**Modify the material name or update an image**

Update the name or content of an image or video when necessary.

> **Important:** You cannot edit preset materials.

1. Hover over the material card and click **Edit**.
2. In the **Edit material** dialog box, modify the material name or add a file.
3. Click OK.

**Delete materials**

Delete images, videos, and other resources when they are no longer needed.

> **Important:** You cannot delete preset materials.
> Before you delete a material, make sure that no page references it.

1. Hover over the material card and click **Delete**.
2. In the dialog box, click OK.

#### 7.4.4 Component management

##### 7.4.4.1 Add components

When you build a service portal, if the preset components cannot meet your business requirements, you can use the component management feature to add custom components.

**Background information**

Components are classified into preset components and custom components. Preset components are standardized components that are predefined by the system and have common features and styles. When you build a service portal, you can directly use the preset components to improve development efficiency. Custom components are components that are designed and developed by users based on business requirements. If the preset components cannot meet the business requirements, developers can add custom components based on the project requirements and component development kit specifications.

**Prerequisites**

You are assigned the operations administrator role.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Component Management**.
4. On the **Component Management** page, click **Add components**.
5. In the **Add components** panel, configure the basic information about the component.

> **Note:** You can click **Download component development kit** to download the component development kit to your computer.
> You can click **Custom Component Description** to view the description of the custom component.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Compone nt name | The unique name of the component. The name must be 1 to 30 characters in length. |
| Compone nt Key | The component key, which indicates the unique identifier of the component. The key must be 1 to 60 characters in length and cannot be the same as an existing component key. |
| Type | The type of the component. Valid values: Navigation, Card, Graphic and text, Display Card, Display components, and Other. |
| Grouping | The group to which the component belongs. You can select multiple groups. Create a group: Click Add Group, enter a group name in the field, and then click Save and use. Modify a group: Move the pointer over the group and click the icon next to the group. Change the group name in the field and click Save. Delete a group: Move the pointer over the group and click the icon next to the group. In the message that appears, click Delete. After you delete a group, all components associated with the group are removed from the group. Proceed with caution. |

6. Click **Submit**.
7. In the **Component added successfully** dialog box, click **Download component**
**development kit** to download the component development kit to your computer.
You can also click **Upload later**. After a component is created, you can customize the component. For more information, see Customize a component and Understand tools and configurations for building custom components. After you customize a component, you can use the component when you build a page. For more information, see Configure a component and Publish a component.

##### 7.4.4.2 Configure a component

After a component is added or if the component configurations need to be updated, you can configure the component.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator. A custom component is developed. For more information, see Customize a component and Understand the tool and configurations for building custom components.

**Limits**

You cannot configure preset components. You cannot configure custom components in the **Verifying** or **Put on shelves** state. You can configure custom components in the **To be configured**, **Verification failed**,
**Configured**, or **Removed** state.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Component Management**
4. On the **Component Management** page, enter a name in the search box or configure the
following parameters to search for the component that you want to configure: **Grouping**,
**Type**, **Status**, and **Classification**.

> **Note:** Valid values of the **Type** parameter: **Navigation**, **Card**, **Graphic and text**, **Display Card**, **Display components**, and **Other**.
> Valid values of the **Status** parameter: **To be configured**, **Verifying**, **Verification failed**, **Configured**, **Removed**, and **Put on shelves**.
> Valid values of the **Classification** parameter: **Preset components** and **Custom** **Components**.

5. Move the pointer over the component card and click **Configuration** in the upper-right
corner of the component card.
6. In the **Configure components** panel, following the instructions to complete the **Upload**
**component** and **Verify component** steps.
i. **Upload component**: In the Upload component step, configure the parameters that are described in the following table and click **Next Step**.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Component name | The name of the component that you specified when you created the component. You cannot modify the component name. |
| Component Key | The component key that you specified when you created the component. You cannot modify the component key. |
| Type | The component type that you specified when you created the component. You cannot modify the component type. |
| Grouping | The component group that you specified when you created the component. You cannot modify the component group. |
| Component executable | Click Upload files to upload a .js file that meets the JavaScript standard. The file cannot exceed 5 MB in size. |
| Component style file | Click Upload files to upload a .css file that meets the CSS standard. The file cannot exceed 5 MB in size. |
| Component configuration file | Click Upload files to upload a .json file that meets the JSON standard. The file cannot exceed 5 MB in size. |

ii. **Verify component**: In the Verify component step, wait until the component is verified and click **Complete**.

##### 7.4.4.3 Preview components

This topic describes how to preview preset and custom components on the Component Management page.

**Prerequisites**

You are assigned the operations administrator role.

**Limits**

You can preview only components in the **Configured**, **Removed**, or **Put on shelves** state.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Component Management**.
4. On the **Component Management** page, enter a component name in the search box or
specify filter conditions, such as **Grouping**, **Type**, **Status**, and **Classification**, to search for a component.

> **Note:** **Type**: Valid values of the parameter include **Navigation**, **Card**, **Graphic and** **text**, **Display Card**, **Display components**, and **Other**.
> **Status**: Valid values of the parameter include **To be configured**, **Verifying**, **Verification failed**, **Configured**, **Removed**, and **Put on shelves**.
> **Classification**: Valid values of the parameter include **Preset components** and **Custom Components**.

5. Move the pointer over the component card and click **Preview** in the upper-right corner of
the component card.
6. In the **Component preview** dialog box, preview the component.

> **Note:** The component preview displays a static preview image of the component instead of a preview rendered in real time.

##### 7.4.4.4 Modify a component

You can modify the basic information about a component when the component is updated. This topic describes how to modify a component.

**Prerequisites**

You are assigned the operations administrator role.

**Limits**

Preset components cannot be modified. Component keys cannot be modified.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Component Management**.
4. On the **Component Management** page, enter a component name in the search box or
specify filter conditions, such as **Grouping**, **Type**, **Status**, and **Classification**, to search for a component.

> **Note:** **Type**: Valid values of the parameter include **Navigation**, **Card**, **Graphic and** **text**, **Display Card**, **Display components**, and **Other**.
> **Status**: Valid values of the parameter include **To be configured**, **Verifying**, **Verification failed**, **Configured**, **Removed**, and **Put on shelves**.
> **Classification**: Valid values of the parameter include **Preset components** and **Custom Components**.

5. Move the pointer over the component card and click **Edit** in the upper-right corner of the
component card.
6. In the **Edit components** panel, modify the basic information about the component,
including the component name, type, and group.
7. Click **Submit**.

##### 7.4.4.5 Publish a component

You can publish a component based on your business requirements. After the component is published, you can use the component when you build a page. This topic describes how to publish a component.

**Prerequisites**

You are assigned the operations administrator role.

**Limits**

You can publish only components in the **Configured** or **Removed** state.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Component Management**.
4. On the **Component Management** page, enter a component name in the search box or
specify filter conditions, such as **Grouping**, **Type**, **Status**, and **Classification**, to search for a component.

> **Note:** **Type**: Valid values of the parameter include **Navigation**, **Card**, **Graphic and** **text**, **Display Card**, **Display components**, and **Other**.
> **Status**: Valid values of the parameter include **To be configured**, **Verifying**, **Verification failed**, **Configured**, **Removed**, and **Put on shelves**.
> **Classification**: Valid values of the parameter include **Preset components** and **Custom Components**.

5. Move the pointer over the component card and click **Shelf** in the upper-right corner of the
component card.
6. In the **Operation confirmation** message, click **OK**.

##### 7.4.4.6 Unpublish a component

You can unpublish a component based on your business requirements. After the component is unpublished, the component becomes unavailable and is no longer displayed on the Component Management page.

**Prerequisites**

You are assigned the operations administrator role.

**Limits**

You can unpublish only components in the **Put on shelves** state.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Component Management**.
4. On the **Component Management** page, enter a component name in the search box or
specify filter conditions, such as **Grouping**, **Type**, **Status**, and **Classification**, to search for a component.

> **Note:** **Type**: Valid values of the parameter include **Navigation**, **Card**, **Graphic and** **text**, **Display Card**, **Display components**, and **Other**.
> **Status**: Valid values of the parameter include **To be configured**, **Verifying**, **Verification failed**, **Configured**, **Removed**, and **Put on shelves**.
> **Classification**: Valid values of the parameter include **Preset components** and **Custom Components**.

5. Move the pointer over the component card and click **Lower shelf** in the upper-right corner
of the component card.
6. In the **Operation confirmation** message, click **OK**.

##### 7.4.4.7 Add to page

The system supports adding components to a page.

**Prerequisites**

The user performing this operation must be an operations administrator by default.

**Constraints**

Only components in the **Published** state support being added to a page.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Component Management**.
4. On the **Component Management** page, use filters such as component name, **Group**,
**Type**, **Status**, and **Category** to quickly locate your target component.

> **Note:** **Type**: Includes **Navigation**, **Card**, **Graphic And Text**, **Display Card**, **Display** **Components**, and **Other**.
> **Status**: Includes **Pending Configuration**, **Verifying**, **Verification Failed**, **Configured**, **Unpublished**, and **Published**.
> **Category**: Includes **Preset components** and **Custom Components**.

5. Click **Add to Page** in the upper-right corner of the component card.
6. In the **Add Page** dialog box, select the page where you want to insert the component.
You can select up to 50 pages in batch. Pages in the following four states cannot be selected: Published (modification pending scheduled release), Pending scheduled release, Draft (approval pending for publication), and Published (modification approval pending).

> After you add the component, it will be inserted at the end of the page. You must publish the page before the component becomes visible externally.

7. Click **OK**.

##### 7.4.4.8 Customize a component

This topic describes how to customize a component.

**Prerequisites**

You have the corresponding development knowledge and experience. After you download the development kit of a component, perform the following steps to customize the component:
1. Create a **DemoComponent** directory under the **src/component** directory. Under the
DemoComponent directory, create **index.jsx** and **index.module.css** files. To simplify operations, the **index.module.css** file is not modified in this example.

```
├── README.md ├── build ├── config-overrides.js ├── package-lock.json ├── package.json ├── public │ └── index.html ├── src │ ├── component │ │ └── .... // Other folders and files. │ │ └── DemoComponent │ │ └── index.jsx │ │ └── index.module.css │ ├── global.d.ts │ ├── index.dev.jsx │ ├── index.js │ └── property.json └── tsconfig.json
```

2. Add the following code to the **index.jsx** file in the **DemoComponent** directory:

```java
import React from "react"; import style from './index.module.css' const DemoComponent = (props) => {
  return (
    <div style={{ width: 1180, margin: "0 auto", backgroundColor: '#eee' }}>
      <div style={{ padding: 20, display: "flex", alignContent: "center"  }}>
        <div style={{ marginRight: 20 }}>External data</div>
        <div>{props.textSetterValue}</div>
      </div>
    </div>
```

); };

```
export default DemoComponent;
```

3. Modify the code in the index.js file under the src directory to import and export the
component that you created.

```java
'use strict'; import DemoComponent from './component/DemoComponent'; export default DemoComponent;
```

##### 7.4.4.9 Understand the tool and configurations for building custom components

**building custom components**

This topic describes the tool and configurations for building custom components.

**Procedure of using a scaffolding tool**

> **Important:** Node.js must be of V14.x or later.

> The project is built by using React. Do not change the major versions of react-dom and react in the scaffolding tool.
> You do not need to use a specific scaffolding kit for component compilation. However, make sure that the output JavaScript code complies with the Universal Module Definition (UMD) standard, and the configuration files and style files meet the platform requirements.
> The scaffolding tool uses react-app-rewired to build a component. For more information, view related component building materials.

1. After you add a component, in the message that appears, click **Download component**
**development kit** to download the scaffolding tool.

> **Note:** You can also download the scaffolding tool in the **Add components** or **Edit** **components** panel.

2. View the directories in the scaffolding tool.

> **Note:** The actual files in the src/component directory shall prevail. The following sample code shows an example.

```
├── README.md // The description file. ├── config-overrides.js // The component configuration file. ├── package-lock.json // The dependency lock file. ├── package.json // The dependency configuration file. ├── public │ └── index.html // The template file used for local development. ├── src │ ├── component │ │ ├── ExampleComponent.module.css // The detailed component style code in a .mo dule.css file. │ │ └── MyButton.tsx // The detailed component execution code in a .tsx file. │ ├── global.d.ts // The global description file. │ ├── index.dev.js // The main execution file in development mode. │ ├── index.js // The main execution file │ └── property.json // The configuration file of the component. └── tsconfig.json // The TypeScript configurations of the scaffolding tool.
```

3. Run the project by referring to the README.md file and open the URL returned from the
console. The following sample code describes the basic configurations of the component: `{`

```json
  "key": "DemoComponent", //The key that you specified when you created the component
```
