#### 7.4.5 Template management

##### 7.4.5.1 Site template

The site template provides preset site templates. You can quickly create a site based on a site template.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operation** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Template Management** > **Site Template**.
4. In the site template list, view the preset site templates.
Click **Preview** to preview the preset site. Click **View Details** to expand the site template details.

##### 7.4.5.2 Page template

The page template displays preset templates. You can quickly create pages and site templates based on these page templates.

###### 7.4.5.2.1 View page templates and page content

View preset and custom page templates, and the page content of each template.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Template Management** > **Page Template**.
4. In the page template list, view the preset and custom page templates. Use the page name
filter at the top of the page to quickly locate a template.
5. Click **View Page** in the **Actions** column to preview the page content.

###### 7.4.5.2.2 Create a page template

Customize a page template based on your business requirements.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Template Management** > **Page Template**.
4. Click **Create Page Template**.
5. In the **Create Page Template** dialog box, configure the page template.

| Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|
| Select Page | Select an existing page. |
| Page Template Name | The name must be 1 to 60 characters in length and cannot be the same as any existing page name. |
| ID | The ID must be 1 to 15 characters in length. It can contain lowercase letters, digits, underscores ( ), and hyphens (-). The first character must be a _ lowercase letter. The ID cannot be the same as any existing page ID. Changing the ID affects the page path. |
| Site Template | Select a site from the associated preset site templates. |

| Page Template Description | Enter a description for the page template. The description must be 1 to 200 characters in length. |
|---|---|

6. Click OK.

###### 7.4.5.2.3 Edit page template

You can modify the configuration when changes are needed for the page template.

**Constraints**

You cannot edit preset page templates.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager management console.
2. In the top navigation bar, select **Operations** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, select **Template Management** > **Page Template**.
4. In the page template list, click **Edit** in the **Actions** column.
5. In the **Edit Page Template** dialog box, modify the page template configuration. For
detailed descriptions of configuration items, see Create a page template.
6. Click **OK**.

###### 7.4.5.2.4 Delete a page template

You can delete a page template when you no longer need it.

**Limits**

The system does not allow you to delete preset page templates.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Portal Management**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Template Management** > **Page Template**.
4. In the page template list, click **Delete** in the **Actions** column.
5. In the **Note** dialog box, click **OK**.

### 7.5 Service support

#### 7.5.1 Ticket management

##### 7.5.1.1 Ticket list

The ticket list displays the tickets that are available for viewing and processing.

###### 7.5.1.1.1 View tickets

You can view the ticket lists on which you have permissions.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.
4. On the **Issues** page, click the **All**, **Created by Me**, **Pending Feedback**, **Pending**
**Confirmation**, **Unclaimed**, **Pending Tasks**, **Handled by Me**, and **Transferred by Me**
tabs to view tickets in different states.

| Tab | Displayed ticket | User and permission |
|---|---|---|
| All | All tickets accessible to the current user. | An operations administrator can view all tickets in the console. An administrator of a service group can view all tickets in the service group. A user who has the permissions to handle tickets can view the tickets submitted by the user, tickets handled by the user, and tickets to be claimed. A regular user can view only the tickets submitted by the user. |
| Created by Me | All tickets submitted by the current user. | All users can view the tickets that they submitted. |
| Pending Feedback | Tickets that are submitted by the current user and are in the Pending Feedback state. | All users can view the tickets that they submitted. |

| Pending Confirmatio n | Tickets that are submitted by the current user and are in the To Be Confirmed state. | All users can view the tickets that they submitted. |
|---|---|---|
| Unclaimed | Tickets that are in the Unclaimed state. | A user who has the permissions to handle tickets can view the tickets to be claimed. |
| Pending Tasks | Tickets that are submitted by the current user and are in the Handling or Suspending state. | A user who has the permissions to handle tickets can view the tickets to be handled by the user. |
| Handled by Me | Tickets whose owner is the current user and that are in the Pending Feedback, To Be Confirmed, or Completed state. | A user who has the permissions to handle tickets can view the tickets handled by the user. |
| Transferred by Me | Tickets that are transferred by the current user. | A user who has the permissions to handle tickets can view the tickets transferred by the user. |

5. Click **Advanced Filter** above the ticket list, configure the **Ticket Number**, **Issue Type**,
**Update Time**, **Handle By**, **Over Time**, and **Status** parameters, and then click **Search** to
quickly filter tickets.
6. Find the ticket that you want to view and click its number or **Details** in the **Actions**
column. On the **Ticket details** page, view the ticket details.

###### 7.5.1.1.2 Withdraw tickets

This topic describes how to withdraw a ticket before it is claimed.

**Prerequisites**

You are the ticket submitter. Tickets are in the **Unclaimed** state.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.
4. Withdraw one or more tickets at a time.

**Withdraw a ticket**

a. On the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to withdraw and click its number or
**Details** in the Actions column.
b. In the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, click **Withdraw** in the upper-right corner. c. In the message that appears, click **OK**. After a ticket is withdrawn, the state of the ticket changes to **Withdrawn**.

**Withdraw multiple tickets at a time**

a. On the Issues page, select the tickets that you want to withdraw. b. Click **Withdraw** in the lower part of the page. c. In the message that appears, click **OK**. After the tickets are withdrawn, the state of the tickets changes to **Withdrawn**.

###### 7.5.1.1.3 Add comments to a ticket

You can add comments to a ticket at any time during ticket processing.

**Prerequisites**

You are the ticket submitter or have the permissions to process tickets.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.
4. On the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to manage and click its number or click
**Details** in the Actions column.
5. On the **Comment** tab of the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, enter
comments and upload attachments.

> **Note:** Supported file formats: PNG, JPG, TXT, RAR, DOC, XLS, ZIP, 7Z, and MP4. A single attachment cannot exceed 512 MB in size. A maximum of five attachments can be uploaded.

6. Click **Comment**.

###### 7.5.1.1.4 Modify a ticket

This topic describes how to modify a ticket.

**Prerequisites**

You are the ticket submitter. The ticket is in the **Withdrawn** state.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.
4. On the **Created by Me** tab of the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to modify and
click its number or **Details** in the Actions column.
5. In the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, click **Edit** in the upper-right
corner.
6. On the **Edit a ticket** page, modify the parameters of the ticket. For more information about
the parameters, see Submit a ticket.
7. Click **Submit**.

###### 7.5.1.1.5 Claim tickets

Users who have the permissions to process tickets can view all tickets that are in the Unclaimed state and claim the tickets for processing.

**Prerequisites**

You have the permissions to process tickets. Tickets are in the **Unclaimed** state.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.
4. Claim one or more tickets at a time.

**Claim a ticket**

a. On the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to claim and click its number or click
**Details** in the Actions column.
b. In the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, click **Claim** in the upperright corner. c. In the message that appears, click **OK**. After a ticket is claimed, the state of the ticket changes to **Handling**.

**Claim multiple tickets**

a. On the Issues page, select the tickets that you want to claim. b. Click **Claim** in the lower part of the page. c. In the message that appears, click **OK**. After a ticket is claimed, the state of the ticket changes to **Handling**.

###### 7.5.1.1.6 Expedite a long-pending ticket

If a ticket remains open for a time after it is submitted, the ticket submitter can request the ticket processer to expedite the progress of the ticket.

**Prerequisites**

You are the ticket submitter. Tickets are in the **Handling** or **Suspending** state.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.
4. On the **Created by Me** tab of the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to manage and
click its number or click **Details** in the Actions column.
5. In the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, click **Urge** in the upper-right
corner. You can expedite a ticket only once per day. If you expedite a ticket multiple times, the system prompts that the operation is repeated.

> After you send a request to expedite a ticket, the ticket processer receives a notification if notification is enabled on the message gateway. This way, the ticket can be processed with higher priority.

6. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

###### 7.5.1.1.7 Submit a withdrawn or pending feedback ticket

**ticket**

A ticket submitter can resubmit withdrawn or pending feedback tickets.

**Prerequisites**

You are the ticket submitter. Tickets are in the **Withdrawn** or **Pending Feedback** state.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.
4. On the **Created by Me** or **Pending Feedback** tab of the Issues page, find the ticket that
you want to manage and click its number or click **Details** in the Actions column.
5. In the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, click **Submit** in the upper-right
corner. For more information about how to submit a newly created ticket, see Submit a ticket.

> **Note:** After you resubmit a withdrawn ticket, no ticket processer is assigned to the ticket. In this case, the ticket is assigned based on service groups, service engineers, and assignment rules.
> After you resubmit a pending feedback ticket, the ticket is assigned to the original ticket processer, and the state of the ticket changes to Handling.
> The ticket processer receives the ticket along with a notification if notification is enabled on the message gateway. This way, the ticket can be processed in a timely manner.

6. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

###### 7.5.1.1.8 Return an in-progress ticket

If a ticket lacks valid descriptions, the ticket processer can return the ticket to the ticket submitter, who can add the required ticket information.

**Prerequisites**

You have the permissions to process tickets. Tickets are in the **Handling** state.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.
4. On the **Pending Tasks** tab of the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to manage and
click its number or click **Details** in the Actions column.
5. On the **Return to Submitter** tab of the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details**
page, enter a comment for returning the ticket and upload attachments.

> **Note:** After the ticket is returned to the ticket submitter, the ticket submitter receives a notification if notification is enabled on the message gateway. This way, the ticket submitter can add the required ticket information in a timely manner.

6. Click **Return to Submitter** in the lower-right corner.
7. In the message that appears, click **OK**. After the ticket is returned to the ticket submitter,
the state of the ticket changes to **Pending Feedback**.

###### 7.5.1.1.9 Transfer tickets

If the processer of a ticket cannot process the ticket, the ticket processer can transfer the ticket to another engineer for processing. Operations administrators can transfer all inprogress tickets to other engineers.

**Prerequisites**

You have the permissions to process tickets. Tickets are in the **Handling** state.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.
4. Transfer one or more tickets at a time.

**Transfer a ticket**

a. On the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to transfer and click its number or click **Details** in the Actions column. b. On the Transfer tab of the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, specify a service group and an engineer, enter a comment, and then upload attachments.

> **Note:** After the ticket is transferred, the engineer to whom the ticket is transferred receives a notification if notification is enabled on the message gateway. This way, the ticket can be processed in a timely manner.

| Paramete r | Description |
|---|---|
| Transfer Service Group | Select the service group to which you want to transfer the ticket from the drop- down list. You can select only one service group. |
| Service Personn el | Select the engineer to whom you want to transfer the ticket. You can select only one engineer. |
| Commen t Content | Enter a comment to provide relevant information about the transfer. |
| Upload Attachm ents | Upload the attachments related to the transfer. |

c. Click **Transfer** in the lower-right corner. d. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

**Transfer multiple tickets**

a. On the Issues page, select the tickets that you want to transfer. b. Click **Forward** in the lower part of the page. c. In the **Ticket transfer** dialog box, specify the transfer information and enter a comment. For more information about the parameters, see the Transfer a ticket section of this topic. d. Click **OK**.

###### 7.5.1.1.10 Reassign tickets

Administrators can reassign tickets in the Handling state to other engineers for handling. After a ticket is reassigned, the service level agreement (SLA) duration of the corresponding node is recalculated.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or a service group administrator. Tickets are in the **Handling** state.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.
4. Reassign one or more tickets at a time.

**Reassign a ticket**

a. On the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to reassign and click its number or
**Details** in the Actions column.
b. On the **Reassign** tab of the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, configure the parameters that are described in the following table.

| Paramete r | Description |
|---|---|
| Reassign Service Group | Select the service group to which you want to reassign the ticket from the drop- down list. You can select only one service group. |
| Service Personn el | Select the engineer to whom you want to reassign the ticket. You can select only one engineer. |
| Commen t Content | Enter a comment to provide relevant information about the reassignment. |
| Upload Attachm ents | Upload the attachments related to the reassignment. |

c. Click **Reassign** in the lower-right corner.

**Reassign multiple tickets at a time**

a. On the Issues page, select the tickets that you want to reassign. b. Click **Reassign** in the lower part of the page. c. In the **Reassign Ticket** dialog box, configure the parameters. For more information about the parameters, see the Reassign a ticket section in this topic. d. Click **OK**.

###### 7.5.1.1.11 Assign tickets

Administrators can assign unclaimed tickets to appropriate engineers for processing.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or a service group administrator. Tickets are in the **Unclaimed** state.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.
4. Assign one or more tickets at a time.

**Assign a ticket**

a. On the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to assign and click its number or click
**Details** in the Actions column.
b. On the **Assign** tab of the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, configure the parameters that are described in the following table.

| Paramete r | Description |
|---|---|
| Assigned Service Group | Select the service group to which you want to assign the ticket from the drop- down list. You can select only one service group. |
| Service Personn el | Select the engineer to whom you want to assign the ticket. You can select only one engineer. |
| Commen t Content | Enter a comment to provide relevant information about the assignment. |
| Upload Attachm ents | Upload the attachments related to the assignment. |

c. Click **Assign** in the lower-right corner.

**Assign multiple tickets**

a. On the Issues page, select the tickets that you want to assign. b. Click **Assign** in the lower part of the page. c. In the **Assignment Information** dialog box, configure the parameters. For more information about the parameters, see Assign a ticket. d. Click **OK**.

###### 7.5.1.1.12 Suspend a ticket

If a ticket that is in progress cannot be processed at the moment, you can suspend the ticket.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator, a service group administrator, or a ticket processer. Tickets are in the **Handling** state.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.
4. On the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to suspend and click its number or click
**Details** in the Actions column.
5. On the **Suspend** tab of the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, enter the
reason for the suspension.
6. Click **Suspend** in the lower-right corner.
7. In the message that appears, click **OK**. After the ticket is suspended, the state of the ticket
changes to **Suspending**.

###### 7.5.1.1.13 Activate a ticket

You can activate a ticket that is suspended.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator, a service group administrator, or a ticket processer. Tickets are in the **Suspending** state.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.
4. On the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to activate and click its number or click
**Details** in the Actions column.
5. On the **Activate** tab of the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, enter a
comment for the activation.
6. Click **Activate** in the lower-right corner.
7. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

###### 7.5.1.1.14 Close a ticket

After a ticket is processed by an engineer, the engineer can close the ticket and transfer it to the ticket submitter for verification.

**Prerequisites**

You have the permissions to process tickets. Tickets are in the **Handling** state.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.
4. On the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to close and click its number or click
**Details** in the Actions column.
5. On the **Close** tab of the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, enter a
comment and upload attachments.

> **Note:** After the ticket is closed, the ticket submitter receives a notification if notification is enabled on the message gateway. Then, the ticket submitter can verify the results.

6. Click **Close** in the lower-right corner.
7. In the message that appears, click **OK**. After the ticket is closed, the state of the ticket
changes to **To Be Confirmed**.

###### 7.5.1.1.15 Verify the results of a pending confirmation ticket

**confirmation ticket**

After a ticket is closed by the ticket processer, the ticket is transferred to the ticket submitter for verification. The ticket submitter can verify the results to check whether the issue is resolved.

**Prerequisites**

You are the ticket submitter. Tickets are in the **To Be Confirmed** state.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.
4. On the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to manage and click its number or click
**Details** in the Actions column.
5. In the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, check whether the issue is
resolved in the ticket.

**If the issue is resolved**

a. On the **Confirm** tab of the **Process Ticket** section, enter a comment and upload attachments. b. Click **Confirm** in the lower-right corner. c. In the message that appears, click **OK**. After the ticket is confirmed, the state of the ticket changes to **Completed**.

**If the issue is not resolved**

a. On the **Unhandled** tab of the **Process Ticket** section, enter a comment and upload attachments.

> **Note:** After you confirm that the issue is not resolved, the ticket processer receives a notification if notification is enabled on the message gateway. This way, the ticket processer can process the ticket in a timely manner.

b. Click **Unhandled** in the lower-right corner. c. In the message that appears, click **OK**. The state of the ticket changes to **Handling**, and the ticket is assigned to the original ticket processer for processing.

###### 7.5.1.1.16 Evaluate a completed ticket

After the submitter of a ticket confirms that the issue is resolved, the submitter can evaluate the ticket.

**Prerequisites**

You are the ticket submitter. Tickets are in the **Completed** state.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.
4. On the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to evaluate and click its number or click
**Details** in the Actions column.
5. On the **Evaluate** tab of the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, rate the
ticket, enter your comment, and then upload attachments as needed.

> **Note:** When you rate a ticket, select at least half a star and at most five stars.

6. Click **Evaluate** in the lower-right corner.
7. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

###### 7.5.1.1.17 Delete tickets

After a ticket is withdrawn by the submitter, the submitter can delete the ticket if it is no longer required.

**Prerequisites**

You are the ticket submitter. Tickets are in the **Withdrawn** state.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.
4. Delete one or more tickets at a time.

**Delete a ticket**

a. On the Issues page, find the ticket that you want to delete and click its number or click
**Details** in the Actions column.
b. In the **Process Ticket** section on the **Ticket details** page, click **Delete** in the upperright corner. c. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

**Delete multiple tickets**

a. On the Issues page, select the tickets that you want to delete. b. Click **Delete** in the lower part of the page. c. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

###### 7.5.1.1.18 Export ticket details

Operations administrators can export ticket details to local machines for storage.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issues**.
4. On the **All** tab, click **Export Ticket Details** above the ticket list to export ticket details as
a **.csv** file to your local machine.

##### 7.5.1.2 Submit a ticket

You can submit tickets to request technical support. A ticket includes the issue type, issue description, and attachments.

**Prerequisites**

You are granted the permissions to submit tickets.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Submit Issues**.

> **Note:** You can also click **Create a Ticket** on the **Ticket List** page to submit a ticket.

4. On the **Create a Ticket** page, configure the parameters that are described in the following
table.

| Parameter or setting | Description |
|---|---|
| Title | The title of the ticket. |
| Issue Type | The issue type of the ticket. Valid values: Product usage, Business affected, Account permission issues, and Billing issues. |
| Problem Description | The description of the issue in the ticket. |
| Custom settings | If custom parameters are available for the issue type of the ticket, configure the custom parameters. |

5. Click **Submit**.

**Form Configuration**, and **SLA Configuration** steps.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Name | The name of the issue type. |
| Description | The description of the issue type. |

ii. Configure the parameters in the Form Configuration step and click **Next**.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Component | Available types of components include Input, Select, Time, and Other. Input: Available components of this type include Input Box, Number Field, and Multi-line Input Box. Select: Available components of this type include Select, Single-select, and Multi-select. Time: Available components of this type include Date and Time Interval. Other: Available components of this type include Attachment, Cloud Service Type, Cascade Selection, Organization, Resource Set, and Cloud Service Instance. |
| Form Design | Drag components from the left-side Component section to this section. After you drag components to this section, you can drag them in the current section to adjust the display order, copy components, and remove components. Click Preview Complete Form in the upper-right corner to preview the designed form. |
| Component Configurati on | In the Form Design section, select a component. Then, configure the component in the Component Configuration section. |

iii. Configure the parameters in the SLA Configuration step and click **Save**.

| Parameter or section | Description |
|---|---|
| Basic operation | This section displays the preset actions and their status, permission descriptions, and notification methods. You cannot modify the preset actions. You can configure notification methods in the Notification Method column. The notification methods include Short Message Service (SMS), email, and DingTalk. |
|   | You can configure custom actions in this section. |

|   | Add a custom action |
|---|---|
| Custom Actions | a. Click Add. b. In the Add Custom Action panel, configure the parameters in the Configuration Call and Pop-up Layer Configuration steps. a. Configuration Call: Configure the Operation Name, Operation Permission Settings, Available Status, Interface call key, and Interface call URL parameters. b. Pop-up Layer Configuration: Design and configure the form. Drag components from the left-side Component section to the Form Design section. In the Form Design section, select a component. Then, configure the component in the Component Configuration section. c. Click Submission. Modify a custom action a. Find the custom action that you want to modify and clickC onfiguration in the Operation column. b. In the Add Custom Action panel, modify the configurations of the action. c. Click Submission. |

**Delete a custom action**

a. Find the custom action that you want to delete and click **Delete** in the Operation column. b. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

| SLA Setti ngs | Targ et Setti ngs | Set time limits for the response to and processing of tickets. This way, you can respond to tickets by level to improve service efficiency. Node Dwell Time: the amount of time from when the ticket is forwarded to the current node to when it is forwarded to the next node. First Node Response Time: the amount of time from when the ticket is forwarded to the current node to when an engineer from a service group first claims the ticket. Node Processing Duration: the amount of time consumed to process the ticket after the assigned ticket processor claims the ticket on the current node. |
|---|---|---|
|   | Servi ce Remi nder | Configure the condition, time, and methods for service notifications. You can specify multiple conditions. A notification is sent if one of the conditions is met. Conditions: Supported conditions include Before Dwell Time Expires, After Dwell Time Expires, Before First Response Time Expires, After First Response Time Expires, Before Node Processing Duration Expires, and After Node Processing Duration Expires. Time: Specify a time, in minutes. Notification methods: Internal messages, text messages, emails, and DingTalk messages are supported. You can select multiple options at a time. Add an entry: Click Add. In the new line that appears, specify a condition, a time, and notification methods. Remove an entry: Click the icon next to the entry. |
|   | Remi nder Obje ct | Select the recipients of service notifications. You can select multiple options at a time. If you select Specify User, you must select one or more users from the Specify User drop-down list. If you select Specify Role, you must select one or more roles from the Specify Role drop-down list. |

This topic describes how to modify an issue type.

You are an operations administrator.

3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Issue Type**.
4. On the **Issue Type** page, find the issue type that you want to copy and click **Copy** in the
Operation column.

##### 7.5.1.5 Ticket dispatch rule

###### 7.5.1.5.1 Create a ticket dispatch rule

Tickets can be automatically assigned to engineers based on ticket dispatch rules. You can create different ticket dispatch rules for different scenarios.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Allocation Rule**.
4. On the **Allocation Rule** page, click **Create a Rule**.
5. In the **Create a Ticket Assignment Rule** panel, configure the parameters that are
described in the following table.

| Parameter |   | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Basic Informat ion | Rule Name | The name of the rule. |
|   | Description | The description of the rule. |
|   | Assign to Service Group | The service group with which you want to associate the rule. You can select only one service group from the drop-down list. If no service group is available, create a service group on the Service Group page. For more information, see Create a service group. |
|   | Priority | The priority of the rule. A greater value indicates a higher priority. Valid values: 1 to 999. Existing rules and their priorities are displayed in the drop-down list. The priority of each rule must be unique. |
| Rule Group |   | The conditions based on which tickets are assigned to engineers. You can add conditions and condition groups to a rule group. Add a condition or a condition group: Note The relationship between conditions and condition groups can be And or Or. And indicates that all conditions must be met. Or indicates that at least one condition must be met. a. Click Add Condition or Add Group. b. Configure the condition, condition type, and condition value. Condition: Select a condition. Supported conditions include organization, service, issue type, description, and ticket content. Condition type: After you select a condition, select a supported condition type. Condition value: This item is displayed after you select a condition type. Set the condition value based on the condition and condition type. Delete a condition or a condition group: Click the icon on the right side of the condition or condition group. |

6. Click **OK**.

This topic describes how to view the created ticket dispatch rules and the service group and rule conditions in a rule.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Tickets** > **Allocation Rule**.
4. On the Allocation rules page, view the ticket dispatch rules.
5. Click **Advanced Filter** above the rule list, configure the following filter conditions, and then
click **Search** to quickly search for ticket dispatch rules: **Rule name**, **Description**, **Assign**
**to Service Group**, and **Status**.
6. Click a rule name. In the **Rule Details** panel, view the rule details.

###### 7.5.1.5.3 Modify a ticket dispatch rule

This topic describes how to modify the basic information, service group, and match conditions of a ticket dispatch rule.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.

##### 7.5.1.6 Data insights

The Data Insight page displays the real-time data and historical data of the ticket service.

###### 7.5.1.6.1 View the ticket overview

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or a service group administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Data Insight**.
4. Click the **Ticket Overview** tab.
5. View the ticket overview.

| Item | Description |
|---|---|
| Overall statistics | Displays the total number of tickets in the Total Tickets card and the numbers of tickets in different states, including Unclaimed, Withdrawn, Handling, Pending Feedback, To Be Confirmed, Completed, and Suspending. |

| Overdue Unprocesse d Ticket Statistics | Displays statistics on overdue tickets in a chart and a table. |
|---|---|
| SLA Trend | Displays the fulfillment trend of the ticket service level agreement (SLA). You can switch between the 1 Month and 1 Week views. |
| Service Group Personnel | Displays the information about service groups, including Service Group Name, People During Business Hours, and Total People in Service Group. |

###### 7.5.1.6.2 View the ticket type analysis

This topic describes how to view the ticket type analysis on the Data Insight page.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or a service group administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Data Insight**.
4. Click the **Ticket Type Analysis** tab.
5. View the analysis information.

| Item | Description |
|---|---|
| Data and Percentage of Tickets of Various Types | Displays the number and percentage of tickets of each type. You can switch between Pie Chart and Column Chart. |
| New Ticket Trend Analysis | Displays the trend of new tickets. You can switch between the1 Month and 1 Week views. |
| Correlation Analysis of Ticket Type and Average Processing Duration | Displays the average amount of time required to resolve tickets of each type in a column chart and a table. |

###### 7.5.1.6.3 View the processing efficiency analysis of tickets

**of tickets**

This topic describes how to view the processing efficiency analysis of tickets on the Data Insight page.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator or a service group administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Issues** > **Data Insight**.
4. Click the **Processing Efficiency Analysis** tab.
5. View the analysis information.

| Item | Description |
|---|---|
| Maximum Waiting Time | Displays the longest waiting time recorded for tickets to be claimed. |
| Maximum Timeout Period | Displays the longest timeout period recorded for completed tickets. |
| Response Duration and Resolution Duration of Service Group | Displays the amount of time required to respond to or resolve a ticket by each service group. |
| Top 10 Tickets with the Longest Processing Duration | Displays the information about the top 10 tickets by processing duration. You can switch between the Resolved and Unresolved views. You can also check the detailed processing information of a ticket. To do so, find the ticket that you want to view and click its number or click Details in the Actions column to go to the ticket details page. |

| Configuratio n item | Description |
|---|---|

| Substitute Employee | Select one or more substitute employees. |
| Substituti on Method | You can choose from: Transfer the shift and all tickets within the shift., Transfer only tickets that are not processed., and Retain and Copy. Transfer the shift and all tickets within the shift.: The system transfers the entire shift and all associated tickets to the substitute employee. Transfer only tickets that are not processed.: The system transfers only unprocessed tickets within the shift to the substitute employee. Processed tickets remain with the original assignee. #### 7.5.2 Document management

##### 7.5.2.1 Documents

Operations administrators can maintain and update documents such as service manuals and usage specifications to control the query and display of documents.

**Background information**

As an operations administrator, you can update and maintain knowledge documents related to your cloud platform by using the document management feature. This allows you to manage documents in a centralized manner. Users can query and view knowledge documents and obtain relevant information. For example, users can query the usage specifications and process descriptions of a cloud service on the service portal and help center. This helps users obtain the latest knowledge and information at the earliest opportunity. Document list: displays all documents on the cloud platform. Document Classification: displays document categories, document groups, and document collections at three levels. Document categories are at level 1, document groups are at level 2, and document collections are at level 3.

**Limits**

You cannot create document groups in, rename, move, or delete a preset document category. You can only copy preset document groups. You cannot create document collections in, rename, move, or delete a preset document group. You cannot rename, move, or delete a preset document collection. You can only copy preset documents.

**Permissions on directories in different states**

> **Note:** Directories may be in the states described in the following table. Different operations can be performed on directories in different states. In the following table, ✓ indicates that the operation is supported, and × indicates that the operation is not supported.

| State/Operation | Delet e a direct ory | Rev oke the publ ishi ng, ena blin g, or disa blin g of a dire ctor y | View the review details of a directory | Ena ble a dire ctor y | Dis abl e a dire ctor y | Mov e a dire ctor y | Rename a directory |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enabled | × | × | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ |
| Enabled (being reviewed for disabling) | × | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | × | × |
| Enabled (review for disabling rejected) | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ | × | ✓ |
| Enabled (disabling failed) | × | × | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ |
| Disabled | ✓ | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ | ✓ |

**Permissions on documents in different states**

> **Note:** Documents may be in the states described in the following table. Different operations can be performed on documents in different states. In the following table, ✓ indicates that the operation is supported, and × indicates that the operation is not supported.

**States related to the editing and publishing of documents**

| State/Operat ion | Mo dif y a do cu me nt | Pu bli sh a do cu me nt | Cop y a doc um ent | Del ete a doc um ent | Re vok e the pu blis hin g, ena bli ng, or dis abl ing of a doc um ent | Vie w the revi ew det ails of a doc ume nt | Ena ble a doc um ent | Dis abl e a doc um ent | Mo ve a doc um ent | Ren ame a doc ume nt | Ma nag e ver sio ns |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | × | × | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Draft (being reviewed for publishing) | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ |
| Draft (review rejected) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | ✓ | × | × | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Draft (publishing failed) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | ✓ | × | × | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Published | ✓ | × | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Published (modifications to be published) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

| Published (being reviewed for publishing modifications) | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Published (review for publishing modifications rejected) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | ✓ | ✓ | × | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Published (failed to publish modifications) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

**States related to the enabling and disabling of documents**

| State/Operat ion | Mo dif y a do cu me nt | Pu bli sh a do cu me nt | Cop y a doc um ent | Del ete a doc um ent | Re vok e the pu blis hin g, ena bli ng, or dis abl ing of a doc um ent | Vie w the revi ew det ails of a doc ume nt | Ena ble a doc um ent | Dis abl e a doc um ent | Mo ve a doc um ent | Ren ame a doc ume nt | Ma nag e ver sio ns |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enabled | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ | ✓ |
| Enabled (being reviewed for disabling) | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | × | × | ✓ |
| Enabled (review for disabling rejected) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ | × | ✓ | ✓ |

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Disabled | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Disabled (being reviewed for enabling) | × | × | ✓ | × | ✓ | ✓ | × | × | × | × | ✓ |

###### 7.5.2.1.1 Create a document category

This topic describes how to create a document category.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Document Management** > **Documents**.
4. In the Document Classification section, click the
icon.
5. In the **Create** dialog box, enter a name in the **Name** field.

> **Note:** A document category consists of document groups and collections. When you create a document category, a document group and a document collection are created in the document category by default. By default, after a document category is created, it is displayed in the upper part of the Document Classification section.
> The default name of a document group is in the Default Group ({Document category name}) format.
> The default name of a document collection is in the Default Document Collection ({Document category name}) format.

6. Click **OK**.

###### 7.5.2.1.2 Create a document group

This topic describes how to create a document group.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Document Management** > **Documents**.
4. In the Document Classification section, find the document category that you want to
manage, move the pointer over the icon to the right of its name, and then select **Create**
**a child**.
5. In the dialog box that appears, enter a name in the **Name** field.

> **Note:** You do not need to configure the Select Location parameter. This parameter is dimmed by default and indicates the document category to which the document group belongs.

6. Click **OK**.

###### 7.5.2.1.3 Create a document collection

This topic describes how to create a document collection.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.

4. In the Document Classification section, find the document group that you want to manage,
move the pointer over the icon to the right of its name, and then select **Create a child**.
5. In the dialog box that appears, enter a name in the **Name** field.

> **Note:** You do not need to configure the Select Location parameter. This parameter is dimmed by default and indicates the document group to which the document collection belongs.

6. Click **OK**.

**group, or document collection**

###### 7.5.2.1.5 Move a document category, document group, or document collection

**group, or document collection**

This topic describes how to move a document category, document group, or document collection to adjust its location.

**Limits**

In a custom document collection, a level-2 or level-3 document category cannot be moved upwards to be a level-1 document category.

**Prerequisites**

You are an operations administrator.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Operations** > **Support**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Document Management** > **Documents**.
4. In the Document Classification section, find the document category, document group, or
document collection that you want to move, move the pointer over the icon to the right of its name, and then select **Move**.
5. In the dialog box that appears, select the location at which you want the document
category, document group, or document collection to be displayed.

> **Important:** You can only move an object to another location at the same level. After you move the object, its subordinate objects are moved accordingly.
> You can place an object before or after the specified object.

6. Click **OK**.

## 8 Security

### 8.1 Overview

The Apsara Uni-manger Management Console uses AccessKey pairs and multi-factor authentication (MFA) to enhance security when you access systems and resources.

| Module | Description |
|---|---|
| AccessKey pairs | AccessKey pairs are used to access cloud resources. You can view the AccessKey pairs of your account. You can create AccessKey pairs within your account. Each account can have at most two AccessKey pairs. You can enable or disable an AccessKey pair of your account. However, at least one AccessKey pair must be enabled within your account. You can delete an AccessKey pair from your account. However, at least one AccessKey pair must be retained within your account. |
| MFA | MFA is an identity authentication method that enhances security by requiring additional verification factors beyond the username and password of an account. You can check whether the MFA feature is enabled for a user. If the MFA feature is disabled for a user, you can enable the feature for the user. However, you cannot disable the MFA feature after it is enabled. You can bind or unbind virtual MFA devices. You can reset MFA keys. |

### 8.2 AccessKey pairs of a personal account

**account**

An AccessKey pair consists of an AccessKey ID and an AccessKey secret. AccessKey pairs are used to authenticate the identity of request senders, which can ensure cloud resource security.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the upper-right corner of the homepage, click the profile picture and click **User**
**Information** in the menu that appears.

| Operation | Procedure |
|---|---|

| View AccessKey pairs | In the AccessKey Pair section, view the AccessKey pairs of your account. Note The AccessKey IDs and AccessKey secrets provide full permissions on cloud resources within your Apsara Stack tenant account. Keep them confidential. |
|---|---|
| Create an AccessKey pair | You can delete your existing AccessKey pairs and create new ones to implement the rotation of AccessKey pairs. i. In the AccessKey Pair section, click Create AccessKey Pair. ii. In the message that appears, click Close. |
| Disable an AccessKey pair | Important If you disable an AccessKey pair, errors may occur in the services or applications that depend on the AccessKey pair. Proceed with caution. i. In the AccessKey Pair section, find the AccessKey pair that you want to disable and click Disabled in the Actions column. ii. In the message that appears, click Disable. |
| Enable an AccessKey pair | In the AccessKey Pair section, find the AccessKey pair that you want to enable and click Enable in the Actions column. |
| Delete an AccessKey pair | Important If you delete an AccessKey pair, errors may occur in the services or applications that depend on the AccessKey pair. Proceed with caution. i. In the AccessKey Pair section, find the AccessKey pair that you want to delete and click Delete in the Actions column. ii. In the message that appears, click Delete. |
| View the logs of an AccessKey pair | i. In the AccessKey Pair section, find the AccessKey pair whose logs you want to view and click View AccessKey Pair Logs in the Actions column. The AccessKey Logs page appears. For more information about AccessKey pair logs, see AccessKey logs. |

### 8.3 MFA

#### 8.3.1 Overview

Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is an authentication method. In addition to username and password authentication, MFA provides an extra layer of protection.

**Introduction to MFA**

When MFA is enabled, you must enter your username and password (first security factor) and then a variable verification code (second security factor) from an MFA device when you log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console. Two-factor authentication enhances security for your account. MFA devices use the Time-based One-time Password (TOTP) algorithm to generate timedependent 6-digit dynamic verification codes. The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console supports software-based virtual MFA devices. You can install software (such as the Alibaba Cloud app) that supports MFA on your mobile device (such as your mobile phone) to act as a virtual MFA device.

**Precautions**

The TOTP algorithm requires that the time of the system clock of the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console remain consistent with the standard time on the Internet. Otherwise, discrepancies in time can lead to inconsistent MFA verification codes and you may be unable to log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

#### 8.3.2 Manage MFA

Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is an authentication method. In addition to username and password authentication, MFA provides an extra layer of protection. You can enable or disable the MFA feature in the console.

**Bind a virtual MFA device**

1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the upper-right corner of the Home page, click the profile picture and select **User**
**Information** in the menu that appears.
3. In the upper-right corner of the **MFA** section, click **Bind Virtual MFA Device**.
4. On the **Bind Virtual MFA Device** page, bind an MFA device as prompted. After an MFA
device is bound, the value of the MFA Status parameter changes to Enabled and the value of the Device Status changes to Bound.

> **Note:** After a virtual MFA device is bound, you must enter a 6-digit MFA verification code in addition to your username and password before you can log on to the Apsara Uni- manager Management Console.

**Disable a virtual MFA device**

1. In the upper-right corner of the **MFA** section on the **User Information** page, click **Disable**
**Virtual MFA Device**.
2. In the message that appears, click **Disable Virtual MFA Device**.
After you disable the MFA feature, you need to only enter your username and password next time you log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

**Forcibly enable the MFA feature**

Administrators, including the platform administrator, operations administrator, and organization administrator, can check whether the MFA feature is enabled for their users. If the MFA feature is disabled for the users, the administrators can forcibly enable the MFA feature for the users.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, click **Enterprise**.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Users** > **Users**.
4. On the Users page, click the **System Users** tab.
5. Find the user for which you want to enable the MFA feature, move the pointer over the
icon in the **Actions** column, and then click **MFA Settings**.
6. In the MFA Settings dialog box, turn on **MFA Settings** and click **OK**.

> **Note:** The MFA feature can be forcibly enabled for users, but cannot be forcibly disabled.
> Before the MFA feature is enabled, the MFA feature of the user is in the **Disabled** **and Unbound** state.
> After the MFA feature is enabled, the MFA feature of the user is in the **Enabled** **and Unbound** state. After the MFA feature is forcibly enabled for a user, the user must go to the Bind Virtual MFA Device page to bind a virtual MFA device before the user can log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.

## 12 OpenAPI Explorer

### 12.1 Overview

This topic describes the permissions and overview of OpenAPI Explorer. OpenAPI Explorer is an integrated portal that allows external developers to use Apsara Stack capabilities. It provides documentation, debugging tools, SDKs, and sample code of APIs. OpenAPI Explorer provides a series of APIs and shares its core capabilities and services with external developers. This way, external developers can access and use these resources to develop innovative and growth services.

**Permissions**

The following table describes the default permissions in OpenAPI Explorer.

| Permission | Description |
|---|---|
| View call statistics | You can view all features in the Call Statistics module. |
| View page integration configurations | You can view all features in Page Integration Configurations. You cannot modify these features. |
| Modify page integration configurations | You can view and modify all feature configurations in Page Integration Configurations. |

Different roles have different permissions in OpenAPI Explorer. The following table describes the default roles and their permissions.

| Role | Permission |
|---|---|
| Organization administrator | Views call statistics and page integration configurations. |
| Operations administrator | Views call statistics and views and modifies page integration configurations. |
| Security auditor | Views call statistics and page integration configurations. |

**Overview of OpenAPI Explorer**

1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Development Tools** > **API & SDK** >
**OpenAPI Explorer**.
3. On the **OpenAPI Explorer** page, select a service or feature based on your business
requirements. The following table describes the services and features.

| Menu | Description |
|---|---|
| Home | The API Integration tab provides API developer guides, API debugging tools, SDK sample code, and API call statistics. To view API call statistics, you must be granted the required permissions. You can search by cloud service or text content. This tab contains the Popular Services and Recent Calls tabs. Note You can click View Cloud Service Endpoint to go to the Service Endpoint page and query the endpoints of each cloud service. On the Page Integration tab, you can view the process of page integration configuration. You can click Page Integration Configuration to go to the Overview page of Page Integration. |
| API Integrati on | API Documentation: provides the API references of cloud services. API Debugging: allows you to debug API operations. API Change History: records the change history of API operations of cloud services. SDK Sample Code: provides SDK sample code of cloud services. Diagnostic Center: allows you to perform intelligent diagnostics on API error messages. MCP Service Management: allows you to create and manage MCP interface services. The MCP service allows you to convert API operations of cloud services into online MCP interfaces. This allows large language models (LLMs) to call API operations to perform operations on cloud resources. |
| Call Statistics | You can view data on the Call Overview, Call Statistics, and Statistical Reports pages. Call Overview: displays the call trends and error distribution. Call Trend: You can select a time range and view the total number of calls, the number of errors, and the error rate within the selected period of time. The number of calls to each cloud service is displayed in a column chart. You can move the pointer over the column chart to view the number of successful calls and the number of failed calls. Error Distribution: You can view the distribution of API errors based on filter conditions such as the call date, cloud service, and API version. Call Statistics: You can specify the filter conditions, such as service, API version, API name, and time range, to query the call details of an API operation of a cloud service. You can view the namespace, number of calls each time, average duration per call, and call success rate of an API operation. You can click Call Source Distribution in the Actions column of an API operation to view the AccessKey ID that is used for calls and identify the source of the operation. Statistical Reports: You can configure the following parameters to create a statistical report task based on your business requirements: Interval, Data Source, Statistical Policy, Keyword, and Custom Aggregation Policy. After a statistical report task is created, you can view the task status and report details at any time. This helps you understand the status of your business. In addition, you can start, stop, or delete statistical report tasks. |

| Automati on Service Desk | The Automation Service Desk module includes the Template, Task, andT erraform Explorer modules. Template: includes Template Management and Template Center. Apsara Stack provides a series of templates based on Terraform to manage cloud resources in a standardized manner. You can also upload custom templates and edit templates online. Task: orchestrates resources based on templates and tracks the status of resources during the orchestration process. Terraform Explorer: debugs Terraform templates online. |
|---|---|
| Page Integrati on | You can configure page integration for Apsara Stack pages to directly embed cloud management pages into third-party platforms. You can hide the top navigation bar and adjust the color of a page to ensure that the page adapts to third-party platforms. This minimizes the effort required to integrate pages into third-party platforms. |

in the top navigation bar.

5. On the **Custom Services** tab, click **Create MCP Service**.
6. On the **Create MCP Service** page, configure the parameters. The following table
describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Name | The name of the MCP service. |
| Organization | The organization to which the MCP service belongs. |
| Resource Set | The resource set to which the MCP service belongs. |
| Region | The region to which the MCP service belongs. |

| Document Language | The language of the MCP service document. Valid values:C hinese and English. |
|---|---|
| Cloud Products and APIs | Configure API operations for the MCP service. Add cloud services and API operations a. Click Add Cloud Product and API. b. In the Create dialog box, select the service, the service version, and API operations to be added. c. Click OK. Add API operations for an added cloud service a. In the Cloud Products and APIs section, find the added cloud service for which you want to add API operations and click Add in the Actions column. b. In the Add API dialog box, select the API operations that you want to add. c. Click OK. Modify an API operation of a service a. In the Cloud Products and APIs section, find the API operation of the service that you want to modify and click Edit in the Actions column. b. In the panel that appears, modify the settings in the API Overview, API Request Description, and API Parameters sections. Note When the answer of the large language model (LLM) that depends on the MCP service is inaccurate, you can modify the API overview, API request description, and API parameters to improve the LLM's understanding of each API operation. When you modify API parameters, you can also delete some optional parameters. When the LLM transmits parameters to the API operation, these deleted parameters are invisible to the API operation. This reduces the error rate of the LLM and the token consumption. After you save the modifications, you must disconnect and reconnect the MCP service on the client to make the modifications take effect. c. Click Save and Submit. Remove an API operation a. In the Cloud Products and APIs section, find the API operation that you want to remove and click Delete in the Actions column. b. In the message that appears, click OK. Remove all API operations of an added cloud service of a version a. In the Cloud Products and APIs section, find the cloud service whose API operations you want to remove and click Delete in the Actions column. b. In the message that appears, click OK. |

| Description | The description of the MCP service. |
|---|---|

7. Click **Create**.
8. In the **Risks** message, read the risk tips and click **I have known the risks and continue**
**the update**.
9. Perform related operations on MCP services. The following table describes the supported
operations.

| Operation | Procedure |
|---|---|

| View the details of an MCP service | i. On the Custom Services tab, find the MCP service that you want to view and click Details in the Actions column. ii. On the MCP Service Details page, view the details of the MCP service. Note The Configuration Information section displays SSE Endpoint. You can click View Configuration Methods to view the MCP client configuration example. These contents are used to connect the MCP client to the MCP service. If you use the MCP client to connect to the MCP service for the first time, you must download the MCP agent plug-in for Java. The plug-in is used to provide identity authentication information when you call an API operation. The myak, mysk, and absolute path of the plug-in must be specified in the configuration information. If the Apsara Stack version is updated, the MCP agent plug-in version may be updated accordingly. If necessary, you can redownload the MCP agent plug-in to your on-premises machine and use the new agent plug-in version. |
|---|---|
| Modify an MCP service | i. On the Custom Services tab, find the MCP service that you want to modify and click Edit in the Actions column. ii. In the Edit dialog box, modify the Name and Description parameters of the MCP service. iii. Click OK. |

| Share an MCP service | i. On the Custom Services tab, find the MCP service that you want to share and click Share in the Actions column. ii. In the Share MCP Service dialog box, select the organization with which the MCP service is to be shared. You can select multiple organizations. After the MCP service is shared with the selected organization, users of the organization can view the shared MCP service on the Shared Services tab of the MCP Service page. Note In the Shared Information list, you can find the organization with which the MCP is to be shared and click Delete in the Actions column to remove the organization. After the organization is removed, the MCP service is no longer displayed on the Shared Services tab visible to the users of the organization. iii. Click OK. |
|---|---|
| Delete an MCP service | i. On the Custom Services tab, find the MCP service that you want to delete and click Delete in the Actions column. Note If a service is shared, you must unshare it before you can delete it. ii. In the message that appears, click OK. |

### 12.3 Call Statistics

This topic describes how to use the Call Statistics module in OpenAPI Explorer.
1. Log on to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. In the top navigation bar, choose **Products** > **Development Tools** > **API & SDK** >
**OpenAPI Explorer**.
3. On the **OpenAPI Explorer** page, click **Call Statistics** in the top navigation bar.
4. Perform the following operations in the **Call Statistics** module:
**Call Overview**: In the left-side navigation pane, click **Call Overview**.
**Call Trend**: Configure the **Call Date** parameter to select a time range and view the
total number of calls, the number of errors, and the error rate within the specified time range. The number of calls to each cloud service is displayed in a column chart. Move the pointer over the column chart to view the numbers of successful and failed calls.
**Error Distribution**: Configure the **Call Date**, **Cloud Service**, and **API Version**
parameters to view the distribution of API errors based on the specified filter conditions.
**Call Statistics**: In the left-side navigation pane, click **Call Statistics**.
Configure the **Service**, **API Version**, **API Name**, and **Called At** parameters to search for the call details of an API operation of a cloud service. The information is displayed in the following columns: **API Name**, **Service**, **Namespace**, **API Version**, **Calls/Times**,
**Average Latency (ms)**, and **Success Rate**.
The value of the **Called At** parameter must be within seven days.

> Click **Call Source Distribution** in the **Actions** column of an API operation to view the **AccessKey** ID and the source service of the API operation.

**Statistical Reports**: In the left-side navigation pane, click **Statistical Reports**.
Create a statistical report task: On the Statistical Reports page, click **Create**
**Statistical Report**. In the Create Task dialog box, configure the parameters described
in the following table and click **OK**.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Task Name | The name of the statistical report task. |
| Interval | The interval at which the statistical report task retrieves statistics. Valid values: 1 Hour 6 Hours 12 Hours 24 Hours |
| Data Source | The source of the statistics. Valid value: pop-sls. |
| Statistical Policy | The method used to retrieve statistics. Valid value: Keyword Retrieval. |
| Keyword | The keywords used to retrieve statistics. Click Add Entry and specify keywords in key-value pairs. |
| Custom Aggregation Policy | The aggregation policy. Select an aggregation policy from the drop-down list. |

View a statistical report task: The created statistical report tasks are displayed in the task list. a. Find the statistical report task that you want to view and click **View Reports** in the
**Actions** column.
b. The execution history of the statistical report task is displayed. Click **View Details** in the **Actions** column of a report to view the report details in the following sections:
**Basic Information**, **Matching Info**, and **Time Distribution**.
Start a statistical report task: Find the statistical report task that you want to start and click **Start** in the **Actions** column If the task changes to the **Running** state, the task is started.

> **Note:** You can start tasks only in the **Canceled** state.

Stop a statistical report task: Find the statistical report task that you want to stop and click **Stop** in the **Actions** column. If the task changes to the **Canceled** state, the task is stopped.

> **Note:** You can stop tasks only in the **Running** state.

Delete a statistical report task: Find the statistical report task that you want to delete and click **Delete** in the **Actions** column. In the message that appears, click **OK**.

### 12.5 Page integration

This topic describes the procedure for page integration.

**Background information**

The Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console provides configuration capabilities for page integration, including customization of page color scheme, language, appearance and theme color, brand logo, and platform version declaration. The console supports hiding original brand information, adjusting layout, and changing page styles to match the style of the customer’s or third-party ISV’s cloud management console, thereby enhancing consistency in user experience.

**Prerequisites**

Before integrating the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console pages into a customerowned or third-party ISV management console, you must complete SSO authentication through the Cloud Management Platform. You must configure unified identity authentication between the management console application (which will integrate Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console pages) and the private cloud Cloud Management Platform. This means configuring the Cloud Management Platform as the Service Provider (SP) and the customerowned or third-party ISV management console as the Identity Provider (IdP), ensuring single sign-on (SSO) support when users navigate between platforms. For specific configuration methods of third-party authentication in the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console, see Third-party authentication.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.
2. Click **Product** in the top navigation bar, then select **Development tools** > **APIs and**
**tools** > **Developer Portal**.
3. On the **Developer Portal** page, click **Page Integration** in the menu bar.
4. On the **Page Integration Overview** page, click **Page open configuration** to complete
Embedding target application configuration, Page style configuration, and Embedded page list configuration.
5. After completing the configuration, embed the required cloud service management pages
into the management console application that needs to integrate Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console pages. On the **Page Integration Overview** page, click **Page URL embedding** to view the operation URLs of the configured cloud service management pages.

**Embedding target application configuration**

Fill in the information of the Management Console application (your own or a third-party ISV Management Console) that needs to integrate pages from the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console.

| Section | Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Switch settings | Integration switch | If you need to embed cloud service management pages from the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console into your Management Console application, turn on the integration switch. When embedded, the original navigation bar on the opened page hides automatically. If you turn off this switch, your Management Console application cannot embed the integrated cloud service management pages via iFrame. |
|   | Hide left-side navigation | Turn on the Hide left-side navigation switch. When your Management Console application displays an integrated cloud service management page, it hides the left-side navigation bar by default to avoid displaying all related pages. After hiding the left- side navigation bar, you can access specific page URLs to display only the required integrated pages within your Management Console application. |
|   | Application Name | Enter the name of the application that needs to integrate pages from the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console. The application name must be 3 to 25 characters long. |

| psara Uni-man |   |   |
|---|---|---|
| Basic informatio n |   |   |
|   | Application Domain Name Address | Enter the domain name address of the application that needs to integrate pages from the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console. This is the domain name of your own or a third-party ISV Management Console. The domain name address must use HTTPS, for example, https://console.example.com. Note You must enter all domain name addresses involved in the application that integrates pages (including the domain name address of the main iFrame page). Otherwise, browser security restrictions may prevent the embedded pages from displaying correctly after integration. When configuring multiple domain name addresses, separate them with commas (,). |
|   | Application description | Provide a brief description of the application that needs to integrate pages from the Apsara Uni-Manager Management Console. |
| Log in authentication integration |   | Use the super account to log in to the console and navigate to Configuration > Third-party configuration to complete login authentication integration. |

**Page style configuration**

Configure the display style of integrated pages to manage the console application page style.

| Section | Configuration item | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Platform language | Please select the language supported by the platform | The Apsara Uni-manager Management Console supports multiple languages. Select the languages required for the integrated console application, including Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and English. |
|   | Select the platform default language | Select the default language for the integrated console application. The embedded Apsara Uni-manager Management Console pages display in this language by default. |
| Appearanc e and theme | Appearance | You can select the appearance style of the integrated pages, including light mode and Dark Mode. |
|   | Theme Color | You can select the theme color of the integrated pages. You can choose Recommended Theme Color or Custom Palette. |

| Page watermark | Switch | You can configure watermarks for integrated pages. After you turn on the switch, specify the watermark content. The watermark content can contain up to 10 characters. |
|---|---|---|

**Embedded page list configuration**

Configure the page URLs of cloud service management pages opened in the Apsara Unimanager Management Console when they are integrated. To ensure that resource operation buttons (such as Create and Modify) on embedded cloud service management pages correctly redirect to the corresponding resource creation or modification pages in the integrating party's Management Console, you must configure the appropriate resource operation link addresses for these buttons. This achieves seamless integration between Management Console resource management operations and the integrating party's business.
1. In the left-side categories **Apsara Stack** and **Alibaba Cloud Public Cloud**, find the target
cloud service.

> **Note:** **Alibaba Cloud Public Cloud** appears only when multi-cloud management is deployed.

2. In the product page list on the right, click **Edit** in the **Actions** column.
3. In the **Edit** dialog box, modify the link URL based on your business requirements.
You can change the link URL to a third-party operation link address. The domain name of the modified link address must match the root domain name of the embedded page, and the address must be an absolute URL.
4. Click **OK**.

## 13 Apsara Stack Skills portal

The Apsara Stack Skills portal is a centralized management portal for open skills in Apsara Stack Enterprise Edition. The portal enables Apsara Stack users to discover, browse, install, and manage skills. Skills are standardized capabilities that AI agents use to call Alibaba Cloud service CLI or MCP and intelligently manage cloud resources on the tenant side.
1. Log in to the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console.
2. Go to the homepage of the Apsara Stack Skills portal.
Method 1: Click **Products** in the top menu bar and choose **Development Tools** > **APIs**
**& SDK** > **Apsara Stack Skills Portal**.
Method 2: Go to the OpenAPI Explorer. a. Click **Products** in the top menu bar and choose **Development Tools** > **APIs & SDK**
> **OpenAPI Explorer**.

b. On the OpenAPI Explorer page, click **Apsara Stack Skills Portal** in the top menu.
3. View the information on the portal homepage.

| Page section | Description |
|---|---|
